# GoodVibes: overview, terms, architecture and where everything is stored

This file describes GoodVibes release 3.3.3 completely. It is written for a language model that operates GoodVibes for a person. Everything a person or an automated client can reach is described here: installing, every program and command, every setting, every slash command, every model tool, every environment variable, every file GoodVibes writes, the operator API and every error. Nothing outside this file is needed.

How to read this file:

- Each part starts with a heading of the form `# Part title`. Sections inside a part use `##` and `###`.
- A reference to another place in this file names its heading in quotes, for example "Settings: layers, scopes and how to change them".
- Text in backticks is exact: a command, a file path, a setting key, a value. Type it as shown.
- `<name>` in a command stands for a value you supply. `[x]` is optional. `a|b` is a choice of one.
- `~` is the home directory of the person whose installation it is.
- The complete lists (settings, commands, slash commands, tools, variables, methods, events, errors, providers) are in the part "Reference" at the end. They are built from the programs themselves.

## What GoodVibes is

GoodVibes is an AI coding and personal-assistant platform that runs on the owner's own machine. It has a terminal coding app, a personal-assistant app, a background daemon and a browser interface. A person talks to a model; the model reads and edits files, runs commands, delegates work to helper agents, answers messages on chat channels, keeps memory and runs scheduled work. Every action the model takes passes a permission check, and a second model (the decision model) can make routine judgment calls so the person is asked less often.

GoodVibes works with many model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, local servers such as Ollama and LM Studio, and others); see "Providers" in the reference. The person brings their own API keys or signs in with a subscription where a provider offers one.

## The programs and how they connect

GoodVibes is four programs. They share one engine and one set of files on the machine.

| Program | Command | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| terminal app | `goodvibes` | The terminal coding app: a full-screen interface for working in a project with a model. Also a command line (`goodvibes run`, `goodvibes status`, `goodvibes service`, and more). |
| Agent | `goodvibes-agent` | The personal-assistant app: a terminal interface and command line for knowledge, memory, routines, reminders, channels and personal operations. It hands coding work to the terminal app (`/agents hand-off`). |
| daemon | `goodvibes-daemon` | The one long-running background program on a machine. It hosts the control plane (the HTTP operator API), the chat channels, cluster membership, scheduled work, the knowledge and memory stores, hosted sessions and the web UI. |
| web UI | none (a page in a browser) | The browser interface, served by the daemon at the same address as the operator API (by default `http://127.0.0.1:3421`). |

How they talk to each other:

- The daemon listens for HTTP on the control-plane address: host `127.0.0.1` and port `3421` by default (settings `controlPlane.host` and `controlPlane.port`). Until `controlPlane.enabled` is `true`, it answers only requests from the same machine.
- The terminal app and Agent are clients of the daemon. They call the daemon's operator API over HTTP, receive its events as a server-sent event stream, and send it the settings it owns. Each app runs its own conversations and model requests in its own process.
- The terminal app uses the daemon on the same machine by default. `daemon.connectedHost.url` points it at a daemon on another machine. Agent uses the daemon on the same machine unless `--runtime-url` or `GOODVIBES_AGENT_RUNTIME_URL` names another address.
- The credential each app presents to its daemon: for its operator calls the terminal app sends the daemon on the same machine `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_TOKEN` when it is set, otherwise the daemon's own operator token (`operator-tokens.json`); a daemon on another machine gets only the token stored for that address in `~/.goodvibes/tui/connected-daemons.json` (or a session from `/accounts sign-in daemon <url>`, kept in the same file), never this machine's token or `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_TOKEN`. Agent looks, in this order, at `GOODVIBES_CONNECTED_HOST_TOKEN`, `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_TOKEN`, its own pairing with that daemon (`~/.goodvibes/agent/connected-host-pairings/pairings.json`), and then the daemon's `operator-tokens.json`, which it presents only when the host address is this machine (a loopback address or one of its own interface addresses).
- The web UI is a built set of static files. The daemon serves them from its own control-plane listener after `goodvibes-daemon webui enable`, so the web UI and the API share one origin.
- Phones and other computers reach a daemon after pairing (`goodvibes pair`, `goodvibes-daemon pair`), through remote access, or through a relay; see the part on the daemon and networking.
- Several daemons on one network can form a cluster and share inbound channel work (`goodvibes-daemon cluster`). One daemon in a cluster is a node.
- Editors that speak the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) drive the terminal app with `goodvibes acp`. MCP clients use `goodvibes-daemon mcp serve`.

The daemon is installed as a user service by default, so it starts at login (Linux: a systemd user service named `goodvibes.service`; macOS: a launchd agent labelled `sh.goodvibes.daemon`). It can also run in the foreground with `goodvibes-daemon` or `goodvibes-daemon serve`.

The engine package also contains a `goodvibes-contract` command for driving contracts from a script. The installers do not install it; its exit codes are listed under "Exit codes" in the reference.

## Glossary

Each term below is used with exactly this meaning everywhere in this file.

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| owner | The person whose installation it is. Some decisions (spending money, loosening security, owner-only actions) are always the owner's. |
| terminal app | The `goodvibes` program. |
| Agent | The `goodvibes-agent` program. |
| daemon | The `goodvibes-daemon` program, the long-running background host. |
| web UI | The browser interface the daemon serves. |
| app | The terminal app or Agent. |
| provider | A model service: OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, a local Ollama server, and so on. Each has an id such as `openai`. |
| model | A model offered by a provider, named `provider:model`, for example `openai:gpt-5.2`. This full name is the model's registry key. |
| sign-in | One way of authenticating to a provider: an API key, a subscription sign-in (OAuth), or none for a local server. |
| session | One saved conversation between the owner and the model, with its tool calls. Sessions are saved per project and can be resumed. |
| turn | One request from the owner and everything the model does to answer it. |
| tool | An action the model can call: read a file, edit a file, run a command, fetch a page, spawn a helper agent. The list is under "Model tools" in the reference. |
| slash command | A command typed into an app's prompt starting with `/`, such as `/model` or `/settings`. |
| helper agent | A second model run the main model starts to do part of the work (the `agent` tool). |
| contract | Work handed to helper agents as a set of units, each checked against acceptance criteria until it passes. |
| the gate | The permission check every tool call passes before it runs. It allows the call, asks the owner, asks the decision model, or refuses. |
| permission mode | Who settles what ordinary rules do not: `ask-me` (the owner is asked about dangerous actions), `jev-decides` (the decision model decides judgment calls; the default), `just-vibes` (work without interrupting; anything that needs the owner is held to the end), `yolo` (every action runs without safety denials; containment, secret storage and payment limits still apply). Setting `permissions.mode`. |
| plan mode | The read-only planning posture (`permissions.mode` value `plan`): the model plans and changes nothing. |
| decision model | The second, small model the gate and other parts ask for routine judgment calls. Jev is the hosted decision model; a local one can be configured (settings `judgment.*`). |
| decision model policy | How GoodVibes uses the decision model (setting `judgment.policy`): `Hybrid` (the default; use it, and continue with fallbacks when none is set or it fails), `Decision Model Only` (stop and report when it fails), `No Decision Model` (never call it). |
| setting | A named value that changes behaviour, written as a dotted key such as `display.stream`. The list is under "Settings" in the reference. |
| project | The directory an app works in (its working directory). Per-project state is kept in `<project>/.goodvibes/`. |
| channel | A chat surface the daemon answers on: Slack, Discord, Telegram, email, and others. |
| node | One daemon in a cluster. |
| operator API | The daemon's HTTP API, used by the apps, the web UI and scripts. Its methods are under "Operator API methods" in the reference. |
| operator token | A bearer token that authorises a client to the operator API. |
| pairing | Giving another device or app a named token for a daemon, usually by a link or QR code. |
| checkpoint | A snapshot of a project's files taken before the model changes them, so a change can be undone. |
| memory | Facts and notes GoodVibes keeps across sessions. |
| knowledge | Documents and sources GoodVibes has read and can search. |
| secret store | Where GoodVibes keeps credentials, encrypted; see "Credentials and the secret store". |

## Architecture

### The daemon

The daemon is the one process on a machine that keeps running when no app is open. It is the home of everything that must work unattended: channels, schedules and triggers, watchers, the owner inbox, payments, pairing, remote access, hosted sessions (conversations whose loop runs inside the daemon), the web UI, and the shared memory and knowledge stores. Settings that the daemon acts on are stored in the daemon's own settings file, and every app reads and writes that one value (see "Settings: layers, scopes and how to change them").

When the daemon is not running, features that live in the daemon report that they are unavailable instead of failing silently.

### Sessions and turns

A turn starts when the owner sends a message. The app sends the conversation to the selected model; the model answers with text, tool calls, or both. Each tool call passes the gate, runs, and its result goes back to the model, until the model answers without asking for more tools. The session is saved under the project (`<project>/.goodvibes/tui/sessions/` for the terminal app) and can be listed and resumed (`goodvibes sessions`, `goodvibes --resume`).

### The gate

Every tool call is classed by its permission category: `read`, `write`, `execute` or `delegate`. The gate weighs the call's category and what it touches against the owner's remembered rules, the per-tool settings (`permissions.tools.*`) and the permission mode. Judgment calls go to the decision model; owner-only decisions, and anything still unsettled, go to the owner. Some actions always ask the owner whatever the mode. The full rules are in the part on permissions and decisions.

### The decision model

The decision model answers short structured questions (is this command safe here, does this message need the owner) so the owner is asked less. By default it is Jev at the hosted address; `judgment.endpoint` and `judgment.model` choose another, and `judgment.policy` chooses how strictly it is relied on. With `No Decision Model`, or with no decision model reachable under `Hybrid`, every decision takes its fallback, which is usually to ask the owner.

### Stores

GoodVibes keeps its state in plain files and SQLite databases under two roots: the home tree `~/.goodvibes/` and each project's `<project>/.goodvibes/`. Settings are JSON files. Credentials are in encrypted secret stores. Memory, the owner inbox, knowledge, the code index and the decision log are SQLite databases. Checkpoints are a separate git repository inside the project's `.goodvibes/` directory, never the project's own git history. The next section lists every location.

## Files and directories GoodVibes creates

### The home tree

The home tree is `~/.goodvibes/`. `GOODVIBES_HOME=<dir>` moves it to `<dir>/.goodvibes/` for the terminal app, the daemon and the Agent; `GOODVIBES_AGENT_HOME=<dir>` moves the Agent alone. An installation made with `scripts/install-from-checkout.sh` sets `GOODVIBES_HOME` to its data directory (default `~/.local/share/goodvibes-data`), so its home tree is `~/.local/share/goodvibes-data/.goodvibes/`. `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME=<dir>` (or `goodvibes-daemon --daemon-home <dir>`) moves only the `daemon/` directory below.

"Edit by hand" says whether a person may change the file with a text editor. A settings file is read again when it changes on disk, so a hand edit takes effect without a restart. Every other file is written by the programs; change it only through the commands named.

| Path (under the home tree) | What it holds | Edit by hand |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tui/settings.json` | The terminal app's own settings. | Yes. JSON; see "Settings: layers, scopes and how to change them". |
| `agent/settings.json` | Agent's own settings. | Yes. |
| `shared/settings.json` | The five text-to-speech keys `tts.provider`, `tts.voice`, `tts.speed`, `tts.llmProvider` and `tts.llmModel`, shared by all three programs. Nothing else is read from this file. | Yes. |
| `shared/subscriptions.json` | Provider subscription sign-ins (such as a ChatGPT subscription signed in with `/provider sign-in`) and their tokens, one file read and written by all three programs, so a sign-in made in one is used by the others. Written with permissions `0600`. | No. Sign in and out with `/provider sign-in` and `/provider sign-out`, or `goodvibes subscription`. |
| `daemon/settings.json` | The daemon's settings: every key the daemon acts on (channels, control plane, schedules, payments, the decision model, and more). | Yes, or use `goodvibes-daemon config set`, which checks the value before writing it. |
| `daemon-host/settings.json` | The daemon's own value of every key that each program keeps separately (for example `service.*`, `update.*`, `permissions.mode` for the daemon's own sessions). The daemon reads it; `goodvibes-daemon config set` writes it. | Yes. |
| `daemon/operator-tokens.json` | The daemon's operator tokens. | No. Manage tokens with the commands in the daemon part. |
| `daemon/secrets.enc` | Credentials the daemon uses (channel tokens, provider keys it needs, card material references), encrypted. | No. Use `goodvibes secrets` or the apps' secret commands. |
| `tui/secrets.enc`, `agent/secrets.enc` | Each app's own encrypted credentials. | No. |
| `tui.secrets.json`, `agent.secrets.json` | Plain-text credential stores, used only when the secret policy allows plain text. | No. |
| `secrets.key` | The random key that encrypts every `secrets.enc`. Without it those stores cannot be read. | Never. Do not delete, move or share it. |
| `tui.json`, `agent.json` | A configuration file each app creates when it starts (`{}` when new). | No. |
| `tui/keybindings.json`, `agent/keybindings.json` | Custom key bindings. | Yes. |
| `tui/guidance.json`, `agent/guidance.json` | Which one-time guidance notices were shown. | No. |
| `tui/discovered-providers.json` | Local model servers found on this machine. | No. |
| `tui/auth-users.json` | Local user accounts for signing in to the daemon and the web UI. | No. Use `goodvibes auth`. |
| `tui/auth-bootstrap.txt` | The first-run bootstrap sign-in credential. Its password signs in only while this file holds it: deleting or clearing the file withdraws it. Setting `admin`'s password deletes the file. | No. `goodvibes auth clear-bootstrap` deletes it (and so withdraws the password). |
| `tui/connected-daemons.json` | The token the terminal app presents to each daemon on another machine, keyed by that daemon's address (written by the setup choice "Connect to an existing running daemon"). | No. |
| `agent/connected-host-pairings/pairings.json` | Agent's pairing with each daemon it connects to. | No. |
| `tui/control-plane/` | Control-plane state: pairing tokens, daemon lifecycle, notification dead letters, occasion state, announcements. | No. |
| `tui/knowledge-*.sqlite` | Knowledge stores. | No. |
| `tui/crashes.jsonl`, `agent/crashes.jsonl` | A record of crashes, one JSON object per line. | No. Read it when reporting a crash. |
| `tui/browser/`, `agent/browser/` | The browser tools' driver (`driver/`), browser profiles with their sign-ins (`profiles/`) and saved screenshots (`screenshots/`). | No. |
| `shared/memory.sqlite`, `shared/memory.vec.sqlite` | Memory records and their search index. | No. Use the memory commands. |
| `shared/owner-inbox.sqlite` | The owner inbox: questions, held actions, purchase windows and reports of unattended runs waiting for the owner. | No. |
| `hosted-sessions/` | Conversations the daemon hosts. | No. |
| `companion-chat/sessions/` | Companion chat conversations (web UI and phone). | No. |
| `project-identities/` | Which project directory has which project id. | No. |
| `voice/` | The managed voice tree, one copy for every program: speech engines and models, with the wake-word classifiers in `voice/wake/models/` and the wake-word front end in `voice/wake/front-end/`. | No. `goodvibes-daemon provision-wake-model` fetches missing wake-word files. |
| `daemon/service/` | The service manager's state for the daemon (process id file, the definition used on a platform without a service manager). | No. |

### The project tree

Each project an app works in gets `<project>/.goodvibes/`. It contains a `.gitignore` holding `*`, so git ignores everything in it and none of it is committed. On first use in a git project the terminal app also adds the line `.goodvibes/` (under the comment `# goodvibes-tui transient state`) to the clone's own exclude file, `.git/info/exclude`, which git does not track, unless the project's `.gitignore` or that file already has it, and prints `[goodvibes] git now ignores '.goodvibes/' in this clone (.git/info/exclude; your .gitignore is unchanged): it holds transient TUI state (logs, session cache, exec output), not project source.` The project's `.gitignore` is never edited.

| Path (under `<project>/.goodvibes/`) | What it holds | Edit by hand |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tui/settings.json`, `agent/settings.json` | Project settings: values for this project only. A repository can carry them, so only presentation, behaviour, contract and some permission keys are honoured, and a permission key only when it is stricter (see the reference entry of each setting). | Yes. |
| `tui/sessions/`, `agent/sessions/` | Saved sessions of this project. | No. Use `goodvibes sessions`. |
| `tui/recovery/` | Journals used to recover an interrupted session. | No. |
| `tui/state/` | Session state the tools keep. | No. |
| `tui/checkpoints/git/` | The checkpoint repository: a separate git repository holding snapshots of the project's files. | No. Use the checkpoint and undo commands. |
| `tui/secrets.enc` | Credentials that belong to this project. A key first found here is used only after the owner confirms it once. | No. |
| `tui/code-index.sqlite` | The project's code search index. | No. |
| `tui/decisions.sqlite` | The decision log: every reading asked of the decision model in this project, answered or failed. | No. |
| `tui/watchers.json` | Watchers defined for this project. | No. |
| `tui/triggers.db` | Supervised triggers. Only the daemon keeps them, so this file exists in the daemon's working directory; both apps use the daemon's triggers. | No. Use `/triggers` or the `trigger` tool. |
| `project-index.json` | The project's file index. | No. |
| `worktrees.json` | Git worktrees GoodVibes created for parallel work. | No. |
| `logs/activity.md` | The activity log of programs working in this project, in Markdown; the previous one is kept as `activity.md.1`. | Read only. |

When the daemon works in a project (its working directory, set by `--working-dir`, `GOODVIBES_WORKING_DIR` or `runtime.workingDir`), it keeps its project state in that project's `.goodvibes/tui/` too: device grants (`devices/`), channel routes (`operator/channel-routes.sqlite`), supervised triggers (`triggers.db`), cluster identity (`cluster/`) and remote runner state (`remote/`).

### Programs, service files and installation records

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `~/.local/bin/goodvibes`, `~/.local/bin/goodvibes-agent`, `~/.local/bin/goodvibes-daemon` | The commands (both installers; `--bin-dir` or `GOODVIBES_INSTALL_DIR` change the directory). |
| `~/.local/bin/webui/` | Web UI bundles installed by `scripts/install.sh`, one directory per version. |
| `~/.local/share/goodvibes/` | A checkout installation's programs, its releases and its receipt `installation.json` (`--prefix` changes it). |
| `~/.local/share/goodvibes-data/` | A checkout installation's data directory (`--data-dir` changes it); its `environment` file is read by the installed `goodvibes`, `goodvibes-agent` and `goodvibes-daemon` commands before they start, which is where `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` and other variables go. |
| `~/.config/systemd/user/goodvibes.service` | The daemon's service definition on Linux. |
| `~/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.goodvibes.daemon.plist` | The daemon's service definition on macOS. |

Installing, updating and removing are described step by step in the part on installing. Uninstalling a release installation never removes the home tree; remove `~/.goodvibes` by hand to erase all data. Uninstalling a checkout installation keeps its data directory unless `--purge` is given.

### Credentials and the secret store

A credential (an API key, a bot token, a password) is looked up in this order, and the first one found is used:

1. An environment variable of the same name.
2. The daemon's stores (`daemon/secrets.enc`, then a plain-text daemon store).
3. The app's own encrypted store (`tui/secrets.enc` or `agent/secrets.enc`).
4. The app's plain-text store (`tui.secrets.json` or `agent.secrets.json`), when the secret policy allows plain text.
5. The project's stores, only after the owner confirmed that key once.

A stored value can be a reference to a password manager (1Password, Bitwarden, Vaultwarden, Bitwarden Secrets Manager) or a command; it is resolved when it is used. Settings files never hold a credential: a setting that names one holds a `goodvibes://secrets/...` reference. Store, list and test credentials with `goodvibes secrets` (and the same command in Agent).

## Settings: layers, scopes and how to change them

### Which file a setting lives in

Each setting key is stored in one of three ways, decided by the key. The "Stored in" of each key's reference entry says which.

| Stored in | Terminal app reads | Agent reads | Daemon reads | Written by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the daemon file (keys the daemon acts on) | `~/.goodvibes/daemon/settings.json` | the same file | the same file | `goodvibes-daemon config set`; a change made in an app is sent to the running daemon, which writes it, or written by the app itself when no daemon is running |
| the shared file (only `tts.provider`, `tts.voice`, `tts.speed`, `tts.llmProvider`, `tts.llmModel`) | `~/.goodvibes/shared/settings.json` | the same file | the same file | any program that changes one of these keys |
| each program's own file (every other key) | `~/.goodvibes/tui/settings.json` | `~/.goodvibes/agent/settings.json` | `~/.goodvibes/daemon-host/settings.json` | the terminal app's `/settings` and `/settings set`; Agent's `/settings`; `goodvibes-daemon config set` |

Keys stored in each program's own file have one value per program. `provider.model` set with `/model` in the terminal app does not change Agent's model, and `service.enabled` set with `goodvibes-daemon config set` changes the daemon's own value, not the one `goodvibes doctor` reads in the terminal app. To change such a key for a program, change it in that program or in its file. `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME` moves the daemon file to `<GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME>/settings.json`.

### How a value is resolved

When a program reads a setting, the value comes from the highest layer that sets it:

1. The default built into the program (lowest).
2. The program's own settings file in the home tree (`tui/`, `agent/` or `daemon-host/settings.json`).
3. The program's project settings file (`<project>/.goodvibes/tui/settings.json`, `<project>/.goodvibes/agent/settings.json`, or for the daemon `<working directory>/.goodvibes/daemon-host/settings.json`), for keys a project may set.
4. The shared settings file, for the five `tts.*` keys it holds.
5. The daemon settings file, for daemon-owned keys.
6. Launch options, for this run only (highest): `-c <key>=<value>` (or `--config`), `--enable <feature>`, `--disable <feature>`, `--model`, `--provider`, `--just-vibes`, `--yolo`, and the daemon's `--hostname` and `--port`.

A change to a key the project file already holds is written to the project file; otherwise it is written to the file the table above names.

Launch options are never saved. A project settings file may set only presentation, behaviour, contract, worktree and some checkpoint and agent keys; for permission keys it is honoured only when it is stricter than the owner's own value. Keys that send data off the machine, run a command, name a credential or a model are ignored in a project file, with a notice.

Some environment variables stand in for a setting when the setting is empty, for example `TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL` for `judgment.model`. Each such variable is named in that setting's reference entry and in "Environment variables".

### Reading and writing a setting

A settings file is JSON with each dotted key written as nested objects. The key `controlPlane.port` with value `3999` is written as:

```json
{
  "controlPlane": {
    "port": 3999
  }
}
```

From the daemon's command line (works whether or not the daemon is running; a running daemon applies most keys at once):

```sh
goodvibes-daemon config get controlPlane.port
goodvibes-daemon config set controlPlane.port 3999
goodvibes-daemon config list
```

`config set` prints:

```text
controlPlane.port = 3999
  written to disk. A running daemon applies most keys live, including a changed control-plane
  host or port; a key that is only read when the daemon starts applies the next time it starts.
```

A value that does not fit the key is refused, nothing is written, and the command exits `1`:

```text
config: could not write controlPlane.port: expected number (integer port in [1, 65535]).
```

A key that does not exist is refused the same way with `not a settings key. Run \`goodvibes-daemon config list\` to see them.` Values are read as JSON first, then `true`, `false` or a number, then as plain text: `config set judgment.policy "No Decision Model"` stores the text, `config set display.stream false` stores the boolean. A daemon-owned key (`controlPlane.port`) goes to the daemon file; any other key (`display.stream`) goes to `~/.goodvibes/daemon-host/settings.json` and changes only the daemon's own value.

When the terminal app or Agent writes a daemon-owned key while a daemon runs, the write goes to that daemon. A daemon that cannot be reached (refused connection, unknown host) gets nothing: the message says the setting was NOT applied. A write that was sent but whose answer was lost or could not be read (a timeout, a dropped connection, an answer this version cannot read) may have been applied, so the app reads the key back once from the daemon: the value it sent is there, and the write is reported done; otherwise the message says the outcome is not known, what the daemon holds now, and to read it back with `goodvibes config get <key>` before setting it again. Several keys sent as one update are settled the same way, and the update reports the value the daemon holds for each key.

Inside the terminal app:

- `/settings` lists what it does; `/settings open [topic|key|words]` opens the settings screen there, and `/settings list`, `get <key>`, `set <key> <value>` and `reset <key>` read and change settings without the screen, as in the Agent.
- `/settings set <key> <value>` sets a key directly.

Inside Agent:

- `/settings` opens the settings screen. `/settings list`, `/settings get <key>`, `/settings set <key> <value>` and `/settings reset <key>` read and change settings without the screen.

For one launch only:

```sh
goodvibes -c display.stream=false
goodvibes-agent --config provider.model=openai:gpt-5.2
goodvibes-daemon -c update.auto=false serve --port 39421
```

By editing the file: open the settings file named in the key's reference entry, add or change the nested key, and save. A running app or daemon reads the file again when it changes. A settings file that is not valid JSON is never skipped, because it may hold permission or safety settings: the program refuses to start and names the file, for example:

```text
Settings file ~/.goodvibes/tui/settings.json refused: could not be read as JSON: JSON Parse error: Unexpected EOF. fix or move the file; a settings file that cannot be parsed may hold permission or safety settings, so it is not skipped
goodvibes failed to start: Global config load failed for /home/me/.goodvibes/tui/settings.json: JSON Parse error: Unexpected EOF
```

Fix the JSON (or move the file away to start from defaults) and start the program again.

A key the program does not know (a misspelling, or a key from a newer release), or one that belongs in another file (a daemon setting in a program's or a project's file), is skipped and the rest of the file applies; so is a value that is not one the setting allows (a renamed value from an earlier release included: it is not read under its new name). It is said once, in one short line naming the key and the file, for example `Setting display.bogusKey ignored (~/.goodvibes/tui/settings.json): not a setting this build knows.`; the next command or program reading the same tree does not repeat it (`<tree>/.goodvibes/settings-notices.json` records what was said). A running terminal app or Agent shows it once per session on its own screen and writes nothing to stderr for it, and when the attached daemon reports the same key in the same file, the line is shown once. The full reason and its remedy are in the activity log.

Which value is in effect, and from which layer, is shown on the settings screen and by `goodvibes status` for the main keys. The full list of keys, with each one's type, default, allowed values and file, is under "Settings" in the reference.

# Installing, running as a service, updating and removing GoodVibes

This part covers everything from an empty machine to a working GoodVibes: the two installers and every option they take, what each one puts on disk, the daemon's background service on Linux and macOS, WSL2, updates, pinning and rolling back a release, uninstalling, every installer refusal with its fix, the `doctor` health checks, and the first-run setup screens of the terminal app and the Agent, one screen at a time.

Terms used here:

- The terminal app is the program `goodvibes`.
- The Agent is the program `goodvibes-agent`.
- The daemon is the program `goodvibes-daemon`.
- The web UI is the browser app that the daemon serves.
- The owner is the person whose installation it is.
- A provider is a model service (for example OpenRouter or Anthropic).
- The suite is the three programs plus the web UI bundle, the browser driver and the native libraries, all from one release. When a later step of an install fails, the replaced programs are put back and so is the browser driver the run had replaced, so the programs and the driver stay from one release.
- The install directory is the directory that holds the programs. It is `~/.local/bin` unless an option changes it.
- A release is a tagged GoodVibes version such as `v3.3.3`, published at `https://github.com/mgd34msu/goodvibes/releases`.

This part describes release 3.3.3.

## Choosing an installation method

GoodVibes has two installers. They produce different layouts and must not be mixed in one install directory.

| Method | Command | Builds from source | Platforms | Data location | Service |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Release installer | `curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh \| sh` | No. It downloads prebuilt, checksum-verified programs. | Linux x64, Linux arm64, macOS x64, macOS arm64, and Windows through WSL2 | `~/.goodvibes` | systemd user unit on Linux, launchd user agent on macOS, written by the daemon itself |
| Checkout installer | `./scripts/install-from-checkout.sh` run inside a clone of the repository | Yes. It builds every program from the checked-out commit. | Linux x64 and Linux arm64 with glibc only | `~/.local/share/goodvibes-data/.goodvibes` | systemd user unit written by the installer |

Use the release installer unless the owner explicitly wants to run code built from a source checkout.

The release installer refuses to touch an install directory that the checkout installer owns (error `INSTALL_E114`). Remove the checkout installation first with its `goodvibes-uninstall` command; see "Building and installing from a source checkout".

## Supported systems and requirements

### Operating systems and processors

| `uname -s` | `uname -m` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Linux` | `x86_64` or `amd64` | Installs the `linux-x64` release files. |
| `Linux` | `aarch64` or `arm64` | Installs the `linux-arm64` release files. |
| `Darwin` | `x86_64` or `amd64` | Installs the `macos-x64` release files. |
| `Darwin` | `aarch64` or `arm64` | Installs the `macos-arm64` release files. |
| `MINGW*`, `MSYS*`, `CYGWIN*`, `Windows_NT` | any | Refused with `INSTALL_E001`. Native Windows is not supported. Use WSL2 (see "Windows through WSL2"). |
| anything else | any | Refused with `INSTALL_E002`. |
| `Linux` or `Darwin` | any other processor | Refused with `INSTALL_E003`. |

The Linux programs are built for glibc-based distributions. The release installer does not check the C library. On a musl distribution such as Alpine the downloaded programs cannot run, and the installer stops with `INSTALL_E017` or `INSTALL_E016` before it replaces anything.

### Tools the release installer needs

The release installer is a POSIX `sh` script. It needs no Bun, Node, Git, compiler or package manager.

| Tool | Why | When missing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `curl` or `wget` | Downloads the release files. `curl` is preferred. Every redirect must stay on HTTPS with either: `wget` asks for each hop's headers first and refuses a hop that is not `https://` (`INSTALL_E131`). | `INSTALL_E004`, `INSTALL_E131` |
| `sha256sum` or `shasum` | Verifies every download against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`. | `INSTALL_E005` |
| `stat` | Holds the identity of the install directory and its claim files during the install. | `INSTALL_E029` |
| `tar`, `awk`, `sed`, `mktemp`, `cmp`, `diff`, `cksum`, `ps`, `pgrep`, `kill` | Unpacking, parsing, comparing and process checks. These are present on every supported system. | The install stops at the first command that fails. |
| `perl` | Runs `--version` on other copies of the commands found on `PATH`, with a 5-second limit. | Only matters when another copy of a command shadows the new one; that copy is then reported as unidentified and is never removed automatically (see "When another copy of a command is found on PATH"). |
| `systemctl` (Linux) or `launchctl` (macOS) | Registers and restarts the daemon's service. | The programs install, and the installer prints the command to start the daemon by hand. |

The installer also needs HTTPS access to `goodvibes.sh` (for the script), to `github.com` and to the GitHub download host that `github.com` redirects release downloads to, and write access to the install directory, to the shell startup file it edits, and to `$TMPDIR` (default `/tmp`). The downloaded programs run once from `$TMPDIR` for verification, so `$TMPDIR` must allow execution. When `/tmp` is mounted `noexec`, set `TMPDIR` to a directory under the home directory.

```sh
mkdir -p "$HOME/.cache/goodvibes-tmp"
curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh | TMPDIR="$HOME/.cache/goodvibes-tmp" sh
```

Run the release installer as the owner's normal user. It does not use `sudo` and does not need root. It does not refuse to run as root, but it then installs into root's home directory and root's user service manager.

### Network access, proxies and machines without internet

Hosts each part contacts (besides the model providers and services the owner configures):

| Who | Address | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The one-line install | `https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh` | Fetching the script. |
| The release installer | `https://github.com/mgd34msu/goodvibes/releases/latest` (a `HEAD` request, for `latest` only) and `https://github.com/mgd34msu/goodvibes/releases/download/<tag>/<file>`, plus the GitHub download host those URLs redirect to | Every install. The repository is fixed in the script; no option changes it. |
| `goodvibes-daemon provision-wake-model` (run by the installer) and every daemon start while the model is missing | `https://github.com/mgd34msu/goodvibes/releases/download/voice-runtimes-v1/<file>`, falling back to `https://github.com/mgd34msu/goodvibes-sdk/releases/download/voice-runtimes-v1/<file>` | Until the wake-word model is present. |
| The daemon's update loop | `update.releasesUrl` (default `https://github.com/mgd34msu/goodvibes/releases/latest`) and the matching `.../releases/download/<tag>/` | First check about 30 seconds after start, then hourly, while `update.auto` is `true`. |
| Launch updates, the Agent's while-running updates and `/update` | `https://github.com/mgd34msu/goodvibes/releases/latest` and `.../releases/download/<tag>/`; fixed, `update.releasesUrl` does not change them | At an interactive start (results kept six hours), hourly in the Agent, on `/update check` and `/update apply`. |
| Browser tools | Playwright's own download servers, for the browser itself | `goodvibes-agent browser provision`, or the first use of a browser tool. |
| The checkout installer | `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/...` and `https://nodejs.org/dist/latest-v22.x/` when the local `bun` or `node` does not fit, and the npm registry for `bun install --frozen-lockfile` | Every run. |

Proxies:

- The release installer downloads with `curl` (or `wget` when `curl` is missing). Both read the standard proxy variables of their own: for `curl`, `https_proxy` (or `HTTPS_PROXY`), `all_proxy` and `no_proxy`; for `wget`, `https_proxy` and `no_proxy`. The installer also runs the downloaded `goodvibes-daemon` (the wake-word download, `webui enable`), which inherits the same environment. Give the first `curl` the proxy too:

  ```sh
  P=http://proxy.example:3128
  curl -x "$P" -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh \
    | https_proxy="$P" HTTPS_PROXY="$P" http_proxy="$P" HTTP_PROXY="$P" sh
  ```

- The programs run on Bun, whose built-in `fetch` uses `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` (Bun's own behaviour, either letter case). The update checks and downloads and provider requests go through the proxy. Requests to this machine never do: while a proxy variable is set, `goodvibes`, `goodvibes-agent` and `goodvibes-daemon` add `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]` and `::1` to `NO_PROXY` and `no_proxy` at start (keeping the entries already there; with `*` nothing is added), and any other loopback address a request names (another `127.x.x.x`, `0.0.0.0`) the first time one is used. So the terminal programs reach their own daemon at `http://127.0.0.1:3421` directly, the daemon's operator token never goes to the proxy, and a local model server such as Ollama is reached directly. Programs they start (a shell command, `curl`) inherit the same list. Add other addresses that must be reached directly (a daemon on the LAN, a model server on another machine) to `NO_PROXY` yourself. For example:

  ```sh
  export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.example:3128 HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.example:3128
  goodvibes
  ```

  For a daemon run as a systemd service, the variables must be in the service's environment, for example with a drop-in file `~/.config/systemd/user/goodvibes.service.d/proxy.conf` holding `[Service]`, `Environment=HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.example:3128` and `Environment=HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.example:3128` lines, then `systemctl --user daemon-reload` and `goodvibes-daemon restart-service`. A drop-in survives `refresh-service`, which rewrites only the unit file itself; remove it by hand when uninstalling.
- Some daemon features connect only directly and refuse while any of `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` or `ALL_PROXY` (in any letter case) is set for the daemon: reading Slack and Discord inboxes over HTTP, reading the owner's mail, and source screening. On a network that reaches the internet only through a proxy, those features cannot work; the daemon needs the proxy variables for everything else it fetches (updates, providers, the decision model).

A machine with no route to GitHub installs from a directory holding a copy of the release: `sh install.sh --from-dir <dir>` (or `GOODVIBES_RELEASE_DIR=<dir>`) reads every file from that directory, checks each against the directory's `SHA256SUMS.txt` exactly as a download is checked, and makes no request to GitHub (see "What each option does"). Also:

- A machine that reaches GitHub through a proxy: set the proxy variables as above.
- Turning off every later network update: add `--no-auto-update` (see "A fresh install with automatic updates off from the very first start"). `--from-dir` skips the wake-word model unless `GOODVIBES_WAKE_MODEL` is set; the daemon still tries that download at each start, and `GOODVIBES_SKIP_WAKE_MODEL_DOWNLOAD=1` in the daemon's environment stops that.
- For the daemon's own updates only, `update.releasesUrl` accepts a feed on the same machine: `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<path>/releases/latest` (or `localhost`, `[::1]`). The feed must answer a `HEAD` request for that URL with a redirect to `<same origin>/<path>/releases/tag/vX.Y.Z`, and serve the release files, `SHA256SUMS.txt` among them, under `<same origin>/<path>/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/`. The terminal programs' updates and the installer cannot use such a feed.
- The checkout installer can run without internet only when the right `bun` and `node` are already on `PATH` and Bun's package cache already holds every dependency.

## Installing with the release installer

### The one-line install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh | sh
```

On a new Linux x64 machine where `~/.local/bin` is not on `PATH`, the shell is bash and the user is `alex`, these are the lines the installer prints, in order. Words in angle brackets are filled in at run time.

```text
Installing GoodVibes v3.3.3 for linux-x64 into /home/alex/.local/bin

Installing goodvibes v3.3.3 ...
  installed  /home/alex/.local/bin/goodvibes

Installing goodvibes-daemon v3.3.3 ...
  installed  /home/alex/.local/bin/goodvibes-daemon
  running:   goodvibes-daemon 3.3.3

Added /home/alex/.local/bin to PATH in /home/alex/.bashrc (installer-managed; uninstall removes it).

Installed: goodvibes 3.3.3
  installed  /home/alex/.local/bin/lib/sqlite-vec-linux-x64/vec0.so

Installing the web UI v3.3.3 ...
  installed  /home/alex/.local/bin/webui/3.3.3
  installed  /home/alex/.local/bin/playwright-core

Installing goodvibes-agent v3.3.3 ...
  installed  /home/alex/.local/bin/goodvibes-agent
  running:   goodvibes-agent 3.3.3

Installing the wake-word model ...
  wake-word model: Wake-word model installed and verified: "hey goodvibes" <model version> (<size>). Turn it on with voice.wake.enabled, nothing further to download.
  web UI: served by the daemon from /home/alex/.local/bin/webui/3.3.3
    http://127.0.0.1:3421
    reachable from this machine only (the control-plane listener is bound to loopback).
    To reach it from another device on your network:  goodvibes-daemon webui enable --lan
    A running daemon applies this within about a second; no restart is needed.

Setting up the goodvibes daemon as a systemd user service ...
  installed the systemd service at /home/alex/.config/systemd/user/goodvibes.service
  service is enabled and running
  lingering: enabled for alex, the daemon starts at boot.

Done. Start with: /home/alex/.local/bin/goodvibes   (health check: /home/alex/.local/bin/goodvibes doctor)
PATH updated in /home/alex/.bashrc; open a new shell (or run: . /home/alex/.bashrc) to use the plain 'goodvibes' command from then on.
Personal agent:   goodvibes-agent
Web UI:           http://127.0.0.1:3421   (this machine only: the daemon is bound to loopback)
                  To reach it from another device on your network:
                    goodvibes-daemon webui enable --lan
```

When the install directory was already on `PATH`, the closing line is `Done. Start with: goodvibes   (health check: goodvibes doctor)` and there is no PATH line.

The `wake-word model:` line is one of these, depending on what happened:

| Outcome | Line after `wake-word model: ` |
| --- | --- |
| Downloaded | `Wake-word model installed and verified: "hey goodvibes" <model version> (<size>). Turn it on with voice.wake.enabled, nothing further to download.` (a sentence about the mobile tflite form is added when that form did not land; it affects nothing on this host) |
| Already present | `The wake-word model is already present and verified (<model version>); nothing was downloaded.` |
| Skipped by `GOODVIBES_SKIP_WAKE_MODEL_DOWNLOAD` | `The wake-word model was not downloaded because GOODVIBES_SKIP_WAKE_MODEL_DOWNLOAD is set. Wake-word detection reports not-provisioned until it is fetched; clear that variable and the next daemon start fetches it automatically.` |
| Download failed | `The wake-word model could not be downloaded (<reason>); installation continues. Wake-word detection reports not-provisioned until it is fetched, and the next daemon start fetches it automatically. Nothing needs doing by hand.` |
| Could not check | `The wake-word model could not be checked (<reason>); installation continues. Wake-word detection reports not-provisioned until it is fetched, and the next daemon start fetches it automatically.` |
| Home directory unusable | `skipped: <reason>` |

After a successful install:

1. Open a new terminal, or run the `. <file>` command the installer printed, so the plain command names work.
2. Run `goodvibes doctor` to check the installation (see "Checking an installation with doctor and status").
3. Run `goodvibes` in a project directory for the first-run setup (see "First run and onboarding").

When `curl` itself cannot download the script (no network, DNS failure, proxy), `curl` prints its own error, such as `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: goodvibes.sh`, and `sh` receives an empty script and does nothing. Nothing is installed. Fix the network and run the command again.

### Passing options

Every option can be given as an environment variable on the `sh` side of the pipe:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh | GOODVIBES_VERSION=v3.3.3 GOODVIBES_WEBUI=0 sh
```

Some options also exist as command-line flags. With `curl | sh`, flags follow `sh -s --`:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v3.3.3 --no-service
```

A downloaded copy of the script takes the same flags directly:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh -o install.sh
sh install.sh --bin-dir "$HOME/bin" --decision-policy Hybrid
```

`sh install.sh --help` prints:

```text
Install released GoodVibes binaries, daemon, agent, browser driver and WebUI.
Usage: install.sh [--version VERSION] [--bin-dir DIR] [--from-dir DIR] [--no-service|--service] [--no-auto-update]
                  [--decision-policy POLICY] [--uninstall]
GOODVIBES_VERSION selects one monorepo release (default: latest). No source build is performed.

Options:
  --version VERSION     Install this release, such as v3.3.3, for every program (default: latest;
                        also GOODVIBES_VERSION).
  --bin-dir|--install-dir DIR  Put the commands in DIR (default: ~/.local/bin; also GOODVIBES_INSTALL_DIR).
  --from-dir DIR        Install from DIR, a directory holding the release files and their SHA256SUMS.txt,
                        with no request to GitHub; every file is checked against that list (also
                        GOODVIBES_RELEASE_DIR). The release is read from the file names unless --version names it.
  --no-service          Do not install the daemon as a service, and record that choice so a daemon started
                        by hand never installs one (also GOODVIBES_DAEMON_SERVICE=0).
  --service             Install the daemon as a service (the default), even when GOODVIBES_DAEMON_SERVICE=0.
  --no-auto-update      Keep the daemon, the terminal app and the Agent from updating themselves, from their
                        first launch (also GOODVIBES_AUTO_UPDATE=0). Update later by running this installer.
  --decision-policy POLICY  Save the decision model policy: Hybrid, "Decision Model Only" or
                        "No Decision Model" (sets judgment.policy).
  --uninstall           Remove the installed programs and services; settings and data in ~/.goodvibes are kept.
  --help|-h             Print this help and exit.
```

A flag given on the command line wins over the matching environment variable. `--no-service` and `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_SERVICE=0` print the same `Daemon service setup skipped (--no-service); service.enabled records that this machine runs without one,` lines.

The complete list of installer options and environment variables, generated from the installer:

`scripts/install.sh` (released programs):

| Option | Value | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--help`, `-h` |  | Print this help and exit. |
| `--uninstall` |  | Remove the installed programs and services; settings and data in ~/.goodvibes are kept. |
| `--no-service` |  | Do not install the daemon as a service, and record that choice so a daemon started by hand never installs one (also GOODVIBES_DAEMON_SERVICE=0). |
| `--service` |  | Install the daemon as a service (the default), even when GOODVIBES_DAEMON_SERVICE=0. |
| `--no-auto-update` |  | Keep the daemon, the terminal app and the Agent from updating themselves, from their first launch (also GOODVIBES_AUTO_UPDATE=0). Update later by running this installer. |
| `--version` | `VERSION` | Install this release, such as v3.3.3, for every program (default: latest; also GOODVIBES_VERSION). |
| `--bin-dir`, `--install-dir` | `DIR` | Put the commands in DIR (default: ~/.local/bin; also GOODVIBES_INSTALL_DIR). |
| `--decision-policy` | `POLICY` | Save the decision model policy: Hybrid, "Decision Model Only" or "No Decision Model" (sets judgment.policy). |
| `--from-dir` | `DIR` | Install from DIR, a directory holding the release files and their SHA256SUMS.txt, with no request to GitHub; every file is checked against that list (also GOODVIBES_RELEASE_DIR). The release is read from the file names unless --version names it. |

`scripts/install-from-checkout.sh` (build from a clone of the repository):

| Option | Value | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--help`, `-h` |  | Print this help and exit. |
| `--uninstall` |  | Run ./scripts/uninstall.sh with the remaining options instead of installing. |
| `--no-service` |  | Do not run the daemon as a systemd user service (recorded in service.enabled, so a daemon started by hand installs none). |
| `--service` |  | Run the daemon as a systemd user service (the default). |
| `--prefix` | `DIR` | Where the programs are installed (default: $HOME/.local/share/goodvibes). |
| `--bin-dir` | `DIR` | Where the commands are linked (default: $HOME/.local/bin, or the previous install's). |
| `--data-dir` | `DIR` | The data directory: GOODVIBES_HOME for every installed command (default: $HOME/.local/share/goodvibes-data, or the previous install's). |
| `--port` | `PORT` | The daemon and WebUI port on 127.0.0.1 (default: 3421, or the previous install's). |
| `--workspace` | `DIR` | The project directory the daemon service works in (default: this checkout, or the previous install's). |
| `--decision-policy` | `POLICY` | Save the decision model policy: Hybrid, "Decision Model Only" or "No Decision Model" (sets judgment.policy). |

`scripts/uninstall.sh`:

| Option | Value | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--prefix` | `DIR` | The checkout installation to remove (default: $HOME/.local/share/goodvibes). |
| `--purge` |  | Also remove that installation data directory (receipt-owned installations only). |
| `--help`, `-h` |  | Print this help and exit. |

Full list: "Installer options" in the part "Reference".

### What each option does

| Option | Values and default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GOODVIBES_VERSION` or `--version VERSION` | `latest` (default) or a release tag | Selects the release for every program. `latest` follows GitHub's "latest release" redirect for `mgd34msu/goodvibes`. A tag may be written `v3.3.3` or `3.3.3`; the installer adds the `v`. A tag must look like `vX.Y.Z`, optionally followed by `-` or `+` and letters, digits, dots or hyphens; anything else is `INSTALL_E009`. `--version` with no value is `INSTALL_E110`. Here `--version` selects a release; it does not print the installer's version. |
| `GOODVIBES_INSTALL_DIR` or `--bin-dir DIR` (alias `--install-dir DIR`) | `$HOME/.local/bin` | The directory that receives the programs and their support files. It is created when missing. A relative path or a symbolic link is resolved to its physical directory once at the start. The web UI goes to `<dir>/webui`, the browser driver to `<dir>/playwright-core`, native libraries to `<dir>/lib`. |
| `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_SERVICE=0` or `--no-service` | `1` (default) | Skips first-run service registration and, when no daemon service is installed, records the choice with `goodvibes-daemon config set service.enabled false`. `service.enabled` is a daemon setting, read by the daemon before it would install itself as a service at its first idle moment and by `goodvibes doctor`, so a daemon started by hand stays without a service and doctor does not ask for one. The installer then prints `Daemon service setup skipped (--no-service); ...` followed by the daemon's path. `--service` (or `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_SERVICE=1`) turns it back on. Any value other than `1` means skip. An already installed service is left installed, recorded as it is, and refreshed and restarted on upgrade. The installer starts no daemon. |
| `GOODVIBES_AUTO_UPDATE=0` or `--no-auto-update` | `1` (default) | Runs `goodvibes-daemon config set update.auto false` and `goodvibes-daemon config set update.autoUpdateAtLaunch false` before any program starts. Both are daemon settings, kept in `~/.goodvibes/daemon/settings.json` and read by the daemon, the terminal app and the Agent, so none of the three updates itself, from its first launch. The closing lines say `Automatic updates: off for goodvibes, goodvibes-daemon and goodvibes-agent.` If the daemon refuses a write, the install still finishes and says how to turn them off. Update later by running the installer again. Any value other than `0` leaves updates on. |
| `GOODVIBES_RELEASE_DIR=DIR` or `--from-dir DIR` | unset (default) | Installs from a directory holding the release's files (the same names as the release assets) and its `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and makes no request to GitHub. Each file is copied from the directory and checked against `SHA256SUMS.txt` exactly as a download is (`INSTALL_E010`, `INSTALL_E011`); a file missing from the directory is `INSTALL_E125`. The release is the one the web UI bundle's name in `SHA256SUMS.txt` names; `--version` must match it (`INSTALL_E129`), and when the list names no bundle `--version` is required (`INSTALL_E128`). A directory without `SHA256SUMS.txt` is `INSTALL_E127`, a directory that does not exist `INSTALL_E130`. The wake-word model is downloaded by the daemon, not shipped with the release, so it is skipped unless `GOODVIBES_WAKE_MODEL` is set. |
| `--decision-policy POLICY` | `Hybrid`, `Decision Model Only`, `No Decision Model` (exact spelling and capitals; quote the two that contain spaces) | After the programs are installed, runs `goodvibes-daemon config set judgment.policy POLICY`. Without this flag the policy is not changed. Any other value is `INSTALL_E111`. If the daemon refuses the write, the install still finishes and the closing lines say `Decision policy:  NOT saved` with the command to run. What each policy means is in the permissions and decisions part of this file. |
| `GOODVIBES_AGENT=0` | `1` (default) | Skips downloading and installing `goodvibes-agent`. An Agent installed earlier stays at its earlier version. The automatic updates and `/update apply` update only the programs present beside the running one, so they never add an Agent that is absent; to add it later, run the install command again without `GOODVIBES_AGENT=0`. The browser driver is still installed, because the daemon and the terminal app use it too. Any value other than `1` means skip. |
| `GOODVIBES_WEBUI=0` | `1` (default) | Skips the web UI bundle and leaves the daemon's web UI settings untouched. The installer prints how to serve a bundle later. Any value other than `1` means skip. |
| `GOODVIBES_WAKE_MODEL=0` | `1` (default) | Skips `goodvibes-daemon provision-wake-model`, which downloads and checksum-verifies the "hey goodvibes" wake-word model into `~/.goodvibes/voice/wake/` (`models/` and `front-end/` below it). Use it on a machine without internet access to that host, or when the wake word is not wanted. A failed download never fails the install, and a running daemon retries at every start. `/voice wake-setup` fetches it later. The environment variable `GOODVIBES_SKIP_WAKE_MODEL_DOWNLOAD=1` (also `true` or `yes`) makes the daemon's own provisioning skip the download. |
| `GOODVIBES_RESTART_DAEMON=0` | `1` (default) | On an upgrade, leaves running daemon and Agent processes alone. They keep running the old programs until restarted. A refreshed service definition then takes effect only at the next `goodvibes-daemon restart-service`; the installer says so. |
| `GOODVIBES_SHADOW_REMOVE` | `ask` (default), `1`, `0` | What to do when another copy of `goodvibes`, `goodvibes-daemon` or `goodvibes-agent` appears earlier on `PATH`. `ask` prompts on the terminal (`/dev/tty`), `1` removes recognised copies without asking, `0` only reports. Any value other than `1` or `0` means `ask`. See "When another copy of a command is found on PATH". |
| `GOODVIBES_UNINSTALL=1` or `--uninstall` | `0` (default) | Uninstalls instead of installing. No release is downloaded. See "Uninstalling". |
| `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_VERSION`, `GOODVIBES_AGENT_VERSION`, `GOODVIBES_WEBUI_VERSION` | default to `GOODVIBES_VERSION` | Kept only for compatibility. Every program comes from one release. If any of them differs from `GOODVIBES_VERSION`, the install stops with `INSTALL_E008`. Do not set them. |
| `TMPDIR` | `/tmp` | Where the installer downloads and verifies the release before it changes anything. It is deleted when the installer exits. |
| `SHELL` | the login shell | Decides which startup file receives the PATH line (see "How the installer handles PATH"). |

`GOODVIBES_VECTOR` is not read by the installer. The native SQLite and vector libraries are always installed.

`GOODVIBES_INSTALL_SH_LIB=1` makes the script define its functions and exit without doing anything. It exists for the installer's own tests. Never set it for a real install.

### Installation recipes

Install the newest release with every default:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh | sh
```

Install one exact release:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh | GOODVIBES_VERSION=v3.3.3 sh
```

Install into a different directory, for example `~/bin`:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh | GOODVIBES_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/bin" sh
```

Install without the background service, and keep it that way:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh | sh -s -- --no-service
```

The installer records the choice (`service.enabled` `false`, a daemon setting in `~/.goodvibes/daemon/settings.json`), so a daemon started by hand never installs the systemd service at its first idle moment (see "Running the daemon without a service") and `goodvibes doctor` reports no service finding. On an existing installation, `goodvibes-daemon config set service.enabled false` records the same choice.

Install with automatic updates off from the first launch:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh | sh -s -- --no-auto-update
```

Install on a machine with no route to GitHub: copy the release's assets, its `SHA256SUMS.txt` and `install.sh` into one directory (from another machine, `gh release download v3.3.3 -R mgd34msu/goodvibes -D goodvibes-v3.3.3`), then run the installer from that copy:

```sh
sh install.sh --from-dir ./goodvibes-v3.3.3 --no-auto-update
```

With no service, no daemon runs until one is started by hand (`cd ~ && nohup goodvibes-daemon >/dev/null 2>&1 &`). The terminal app and the Agent never start a daemon that has no service: at start they only start an installed service that is stopped, and otherwise say that no daemon answers.

Install only the terminal app and the daemon, without the Agent, the web UI or the wake-word model:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh | GOODVIBES_AGENT=0 GOODVIBES_WEBUI=0 GOODVIBES_WAKE_MODEL=0 sh
```

Install with no decision model at all:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh | sh -s -- --decision-policy 'No Decision Model'
```

Install unattended (CI, a provisioning script, no terminal). Older copies on `PATH` are then removed only when `GOODVIBES_SHADOW_REMOVE=1`; with the default, an unanswerable question leaves them in place and the install still succeeds:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh | GOODVIBES_VERSION=v3.3.3 GOODVIBES_SHADOW_REMOVE=1 sh
```

Upgrade an existing installation to the newest release: run the same install command again. See "Updating".

### What the installer does, in order

1. Reads its options and checks the operating system and processor.
2. If the install directory holds commands that link into a checkout installation (a `.../commands/goodvibes` link with an `installation.json` beside it), stops with `INSTALL_E114`.
3. Resolves the release tag. For `latest` it asks GitHub for the latest release and requires a tag of the form `vX.Y.Z` (`INSTALL_E006`, `INSTALL_E007`, `INSTALL_E123`); with `--from-dir` it reads the tag from the directory's `SHA256SUMS.txt` instead.
4. Downloads `SHA256SUMS.txt` and every file the platform needs from `https://github.com/mgd34msu/goodvibes/releases/download/<tag>/` (with `--from-dir`, copies them from that directory) into a private directory under `$TMPDIR`, and checks each against exactly one checksum line (`INSTALL_E010`, `INSTALL_E011`). Unpacks the browser driver and the web UI there and checks their entry files (`INSTALL_E012` to `INSTALL_E015`). On Linux, runs the downloaded daemon's runtime once to confirm the daemon's release record (`INSTALL_E016`, `INSTALL_E017`). Nothing installed has changed yet.
5. Claims the install directory: creates `goodvibes-daemon.update-transaction`, `goodvibes.update-transaction` and `goodvibes-agent.update-transaction` in it, plus a private directory `.goodvibes-install-claim.<random>`. A claim held by a running install or update stops this install (`INSTALL_E118`). A claim left by a process that no longer runs is recovered first: an interrupted earlier install is undone or finished, and its claims are released (`recovered` or `released` lines).
6. Refuses when partial files from an interrupted update are still beside the programs (`INSTALL_E043` to `INSTALL_E045`), or when `lib` is a symbolic link (`INSTALL_E046`).
7. When `.goodvibes-reader-requirements.json` exists in the install directory, asks each downloaded program whether it can read the saved data. A release too old to read it is refused and nothing is replaced (`INSTALL_E057`, `INSTALL_E058`).
8. Refuses when backups from an interrupted earlier install remain (`INSTALL_E027`).
9. Replaces the programs. Each file is copied in as `<file>.incoming` and renamed over the old one, so running processes keep the program they started with. Before each rename the old file is kept as `<file>.goodvibes-previous`, and every replacement is recorded in a swap journal in the private claim directory. Order: `goodvibes`, then `goodvibes-daemon` (and on macOS its SQLite library), then the PATH line, then a `goodvibes --version` check (`INSTALL_E115`), then the vector library, then the web UI directory, then the browser driver directory, then `goodvibes-agent`.
10. Marks the swap finished, deletes the `.goodvibes-previous` backups and releases the claims. If anything fails or the installer is interrupted before this point, the previous programs are put back automatically (see "When an installation fails or is interrupted").
11. Saves the decision policy when `--decision-policy` was given, and turns automatic updates off when `--no-auto-update` was given.
12. Runs `goodvibes-daemon provision-wake-model` unless `GOODVIBES_WAKE_MODEL=0`.
13. Runs `goodvibes-daemon webui enable --bundle-dir <dir>/webui/<version>` unless `GOODVIBES_WEBUI=0`. The daemon writes the web UI settings and prints the address. This never widens network exposure: a daemon bound to loopback keeps serving this machine only.
14. Asks the daemon about its service (`goodvibes-daemon service-status --json`, whose `productServices` lists every daemon service GoodVibes wrote for this user). With `--no-service` and no service installed, records `service.enabled` `false`. When a service definition that GoodVibes wrote exists, runs `goodvibes-daemon refresh-service` so the definition matches the new program.
15. Restarts every running GoodVibes daemon service of this user (the default one and any second daemon under its own `service.serviceName`), a daemon started by hand without a terminal, and Agent processes without a terminal, so they use the new programs (unless `GOODVIBES_RESTART_DAEMON=0`). A program attached to a terminal (an interactive `goodvibes-agent`, a daemon in the foreground) is never stopped: it keeps running the previous version and the installer names it and asks for it to be restarted there.
16. On a first install, when no daemon is running and no service definition exists, runs `goodvibes-daemon install-service`, which writes the service, starts it and tries to enable lingering (unless `--no-service`).
17. Checks that typing each command name runs the copy just installed, and handles shadowing copies.
18. Prints the closing lines.

### What lands where

Paths below use the default install directory `~/.local/bin` and the `linux-x64` platform. Replace `linux-x64` with `linux-arm64`, `macos-x64` or `macos-arm64`, and the vector library platform with `linux-arm64`, `darwin-x64` or `darwin-arm64`.

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `~/.local/bin/goodvibes` | The terminal app. |
| `~/.local/bin/goodvibes-daemon` | The daemon. |
| `~/.local/bin/goodvibes-agent` | The Agent. Absent with `GOODVIBES_AGENT=0` on a first install. |
| `~/.local/bin/<program>.bun`, `<program>.bun.json`, `<program>.bun.LICENSE.md` | Linux only. A pinned Bun runtime shipped beside each compiled program, with its description and licence. The program uses it for work it runs in a separate Bun process; the installer and the updates always replace it together with its program. |
| `~/.local/bin/<program>.readers.json` | The data formats this program can read, when the release publishes that record. On Linux the daemon has none; on macOS all three can have one. |
| `~/.local/bin/daemon-installation.json` | Linux only. The daemon's record of the release it was installed from. |
| `~/.local/bin/lib/sqlite-vec-linux-x64/vec0.so` | The vector-search extension (`vec0.dylib` under `sqlite-vec-darwin-<arch>` on macOS). All three programs load it from here. |
| `~/.local/bin/lib/sqlite-darwin-<arch>/libsqlite3.dylib` and `libsqlite3.dylib.json` | macOS only. The SQLite library the daemon uses, and its record. |
| `~/.local/bin/playwright-core/` | The browser driver used by browser tools. Browsers themselves are downloaded later into a separate cache when first needed (`goodvibes-agent browser provision`). Holds `.goodvibes-release.json` naming its release. |
| `~/.local/bin/webui/<version>/` | The web UI bundle for that release, for example `webui/3.3.3/`. Every release the installer installs gets its own directory; older ones are never deleted by the installer. Holds `.goodvibes-release.json`. |
| `~/.local/bin/.goodvibes-reader-requirements.json` | Written by the programs when saved data needs a minimum reader. The installer only reads it. Never delete it to force a downgrade. |
| `~/.local/bin/<program>.previous` and other `*.previous` files | Rollback copies kept by an automatic update or `/update apply`. See "Rolling back". |
| `~/.config/systemd/user/goodvibes.service` | Linux. The daemon's service, written by `goodvibes-daemon install-service`. |
| `~/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.goodvibes.daemon.plist` | macOS. The daemon's service, written by `goodvibes-daemon install-service`. |
| `~/.goodvibes/` | All settings, sessions, memory, keys and tokens. Created by the programs on first use. Kept by every uninstall. |
| `~/.goodvibes/voice/` | The managed voice files. The wake-word model is in `~/.goodvibes/voice/wake/` (`models/`, `front-end/`). |
| `~/.goodvibes/logs/activity.md` | The daemon's activity log when its working directory is the home directory (as for the release service). It is renamed to `activity.md.1` at 10 MB. Every program writes such a log under `<its working directory>/.goodvibes/logs/`. |
| `~/.goodvibes/daemon/service/` | The service's own state directory: the pid file and log of the `manual` platform. The log path the status reports here (`systemd.log`, `launchd.log`) is written only by the `manual` platform (see "Using the service manager directly"). |
| One line pair in `~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.zshrc`, `~/.config/fish/config.fish` or `~/.profile` | The PATH line, only when the install directory was not on `PATH`. |

During an install, these exist only temporarily: `<program>.update-transaction` (claims), `.goodvibes-install-claim.<random>/` (private claim directory with the swap journal), `<file>.incoming`, `<file>.goodvibes-previous`, `<dir>.directory-update.lock` and `.goodvibes-directory-install.<random>/`. If one remains after the installer has exited, an install was interrupted; see "Installer errors and their fixes".

### Moved homes: `GOODVIBES_HOME`, `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME` and `GOODVIBES_AGENT_HOME`

The release installer sets none of these; every path above assumes they are unset. Three environment variables move parts of the tree:

| Variable | Read by | What moves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GOODVIBES_HOME=<dir>` | the terminal app, the daemon and the Agent | The tree root: everything under `~/.goodvibes/` is used from `<dir>/.goodvibes/` instead (each program's settings, the daemon's own settings file `daemon-host/settings.json`, local users, device tokens, sessions, memory and the other stores under `tui/`, the voice tree, the secret stores), and the daemon home with it unless `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME` is set. |
| `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME=<dir>` (or the daemon's `--daemon-home <dir>`) | the daemon, and every client that reads the daemon's files | The daemon home, which holds exactly: `settings.json` (the daemon-owned settings), the daemon secret store (`secrets.enc` or `secrets.json`), `operator-tokens.json`, `owner-profile.md` and `daemon-settings.json`. Order: `--daemon-home`, then `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME`, then `<tree root>/.goodvibes/daemon`. For the daemon itself a moved daemon home is also the tree root when `GOODVIBES_HOME` is not set, so everything else it keeps moves to `<dir>/.goodvibes/`; a client reads only the daemon's files there. |
| `GOODVIBES_AGENT_HOME=<dir>` | the Agent only | Moves the Agent alone, ahead of `GOODVIBES_HOME`: its settings, sessions, memory, skills, personas and routines move to `<dir>/.goodvibes/agent/`, its secret stores and `secrets.key` to `<dir>/.goodvibes/`, and the daemon files it reads to `<dir>/.goodvibes/daemon/` unless `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME` is set. Without it the Agent's tree is `GOODVIBES_HOME`'s, else the login home's, the same as the terminal app's and the daemon's, so the three share one `secrets.key`. |

A moved daemon home isolates a daemon: with `--daemon-home <dir>` (or `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME=<dir>`) and no `GOODVIBES_HOME`, local users and the bootstrap file, device tokens, sessions, memory, the daemon's other stores and its client-scoped settings live under `<dir>/.goodvibes/`, so two daemons with different daemon homes share none of them. To run a fully separate daemon (for testing, say), give it its own daemon home and its own port (`goodvibes-daemon --daemon-home <dir> config set controlPlane.port <n>`). `GOODVIBES_HOME=<dir>` does the same, with the daemon home at `<dir>/.goodvibes/daemon`.

A daemon started with any of `GOODVIBES_HOME`, `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME` or `--daemon-home` set never updates itself and never promotes itself to the service. The service definition itself always stays under the login home (`~/.config/systemd/user`, `~/Library/LaunchAgents`), and so does the service's state directory `~/.goodvibes/daemon/service/`, whatever these variables say.

### How the installer handles PATH

When the install directory is already on `PATH`, the installer changes no startup file.

Otherwise it appends two lines to one startup file, chosen from `$SHELL`:

| `$SHELL` ends in | File | Line written after the marker comment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/zsh` | `~/.zshrc` | `export PATH="<dir>:$PATH"` |
| `/bash` | `~/.bashrc`, or `~/.bash_profile` when that exists and `~/.bashrc` does not | `export PATH="<dir>:$PATH"` |
| `/fish` | `~/.config/fish/config.fish` | `set -gx PATH <dir> $PATH` |
| anything else | `~/.profile` | `export PATH="<dir>:$PATH"` |

The marker comment is `# managed by goodvibes install.sh`. Running the installer again does not add a second line for the same directory. Installing into a second directory adds a second pair. Uninstalling removes only the pair for its own directory.

The current shell does not see the change. Open a new terminal or run `. ~/.bashrc` (with the file the installer named).

### When another copy of a command is found on PATH

After installing, the installer checks each of `goodvibes`, `goodvibes-daemon` and `goodvibes-agent`. It models the shell the owner is about to open: when it wrote (or finds) its PATH line, the install directory counts as first on `PATH`.

When the install directory is not on `PATH` at all and no PATH line exists, it prints:

```text
PROBLEM: /home/alex/bin/goodvibes is installed, but /home/alex/bin is not on your PATH,
         so typing "goodvibes" does not reach it.
         Add it to your PATH, or run it by full path: /home/alex/bin/goodvibes
```

When a directory earlier on `PATH` holds another `goodvibes`, it prints which copy wins and the version of each:

```text
PROBLEM: typing "goodvibes" does not run the copy this installer maintains.
         wins on PATH: /home/alex/.bun/bin/goodvibes (version 1.18.1)
         installed here: /home/alex/.local/bin/goodvibes (version 3.3.3)
```

Then, for each earlier copy:

- A copy that is the same file reached by another path is ignored.
- A copy the installer recognises as an earlier GoodVibes is offered for removal. It is recognised only when it is inside the home directory, answers `--version` with exactly `<command> <version>`, and is either a plain file this installer recorded writing (it lists every program it places in `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/goodvibes/installed-programs`; a file not listed there is reported and never removed) or a link from one of the old packages `@pellux/goodvibes-tui`, `@pellux/goodvibes-daemon` or `@pellux/goodvibes-agent` installed globally by `bun` or `npm`. The installer prints the exact removal command (`rm -- '<path>'`, `bun remove -g --ignore-scripts <package>` with that Bun's global directories, or `npm --prefix <prefix> rm -g --ignore-scripts <package>`) and asks `Remove it now? [y/N]` on the terminal. With `GOODVIBES_SHADOW_REMOVE=1` it removes without asking; with `0` it never removes.
- Any other copy is reported as `not something we can identify as one of our programs` and is never touched. Remove it yourself, or put the install directory earlier on `PATH`.

When no terminal is available to ask (a piped install with no controlling terminal), the copy is left in place, the installer says `(no terminal available to ask; leaving this copy in place for now; ...)`, and the install still succeeds.

When a shadowing copy remains for any other reason (declined, unidentified, removal failed, or the install directory is not on `PATH`), the installer ends with:

```text
Install FAILED to become reachable: another copy earlier on your PATH still
answers one or more of these commands. Until that is resolved, upgrading here
changes nothing you can run. Fix the copies named above, then re-run this
installer. To run this install directly in the meantime: /home/alex/.local/bin/goodvibes
```

and exits with status `3`. The programs are installed and the service is set up; only the command names are unresolved. Remove or rename the copies it named, or reorder `PATH`, then run the installer again.

### Exit status of the release installer

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Installed (or uninstalled) and every command name reaches the installed copy. Notes printed with `NOTE:` did not fail the install. |
| `1` | Refused or failed. The message ends with an id such as `(INSTALL_E036)`. If the failure came after programs began to be replaced, the previous programs were put back unless the message says otherwise. |
| `3` | Installed, but another copy earlier on `PATH` still answers a command name. |
| `129`, `130`, `143` | Interrupted by a hang-up, Ctrl-C or a termination signal. The installer first undid any partial replacement. |

Every refusal is printed to standard error as `install.sh: <sentence> (INSTALL_E###)`. The id never changes meaning between releases; look it up in "Installer errors and their fixes".

### When an installation fails or is interrupted

Nothing installed changes until every file of the release has been downloaded and verified. A failure before the replacement step (bad network, wrong version, checksum mismatch, a refusal) leaves the existing installation exactly as it was.

Once replacement has begun, every replaced file is kept as `<file>.goodvibes-previous` and recorded in the swap journal. If the install then fails, or is stopped with Ctrl-C, a termination signal or a closed terminal, the installer:

1. puts every previous file back and deletes every file it had newly created;
2. releases its claims;
3. prints:

```text
install.sh: installation did not finish. The previous programs were restored and the installation claims were released; running services were not touched.
install.sh: to try again, re-run the installer: curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh | GOODVIBES_VERSION=v3.3.3 sh
```
