| `INSTALL_E116` | Suite files were installed, but this run's transaction claims in `<dir>` changed, so services were not started. | A claim changed after the programs were in place. The new programs are installed. | Retry once nothing else runs; the retry releases stale claims and finishes the service steps. |
| `INSTALL_E117` | The installation claim `<path>` cannot be read (or could not be released), so its owner is unknown; nothing was changed. | A damaged `*.update-transaction` file. | If no install or update runs, run the printed `rm -rf -- <path>`, retry. |
| `INSTALL_E118` (1) | Another goodvibes update or install (process `<pid>`) is replacing programs in `<dir>` and holds `<claim>`; nothing was changed. Wait for it to finish, then re-run the installer. | A running process holds a `*.update-transaction` claim: another installer or uninstaller, `/update apply` or `/update rollback`, a launch update, the Agent's while-running update, or the daemon's update loop while it replaces files. The installer judges the owner alive only when that pid exists and started no later than the claim was written (a few seconds of slack); a pid reused by another program after the owner died counts as gone, and such a claim is recovered automatically. | See which process it is: `ps -o pid,lstart,args -p <pid>`. When it is an install, `/update` or a launch update, wait until it exits, then run the install command again. A daemon update holds the claim only while it writes and renames the new files, after the download; a `pending:` line in `goodvibes-daemon update` means a release waits for an idle moment and holds no claim yet. When the holder is a daemon that does not finish (the claim stays for minutes), stop that daemon (`goodvibes-daemon stop-service`, or `kill <pid>` for a hand-started one, then `kill -9 <pid>` only if it does not exit) and run the install command again: the claim of a process that is gone is recovered. When `ps` shows a program that is not GoodVibes, run the install command again; if the refusal repeats, the claim has no start time and was left behind: once no GoodVibes install or update runs, `rm -f -- '<claim>'` and run it again. |
| `INSTALL_E118` (2) | Another goodvibes update or install (process `<pid>`) claimed `<claim>` while this run was releasing a claim left by a process that is gone; its claim was left in place and nothing was changed. Wait for it to finish, then re-run the installer. | While this run released a dead process's claim, a live install or update took the same claim. `<pid>` is `unknown` when that claim could not be read. | As (1). |
| `INSTALL_E118` (3) | Another goodvibes update or install (process `<pid>`) claimed `<claim>` while this run was releasing a claim left by a process that is gone, and a third claim took the path before its claim could be put back; nothing was changed. Its claim is at `<taken claim>`: once no goodvibes install or update is running, remove it and re-run the installer. | Three runs raced for the same claim. The second run's claim was moved into this run's private claim directory and could not be put back. | Wait until no GoodVibes install or update runs (no installer or uninstaller runs in another terminal, no `/update apply` or `/update rollback` is in progress, and `goodvibes-daemon update` shows no `pending:` line), then `rm -f -- '<taken claim>'` with the path from the message, and run the install command again. |
| `INSTALL_E119` | An installation interrupted earlier (process `<pid>`, no longer running) could not be undone automatically; nothing else was changed. | Recovery of a killed install failed. | Read its journal (`R<file>` lines: put `<file>.goodvibes-previous` back; `N<file>` lines: delete `<file>`), then run the printed `rm -rf -- ...` command and retry. |
| `INSTALL_E120` | An update or install that is no longer running (process `<pid>`) left `<claim>` with partial files beside the program; nothing was changed. | A killed automatic update. | If `<program>` is missing, put its `.update-previous` copy back with `mv -f`; then delete the listed partial files and the claim, retry. |
| `INSTALL_E121` | Could not create the swap journal in `<dir>`; nothing was replaced. | Disk full or no permission. | Free space, fix permissions, retry. |
| `INSTALL_E122` | The installed uninstaller of `<prefix>` is missing and no Bun was found to run this checkout's copy; nothing was removed. | As `INSTALL_E113`, with a checkout but no Bun. | Install Bun, then run the printed `bun <checkout>/scripts/uninstall.ts --prefix <prefix>`. |
| `INSTALL_E123` | the latest release of mgd34msu/goodvibes is `<tag>`, which is not a suite release; set GOODVIBES_VERSION=vX.Y.Z | The newest release on GitHub is not a suite release. | Set `GOODVIBES_VERSION` to the newest `vX.Y.Z` tag. |
| `INSTALL_E124` | Every program was replaced, but the swap journal in `<dir>` could not be marked finished, so the previous programs are being put back. | Disk full or no permission at the last step. | Free space, retry. |
| `INSTALL_E131` | a download was redirected to `<url>`, which is not https; nothing more was downloaded | With only `wget` installed, a download redirected to a plain-http address (or more than 10 times). | Install `curl`, or copy the release files over https into a directory and run the installer with `--from-dir`. |

Messages without an id:

| Message | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `install.sh: this run's installation claims in <dir> changed while it ran, so they were left in place. ...` | The install finished or stopped, but its claims could not be released safely. | Retry once nothing else runs; claims of finished processes are released automatically. |
| `install.sh: original uninstall claims changed; inspect retained transaction files in <dir> before retrying.` | The same, for an uninstall. | Look at the `*.update-transaction` files, then retry. |
| `PROBLEM: ...` and `Install FAILED to become reachable: ...` | See "When another copy of a command is found on PATH". Exit `3`. | As described there. |
| `NOTE: the installed ... failed`, `NOTE: restart failed; restart it yourself with: ...` and other `NOTE:` lines | A late step did not finish. The install succeeded. | Run the command the note prints. |
| `curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404` (or another `curl:`/`wget:` error) with no id | A download failed: most often the tag in `GOODVIBES_VERSION` does not exist, or the network dropped. Nothing installed was changed. | Check the tag on `https://github.com/mgd34msu/goodvibes/releases` and the network, then retry. |
| `mkdir: cannot create directory ...` or `mktemp: ...` with no id | The install directory or `$TMPDIR` is not writable. | Choose a writable `GOODVIBES_INSTALL_DIR` or `TMPDIR`. |

## Checking an installation with doctor and status

### `goodvibes doctor`

`goodvibes doctor` prints the terminal app's view of the whole installation, then a list of findings. It changes nothing, and it never updates the program.

```sh
goodvibes doctor            # report; exit 1 only when a risk finding exists
goodvibes doctor --json     # the same as JSON
goodvibes doctor --strict   # exit 1 when any finding exists, warnings included (for CI)
```

Every finding has a severity. `warning` is advisory: the installation works, and the finding is a note. `risk` is must-fix: the product's help and messages call such a finding a "must-fix finding". The exit status is `0` when no `risk` finding exists, `1` when one does, and with `--strict` `1` when any finding exists.

Sections, in order:

| Section | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| header | `workingDir` and `homeDir`. |
| `Provider:` | The provider, the model (`provider:model`), the reasoning effort and what this model supports, the sign-in in use (for example `API key (OPENROUTER_API_KEY)`), and where the model list comes from. |
| `Decision model:` | The `judgment.policy` value and whether a decision model is in use. |
| `Auth:` | The permission mode with its meaning, `behavior.autoApprove`, the secret storage policy, and whether the local user store, the bootstrap credential and the operator token file exist (with their paths). |
| `Service:` | `service.enabled`, `service.autostart`, `service.restartOnFailure`, the platform, whether the service is installed and running, its pid, the definition path and the log path. |
| `Surfaces:` | Whether the control plane, the HTTP listener and the web surface are on, with their addresses (defaults `127.0.0.1:3421`, `127.0.0.1:3422`, `127.0.0.1:3423`), and whether other machines are served (`controlPlane.enabled`). The web UI itself is served on the control plane's address. |
| `Onboarding:` | Whether the first-run marker exists, its scope and time. |
| `Crashes:` | Recorded crashes, from `~/.goodvibes/tui/crashes.jsonl`. |
| `Workspace:` | Trust level (`trusted`, `restricted` or `undecided`), whether the workspace is registered for checkpoints, and its root. |
| `Exec sandbox:` | Whether the command sandbox is active and available (bubblewrap on Linux) and whether network isolation is confirmed. |
| `Relay:` | Relay settings. |
| `Exposure (report only: no changes made):` | For each surface: on or off, local or network, address, how it authenticates, and its browser origin policy. |
| `Warnings:` | One block per finding: `[<severity>:<area>:<id>] <summary>`, then `cause:`, `impact:` and `action:` lines. A service or endpoint finding is one record with one remedy: `goodvibes service status` and `service check` print the same summary with that remedy under it as `Fix: <action>`, and `goodvibes-agent doctor` prints the same record for an endpoint or log finding. |

All service findings use the terminal app's own `service.*` values, from `~/.goodvibes/tui/settings.json` (see "Service settings"). A command that writes the daemon's file (`goodvibes-daemon config set service.<key> ...`) changes what the daemon does, not what `goodvibes doctor` reports. The auth findings use the terminal app's files `~/.goodvibes/tui/auth-users.json` and `~/.goodvibes/tui/auth-bootstrap.txt`. `<endpoint>` is one of `controlPlane`, `httpListener` and `web`. The `<area>` in each `[<severity>:<area>:<id>]` line is `service` (the `service-*`, `endpoint-*` and `unrecognized-host-mode-*` findings), `onboarding`, `auth` (the two `network-surface-*` findings), `security` (`auto-approve-enabled`, `allow-all-permissions`), `secrets`, `network` (`network-http-listener-enabled`, `control-plane-cors-wildcard-origin`), `install` and `sandbox`. The table lists every finding `goodvibes doctor` can show; the Provider, Decision model, Crashes, Workspace and Relay sections only report and add no findings. The control plane is "on" whenever the daemon is enabled (`daemon.enabled`, default `true`); it "serves other machines" when `controlPlane.enabled` is also `true`. A surface is network-reachable when it is on and its host mode is not `local` and its host is not a loopback address.

| Finding id | Severity | Reported exactly when | What clears it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onboarding-incomplete` | warning | The first-run marker `~/.goodvibes/tui/onboarding-checked.json` does not exist. | Start `goodvibes` and finish first run, or run `/setup` → `Run first-run again`. |
| `service-not-installed` | warning | `service.enabled` is `true`, the daemon (or a server-backed endpoint) is on, and the service manager reports no daemon service installed. | `goodvibes-daemon install-service`. For a machine that runs without a service: `goodvibes-daemon config set service.enabled false` (the release installer's `--no-service` does this). |
| `service-not-running` | warning | A daemon service is installed and the service manager reports it stopped. | `goodvibes-daemon start-service` (read `goodvibes-daemon service-status` and `journalctl --user -u goodvibes.service` if it stops again). |
| `service-manager-error` | warning | `service.enabled` is `true` and systemd or launchd could not be asked; the summary carries the reason. The other service findings wait for an answer. | Run doctor from a logged-in session with a user service manager (see "Service problems and fixes"), or record a machine without a service: `goodvibes-daemon config set service.enabled false`. |
| `service-autostart-disabled` | warning | A daemon service is installed and the service manager reports it not enabled to start at login (systemd's unit file state). A fresh release install, whose `install-service` enables the unit, does not show it. | `goodvibes-daemon install-service` (it enables the unit again). |
| `service-restart-disabled` | warning | A daemon service is installed and `service.restartOnFailure` is `false`. | `goodvibes-daemon config set service.restartOnFailure true`, then `goodvibes-daemon refresh-service`. |
| `service-log-unreadable` | warning | The reported service log file exists but cannot be read. | Fix its permissions. |
| `endpoint-unreachable-<endpoint>` | warning | Only in `goodvibes service check` and after `goodvibes service start` or `restart`, never in `goodvibes doctor`: an enabled endpoint did not accept a TCP connection. | `goodvibes-daemon start-service`; its log says why a bind failed (`goodvibes-daemon service-status`). |
| `endpoint-conflict-<a>-<b>` | warning | Two enabled endpoints have the same port and either the same host or one of them bound to `0.0.0.0` or `::`. | `goodvibes-daemon config set <b>.port <port>` (give one of them another port). |
| `unrecognized-host-mode-<endpoint>` | warning | `<endpoint>.hostMode` is not `local`, `network` or `custom` (checked whether or not the endpoint is on). The daemon cannot start that endpoint. | Set it to one of the three. |
| `install-missing-vendor-binaries` | warning | Only for a terminal app installed as a `bun`/`npm` package: its `vendor/` directory lacks the app or daemon program. | Run the command the finding names. |
| `install-broken-daemon-path` | warning | Not for a run from source. The terminal app found no daemon program: none at `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_COMMAND`, none in its own package directories, none beside its own executable (`goodvibes-daemon` or `goodvibes-daemon-<platform>`), and none on `PATH`; or `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_COMMAND` names an absolute path that does not exist. | Run the install command again. The finding prints `curl -fsSL https://goodvibes.sh/install.sh \| sh`, which installs into `~/.local/bin`; for another directory add `GOODVIBES_INSTALL_DIR=<dir>`. Or unset a wrong `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_COMMAND`. |
| `exec-sandbox-unavailable` | warning | `sandbox.enabled` is `true`, the `exec-sandbox` feature is on, and no sandbox is available on this host. | Install bubblewrap (`bwrap`) on Linux, or set `sandbox.enabled` to `false`. |
| `network-http-listener-enabled` | warning | `danger.httpListener` is `true` and the listener is network-reachable. | Keep secrets or signature checks on every webhook surface, or bind it to loopback. |
| `network-surface-without-local-users` | risk | At least one surface is network-reachable (the control plane counts only when it serves other machines) and `~/.goodvibes/tui/auth-users.json` does not exist. | Create a local admin user (the Access screen of the setup wizard), or make the control plane and web surface local again with `goodvibes-daemon webui enable --loopback` (the HTTP listener has its own `httpListener.hostMode`). |
| `network-surface-with-bootstrap-credential` | risk | At least one surface is network-reachable and `~/.goodvibes/tui/auth-bootstrap.txt` exists. | Replace the bootstrap credential with a named admin user (the Access screen of the setup wizard removes the file). |
| `auto-approve-enabled` | risk | `behavior.autoApprove` is `true`. | `/settings set behavior.autoApprove false` inside `goodvibes`. |
| `allow-all-permissions` | risk | `permissions.mode` is `yolo` (or the older name `allow-all`). | Choose `ask-me`, `jev-decides` or `just-vibes` in `/settings`, unless `yolo` is intended. |
| `plaintext-secrets-allowed` | risk | `storage.secretPolicy` is `plaintext_allowed`. | `/settings set storage.secretPolicy preferred_secure` (or `require_secure`). |
| `control-plane-cors-wildcard-origin` | risk | The control plane serves other machines and is network-reachable, `controlPlane.cors.enabled` is `true`, and `controlPlane.cors.allowedOrigins` contains `*`. | List the exact trusted origins instead of `*`. |

`goodvibes doctor` reads what the service manager reports, not the service settings, so it is clean both on a fresh release install with its service running and on an installation made without a service on purpose (`--no-service`, which records `service.enabled` `false`): with `service.enabled` `false` doctor reports no service finding at all.

`goodvibes doctor explain <tool|command>`, `goodvibes doctor routing` and `goodvibes doctor hooks` are covered in the terminal app part of this file.

### `goodvibes-agent doctor`

`goodvibes-agent doctor` prints the Agent's view: provider, decision model, auth, the connected daemon ("connected host": its address, whether it answers, whether it is compatible, whether the Agent has an access token), the host's relay settings, the Agent's role, onboarding, crashes (`~/.goodvibes/agent/crashes.jsonl`), checkpoints and readiness checks, then warnings. It takes `--json` and `--strict`. It never updates the program.

The daemon address the Agent uses, here and everywhere else, is built from `controlPlane.host` and `controlPlane.port` (a host of `0.0.0.0` or `::` is dialled as loopback). These are daemon-owned settings, read from the daemon's own file `~/.goodvibes/daemon/settings.json`, so the Agent follows a port changed with `goodvibes-daemon config set controlPlane.port <n>`. With nothing set, the address is `http://127.0.0.1:3421`. The global option `--runtime-url <url>` (or the environment variable `GOODVIBES_AGENT_RUNTIME_URL`, older name `GOODVIBES_AGENT_BASE_URL`) replaces it for one run.

Severity `note` describes the arrangement and never fails. `risk` is must-fix. The areas are `runtime` (the `external-runtime-*`, `agent-knowledge-*`, `runtime-*` findings), `auth` (`external-runtime-token-missing`), `onboarding`, `security` and `secrets`. The exit status is `1` when a `risk` finding exists, and with `--strict` when any `warning` or `risk` exists; otherwise `0`.

| Finding id | Severity | Reported exactly when | What clears it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `external-runtime-unreachable` | warning | The daemon does not answer at the address. | Start the daemon (`goodvibes-daemon start-service`, or by hand), then `goodvibes-agent status`. |
| `external-runtime-incompatible` | warning | The daemon answers, but its Agent routes are unavailable or incompatible, or they could not be checked because the Agent has no operator token or the daemon refused its status request. A reachable daemon with no token therefore shows this together with `external-runtime-token-missing`. | Pair first (next row); if it remains, update the daemon to the same release. |
| `external-runtime-token-missing` | warning | None of the four credential sources gave a token (see "Pairing the Agent with the daemon" for the order): no token variable, no pairing record for the address, and no `operator-tokens.json` in the daemon home. Reported whether or not the daemon answers. | Pair: `goodvibes-agent setup pair --apply` (see "Pairing the Agent with the daemon"). |
| `agent-knowledge-route-not-ready` | warning | The daemon answers, the Agent has a token, the routes were checked, and the Agent Knowledge route is not ready. | Update the daemon; check `goodvibes-agent compat`. |
| `runtime-connection-<slug>` | warning | An issue the Agent's service check reported (the slug is made from its text). | Follow its action line. |
| `runtime-posture-<slug>` | note | An advisory about the arrangement. | None, unless it is not what was intended. |
| `onboarding-incomplete` | warning | The Agent's setup completion marker does not exist (`Agent setup has not been applied for this user.`). It is written by **Apply & close** in the setup workspace. | Open `goodvibes-agent`, finish setup and choose **Apply & close**. |
| `auto-approve-enabled` | risk | The Agent's `behavior.autoApprove` is `true`. | `/settings set behavior.autoApprove false` inside `goodvibes-agent`. |
| `allow-all-permissions` | risk | The Agent's permission mode is `yolo`. | Choose another mode in the Agent's settings. |
| `plaintext-secrets-allowed` | risk | The Agent's `storage.secretPolicy` is `plaintext_allowed`. | `/settings set storage.secretPolicy preferred_secure`. |

### Status commands

| Command | Prints |
| --- | --- |
| `goodvibes status` (`--json`) | The terminal app's configuration, provider, auth, service, surfaces and onboarding state, without the findings. Exit `0`. |
| `goodvibes setup status` | `checked: yes|no`, `scope`, `source`, `mode`, `updatedAt` and `workingDir` of the first-run marker. |
| `goodvibes-agent status` (`--json`) | The Agent's configuration, provider, auth, connected daemon and setup state. Exit `0`. |
| `goodvibes-agent setup status` | The selected daemon address, whether the Agent holds an accepted credential for it, and the setup marker (`checked`, `scope`, `origin`, `mode`, `updated`). |
| `goodvibes-daemon status` | What a running daemon is doing (described in the daemon part of this file). |
| `goodvibes-daemon service-status` | The service state (see "The daemon's service commands"). |

## First run and onboarding

### Before the first start

A release install leaves the daemon running as a service, the web UI served at `http://127.0.0.1:3421`, and no model provider configured. The default model is `openrouter:openrouter/free`, which needs an OpenRouter API key in `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. Any other provider works too; providers and sign-ins are described in the terminal app part of this file.

The quickest path to a working first session, when the owner has an OpenRouter key:

```sh
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY='<your-openrouter-api-key>'
cd ~/code/my-project
goodvibes
```

With a key for the default model's provider present, the first start asks nothing: the conversation opens with its starting prompts (below), and the first-run marker is written.

### First run: three steps, the same in the terminal app and the Agent

`goodvibes` and `goodvibes-agent` run the same first run. It opens exactly when the model the session will use is not ready (its provider has no key or sign-in and is not keyless); a ready model opens the conversation directly and writes the first-run marker (`~/.goodvibes/tui/onboarding-checked.json`, the Agent's under `~/.goodvibes/agent/`). Leaving at any step and starting again picks up from the facts: a provider chosen in settings but not signed in opens step 2 for it; otherwise step 1.

**Step 1, `Welcome to GoodVibes` (`1 of 3`): `Which model should answer you?`** One row per offer, then `Another provider…` with the count of the other registered providers (`38 more`):

| Row | How | Shown with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ChatGPT subscription` | `sign in with your browser` | OpenAI's subscription sign-in. |
| `Anthropic` | `paste an API key` | |
| `OpenRouter` | `paste an API key` | `has a free model` when its model list has a free model. |
| `A model on this computer` | | `found <server> with <n> models` (green) once the scan of this computer found a model server (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp and the like); `looking for models on this computer…` while it runs; `none found` after it found none. |

The terminal app starts that scan of this computer (never the network) when first run opens; the Agent's start-up already scans this computer. When a key in the environment already makes a provider usable, a line under the rows says `Found in your environment: <VARIABLE> · press a to use it and skip this step`. Keys: Up and Down move, Enter chooses, `a` uses the found key (the provider's default model is chosen and step 2 is skipped), Esc is "set up later". Choosing `Another provider…` opens the full provider picker; choosing a ready model there finishes first run.

**Step 2 (`2 of 3`)** depends on the row:

- A key: `Sign in to <name>`, `Paste your <name> API key.`, a masked field (no character of the key is shown) and `It is stored in secure storage, never shown again.` (`the settings file` when `storage.secretPolicy` is `plaintext_allowed`). Enter stores the key for this user (as `/secrets set --user <VARIABLE>` does) and checks it with one model-list request to the provider. A refused key is removed again and the step says `That key was refused by <name> (401). Check it and paste it again.`; an unreachable provider `GoodVibes couldn't reach <name>. Check your connection and try again.` Esc or Shift+Tab goes back to step 1, as the key row says (`esc / shift+tab back`).
- The browser: `GoodVibes opened your browser to sign in.`, then `If it didn't open, go to:` and the whole sign-in address, and `Waiting for you to finish in the browser…` while the sign-in page's answer is awaited. When the browser could not be opened, or the provider's sign-in ends on a code, `Paste the code the page shows:` takes the code (or the address the browser ended on). `c` copies the address, Enter continues, Esc or Shift+Tab goes back. A sign-in cancelled in the browser says `Sign-in was cancelled in the browser. Press ⏎ to start again.`
- A model on this computer: `Which model on this computer?` and the models found, each with its server, its size where the server reports one in the model list it already gives (Ollama's parameter size, LM Studio's `params_string`) and its context window; Enter chooses one. With none found, it says so and Enter looks again.

**Step 3 is the conversation.** The splash (the logo, its lines, the hint and the version) is drawn exactly as on every start, at the same place; under it, only in the rows left free above the composer, GoodVibes adds:

1. On the first run only: `You're set.  Answering with <model> · signed in` (`no sign-in needed` for a model on this computer) and `3 of 3`.
2. On every empty conversation: `Try one of these in <folder>:` and three starting prompts for the folder: `What does this project do, and how do I run its tests?` (`This folder is empty. What should we build here?` in an empty folder), `Find something in this code worth fixing and show me.` (`Summarise what is in this folder.` with no code), and `Add a --verbose flag and run the tests.` when a manifest declares a command-line entry and a test command is found (`Make one small improvement and run the tests.` with tests only, `Make one small improvement and show me the change.` without tests). Tab in an empty composer puts the next prompt in the composer, unsent; a click on a prompt does the same.
3. On the first run only: what GoodVibes asks before, for the permission mode in force (for example `GoodVibes asks before it runs commands or changes things outside this folder.`), that Shift+Tab changes how often it asks, and the command that opens the remaining setup, wrapped to the screen's width so it takes as few rows as its words need.

The three parts follow each other with no blank row between them; rows left over become blank rows (first one under the splash, then one above the composer). At 120x36 all three show in both programs. When the free rows are too few for all of them, the starting prompts are left out first, then the sentence, each whole (the logo always keeps its place); on an 80x24 terminal the terminal app has no free rows under its splash, so nothing is added there. Notices are never drawn over these screens: they are counted on the status bar (`ctrl+n` opens them). Nothing of first run is written into the conversation.

Esc on step 1 ("set up later") marks nothing and writes nothing; the conversation then says `Not set up yet.  Choose a model with /model, or run /setup.` and shows no starting prompts. The next start opens first run again.

`/setup` opens the setup topics at any time in both programs (below), and `goodvibes setup` (`goodvibes-agent setup` in the Agent) starts the program with them open. `/setup` → `Run first-run again` opens the three steps again.

The first time GoodVibes wants to write or run something in a folder, it asks whether to trust that folder. Trust levels are covered in the permissions part of this file.

### `/setup`: one form per topic

`/setup` in the terminal app lists the setup topics (the whole list is under `/setup` in the terminal app part); each topic opens one form that fills the screen, titled `/setup` and the topic, with the topic's sentence, its rows and **Save** as the last row. There is no list of other screens and no step count: another topic is another `/setup` choice. Each form holds the rows of the former wizard screens listed below for its topic.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Up, Down | Move between rows. |
| Page Up, Page Down, Home, End | Move by a page, or to the first or last row. |
| Enter or Space | Change the selected row: tick a checkbox, pick the next option of a choice, open the model picker, run an action, or start editing a text field. |
| Typing a character on a text field | Starts editing it with that character. |
| Enter (while editing) | Saves the text. |
| Esc (while editing) | Cancels the edit. |
| Backspace / Delete or Ctrl+U | Deletes one character / clears the field. |
| Esc | Close the form without saving. |

Nothing is saved until **Save**; a form closed with Esc keeps nothing of what was chosen in it. While the form loads current settings it shows **Loading current settings**, with every row locked. If loading fails it shows **Current settings unavailable** with the reason; press Enter to try again or Esc to close.

Which topic holds which former screen: `Keep everything on this computer`, `Open GoodVibes in a browser`, `Use it from other devices` and `Receive webhooks` each hold their row of Capabilities and their part of Network setup (and the sign-in account of Access when the computer opens to the network); `Connect chat apps and services` holds its capability row, Choose external surfaces and one block per chosen surface; `Use Cloudflare` holds its capability row and Cloudflare batch setup; `Sign in or out of a provider` holds AI provider access without the keys, and the subscription acknowledgement; `Store a password or key` holds the provider keys and the secret storage policy; `Who can sign in here` holds the account rows of Access; `Choose a model` holds Default model; `How GoodVibes works with you` holds Shell experience; and the seven feature topics hold Safety, Context, Telemetry, Automation, Devices, Runtime and Advanced.

### Setup form rows: Choose GoodVibes capabilities

Tick what GoodVibes should be able to do. "Local TUI Only" and the other five exclude each other: ticking any other one unticks "Local TUI Only", and unticking all others ticks it again.

| Checkbox | Default | What choosing it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local TUI Only (No Servers) | ticked | GoodVibes is used only in this terminal: no browser access, no HTTP listener, no external app surface, no network setup. A daemon bound to loopback still runs for this machine. Leaves the service settings as they are and binds every surface to loopback. |
| Open GoodVibes in a Browser | | Turns on the web surface and service mode. With the Network screen's default, the daemon is bound to the local network. |
| Let other devices use GoodVibes | | Makes the enabled services reachable from other devices on the LAN. Requires a local admin user. |
| Receive webhooks or events from other tools | | Turns on the HTTP listener for incoming webhooks and events. |
| Connect GoodVibes to external apps and services | | Adds the Services screen, where chat apps and other surfaces are chosen. |
| Use Cloudflare for batch or remote daemon work | | Adds the Cloudflare screen. |

Two action rows: **Select all server-backed capabilities** ticks every capability except "Local TUI Only". **Use Local TUI Only (No Servers)** clears them all.

Any choice other than "Local TUI Only" saves `service.enabled`, `service.autostart`, `service.restartOnFailure` and `controlPlane.enabled` as `true`. The form itself does not install anything; the running daemon applies `service.autostart` (installing and enabling the service when it is not), and with no daemon running, the next daemon start applies it to an installed service, or run `goodvibes-daemon install-service`.

Keeping "Local TUI Only" saves `controlPlane.enabled` as `false` and leaves the service settings as they are: the daemon's service, which the release installer set up, keeps running and is still recorded and checked as running.

### Setup form rows: Network setup (only with a server capability)

| Field | Options and default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Network mode | **Local Network (Default)** or **Custom** | Local Network binds each enabled surface to all interfaces (`0.0.0.0`, host mode `network`) on its configured port. Custom asks for addresses and ports. |
| GoodVibes daemon source | **Start a new daemon** (default) or **Connect to an existing running daemon** | Which daemon this terminal app talks to. Connecting saves `daemon.connectedHost.url`; starting clears it. |
| Existing daemon host, port, token (connect only) | `127.0.0.1`, `3421`, empty | The address and bearer token of the existing daemon. The token is saved in `~/.goodvibes/tui/connected-daemons.json` (under `GOODVIBES_HOME` when that is set), keyed by the daemon's address; this machine's own daemon's `operator-tokens.json` is never written, so the local daemon and its other clients keep their token. The address is saved as `daemon.connectedHost.url`. |
| Connect to this daemon now (connect only) | action | Applies the host, port and token at once and checks the connection; the result prints below. |
| Use the same IP address for all services (custom only) | checkbox | One address for every surface, set in **Shared IP address**. |
| GoodVibes service port / IP address (custom, browser or LAN chosen) | `3421`, `0.0.0.0` | `controlPlane.port`, `controlPlane.host` (host mode `custom`). |
| Browser surface port / IP address (custom, browser or LAN chosen) | `3423`, `0.0.0.0` | `web.port`, `web.host`. |
| HTTP listener port / IP address (custom, webhooks or external apps chosen) | `3422`, `0.0.0.0` | `httpListener.port`, `httpListener.host`. |

When a network-reachable surface has TLS off, the screen shows `TLS off: <surface> transmits plaintext`. When the HTTP listener is on, it notes that browser CORS stays off until `controlPlane.cors.enabled` and `controlPlane.cors.allowedOrigins` are set.

### Saving a form

**Save** applies only what changed on the form: a setting whose value equals what the form read is not written, an acknowledgement is recorded only by a form that shows it, and the sign-in account only by a form that shows its rows. While a row on the form is missing, refused (a confirmation that does not match, a bad port) or a required acknowledgement is unticked, **Save** shows `Blocked` instead of `Ready` and its detail lists what to finish. **Save** writes the changes, then reads each value back. A daemon-owned setting is sent to the running daemon; when no daemon is listening on its address, it is written to the daemon's settings file for the next daemon start. On success the form closes and prints a summary of the checks. When some checks fail it says `Setup saved your settings, but <n> check(s) of them failed; ...` and lists them. When the save itself fails, the form stays open with **Apply did not complete** and the reasons at its top; fix them and save again.

### The Agent's first run

The Agent's first start runs the same three-step first run as the terminal app (above). `goodvibes-agent setup` (or `goodvibes-agent onboarding`) starts the Agent on `/setup`, whose topics are listed in the Agent part; a topic opens the workspace with only that topic's rows. The setup pages below are the workspace's Onboarding areas, opened with `/agent` or `Ctrl+G`.

Keys: Up and Down move, Left and Right switch between the page list and the page, Enter opens a row, `/` searches, Ctrl+] goes to the next area, Ctrl+R checks the daemon again, Esc closes, and typing a letter closes the workspace with that letter in the message box.

The setup pages appear as they become relevant, and a status line names the next step, the first one not yet ready (`Picking up where you left off: <step>.`).

| Page | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| Models | The main chat model and reasoning effort, plus optional helper, tool, spoken-turn and embedding routes, a custom system prompt file, a local model benchmark and prompt cache settings. |
| Behavior | Interaction mode, verbosity per area, reasoning effort, guidance mode, auto-compact threshold, context warnings, notifications, resume summaries, visible thinking. |
| Tools & Permissions | Execution mode (`permissions.mode`), allow/prompt/deny for file reads, writes, edits, shell commands and network fetches, adding an MCP server, linking and testing secret references, and tool limits. |
| Interface | Streaming, theme, theme mode, line numbers, collapse threshold, token speed, tool previews, where operational and system messages appear. |
| Messaging | Turning on and filling in ntfy, Slack, Discord, webhooks, Telegram, Google Chat, home automation, Signal, WhatsApp and iMessage, plus checking, diagnosing, guided setup and test sends. Nothing is sent without an explicit send. |
| Voice & Media | Spoken replies, text-to-speech provider and voice, telephony, image input, media generation, and voice readiness. |
| Local Context | VIBE.md and project context files, importing persona, skill and routine files, creating personas, memories, skills, routines and notes, and adding URLs, files, bookmarks or browser history to Agent Knowledge. |

The setup pages also show a checklist, each item `ready`, `recommended`, `optional` or `blocked`: Connected host, Connected-host auth, Provider and model, Provider subscriptions, Agent Knowledge, Agent profile, Persona, Skills, Routines, Local memory, Scratchpad notes, Channels, Voice and media. Only a chosen provider and model is required to chat. Without a reachable daemon the host items are `optional` and the Agent still chats; schedules, channels and Agent Knowledge need the daemon.

Once the Agent can chat, an **Apply & close** row appears at the bottom of the setup pages. Choosing it records setup as done and shows a recap; choosing it again closes the workspace.

### Pairing the Agent with the daemon

The Agent needs its own credential for the daemon (`goodvibes-agent doctor` reports `external-runtime-token-missing` until it has one). Pair it on the machine where the daemon runs:

```sh
goodvibes-agent setup pair                 # preview: what would be paired, nothing changes
goodvibes-agent setup pair --apply         # asks you to type a confirmation word, then pairs
goodvibes-agent setup pair --name laptop --apply   # names the device (default "GoodVibes Agent")
goodvibes-agent setup unpair               # forgets the stored credential for the selected daemon
```

`--apply` needs an interactive terminal and a typed confirmation; it cannot be scripted (`--yes` is refused) and refuses `--json` output. Usage errors exit `2`. The daemon address is `controlPlane.host` and `controlPlane.port` (default `127.0.0.1:3421`); `--runtime-url <url>` selects another. Pairing other devices and remote daemons is covered in the daemon part of this file.

The Agent picks the credential it sends to the daemon in this order; the first step that applies decides:

1. The environment variable `GOODVIBES_CONNECTED_HOST_TOKEN`, when set and not empty.
2. The environment variable `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_TOKEN`, when set and not empty.
3. The Agent's stored pairing for that daemon address (written by `goodvibes-agent setup pair --apply`). When a pairing record exists but its token cannot be used, the search stops here with the reason: a lost pairing reply (`goodvibes-agent setup pair` repeats the request) or an unreadable pairing store.
4. The `token` field of `operator-tokens.json` in the daemon home (`~/.goodvibes/daemon/operator-tokens.json`, or the directory `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME` names, or `<GOODVIBES_AGENT_HOME>/.goodvibes/daemon/`). This file exists on the machine where the daemon runs, and is used only when the daemon address is this machine (a loopback address or one of its own interface addresses); it is never sent to a daemon elsewhere.

`goodvibes-agent doctor` shows the source on its `access token:` line (`env:GOODVIBES_CONNECTED_HOST_TOKEN`, `env:GOODVIBES_DAEMON_TOKEN`, `Agent host-bound pairing store` or the file path). A token from step 1 or 2 hides a stored pairing; unset both variables to use the pairing.

### Settings, models and providers after setup

- `/setup` opens one topic's form with the current settings loaded.
- `/model` changes the model; `/settings` opens every setting; `/settings set <key> <value>` sets one in the terminal app.
- `/settings set <key> <value>` sets one in the Agent.
- `goodvibes-daemon config set <key> <value>` sets one for the daemon.

These are described in full in the terminal app, Agent and daemon parts of this file.

# The terminal app (`goodvibes`)

This part describes the terminal app, `goodvibes`, from launch to every command it offers. It covers the command line, the interface, every slash command, sessions, models and providers, tools, helper agents and worktrees, contracts and workstreams, checkpoints and undo, memory and knowledge, MCP servers, plugins, skills, hooks, headless runs and the Agent Client Protocol. The Agent (`goodvibes-agent`) shares most of this; the next part lists what it does differently.

## What the terminal app is

The terminal app is an interactive coding and operations assistant that runs in a terminal window.
It holds a conversation with a model, and the model works through tools: it reads and edits files, runs commands, searches, fetches web pages, starts helper agents and more.
Each tool call passes the permission gate, which allows it, refuses it, asks the owner, or lets the decision model decide, according to the permission mode.
The conversation loop runs inside the terminal app process.
Daemon-owned features (schedules, channels, the owner inbox, devices, hosted sessions, clusters, mail, calendar, CI watches) are reached through the daemon's operator API; when no daemon answers, those commands say so and change nothing.
The terminal app keeps its own state under `~/.goodvibes/tui/` (user scope) and `<project>/.goodvibes/tui/` (project scope), where `<project>` is the working directory.
State shared by every GoodVibes program on the machine lives under `~/.goodvibes/shared/`.

Terms used in this part:

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| working directory | The directory the terminal app treats as the project. It is the current directory unless `--cd` or `tui <path>` names another. |
| session | One saved conversation. Sessions are stored per project in `<project>/.goodvibes/tui/sessions/`. |
| turn | One prompt from the owner and everything the model does until it answers. |
| slash command | A line typed in the composer that starts with `/`, such as `/model`. Slash commands run in the terminal app; they are not sent to the model. |
| composer | The text input box at the bottom of the screen. |
| registry key | A model's full name in the form `<provider>:<model-id>`, for example `openai:gpt-5.4`. |
| helper agent | A subagent the model starts with the `agent` tool. It has its own conversation and a narrower tool set. |
| contract | A tracked unit of delegated work with acceptance criteria that are checked before it counts as done. |
| workstream | A contract started from an owner request, planned into units and run by helper agents. |
| checkpoint | A snapshot of the workspace files that `/checkpoint restore` and `/checkpoint rewind` can return to (see "Restoring a checkpoint"). |
| view | A full-screen modal over the conversation, such as Agents, Usage or Changes. `Esc` closes it. |

## Launching the terminal app

### Launch forms

```sh
goodvibes                          # open the terminal app in the current directory
goodvibes tui ~/work/project       # open it with ~/work/project as the working directory
goodvibes "review this repo"       # open it with that prompt already sent as the first turn
goodvibes --cd ~/work/project      # same as tui <path>; --working-dir and -C are aliases
goodvibes --no-alt-screen          # keep output in the terminal's normal scrollback
goodvibes open goodvibes://open/agents   # open the app on one view
```

`goodvibes app` is an alias of `goodvibes tui`.
A launch whose model is not ready opens first run (choose a provider, sign in, then the conversation with starting prompts for the folder; see the install part of this file); `goodvibes onboarding` (alias `goodvibes setup`) opens the full setup wizard on demand.
The onboarding screens are described under "First run and onboarding" in the install part.

`goodvibes open <link>` takes exactly one link of the form `goodvibes://open/<view>[?target=<id>[:<kind>]]`.
In a process view (agents, tasks, orchestration) the target selects that process; in another view the app opens the view and says the target was not used.
A link that is missing or not of that form is refused:

```text
$ goodvibes open notalink
goodvibes open takes one link: goodvibes://open/<view>[?target=<id>[:<kind>]] ("notalink" is not one).
```

The exit code is `2`.
`/deeplink review` inside the app lists every view link.

### Global options

The complete help of every command, as the program prints it, is under "Command line: `goodvibes`" in the reference part.

How each option behaves:

| Option | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `-m, --model <registryKey>` | Uses this model for this launch. The text before the first colon names the provider (`openai:gpt-5.4`, `Ollama:llama3:8b`), which is then selected unless `--provider` is also given. The provider is any registered one (built-in, custom, or a server found by `/scan`), named by its id or display name without regard to case, so `-m ollama:llama3:8b` is the scanned `Ollama` server's model. A name no registered provider has is an error listing the registered providers when the model is used (`models current`, `run`, the interactive app). A value with no colon, or with a slash before its first colon (`meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free`), is a model id under the configured provider. A model id that itself holds a colon needs its provider: `-m ollama:llama3:8b`, or `--provider Ollama -m llama3:8b`. |
| `--provider <id>` | Uses this provider for this launch. |
| `-C, --cd <dir>`, `--working-dir <dir>` | Sets the working directory for this launch. Sessions and project settings are read from that directory. |
| `--daemon-home <dir>` | Uses this daemon home (default `~/.goodvibes/daemon`) for every command that reads the operator token or daemon settings. It wins over the `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME` environment variable. |
| `-c, --config <key=value>` | Overrides one setting for this launch only. It may be repeated. Nothing is saved. |
| `--enable <feature>`, `--disable <feature>` | Turns one feature flag on or off for this launch. The value is a feature id, not a setting key. An unknown id is refused and the error lists the known ids. |
| `-p, --prompt <text>` | Runs one prompt without the interface (the same as `run`). |
| `--print` | Selects non-interactive run mode (the same as `run`) when no command is given. |
| `-o, --output <format>` | Output format for `run` and for commands that print data: `text`, `json` or `stream-json`. Another value is refused with `-o must be one of: text, json, stream-json.` and exit `2`. `--json` means `--output json`. `--output-format <format>` is accepted as the same option and prints `[goodvibes] warning: --output-format is deprecated; use --output (or -o) instead.` on standard error; standard output is unchanged. When two of these are given, the last one wins. |
| `--just-vibes` | Sets the permission mode to `just-vibes` for this launch only: work continues without asking, and anything that needs the owner is held and listed at the end. It is the same as `--config permissions.mode=just-vibes`. |
| `--yolo` | Sets the permission mode to `yolo` for this launch only: every action runs without safety denials; `Pre:tool:*` hooks and never-run rules still apply. Containment, secret storage and payment limits still apply. `--no-worries-just-vibes` is an unlisted spelling of the same option. It may come before or after the command word (`goodvibes --yolo run ...` or `goodvibes run --yolo ...`). |
| `--no-alt-screen` | Keeps the interface in the normal scrollback instead of the alternate screen. |
| `--port <port>`, `--hostname <host>` (`--host`) | Port and bind address for `web` and `surfaces enable`. The port must be 1 to 65535. |
| `--open` | Opens a browser where the command supports it (`web`, `subscription login <provider> start`). |
| `-r, --resume [id\|latest]` | Opens a saved session. Without an id it opens the last session of this working directory. |
| `-s, --session <id>` | `run` only: continue that saved session. Every other command refuses it. |
| `--continue` | Opens the last session of this working directory. |
| `--fork [id]` | Bare `--fork` forks the session that is active when the app starts. `--fork <id>` opens that session, then forks it. `run` refuses `--fork`. |
| `--timeout <duration>` | `run` only: cancel after this long. A bare number is seconds; `ms`, `s`, `m` and `h` suffixes are accepted. Exit code `124`. |
| `--max-turns <n>` | `run` only: stop after `n` model answers that still ask for tools. Exit code `1`. |
| `--omit-accumulated` | `run` with `stream-json` only: leave `accumulated` out of `STREAM_DELTA` frames. |
| `--answer-permissions` | `run` with `stream-json` only: read owner answers to permission prompts from standard input. |
| `-y, --yes` | Confirms a command that would otherwise only preview (for example `plugin bundles install`, `support-bundle import`). |
| `--non-interactive` | Disables every interactive prompt and implies `--yes`. |
| `--strict` | `doctor` only: also fail on advisory findings. |
| `-h, --help` | Prints help. `goodvibes help <command>` prints one command's help. |
| `-v, --version` | Prints `goodvibes 3.3.3`. |

Only one of `--continue`, `--resume` and `--fork` may be given on one launch.

### Rules of the command-line parser

- A flag that takes a value refuses a value that begins with `-`. Use the equals form: `--prompt='- item'`.
- `--` ends option parsing. Every word after it is a positional argument: `goodvibes run -- --literal-text`. A command never reads one of its own options (`--yes`, `--apply`) from a word after `--`.
- An unquoted word in a prompt that equals a command name or alias (`doctor`, `auth`, `task`) is read as that command. Quote the whole prompt.
- After a command word, an option that command does not take is refused with exit code `2`, and the error lists the options it accepts.
- A run-only flag (`--timeout`, `--max-turns`, `--omit-accumulated`, `--answer-permissions`) on any other command is refused with exit code `2`:

```text
$ goodvibes status --timeout 5
--timeout, --max-turns, --omit-accumulated and --answer-permissions apply only to the run command.
```

- A lone first word that is a command mistyped by one slip of the fingers is refused, with exit code `2`: five or more letters, and the command with two neighbouring letters swapped or one letter doubled:

```text
$ goodvibes stauts
Unknown command: stauts. Did you mean `goodvibes status`? To start with "stauts" as the first prompt instead, run: goodvibes -- stauts
```

- Any other lone word is a one-word prompt and starts the app with it (`goodvibes hello`, `goodvibes fix`, `goodvibes frobnicate`). When it is one or two letters from a command (`hello`, `staus`), a warning names that command.

### Environment variables the terminal app reads

The complete list of environment variables is under "Environment variables" in the reference part. The ones that change how the terminal app starts:

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME` | Daemon home directory used to find the operator token and daemon settings. `--daemon-home` overrides it. |
| `GOODVIBES_HOME` | Home directory used by `goodvibes acp` for its embedded sessions. |
| `ACP_AGENT_CMD` | Replaces the command `/remote dispatch` and `/remote dispatch-pool` start as an ACP subagent (by default this program's own `acp` command). Give it as a JSON array of program and arguments, for example `["/path/to/agent","acp"]`; a value that is not an array is used as one path when such a file exists, otherwise split on spaces. A value that starts with `[` but is not a JSON array of non-empty strings is refused with the reason. |
| `EDITOR`, `VISUAL` | The editor `/editor` and `/template edit` open. |
| Provider key variables (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and the others in the provider list) | Sign a provider in with an API key. An environment variable wins over a key stored with `/secrets`. |

## Command-line commands

Every command below prints text by default. Commands that print data accept `--json` (or `--output json`) and then print one JSON value.
A command that refuses prints the reason on standard error and exits non-zero; the refusal names what to run next.
Exit codes shared by all programs are under "Exit codes" in the reference part; the codes each command uses are given with the command.

### `goodvibes run` (alias `exec`, `e`)

`run` sends one prompt to the model without the interface, prints the result and exits.
It is described in full under the heading "Headless runs" below.

```sh
goodvibes run "summarize the current project"
goodvibes run --output json "list risks"
goodvibes exec --output stream-json --omit-accumulated --timeout 10m "fix lint"
goodvibes run --continue "and now write the tests"
```

A run with no prompt is refused:

```text
$ goodvibes run
A prompt is required.
```

The exit code is `2`.

### `goodvibes status`

`status` prints the configuration posture: working directory, home directory, provider and model, reasoning effort, sign-in, decision model, permission mode, local auth files, daemon service, surfaces, onboarding, crashes, workspace trust and the exec sandbox.
The `provider` and `model` lines name what a turn started now would use: the saved model, or this launch's `-m`/`--provider`, resolved against the registered providers (custom ones and the servers the last `/scan` saved) the same way a run resolves it, so `-m ollama:llama3:8b` shows `provider: Ollama`. When no registered provider has the name, a `problem:` line says so, lists the registered providers and says how to choose another. The Agent's `status` does the same.
It always exits `0`.

```text
$ goodvibes status
GoodVibes status
  workingDir: /home/me/work/project
  homeDir: /home/me

Provider:
  provider: openrouter
  model: openrouter:openrouter/free
  reasoning: medium
  sign-in: no subscription and no OPENROUTER_API_KEY in the environment. If you saved a key with /secrets, the app uses it (this report does not read stored keys); otherwise sign in with: export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<key>, or /secrets in the app
  ...
Decision model:
  when it is missing or fails: Hybrid (default)
  No decision model is in use: none is set, so decisions take their fallbacks. To use one, choose a Decision model in /settings open.

Auth:
  permissions: Jev decides (jev-decides)
  ...
Surfaces:
  controlPlane: yes (local 127.0.0.1:3421)
  httpListener: no (local 127.0.0.1:3422)
  web: yes (local 127.0.0.1:3423)
...
Workspace:
  trust: undecided
  registration: not registered (never asked)
```

With no model configured the terminal app selects `openrouter:openrouter/free`.
`goodvibes status --json` prints the same facts as one JSON object.

### `goodvibes doctor`

`doctor` prints `status` plus setup warnings, each with its cause and next step.
It exits `0` when the install is usable and non-zero only for a must-fix finding; `--strict` also fails on advisory findings.
Its three sub-reports explain one decision each:

| Command | What it prints |
| --- | --- |
| `goodvibes doctor explain <tool\|command>` | How the permission gate would decide one tool call or shell command under the mode in force, with the decision model, the remembered and never-run rules and the tool's path containment, without running it (see "Explaining a decision: `goodvibes doctor explain`" in the permissions part). |
| `goodvibes doctor routing` | Which provider and model serve each role (main chat, helper, tool model, TTS model, embeddings). |
| `goodvibes doctor hooks [--json]` | Every registered hook, where it came from and whether it validates. |

Worked example:

```text
$ goodvibes doctor explain "rm -rf build"
GoodVibes doctor: explain permission decision
  subject     : rm -rf build
  resolved as : shell command run through the "exec" tool: rm -rf build
  tool        : exec  (category: execute)
...
Analysis (from the platform analyzer):
  risk        : HIGH (shell)
Current settings:
  mode        : ask-me (Ask me) in force; set: jev-decides
                not jev-decides, because no decision model is set, so every call Jev would decide asks you (to use one, choose a Decision model in /settings open)
...
  rules       : the remembered rules of this project were read
  decision model: not consulted: No decision model is in use: none is set, so decisions take their fallbacks. To use one, choose a Decision model in /settings open. The verdict is the one the gate gives without a decision model.
...
Decision: ASK
  decided by : user_prompt (user_denied)
  because    : This reaches a Human-in-the-Loop approval prompt; the outcome depends on your response at the prompt.
```

A file write is explained with the tool name and path: `goodvibes doctor explain write ./src/app.ts`.
Every `doctor` finding is described under "Checking an installation with doctor and status" in the install part.

### `goodvibes setup`

`goodvibes setup` opens the terminal app on `/setup`: the setup topics, one form each.
`goodvibes setup status` prints whether first run has been done for this user and exits:

```text
$ goodvibes setup status
GoodVibes onboarding status
  checked: no
  scope: none
  source: n/a
  mode: n/a
  updatedAt: n/a
  workingDir: /home/me/work/project
```

### `goodvibes models` (alias `model`)

`models` lists, selects and pins models.

| Form | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `goodvibes models` | Lists selectable models, the current one marked `*`. Text output shows at most a fixed number of rows and says `showing N of M`; JSON output lists every match. |
| `goodvibes models <provider-or-text>` or `models list <text>` | Lists models whose provider equals the word or whose registry key contains it. |
| `goodvibes models current` | Prints the current model, provider, sign-in kind, whether the provider is configured and the context window. |
| `goodvibes models use <registryKey>` (alias `set`) | Saves this model as the main chat model (`provider.model`). |
| `goodvibes models pin <registryKey>` / `unpin <registryKey>` | Adds the model to, or removes it from, the pinned favorites. |
| `goodvibes models pinned` | Lists pinned models. |
| `goodvibes models recent` | Lists the 25 most recently used models. |
| `goodvibes models chain [filter]` (alias `chains`) | Lists the backend order of every `synthetic` model (see "Synthetic failover" below). This form is not in the program's help. |

Worked examples:

```text
$ goodvibes models use openai:gpt-5.4
Model selected: openai:gpt-5.4

$ goodvibes models current
GoodVibes current model
  model: openai:gpt-5.4
  provider: openai
  setup: Unknown
  provider configured: no
  context: 1,050,000
```

Failure cases:

```text
$ goodvibes models use nosuchmodel
Unknown model: nosuchmodel. Nothing was changed. Name the provider to save a model that is not in the local catalog: goodvibes models use <provider>:nosuchmodel
```

The exit code is `1`.
A model that the local catalog does not know is saved when it is named with its provider (`goodvibes models use openai:new-model`); the provider's own answer decides later whether it exists.
`models pin` refuses a registry key that is not selectable: `Unknown model: <key>. Nothing was pinned.`

### `goodvibes providers` (alias `provider`)

`providers` shows each provider's setup class, whether it is configured, how it signs in, how many models it lists and its sign-in routes.

| Form | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `goodvibes providers` or `providers list` | One line per provider; the current one is marked `*`. |
| `goodvibes providers current` | The current provider, model and sign-in routes. |
| `goodvibes providers inspect <provider>` | Every sign-in route of one provider with its state and a detail line saying what to do. |
| `goodvibes providers use <provider> [registryKey]` | Switches the main chat route to the provider and, when given, the model. |

Worked example:

```text
$ goodvibes providers inspect openai
Provider openai
  active: yes
  setup: Unknown
  configured: no
  via: api-key
  models: 53
  auth routes: 1/4 configured, 0/4 usable
    Ambient API key [api-key; not configured, not usable, unconfigured] - No direct API key is configured.
    SecretRef-backed API key [secret-ref; not configured, not usable, unconfigured] - No SecretRef-backed credential is configured.
    Service OAuth [service-oauth; not configured, not usable, unconfigured] - Service OAuth metadata exists, but the credential path is incomplete.
    Subscription OAuth [subscription-oauth; configured, not usable, unconfigured] - A built-in subscription OAuth adapter is available, but no session is stored yet.
  detail: Not signed in: sign in with a ChatGPT subscription (/provider sign-in openai) or set OPENAI_API_KEY.
```

A line of `goodvibes providers` reads like this:

```text
  * openai             setup=unknown configured=no via=api-key models=53 routes=1/4 configured, 0/4 usable Not signed in: sign in with a ChatGPT subscription (/provider sign-in openai) or set OPENAI_API_KEY.
```

### `goodvibes subscription` (alias `subscriptions`)

`subscription` signs a provider in with a subscription account instead of an API key. OpenAI (a ChatGPT subscription) is the built-in subscription provider.

| Form | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `goodvibes subscription list` | Active and pending subscription sign-ins. |
| `goodvibes subscription providers` | Providers that offer subscription sign-in, with their redirect address. |
| `goodvibes subscription inspect <provider>` | One provider's stored sign-in: whether it is active or pending, token type and expiry. Never prints a token: with `--output json` the stored sign-in is `{ configured, tokenType, expiresAt, refreshToken: present\|absent, scopes, overrideAmbientApiKeys, createdAt, updatedAt }`. |
| `goodvibes subscription login <provider> start [--open]` | Starts the sign-in, saves a pending record and prints the authorization address. `--open` opens it in a browser. `goodvibes subscription start <provider>` is a shorter form. |
| `goodvibes subscription login <provider> finish <code-or-url>` | Finishes the sign-in with the code, or the whole redirect address the browser landed on. `goodvibes subscription finish <provider> <code-or-url>` is a shorter form. |
| `goodvibes subscription refresh <provider>` | Refreshes the stored token. This form is not in the program's help. |
| `goodvibes subscription logout <provider>` | Removes the stored or pending sign-in. |

The full sign-in, in order:

1. Run `goodvibes subscription login openai start --open`. It prints the authorization address and opens it:

```text
Subscription OAuth started: openai
  source: builtin
  state: <state>
  redirectUri: http://localhost:1455/auth/callback
  next: goodvibes subscription login openai finish <code-or-url>
  authorizationUrl:
  https://auth.openai.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&...
```

2. Sign in in the browser. The browser is sent to `http://localhost:1455/auth/callback?code=...`. The page may fail to load; that does not matter.
3. Copy the whole address from the browser's address bar and run `goodvibes subscription login openai finish '<the address>'`. It prints `Stored subscription session for openai.` with the token type and expiry.
4. Run `goodvibes providers inspect openai` to confirm that the `Subscription OAuth` route is usable.

Inside the terminal app, `/provider sign-in openai` does the same and waits for the browser to return to the local callback address; when the browser returns there the sign-in finishes without step 3.

Failure cases:

- `goodvibes subscription inspect nosuch` prints `No stored or available subscription provider named nosuch.` and exits `1`.
- A code that the provider refuses prints the provider's error (for example `OAuth token exchange failed (401)`) and exits `1`; start again with `login <provider> start`.
- `goodvibes subscription logout <provider>` with nothing stored prints `No stored subscription session existed for <provider>.` and exits `1`.

When OpenAI has both a subscription sign-in and an API key, requests use the subscription; a request the subscription fails is sent again to the same model with the API key, and the turn says so once.

### `goodvibes secrets` (alias `secret`)

`secrets` stores credentials in the GoodVibes secret store and links names to external secret references.
A secret reference has the form `goodvibes://secrets/<source>/<path>` and never contains the value.

| Form | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `goodvibes secrets list` | The storage policy, whether secure storage is available, and the stored key names with their scope. Never prints values. |
| `goodvibes secrets providers` | The reference sources: `env`, `goodvibes`, `file`, `exec`, `1password`, `bitwarden`, `vaultwarden`, `bitwarden-secrets-manager`. |
| `goodvibes secrets test <ref>` | Checks that a reference resolves, without printing the value. |
| `goodvibes secrets set <KEY> <value> [--user\|--project] [--secure\|--plaintext]` | Stores a value. `--plaintext` stores it unencrypted. |
| `goodvibes secrets set <KEY> --stdin` | Reads the value from standard input. Use it for a value that starts with `--`, and to keep the value out of shell history. |
| `goodvibes secrets link <KEY> <ref> [--user\|--project] [--secure\|--plaintext]` | Makes `<KEY>` resolve through the reference. |
| `goodvibes secrets delete <KEY> [--user\|--project] [--secure\|--plaintext]` | Deletes a stored key. |

Put flags after the positional words: the `secrets` helper reads the word after a flag as that flag's value.

Worked example:

```text
$ printf '%s' '<your-api-key>' | goodvibes secrets set OPENAI_API_KEY --stdin --user
[secrets] Stored: OPENAI_API_KEY

$ goodvibes secrets list
GoodVibes secrets
  policy: preferred_secure
  secure available: yes
  stored keys: 1
    OPENAI_API_KEY (user-secure)

$ goodvibes secrets link GITHUB_TOKEN goodvibes://secrets/env/GH_TOKEN --user
$ goodvibes secrets test goodvibes://secrets/env/GH_TOKEN
```

A key stored with `--plaintext` is listed with `-plaintext` in its scope and `secrets list` adds `warning: plaintext fallback secrets are present`.
A provider reads its key from the environment first, then from the secret store.

### `goodvibes sessions` (alias `session`)

`sessions` lists and opens saved sessions of the working directory.

| Form | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `goodvibes sessions list` | One line per session: id, message count, last save time, title. |
| `goodvibes sessions show <id\|name>` | One session's details. |
| `goodvibes sessions export <id\|name> [path]` | Writes the session to a JSON file (or prints it when no path is given). |
| `goodvibes sessions resume <id\|name>` | Opens the terminal app on that session. |

```text
$ goodvibes sessions list
GoodVibes sessions (3)
  user-0008b454  messages=34  2026-11-18T16:43:26.464Z  hello
  user-51cf10f8  messages=11  2026-11-18T04:56:35.305Z  find all of the implicit state machines in this
  user-7d4c6370  messages=8  2026-11-18T04:52:01.662Z  (untitled)

$ goodvibes sessions show nope
Session not found: nope
```

`sessions show` of a missing session exits `1`.

### `goodvibes tasks` (alias `task`)

`tasks` reads runtime tasks from the daemon.

| Form | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `goodvibes tasks list` | Tasks the daemon holds. |
| `goodvibes tasks show <taskId>` | One task. |
| `goodvibes tasks submit <prompt>` | Submits a non-interactive task to the daemon. |

When no daemon answers, `tasks list` says so and exits `0`:

```text
GoodVibes tasks
  None listed: no daemon could be asked (Authentication failed · Token is invalid or has expired · Verify your credentials and token store configuration.); tasks exist only in the daemon or inside a running session.
```

### `goodvibes auth`

`auth` manages the local user store of the daemon and listener (usernames, passwords, sessions, the bootstrap credential).
Changes are written to the user store; a running daemon reads the user file again at its next sign-in check.

| Form | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `goodvibes auth` or `auth status` | Auth posture. |
| `goodvibes auth users` | Local users. |
| `goodvibes auth sessions` | The sign-in sessions the daemon on this machine holds: `<username> expires=<time> id=<session id>` per session. It asks the running daemon at its loopback address with this machine's operator token; with no daemon answering it prints why and exits `1`. |
| `goodvibes auth add-user <username> [--password <value>\|--password-stdin] [--role <role>]` | Adds a user. Without a password flag it reads `GOODVIBES_AUTH_PASSWORD`. `--role` may be repeated; the default role is `user`. |
| `goodvibes auth delete-user <username>` | Deletes a user. A running daemon (or terminal app) re-reads the user file at its next sign-in or session check, within a few seconds, and ends that user's sessions then; no restart is needed. Prints `Auth user deleted: <username>` and that note; an unknown user prints `No auth user found: <username>` (exit `1`). |
| `goodvibes auth rotate-password <username> [--password <value>\|--password-stdin]` | Sets a new password. A running daemon ends that user's sessions at its next sign-in or session check, within a few seconds, without a restart. Prints `Auth password rotated: <username>` and that note. |
| `goodvibes auth revoke-session <session-id-or-token>` | Ends that session on the running daemon at once (through `local_auth.sessions.delete`): `Auth session revoked on the running daemon.` An unknown session, or no daemon answering, prints the daemon's reason and exits `1`. Take the id from `goodvibes auth sessions`. |
| `goodvibes auth revoke-sessions <username>` | Ends every session of that user on the running daemon: `Auth sessions revoked for <username> on the running daemon: <n>`; `The running daemon holds no auth sessions for <username>.` (exit `1`) when it holds none. |
| `goodvibes auth clear-bootstrap` | Deletes the bootstrap credential file. |

```sh
printf '%s\n' '<new-password>' | goodvibes auth add-user admin --password-stdin --role admin
```

Sessions live in the memory of the running daemon; this command cannot end them. Restart the daemon to end them all.
Local accounts are described under "Sign-in users" in the daemon part.

### `goodvibes acp`

`acp` runs the terminal app as an Agent Client Protocol agent on standard input and output. It is described under the heading "Editors: the Agent Client Protocol" below.

### `goodvibes host pair` and `goodvibes host unpair`

`host pair` reviews and creates the credential this terminal app uses to call its host daemon.

```sh
goodvibes host pair                         # review only: prints what pairing would do
goodvibes host pair --bootstrap-shared      # review using the daemon's shared bootstrap credential
goodvibes host pair --apply                 # create the credential; asks for fresh confirmation
goodvibes host unpair                       # forget the stored credential here
```

`--url <exact-origin>` names the host and `--name <device-name>` names the credential.
`--apply` needs a fresh confirmation typed in an owner terminal; `--yes` is not accepted for it.
`unpair` forgets the credential here only; it stays valid on the host until it is revoked there.
Host pairing is described under "Host pairing: giving the terminal app its own credential" in the daemon part.

### `goodvibes pair` (aliases `qrcode`, `qr`)

`pair` mints a named, revocable device token on the connected daemon and prints its pairing link and a QR code for a phone or browser.

```sh
goodvibes pair --name "my phone"
```

Device pairing is described under "Pairing a phone or another browser" in the daemon part.

### `goodvibes web`, `surfaces`, `listener`, `control-plane`, `service`, `remote`

These commands report and change the daemon's network surfaces and service. They are described in full under "Network exposure", "Serving the web UI" and "Service commands" in the daemon part, and under "The daemon's background service" in the install part; their usage is:

| Command | Usage | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `web` | `goodvibes web [--open] [--hostname <h>] [--port <p>]` | Prints where the web UI is served (see below); `--open` opens that address. `--hostname`/`--port` name a development server's endpoint instead for this one command. |
| `surfaces` (alias `surface`) | `surfaces [list]`, `surfaces check [<web\|listener\|control-plane\|surfaceId>]`, `surfaces show <...>`, `surfaces enable <...>`, `surfaces disable <...>` | Inspects and turns on or off the web UI, the control plane, the HTTP listener and each channel surface (for example `slack`). |
| `listener test [--json]` (aliases `http-listener`, `webhook`) | | Checks HTTP listener and webhook readiness. |
| `control-plane status [--json]` (aliases `controlplane`, `cp`) | | Daemon bind posture, reachability, local auth, bootstrap credential and operator tokens. |
| `service` (alias `services`) | `service status`, `service check [--json]`, `service install\|start\|stop\|restart\|uninstall` | The daemon's background service. |
| `remote` (alias `bridge`) | | Remote runner pools, runner contracts, review artifacts and private-host fetch posture. |

```text
$ goodvibes web
GoodVibes web
  enabled: yes
  served by: the daemon, on its control-plane listener
  url: http://127.0.0.1:3421
  development endpoint (web.host/web.port): local 127.0.0.1:3423

$ goodvibes remote
GoodVibes remote status
  runner pools: 0
  contracts: 0
  review artifacts: 0
  private-host remote fetch: no
```

The `url:` line has one owner, the same one pairing links, notification links and `tailscale.serve.run` use: the daemon's control-plane address while it serves the bundle (after `goodvibes-daemon webui enable`, see "Serving the web UI" in the daemon part), otherwise a set `web.publicBaseUrl` naming where a web UI runs, otherwise `none: no web UI is served; serve the bundle with goodvibes-daemon webui enable --bundle-dir <dir>` (and `--open` prints `nothing to open`). When `web.publicBaseUrl` names a different address for other devices (a tunnel), a `public url (links for other devices):` line shows it. `web.host`/`web.port` (3423) are only where the web UI's development server listens; nothing else binds them. `--json` gives `url` (null when none is served), `servedByDaemon` and, when set, `publicUrl`.

### `goodvibes support-bundle` (aliases `bundle`, `bundles`)

A support bundle is a redacted snapshot of configuration, diagnostics and posture, for a support request or for moving settings to another machine.

| Form | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `goodvibes support-bundle export [path]` | Writes the bundle. |
| `goodvibes support-bundle inspect <path>` | Prints what a bundle holds. |
| `goodvibes support-bundle import <path> [--include-security] [--yes]` | Applies the bundle's setting values. |

`import` refuses a bundle from another product or format version.
It imports only values that differ from the current settings.
It holds back permission, sandbox, listener, service and storage settings unless `--include-security` is given.
It applies all values or none.
Without `--yes` it lists each change as `current -> new`, changes nothing and exits `2`.
With `daemon.connectedHost.url` set, the daemon's settings go to that daemon with the token stored for it (or an `/accounts sign-in daemon` session); with none stored, nothing is sent and the import fails with `CREDENTIAL_NOT_FOR_TARGET`. This machine's daemon token is never sent to another daemon.

```sh
goodvibes support-bundle export goodvibes-bundle.json
goodvibes support-bundle inspect goodvibes-bundle.json
goodvibes support-bundle import goodvibes-bundle.json          # preview, exit 2
goodvibes support-bundle import goodvibes-bundle.json --yes    # apply
```

`plugin bundles` is a different command (capability bundles; see "Plugins" below).

### `goodvibes hooks validate`

`hooks validate` checks the hooks file (`hooks.json` in the working directory, or the file `tools.hooksFile` names) against the hook loader's rules, and prints one line per hook.
It exits `1` when any hook is invalid.

```text
$ goodvibes hooks validate
GoodVibes hooks validation
  file: /home/me/work/project/hooks.json
  hooks: 2 total, 1 pass, 1 fail
  FAIL  pre:tool:exec #0 (unnamed): "pre:tool:exec" is not a recognized hook event point: no registered hook point matches it (phases are Pre, Post, Fail, Change and Lifecycle, and case matters); /hooks contracts lists them
  PASS  Post:tool:write #0 (unnamed) (contract: observe/non_blocking)
  result: 1 problem(s) found.
```

With no hooks file it prints `no hooks file present: nothing to validate.` and exits `0`.

### `goodvibes plugin` (alias `plugins`)

| Form | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `goodvibes plugin init <name> [directory]` | Writes a minimal plugin (`manifest.json` and `index.js`), validates it, and says whether the apps load plugins from that directory. |
| `goodvibes plugin validate <path>` | Runs the plugin loader's checks on a plugin directory and says whether the apps load plugins from it. |
| `goodvibes plugin trust <name> <untrusted\|limited\|trusted> [note]` | Sets the plugin's trust tier for every GoodVibes program on this machine. Marking a plugin `trusted` whose signature does not verify needs `--yes`. |
| `goodvibes plugin verify <name>` | Checks the plugin's signature against its saved publisher key. |
| `goodvibes plugin capabilities <name>` | Prints what the plugin declares and what its tier grants. |
| `goodvibes plugin bundles browse <index-url-or-file>` | Lists the capability bundles in a marketplace index. |
| `goodvibes plugin bundles install <ref> --sha256 <pin> [--ref <git-ref>] [--yes]` | Verifies and, with `--yes`, installs a capability bundle. |
| `goodvibes plugin bundles uninstall <id>` | Removes an installed bundle. |
| `goodvibes plugin bundles list` | Lists installed bundles. |

Worked example:

```text
$ goodvibes plugin init my-plugin
Scaffolded plugin "my-plugin" at /home/me/work/project/.goodvibes/plugins/my-plugin
  created: manifest.json, index.js
  validation: PASS; the plugin loader accepts this manifest and entry.
  next: a plugin starts disabled. In the terminal app or the Agent run /plugin enable my-plugin (no restart needed).
```

Without a directory, `plugin init <name>` writes `<project>/.goodvibes/plugins/<name>/`, where the loader looks. With a directory it writes there. The apps load a plugin only from a folder directly inside `<project>/.goodvibes/plugins/` (when the app runs in that project) or `~/.goodvibes/plugins/`.
