| Some allowed and some not (`?domains=providers,session,automation` for a non-admin) | The stream opens with the allowed ones. `ready` names the refused ones: `{"clientId":"cp-cb69c602","domains":["providers","automation"],"transport":"sse","withheldDomains":["session"],"resume":{"resume":"none"}}`. |
| None allowed (`?domains=session,turn,tools` for a non-admin), or a credential that may receive nothing | `403` `{"error":"This credential may not receive the requested event domains: session, turn, tools.","code":"EVENT_ACCESS_DENIED","category":"authorization","status":403,"state":"the event stream was not opened","next":["Sign in as an admin, or open the stream with domains this credential may read."],"withheldDomains":["session","turn","tools"]}` |

Always read `withheldDomains` in the `ready` frame: a stream that opened is not a stream that carries everything asked for.

#### What a stream without `domains` carries

Two kinds of frame travel on a stream, and `domains` filters them differently (from the code, `control-plane/gateway.ts` and `gateway-scope-enforcement.ts`; the admin results observed on a 3.3.2 daemon):

| Frames | Opened without `domains` | Opened with `domains=<list>` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runtime events (`turn`, `tools`, `gate`, `config`, ... frames named after their domain: `TURN_*`, `TOOL_*` and the rest) | Only the 14 default domains: `session`, `tasks`, `agents`, `automation`, `routes`, `control-plane`, `deliveries`, `surfaces`, `watchers`, `transport`, `ops`, `knowledge`, `providers`, `turn`. These are what the `ready` frame lists. No `tools`, `gate`, `config`, `fleet`, `contracts` or `mcp` runtime events, so no tool calls. | Exactly the listed domains. |
| Broadcast events: `approval-update` and `owner-inbox-update` (tagged `gate`), `session-update` and `hosted-session-update` (tagged `session`), and the untagged ones (`surface-message`, the `remote-*` events) | All of them, whatever the `ready` frame lists, so approvals do arrive. | A tagged one only when its tag is listed (`approval-update` needs `gate` in the list); an untagged one always. |

Access applies on top in both cases: a non-admin credential never receives an admin-only event or domain (`approval-update`, `owner-inbox-update`, `session-update`, `hosted-session-update`, the `session`, `turn`, `tools`, `tasks`, `agents`, `gate` domains and the others in "Access of every event"), except that `read:own-sessions` opens the `turn`, `tools`, `gate` and `session` frames and the `approval-update` and `hosted-session-update` events of the caller's own sessions; a non-admin stream without `domains` opens on the defaults it may read and lists the rest under `withheldDomains`.

So an admin client that wants approvals can open the stream without `domains` (it then also gets every session update but no tool calls), or name its domains and include `gate`: `?domains=gate,session,turn,tools`. A stream opened with `?domains=session` gets no `approval-update`. Listing `domains` replaces the defaults; it does not add to them.

### Reconnecting

- If no frame (not even a heartbeat) arrives for 35 seconds, the connection is dead: reconnect.
- Reconnect with the header `Last-Event-ID: <id of the last event you processed>`. The `ready` frame's `resume` says what happened:
  - `{"resume":"resumed","sinceId":"...","replayed":<n>}`: the events after that id were replayed, in order. Nothing was missed.
  - `{"resume":"unresolved","sinceId":"..."}`: that id is no longer in the daemon's buffer of the last 500 events (or the daemon restarted). Nothing was replayed. Re-read state (`GET /api/sessions/{id}`, `GET /api/approvals`, `GET /api/tasks`) before trusting the stream.
  - `{"resume":"none"}`: no `Last-Event-ID` was sent. The daemon sends up to 20 recent events, plus the start of any turn still running, so a client can render it.
- After a `gap` event, reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` set to its `afterId`.
- A turn's end is always one of `TURN_COMPLETED`, `TURN_ERROR`, `TURN_CANCEL`, `PREFLIGHT_FAIL`. After any reconnect that is not `resumed`, check the session's state instead of waiting for an end event that may already have been sent.
- Back off between attempts (for example 1, 2, 4, 8 seconds, up to 30).
- A `401` on reconnect, or a `closed` frame, means the credential was revoked or expired; do not retry with it.

### Per-session stream

`GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/events` (admin) carries only that session's events (and events with no session) on the default domains plus `tools`, with the same frames and reconnect rules. It takes no `domains` parameter.

### Telemetry stream

`GET /api/v1/telemetry/stream` (scope `read:telemetry`) is a separate Server-Sent Events stream of telemetry records. See "Telemetry" in "The daemon, the web UI and networking".

## Rate limits

| What | Limit | Answer when exceeded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /login` | 5 per minute per address | `429` `RATE_LIMITED` |
| `POST /api/remote/pair/request` | 10 per minute per address | `429` `RATE_LIMITED`, `Retry-After: 60` |
| Companion chat messages | `runtime.companionChatLimiter.perSessionLimit` per 60 seconds per session (0 means `GOODVIBES_CHAT_LIMITER_THRESHOLD`, else 10) | refused |

These are the request-rate limits the daemon applies to its own routes. Provider rate limits come back as errors on the turn (`RATE_LIMITED` with `retryAfterMs` when the provider gave one).

## OpenAI-compatible endpoints

When `controlPlane.openaiCompatible.enabled` is `true` (default), the daemon answers OpenAI-style requests under `controlPlane.openaiCompatible.pathPrefix` (default `/v1`). There are three routes and no others (no `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/completions` or `/v1/responses`):

| Route | Access |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/models` | Any valid credential (a scoped device token works). |
| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | Admin. A non-admin gets the daemon's own `403` body `{"error":"Admin role required","code":"ADMIN_REQUIRED",...}`, not the OpenAI shape, because these requests spend provider money. |
| `GET /v1/chat/completions/{id}` | Admin. Reads back a completion that was queued as batch work. |

No credential answers `401` `AUTH_REQUIRED` in the daemon's own shape.

### Model ids

`GET /v1/models` answers `{"object":"list","data":[{"id":"...","object":"model","created":<seconds>,"owned_by":"<provider>"},...]}`, sorted by id. It always contains `goodvibes/current`, which means the daemon's current model (whatever it is when the request arrives); the others are registry keys `provider:model`, such as `openrouter:openrouter/free` or `decision-router:auto`. A request's `model` may be `goodvibes/current`, a registry key, or a bare model id when exactly one provider has it. `model` is required: there is no default.

### Request

`POST /v1/chat/completions` takes the OpenAI chat-completions body:

| Field | Handling |
| --- | --- |
| `model` | Required. Missing: `400` `model_not_found` `Missing required field: model.`. Unknown: `400` `model_not_found` naming candidates (`Unknown model 'nope-model-x'. Did you mean: ...`). |
| `messages` | Required (missing: `400` `missing_messages`). Roles `system` and `developer` (joined into the system prompt), `user`, `assistant` (with `tool_calls`), `tool` (with `tool_call_id`). Any other role, a message that is not an object or has no role, or a tool message without `tool_call_id` is `400` `invalid_messages`. |
| `stream` | `true` streams `chat.completion.chunk` objects as `data: {...}` lines and ends with `data: [DONE]`; the last chunk before `[DONE]` carries `usage`. |
| `max_completion_tokens`, `max_tokens` | Applied (the first wins). |
| `tools` | Offered to the model as in the OpenAI API; tool calls come back to the caller in `tool_calls`. GoodVibes' own tools are not run. |
| `tool_choice` | `auto` or `none` (`none` offers no tools). Anything else is refused. |
| `reasoning_effort` | Applied. |
| `response_format` | Only `{"type":"text"}`. Anything else is refused. |
| `n` | Only `1`. Anything else is refused. |
| `stop` | Only absent or `[]`. Anything else is refused. |
| `logprobs` | Only absent or `false`. `true` is refused. |
| `temperature`, `top_p`, `presence_penalty`, `frequency_penalty`, `seed`, `logit_bias`, `top_logprobs` | Ignored. The request is served, and the response header `x-goodvibes-ignored-params` names the ones that were sent, comma-separated. |

A refused parameter answers `400` with `type` `invalid_request_error`, `code` `unsupported_parameter` and `param` naming it, for example `{"error":{"message":"This endpoint returns one choice per request. Remove \"n\" and resend.","type":"invalid_request_error","param":"n","code":"unsupported_parameter"}}` or `Stop sequences are not applied by this endpoint. Remove "stop" and resend.`.

### Response

```json
{"id":"chatcmpl-goodvibes-<uuid>","object":"chat.completion","created":1795025562,"model":"goodvibes/current",
 "choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Hello.","tool_calls":[...]},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"stop"}],
 "usage":{"prompt_tokens":18104,"completion_tokens":7,"total_tokens":18111}}
```

`model` echoes what you asked for (`goodvibes/current` stays `goodvibes/current`). `finish_reason` is `stop`, `length` (the token limit), `tool_calls` or `content_filter`. `usage.prompt_tokens` includes cached prompt tokens. `tool_calls` is present only when the model called a tool. Cost is not reported.

### Errors

Every error from these routes, except the credential refusals above, has the OpenAI shape `{"error":{"message":"...","type":"...","param":<name or null>,"code":"..."}}`. `type` follows the status: `401` `authentication_error`, `403` `permission_error`, `404` `not_found_error`, `429` `rate_limit_error`, other `4xx` `invalid_request_error`, `5xx` `server_error`. A provider failure keeps the provider's status (`502` when it gave none) with code `provider_error`. A body that is not JSON is `400` `invalid_json`.

### Batch execution

The header `x-goodvibes-execution` takes `batch` or `live` (anything else: `400` `invalid_execution`). With `batch`, and `batch.mode` not `off`, the request is queued as provider batch work and answered `202` with `{"id":"<job id>","object":"chat.completion.batch_job","status":"queued","created":...,"model":"...","poll":"/v1/chat/completions/<job id>"}` and a `location` header. `GET` that path: `202` with the same body while it waits, `200` with the completion when done, `409` `batch_cancelled`, `410` `batch_expired`, or `502` when it failed. `batch.mode` off with `batch` asked is `409` `batch_disabled`; `batch` with `"stream": true` is `400` `batch_stream_unsupported`.

### With an OpenAI client

Python (`pip install openai`), using an admin token:

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:3421/v1", api_key=os.environ["GV_TOKEN"])
print([m.id for m in client.models.list().data][:5])
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="goodvibes/current",
    messages=[{"role": "system", "content": "Answer in one word."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Say hello."}],
    max_tokens=20,
)
print(reply.choices[0].message.content, reply.usage)
for chunk in client.chat.completions.create(model="goodvibes/current", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Count to 3."}], stream=True):
    print(chunk.choices[0].delta.content or "", end="")
```

TypeScript (`npm install openai`):

```ts
import OpenAI from 'openai';
const client = new OpenAI({ baseURL: 'http://127.0.0.1:3421/v1', apiKey: process.env.GV_TOKEN! });
const reply = await client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'goodvibes/current', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Say hello.' }] });
console.log(reply.choices[0]!.message.content);
```

The client sends the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, which is what the daemon reads. Do not pass `n`, `stop` or a JSON `response_format`; they are refused.

## The MCP bridge

`goodvibes-daemon mcp serve` exposes the operator API as MCP tools over standard input and output, for MCP clients. See "`mcp serve`" in "The daemon, the web UI and networking".

## SDK entry points

The package `@goodvibes/engine` (version 3.3.3) contains typed clients for this API. It does not call model providers itself; the daemon does.

How it is published: two packages of the repository are publishable, `@goodvibes/engine` (`packages/engine`) and `@goodvibes/judgment` (`packages/judgment`); the products (`goodvibes`, `goodvibes-agent`, the daemon, the web UI) are private and never published. The release workflow publishes the two packages to `https://registry.npmjs.org` with provenance only when a release runs from a version tag and the repository variable `PUBLISH_NPM` is `true`; otherwise a release produces the native GitHub release and its installer assets and publishes nothing to npm. The repository does not record that variable's value, so whether a given version is on npm is answered by the registry, not by the source:

```sh
npm view @goodvibes/engine versions --json
```

When the version you need is there, install it like any package:

```sh
bun add @goodvibes/engine@3.3.3
npm install @goodvibes/engine@3.3.3
```

When it is not, use it from a source checkout of the same version, inside that checkout's workspace:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mgd34msu/goodvibes.git
cd goodvibes
git checkout v3.3.3
bun install
bun run build                 # produces the dist/ directories the package's exports name
mkdir -p products/my-client
cat > products/my-client/package.json <<'JSON'
{ "name": "my-client", "private": true, "type": "module",
  "dependencies": { "@goodvibes/engine": "workspace:*" } }
JSON
bun install                   # links the new workspace
bun products/my-client/main.ts
```

Every folder under `packages/` and `products/` is a workspace, and a script must live inside the checkout for `@goodvibes/engine` to resolve; a script elsewhere fails with `Cannot find module '@goodvibes/engine/...'`. Under Bun the package's `bun` export condition loads the TypeScript sources directly.

Do not make a tarball of the package by hand from a checkout (`npm pack` or `bun pm pack` in `packages/engine`): the tarball keeps the `bun` export condition, which names `src/` files the tarball does not contain, so imports under Bun fail. The release removes that condition when it stages the packages; only a registry release or the checkout's workspace gives a working package.

| Import | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `@goodvibes/engine/platform` | `createGoodVibesPlatform({ baseUrl, authToken })` for Bun and Node: `operator` (typed methods), `realtime` (events), `auth`, `peer`. Also `createMemoryTokenStore`. |
| `@goodvibes/engine/platform/browser` | `createBrowserGoodVibesPlatform`, for web pages. |
| `@goodvibes/engine/platform/react-native`, `@goodvibes/engine/platform/expo` | `createReactNativeGoodVibesPlatform`, `createExpoGoodVibesPlatform`. |
| `@goodvibes/engine/platform/auth` | `createMemoryTokenStore`, `createBrowserTokenStore`. |
| `@goodvibes/engine/operator-client` | `createOperatorApiClient({ baseUrl, authToken })`: the operator client alone. |
| `@goodvibes/engine/transport-http` | The HTTP transport, retry, Server-Sent Events reader, private-network checks. |
| `@goodvibes/engine/transport-realtime` | Event buses and `forSession(events, sessionId)`. |
| `@goodvibes/engine/peer-client` | The peer API client for remote nodes. |
| `@goodvibes/engine/contracts` | The operator and peer contracts, method ids, event domains. |
| `@goodvibes/engine/errors` | `GoodVibesError`, `HttpStatusError`, `ContractError` and the error codes. |
| `@goodvibes/engine/platform/daemon` | `dispatchDaemonApiRoutes` and the pieces for embedding a daemon in your own Bun server. |
| `@goodvibes/engine/daemon-api/relay-server-entry` | The relay server program. |

Example, verified against a 3.3.1 daemon:

```ts
import { createGoodVibesPlatform } from '@goodvibes/engine/platform';
import { forSession } from '@goodvibes/engine/transport-realtime';

const baseUrl = 'http://127.0.0.1:3421';
const token = process.env.GV_TOKEN!;
const gv = createGoodVibesPlatform({ baseUrl, authToken: token });

// Typed methods that have a REST route:
const auth = await gv.operator.invoke('control.auth.current', {});
const sessions = await gv.operator.sessions.list();

// Invoke-only methods are not reachable through operator.invoke(); call the invoke route:
const res = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/api/control-plane/methods/sessions.hosted.create/invoke`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ body: { workspaceRoot: '/home/alex/projects/app', detachPolicy: 'survive' } }),
});
const { session } = await res.json();

// Live events for that session only:
const events = forSession(gv.realtime.viaSse(), session.id);
events.turn.onEnvelope('STREAM_DELTA', (e) => process.stdout.write(e.payload.content));
```

Facts about the SDK:

- `gv.operator` has `invoke(methodId, input)`, `stream`, `listOperations`, `getOperation`, and namespaces `sessions`, `tasks`, `approvals`, `providers`, `accounts`, `localAuth`, `control`, `telemetry`.
- `operator.invoke()` works only for methods with a REST route. For an invoke-only method it throws `GoodVibesError` with code `CONTRACT_MISMATCH` (`Operator method "sessions.hosted.list" does not expose an HTTP binding`). Call the invoke route, or send a WebSocket `call` frame.
- A refused request throws `HttpStatusError` with `code` and `status`, for example `code` `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `status` `404`.
- Responses are checked against the contract's output schema by default (`validateResponses: true`); a mismatch throws `ContractError`, which usually means the daemon runs another version.
- `gv.realtime.viaSse()` and `gv.realtime.viaWebSocket()` return event buses with one property per domain (`session`, `turn`, `tools`, `tasks`, `agents`, ...). The connection opens on the first subscription. `viaWebSocket()` sends the token as `Authorization: Bearer` on the upgrade request (Bun and Node 22+ WebSocket accept upgrade headers), so a client that has only a token connects; the token is sent only to `baseUrl`'s own origin.
- When a request is refused with `401`, the client refreshes its token and repeats the request once, but only under the same sign-in: if the stored token now belongs to another login (someone signed in since), the request is not repeated and fails with `401` `AUTH_REQUIRED` ("Signed in as someone else since this request was sent").
- The browser entry's event stream (`streams.open`) refuses an absolute URL on another origin with `CREDENTIAL_NOT_FOR_TARGET` before anything is sent; the token and headers go only to the daemon the client was made for.

## Method and event reference

Every operator method (id, REST route or invoke-only, scopes) is listed in "Operator API methods" in the reference. Every event is listed in "Event streams a client subscribes to" and "Runtime events by domain", and every error code in "Codes any route may answer" and "Codes a method declares". `GET /api/control-plane/methods/{methodId}` returns any one method's full input and output schema from the running daemon.

# Reference

This appendix holds every complete list GoodVibes keeps in its code. Each list below is built from the program itself each time this file is generated, so it matches release 3.3.3 exactly. The other parts of this file explain how to use these things; this part is where to look up an exact name, flag, default or value.

## Settings

Every setting key the programs accept, grouped by its first segment. Each entry gives the key, what it does, its type, its default value as written in a settings file, the values it allows (an enumeration or a range), which file stores it, whether a project's own settings file may set it, and the environment variable that stands in for it when there is one.

How to read an entry. "Stored in" names one of three places, decided by the key:

- **The daemon file**: `~/.goodvibes/daemon/settings.json` (`<GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME>/settings.json` when that variable is set). There is one value, and the terminal app, Agent and the daemon all read it. `goodvibes-daemon config set <key> <value>` writes it. A change made in an app (`/settings`, `/settings set`) is sent to the running daemon, which writes it; with no daemon running the app writes the file itself.
- **The shared file**: `~/.goodvibes/shared/settings.json`. Only the five keys `tts.provider`, `tts.voice`, `tts.speed`, `tts.llmProvider` and `tts.llmModel` are read from it. A value there wins over each program's own file, and a change made in any program is written there.
- **Each program's own file**: every other key. Each program keeps its own value: the terminal app reads `~/.goodvibes/tui/settings.json` (its `/settings` and `/settings set` write it), Agent reads `~/.goodvibes/agent/settings.json` (its `/settings` writes it), and the daemon reads `~/.goodvibes/daemon-host/settings.json` (`goodvibes-daemon config set` writes it). Setting a key in one program does not change it in the others.

A few keys exist in one app only; their entries say so.

"A project file may set it" refers to the project's own file: `<project>/.goodvibes/tui/settings.json` for the terminal app, `<project>/.goodvibes/agent/settings.json` for Agent, and `<working directory>/.goodvibes/daemon-host/settings.json` for the daemon. It travels with a repository, so keys that could be abused are refused there or accepted only when stricter. A write to a key the project file already holds goes to the project file. See "Settings: layers, scopes and how to change them" in the overview.

A value in backticks is written exactly as shown in JSON (`true`, `30`, `"ask-me"`).

### agents

- `agents.contextCompactThreshold`: Fraction of the model context window at which the agent context-window guard triggers sub-agent conversation compaction (estimated system + messages + tool tokens above this fraction compacts). Distinct from behavior.autoCompactThreshold, which governs main-session conversation compaction.
  - type `number`; default `0.85`; allowed: number in [0.1, 0.99].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `agents.contextWindowGuard`: Before each sub-agent provider call, estimate total token count (system prompt + messages + tool definitions) and compact the conversation past agents.contextCompactThreshold, with layered system-prompt assembly for small windows and a single compaction retry on context-size errors. Turn off to revert to unchecked provider calls.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `agents.maxTurns`: Per-agent turn budget. Zero (default) continues until completion, cancellation, or a call that keeps returning the same result (8 identical calls with identical results end the run as repeated_call). A positive value stops the run with a max-turns outcome. A positive agents.maxTurnsCap remains an owner-controlled ceiling.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: integer in [0, 9007199254740991].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `agents.maxTurnsCap`: Owner-controlled ceiling on per-spawn turn budgets. Zero (default) disables this ceiling; a positive value cannot be raised by a spawn override.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: integer in [0, 9007199254740991].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `agents.passiveInjection.budgetTokens`: Default hard token budget for per-turn passive knowledge/code injection. The effective budget is min(this value, 3% of the model context window). Set 0 to disable injection. A per-run passiveKnowledgeInjectionBudgetTokens override still wins.
  - type `number`; default `800`; allowed: integer in [0, 1000000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `agents.passiveInjection.code`: Additionally inject similarity-ranked chunks from the repo source-code index each turn as untrusted reference pointers, sharing the knowledge-injection budget and relevance floor, each with an honest match label on the turn record. Default off: code chunks carry no review provenance, so this is deliberately opt-in. Also respects storage.codeIndexEnabled.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `agents.passiveInjection.codeLimit`: Maximum number of source-code chunks injected per turn by passive code injection (chunks share the passive-injection token budget and relevance floor).
  - type `number`; default `3`; allowed: integer in [0, 100].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `agents.passiveInjection.knowledge`: Re-retrieve project-memory knowledge each turn against the evolving conversation (steers, new sub-topics), under the hard token budget with a visible per-turn injection record on the agent record and session transcript. Default on: the block is hard-budgeted and every turn is honestly recorded. Turn off to revert to spawn-time-only injection.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `agents.passiveInjection.relevanceFloor`: Minimum relevance score (higher = stricter) a knowledge/code candidate must clear to be eligible for per-turn passive injection. Filters filler before the token budget is applied. A per-run passiveKnowledgeInjectionRelevanceFloor override still wins.
  - type `number`; default `95`; allowed: integer in [0, 1000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

### atRest

- `atRest.redactionEnabled`: When true (default), credential patterns (API keys, bearer tokens, GitHub/GitLab/Slack/AWS credentials) are redacted at WRITE time from the on-disk transcript journal (per-agent <agentId>.jsonl), reusing the same pattern set as the telemetry egress. Home paths are NOT redacted. The local execution ledger gets the same treatment only when the application embedding the platform wires the policy in. Crash reports are always redacted, whatever this setting says. A redacted value shows a [REDACTED_*] marker, a record never pretends the content was absent. Set false ONLY for local debugging where plaintext secrets in the transcript journal are acceptable.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `atRest.retentionMaxAgeDays`: Age cap (days) for the append-only files: per-agent transcript journals, the execution ledger, the activity log, crash logs and crash-recovery snapshots. Files older than this are pruned at start and every six hours (the journal also prunes on each new agent session; the ledger on each export). Saved conversations are never pruned by it. Generous by default; bounded so the files cannot grow without limit.
  - type `number`; default `30`; allowed: integer in [1, 365].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `atRest.retentionMaxTotalMb`: Total-size cap (MB) for each of the append-only file sets named under atRest.retentionMaxAgeDays (transcript journals, execution ledger, activity log, crash logs, crash-recovery snapshots). When exceeded, the oldest are deleted first (rotated backups before freshly-written active files) until under budget. Saved conversations are never deleted by it.
  - type `number`; default `512`; allowed: integer in [1, 1048576].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

### automation

- `automation.catchUpWindowMinutes`: How long after startup the engine should catch up missed runs. The same window (at least 5 minutes) is also how long a running run whose agent has vanished is left before it is failed as "Agent state lost", so a large value keeps such a run holding a concurrency slot for as long.
  - type `number`; default `30`; allowed: integer in [0, 1440].

  - A project file may not set it.

- `automation.deleteAfterRun`: Default for the deleteAfterRun flag of newly created one-shot (at) automation jobs: a job with the flag is deleted after its first successful run. Recurring jobs are never deleted by this default. Existing jobs keep the value they were created with.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `automation.enabled`: Enable the automation subsystem (durable routines, schedule evaluation, run history). Default on: with no routines defined it idles and surfaces a how-to-create-your-first-routine empty state.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

### batch

- `batch.fallback`: What a batch job does when its provider has no Batch API: live runs the request once, now, as an ordinary request and answers the job already finished; fail refuses the job. A job that asks for a live execution mode is refused either way: the batch API only queues.
  - type `enum`; default `"live"`; allowed: `live`, `fail`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `batch.maxDelayMs`: Maximum time a queued local batch job should wait before the daemon submits its provider batch.
  - type `number`; default `300000`; allowed: integer in [0, 86400000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `batch.maxJobsPerProviderBatch`: Maximum platform jobs grouped into a single upstream provider batch submission.
  - type `number`; default `100`; allowed: integer in [1, 100000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `batch.maxQueueMessagesPerDay`: Daily Cloudflare queue message budget, enforced by the provisioned Worker (its Durable Object coordinator counts per UTC day): past it, the Worker answers 429 QUEUE_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED with the use so far and when it resets, and nothing more is queued. 0 means no limit. Takes effect at the next /cloudflare provision.
  - type `number`; default `1000`; allowed: integer in [0, 10000000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `batch.maxQueuePayloadBytes`: Maximum Cloudflare queue message payload size in bytes; a larger cloudflare-queue job is refused (HTTP 413). Queue messages should be signals, not full prompt archives.
  - type `number`; default `16384`; allowed: integer in [1024, 131072].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `batch.mode`: Daemon provider Batch API mode. off: nothing is queued (the batch job API refuses with BATCH_DISABLED). explicit: the batch job API is open, and a non-streaming OpenAI-compatible chat completion is queued when it sends x-goodvibes-execution: batch. eligible-by-default: every non-streaming OpenAI-compatible chat completion whose provider has a Batch API is queued unless it sends x-goodvibes-execution: live (one whose provider cannot batch runs live as usual; batch.fallback applies only to an explicit batch request); a queued one is answered 202 with the job id and read back at <pathPrefix>/chat/completions/<id>. Streaming requests and terminal, companion and web chat always run live.
  - type `enum`; default `"off"`; allowed: `off`, `explicit`, `eligible-by-default`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `batch.queueBackend`: Queue backend for daemon batch signals. local stores jobs under the daemon config directory; cloudflare sends them through the provisioned Worker's queue. /cloudflare provision switches this to cloudflare only after the Worker reaches the daemon.
  - type `enum`; default `"local"`; allowed: `local`, `cloudflare`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `batch.tickIntervalMs`: Daemon-local batch scheduler tick interval in milliseconds. Read once when the scheduler starts: a new value applies after the next restart.
  - type `number`; default `60000`; allowed: integer in [5000, 3600000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

### browser

- `browser.network.pinned`: Off (default): the browser checks each host a page asks for (resolved once per browser context) and lets the browser connect itself, which is fastest but lets a name that answers differently a moment later (DNS rebinding) reach an address the check refused. On: every request a page makes is fetched by GoodVibes through the address that was checked, redirects are checked hop by hop, and the answer is handed to the page, so a name that re-resolves to a private or metadata address after the check is never reached. Costs a copy of every response through this process. Turn it on when browsing sites you do not trust from a machine on a private network. Applies to browser sessions started after the change.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

### calendar

- `calendar.google.clientId`: The OAuth client id for a Google Calendar app registered by whoever set up this environment. Client ids are not secrets (RFC 8252) and are stored in plain config.
  - type `string`; default `""`.

  - A project file may not set it.

- `calendar.google.clientSecretRef`: A reference into the secret store naming the Google OAuth client secret, needed only for a confidential (Web-app) client registration, a Desktop-app client using PKCE needs none. Any non-empty value marks the secret as stored; it is always read from the name derived from this setting's key, not from where the reference text points. The secret itself is stored in the daemon secret tier, never in config.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a credential: the settings file holds only a `goodvibes://secrets/...` reference to it.

- `calendar.google.icsUrl`: A reference into the secret store naming the private calendar feed address (the "secret address in iCal format" from Google Calendar's Integrate Calendar settings). It is a URL rather than a password, but it grants read access to the operator's calendar to anyone holding it, so it is treated as a credential: the address itself is stored in the daemon secret tier, never in config. This is the read-only, credential-free route used when an app password is the mail connection, Google refuses Basic authentication on its CalDAV endpoint, so an app password cannot reach Calendar that way. Calendar writes require the OAuth path (calendar.google.clientId and the refresh token below).
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a credential: the settings file holds only a `goodvibes://secrets/...` reference to it.

- `calendar.microsoft.clientId`: The OAuth client id for a Microsoft Entra app registration, for connecting an Outlook calendar. Client ids are not secrets and are stored in plain config.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `calendar.microsoft.clientSecretRef`: A reference into the secret store naming the Microsoft OAuth client secret, needed only for a confidential registration, a public client with "Allow public client flows" enabled needs none. Any non-empty value marks the secret as stored; it is always read from the name derived from this setting's key, not from where the reference text points. The secret itself is stored in the daemon secret tier, never in config.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a credential: the settings file holds only a `goodvibes://secrets/...` reference to it.

  - A project file may not set it.

- `cloudflare.kvNamespaceName`: Cloudflare KV namespace that records each queued job's delivery state (queued, delivered with the daemon job id, rejected), served by the Worker at /batch/queue/jobs/<id>, so a redelivered message is acknowledged without a second daemon call.
  - type `string`; default `"goodvibes-runtime"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cloudflare.maxQueueOpsPerDay`: Daily Cloudflare queue operation budget, enforced by the provisioned Worker (its Durable Object coordinator counts per UTC day): past it, the Worker answers 429 QUEUE_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED with the use so far and when it resets. 0 means no limit. Takes effect at the next /cloudflare provision.
  - type `number`; default `10000`; allowed: integer in [0, 10000000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cloudflare.queueName`: Cloudflare Queue binding/name for GoodVibes batch job signals.
  - type `string`; default `"goodvibes-batch"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cloudflare.r2BucketName`: Cloudflare R2 bucket that holds queued job bodies so queue messages carry only their key; a body is deleted once the daemon has the job.
  - type `string`; default `"goodvibes-artifacts"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cloudflare.secretsStoreId`: Cloudflare Secrets Store id selected or created by GoodVibes provisioning.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cloudflare.secretsStoreName`: Name of the Cloudflare Secrets Store that optional GoodVibes provisioning creates and manages (the store holds the secrets; this is its name)
  - type `string`; default `"goodvibes"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cloudflare.tunnelId`: Cloudflare Zero Trust Tunnel id selected or created by GoodVibes provisioning.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cloudflare.tunnelName`: Zero Trust Tunnel name managed by GoodVibes provisioning when tunnel integration is enabled.
  - type `string`; default `"goodvibes-daemon"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cloudflare.tunnelTokenRef`: GoodVibes secret reference for the cloudflared tunnel token generated by provisioning.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a credential: the settings file holds only a `goodvibes://secrets/...` reference to it.

- `cloudflare.workerBaseUrl`: Optional deployed GoodVibes Cloudflare Worker base URL used by clients that proxy batch signals through Workers.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cloudflare.workerClientTokenRef`: Optional GoodVibes secret reference for the bearer token clients use when calling the Cloudflare Worker.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a credential: the settings file holds only a `goodvibes://secrets/...` reference to it.

- `cloudflare.workerCron`: Cron trigger installed on the GoodVibes Cloudflare Worker for batch scheduler ticks.
  - type `string`; default `"*/5 * * * *"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cloudflare.workerHostname`: Optional custom hostname for the GoodVibes Cloudflare Worker when DNS automation is enabled.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cloudflare.workerName`: Cloudflare Worker script name managed by GoodVibes provisioning.
  - type `string`; default `"goodvibes-batch-worker"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cloudflare.workerSubdomain`: Cloudflare account workers.dev subdomain used to infer cloudflare.workerBaseUrl.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).

- `cloudflare.workerTokenRef`: Optional GoodVibes secret reference for the Worker-to-daemon bearer token.
  - type `string`; default `""`.

- `cloudflare.zoneId`: Optional Cloudflare zone id selected for platform-managed DNS and Zero Trust Access hostnames.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
