### cluster

- `cluster.beaconSeconds`: How often this machine advertises its group on the local network, in seconds. The advertisement carries the group's id, its name, how many machines are in it and this build's version, and nothing else. It is what lets a new machine running `cluster join` see the group and pick it from a list. Lower means a new machine finds the group faster; higher means slightly less traffic. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `15`; allowed: integer in [5, 3600].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cluster.bootProbeSeconds`: How long a starting node listens for an existing responsible node before claiming the role itself, in seconds. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `3`; allowed: integer in [1, 300].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cluster.enabled`: Let this machine share inbound channel work with your OTHER goodvibes machines on this network, so exactly one of them reads each inbox (Telegram polling, ntfy subscriptions, inbox pollers) instead of all of them answering the same message. For a homelab where you run goodvibes on several machines that are all yours and configured with the same surfaces: switch it on everywhere and they sort it out between themselves, including taking over at once when one is shut down normally, and within about 20 seconds when one crashes (cluster.masterTimeoutSeconds, 15 by default, plus a short election). Off by default because switching it on asserts that every goodvibes node on this network belongs to you, on a shared network (an office, a shared house) a stranger's node would join the same coordination and one of you would stop receiving messages with nothing to indicate why. Outbound sends, sessions and the control plane are unaffected either way.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cluster.heartbeatSeconds`: How often the responsible node tells the others it is still alive, in seconds. Lower means slightly faster notice that a node is alive and more network chatter; it does not by itself shorten a crash takeover, which waits for cluster.masterTimeoutSeconds. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `5`; allowed: integer in [1, 3600].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cluster.keyRotationGraceMinutes`: How long both the new and the previous internal group key are accepted around a rotation, in minutes. This exists so that machines which have not yet picked up the new key are still heard while they catch up, without it, a rotation would look like every other machine going silent at once, and the group would needlessly hand work around. Raise it if your machines are often asleep or on a flaky link. It does NOT apply when you remove a machine: that rotation takes effect at once, which is the point of it. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `5`; allowed: integer in [1, 120].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cluster.keyRotationHours`: How often the group replaces the internal key it signs coordination messages with, in hours. This is NOT the join key you type when adding a machine, that one is stable and changes only when you change it. This key rotates by itself, is never shown to you, and rotating it limits how long a copy taken off an old disk or a backup would be accepted. Lower means a shorter window and a little more network traffic once per rotation; the changeover never interrupts anything, because both the new key and the previous one are accepted for a few minutes either side of it. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `24`; allowed: integer in [1, 8760].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cluster.masterTimeoutSeconds`: How long a standby node waits without a heartbeat before it decides the responsible node has crashed and holds an election, in seconds. This is the CRASH path only: a node shut down normally hands over immediately, so ordinary restarts never wait this out. Used as at least two heartbeats: a value below that is raised to two heartbeats at runtime. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `15`; allowed: integer in [2, 86400].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cluster.multicastGroup`: IPv4 multicast group the nodes coordinate over. The default sits in the administratively-scoped range (239.0.0.0/8), which routers do not forward off the local network. Every node that should coordinate must share this value. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `string`; default `"239.255.71.86"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cluster.nodeName`: A name for THIS machine in the group's member list (`cluster nodes` and the web UI), such as "desktop" or "laptop", so you can tell the machines apart when removing one or reading which machine holds a surface. Up to 48 characters. Empty, the default, shows "machine" and the first 8 characters of its node id; the hostname is never used, because the member list replicates and the group is advertised on the network. Kept on this machine only. Other machines record the name this machine had when it created or joined the group. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `string`; default `""`; allowed: up to 48 characters.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cluster.peers`: Static list of cluster peers (host or host:port) contacted directly as well as over multicast. Set it on a network that drops multicast, so the nodes still find each other.
  - type `array`; default `[]`; allowed: list of host or host:port strings, for example ["10.0.0.2", "10.0.0.3:4000"].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cluster.port`: UDP port used for node-to-node coordination on the local network. Every node that should coordinate must share this port. Change it only to avoid a collision with something else on your network. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `61860`; allowed: integer port in [1, 65535]; a port this machine listens on.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cluster.revocationRetentionMinutes`: How long a removed or revoked entry (a deleted schedule, a revoked device token, user, grant or peer) is kept on the group's record before it is dropped, in minutes; 43200 (30 days) by default. A machine that has not heard the group for longer than this, or has never synced with the group it is in, takes the group's record as the truth when it returns: what the group no longer holds is dropped on that machine, not brought back, unless that machine made it after it last synced, and `cluster status` lists what was dropped. It must span four gossip rounds: at least 4 x cluster.rosterGossipSeconds (counted as 30 when lower), in minutes rounded up, so 4 with the default gossip; a lower value is refused naming the minimum, and one in a hand-edited file is raised to it. Set the same value on every machine.
  - type `number`; default `43200`; allowed: integer in [1, 525600].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cluster.rosterGossipSeconds`: How often this machine tells the others which revision of the group's shared settings and of its record (members, removals, key generations, devices, users) it holds, in seconds. A change is sent to every machine when it is made; this is how a machine that missed one (a lost message, or switched off at the time) notices and takes it. Checked on a 30 second timer, so any value below 30 behaves as 30. Higher means a missed change settles more slowly. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `60`; allowed: integer in [10, 3600].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `cluster.secret`: Optional shared phrase for coordinating machines that are not in a group (no `cluster create` or `cluster join`). When set, their coordination messages are signed with it and any message that does not verify is ignored, so only nodes that know the phrase can take the responsible role; every such node must use the same value. When it names a stored secret that cannot be read, this machine sends and takes no coordination messages at all until it can (rather than run unsigned), and `cluster status` says election traffic is unavailable. Inside a group it is not used: the group key signs every coordination message.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a credential: the settings file holds only a `goodvibes://secrets/...` reference to it.

### contract

- `contract.acceptanceStakes`: How strong a reading must be before a criterion counts as met: high (default) or critical (the strictest declared pass band)
  - type `enum`; default `"high"`; allowed: `high`, `critical`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.autoCommit`: Commit the deliverable when a contract passes: worktree mode merges the contract branch, shared mode commits the paths the contract touched.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.commitScope`: What a passing contract commits: off (never commit; the work is left as uncommitted changes), scoped (only the contract's own changes, default), all (the whole working tree in shared mode)
  - type `enum`; default `"scoped"`; allowed: `off`, `scoped`, `all`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.defaultAttempts`: Independent attempts per unit when the request does not ask for several; above 1, the best passing attempt is selected.
  - type `number`; default `1`; allowed: integer in [1, 5].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.evidenceNudgeLimit`: Consecutive checks where the work does not show a criterion is met before the owner is asked to confirm; 0 disables this limit.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: integer in [0, 9007199254740991].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.gateTimeoutMs`: Timeout in ms for each quality gate command and for a /test run (default 15 minutes); a gate past it is stopped and reported unverified; 0 runs until completion or cancellation.
  - type `number`; default `900000`; allowed: integer in [0, 2147483647].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.gates`: Quality gates a contract runs before it reports work done: each is { name, command, enabled } with optional required and verification. Any gate passes or fails on its command's exit code. A list with a gate that cannot run is refused when saved.
  - type `array`; default `[{"name":"typecheck","command":"npx tsc --noEmit","enabled":false},{"name":"lint","command":"npx eslint . --max-warnings 0","enabled":false},{"name":"build","command":"npm run build","enabled":false}]`; allowed: list of { name, command, enabled } objects with optional required (true or false) and verification ("command" or "assertions"); each name once, and an enabled gate needs a command.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `contract.heartbeatTimeoutMs`: Silence in ms after which a running unit agent is restarted once, then failed. An exec command within its own timeout_ms, or without one, is not silence. 0 = off.
  - type `number`; default `600000`; allowed: finite number >= 0.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.isolation`: Where contract work runs: auto (a git worktree when the project is a git repository with a commit, otherwise the shared tree), worktree, or shared.
  - type `enum`; default `"auto"`; allowed: `auto`, `worktree`, `shared`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.judgmentCallBudget`: Decision-model calls one contract may spend on its checks, plans and corrections; once spent, the next correction goes to the owner with what was spent and what is still unmet instead of another fix round. 0 disables this budget.
  - type `number`; default `400`; allowed: integer in [0, 9007199254740991].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.maxActiveContracts`: Contracts that may run at once; further contracts wait in a queue.
  - type `number`; default `6`; allowed: integer in [1, 64].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.maxFixRounds`: Planned-fix rounds plus fresh agents for one unit, group or deliverable before the owner decides; 0 disables this limit.
  - type `number`; default `3`; allowed: integer in [0, 9007199254740991].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.maxNudgesPerUnit`: The most corrections one unit receives before it is treated as stalled; 0 disables this limit.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: integer in [0, 9007199254740991].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.maxParallelUnits`: Units of one group that may run at once in worktree mode (shared mode always runs one)
  - type `number`; default `64`; allowed: integer in [1, 256].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.maxUnits`: The most units one contract plan may hold; 0 disables this limit.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: integer in [0, 9007199254740991].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.midRunChecks`: Check a unit's work at the end of each turn that changed files, not only when the unit agent tries to finish.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.nudgeTtlMs`: How long in ms a correction sent to a running unit agent waits to be read before it expires.
  - type `number`; default `300000`; allowed: integer in [1000, 3600000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.planRepairLimit`: Times the planner is asked to repair a plan that fails its checks before the owner decides; 0 disables this limit (planning then stops only when the same problem comes back)
  - type `number`; default `3`; allowed: integer in [0, 9007199254740991].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.stallLimit`: Consecutive checks without progress that mark a unit as stalled and hand it to correction; 0 disables this limit.
  - type `number`; default `3`; allowed: integer in [0, 9007199254740991].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.transportRetryDelayMs`: Wait in ms before the first restart of a unit after a transient failure; it doubles for each further restart (at most 60000). A Retry-After the provider sent is used instead.
  - type `number`; default `5000`; allowed: number in [0, 60000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `contract.transportRetryLimit`: How many times a unit whose agent failed on a transient error (a 5xx, 408 or 429 answer, a connection error, or a failure nothing could classify while the decision model is unavailable) is restarted with a fresh agent before the contract fails. 0 disables the retry.
  - type `number`; default `3`; allowed: number in [0, 5].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

### controlPlane

- `controlPlane.cors.allowedOrigins`: Comma-separated explicit allowlist of browser origins permitted to make cross-origin requests when controlPlane.cors.enabled is true (e.g. http://localhost:5173). Empty refuses every cross-origin request. The WebSocket upgrade origin check reads this list on its own, whether or not controlPlane.cors.enabled is true.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `controlPlane.cors.enabled`: Answer OPTIONS preflight and emit Access-Control-Allow-* headers for allowlisted origins (opt-in; off by default). Never wildcards; credentials are allowlist-gated.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `controlPlane.enabled`: Whether the control plane is served to other machines. Off (default): the daemon listener answers only requests from this machine (loopback or one of its own addresses), whatever controlPlane.hostMode binds, and refuses any other address with CONTROL_PLANE_LOCAL_ONLY naming this setting. On: every address the binding reaches is served (paired devices, the web UI from another device, a reverse proxy). Channel webhooks under /webhook/ are answered either way; each surface's own switch decides them. Takes effect on the next request; the outbound relay has its own switch (relay.enabled). goodvibes-daemon webui enable --lan turns it on with the network binding.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `controlPlane.gateway`: The shared gateway/control-plane host serving state snapshots, live streams (SSE/WS), and authenticated control APIs to terminal hosts and remote clients. Default on so a stock daemon can stream companion chat; every streaming endpoint stays auth-gated and the default bind stays loopback. Turn off for a request/response-only daemon.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `controlPlane.host`: Bind host for the control-plane HTTP server, used when controlPlane.hostMode is custom.
  - type `string`; default `"127.0.0.1"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `controlPlane.hostMode`: Network binding mode for the control-plane listener: local (127.0.0.1, default port), network (0.0.0.0, default port), custom (the host and port below). This and host decide what the listener binds; whether another machine is then served is controlPlane.enabled.
  - type `enum`; default `"local"`; allowed: `local`, `network`, `custom`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `controlPlane.openaiCompatible.enabled`: Expose OpenAI-compatible /v1/models and /v1/chat/completions routes on the authenticated daemon.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `controlPlane.openaiCompatible.pathPrefix`: Path prefix for the daemon OpenAI-compatible routes.
  - type `string`; default `"/v1"`; allowed: a path such as /v1: segments of letters, digits, . _ ~ -, with no trailing slash and not just /.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `controlPlane.port`: Bind port for the control-plane HTTP server.
  - type `number`; default `3421`; allowed: integer port in [1, 65535]; a port this machine listens on.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `controlPlane.publicBaseUrl`: Override for a genuinely external control-plane address (tunnel or reverse proxy). Leave empty, the everyday base URL is derived from hostMode/host/port/tls.mode, so it cannot drift. Set this only when an off-box address differs from the bind.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `controlPlane.streamMode`: Which live update stream the daemon listener serves: sse serves GET /api/control-plane/events only, websocket serves the /api/control-plane/ws upgrade only, both serves both. The other one is refused with STREAM_MODE_NOT_SERVED naming this setting. The terminal apps and the web UI read the Server-Sent Events stream, so websocket alone leaves them without live updates. Takes effect on the next request.
  - type `enum`; default `"sse"`; allowed: `sse`, `websocket`, `both`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `controlPlane.tls.certFile`: Certificate chain PEM path for direct control-plane TLS (empty = certs/fullchain.pem under this surface's settings directory, e.g. ~/.goodvibes/tui/certs/fullchain.pem for the terminal app and the daemon)
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `controlPlane.tls.keyFile`: Filesystem pathname of the PEM file used for direct control-plane TLS. This setting stores a path, not the private key contents. Empty uses certs/privkey.pem under this surface's settings directory (e.g. ~/.goodvibes/tui/certs/privkey.pem for the terminal app and the daemon).
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `controlPlane.tls.mode`: TLS mode for the control-plane HTTP server.
  - type `enum`; default `"off"`; allowed: `off`, `proxy`, `direct`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `controlPlane.trustProxy`: Trust proxy forwarding headers such as x-forwarded-for for the control plane.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would open a listener, a remote entry point or local fetching counts as loosening security.

- `controlPlane.webui.bundleDir`: Directory holding the built web UI bundle (index.html + assets) served when controlPlane.webui.serve is true. Takes precedence over web.staticAssetsDir: this key is the specific answer for this daemon, so when it names a directory that is the one served. Empty falls back to web.staticAssetsDir.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `controlPlane.webui.serve`: Serve a built web UI bundle same-origin from the daemon (opt-in; loopback default unchanged). The bundle is public and the app token-authenticates its own API calls.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

### conversationGate

- `conversationGate.gatedSurfaces`: Channel surfaces whose inbound messages pass the conversation gate before a session sees them.
  - type `array`; default `["ntfy","telegram","slack","discord","homeassistant","google-chat","signal","whatsapp","telephony","imessage","msteams","bluebubbles","mattermost","matrix"]`; allowed: list of surface names, for example ["slack", "telegram"].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `conversationGate.maxPendingProposals`: Maximum work proposals awaiting an answer at once across all channels. The oldest is dropped past this cap. Between 1 and 200.
  - type `number`; default `20`; allowed: integer in [1, 200].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `conversationGate.mode`: How inbound channel messages are treated. propose (default): a message gets a conversational reply, and anything that reads as a work request is proposed and waits for your agreement over the same channel. confirm-all: every inbound message is confirmed before any agent runs. off: an inbound message starts work immediately (pre-1.14 behavior). Never applies to goodvibes-tui, and never to already-authorized work such as schedules, triggers, and on-exit chains.
  - type `enum`; default `"propose"`; allowed: `propose`, `confirm-all`, `off`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `conversationGate.proposalTtlMs`: How long an unanswered work proposal stays answerable, in milliseconds. After this it expires and a late reply is reported as expired rather than starting stale work. Between 1 minute and 24 hours.
  - type `number`; default `1800000`; allowed: integer in [60000, 86400000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

### daemon

- `daemon.connectedHost.enabled`: Whether this surface may DIAL the daemon it is connected to. On (the default), the features that reach a connected host work: the session-inputs poll that delivers inbound messages, conversation rewind registration, the live approvals stream, daemon-routed conversation turns, and the operator verbs. Off, each of those refuses plainly rather than failing at a connection. This is separate from daemon.enabled on purpose: adopting a daemon of your own and talking to one that is already there are different decisions, and while they shared a single key, turning adoption off silently stopped the inputs poll, the approvals stream and rewind registration on machines whose connected host was live and answering, the session and memory spines kept dialing the same host perfectly well, which is how the split showed itself.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `daemon.connectedHost.url`: Where the terminal (goodvibes) dials its daemon, as an origin such as http://10.0.0.7:3421. Empty (the default) means the daemon on this machine, at the address derived from controlPlane.hostMode, controlPlane.host and controlPlane.port; those settings describe only how a local daemon listens. Setup's "Connect to an existing daemon" writes this, so finishing setup or changing the local bind does not move the terminal off the daemon it connected to. Clear it to go back to the daemon on this machine.
  - type `string`; default `""`; allowed: empty, or an http(s) origin with no path, user name or password, e.g. http://10.0.0.7:3421.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `daemon.enabled`: Whether THIS surface ADOPTS a session daemon of its own, the background service hosting the shared session broker and companion chat, bound to loopback (127.0.0.1). On (the default), the surface looks for one and adopts it. Off, it makes no adoption attempt and probes no port. It does not control the daemon process itself: a daemon started on its own runs regardless of this setting, which is a per-surface choice about adopting one. It is also NOT the switch for talking to a daemon this surface is already connected to, that is daemon.connectedHost.enabled, and the two were one key until they were split apart.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `daemon.timezone`: IANA timezone name the daemon reckons CALENDAR DAYS in, e.g. 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London'. Empty means UTC. This is the daemon's own location, not a display preference and not a per-schedule zone (schedules keep their own). Anything that resets daily reads it: the payment capability's daily budgets roll over at midnight in this zone. Changing it does not refill a spent budget: each spend keeps the day it was made on and counts until that day is over, and an agent cannot change it in a way that moves today; only the owner can.
  - type `string`; default `""`; allowed: empty (UTC) or an IANA timezone name like 'America/New_York'.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would move the day your daily spending limits are counted in counts as loosening security.

### danger

- `danger.httpListener`: Enable HTTP webhook listener for receiving external events.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would open a listener, a remote entry point or local fetching counts as loosening security.

### device

- `device.capabilities.allowAlwaysOffer`: Which capabilities may offer a durable "always allow" on their confirmation prompt. every-capability (stock): all of them, front camera, screen capture, precise location, and clipboard included. standard-only: the elevated ones (front camera, screen capture, precise location, clipboard read) still ask every time and never offer a grant, while everyday ones can be granted. never: no durable grant is ever offered anywhere; existing grants stop being honoured.
  - type `enum`; default `"every-capability"`; allowed: `every-capability`, `standard-only`, `never`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `device.capabilities.mode`: How a paired phone's camera, screen, location, clipboard, and device commands are reached. honor-grants (stock): every capability asks the first time and every time after, unless you chose "always allow" for that one capability on that one phone. ask-every-time: the prompt appears on every single request, permissions.mode yolo included, and no durable grant is ever consulted or offered, use it when someone else is holding the phone. off: no capability request reaches any paired device at all.
  - type `enum`; default `"honor-grants"`; allowed: `off`, `ask-every-time`, `honor-grants`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `device.capabilities.requestTimeoutSeconds`: How long the agent waits for a phone to answer one capability request before giving up. A phone that is asleep or off the network usually answers within a few seconds of waking; a long timeout keeps a slow wake from failing, a short one keeps the agent from stalling.
  - type `number`; default `60`; allowed: integer in [5, 600].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `device.capture.maxArtifacts`: How many captures are kept at once across all paired phones. The count is enforced when housekeeping runs (see device.capture.sweepIntervalMinutes): then the oldest past it are deleted even while inside the retention window. A burst of captures can exceed it until the next sweep.
  - type `number`; default `200`; allowed: integer in [1, 5000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `device.capture.retentionHours`: How long a picture taken by the phone's camera or screen capture is kept before it is deleted and the deletion recorded. Stock is 24 hours: long enough for the work the picture was taken for, short enough that a photo of your desk is not still on disk next week.
  - type `number`; default `24`; allowed: integer in [1, 720].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `device.capture.sweepIntervalMinutes`: How often housekeeping runs over stored captures and grants while the runtime is up. A sweep also runs at every start; this interval is what keeps a long-running daemon from going days without one. Each sweep writes what it removed and why.
  - type `number`; default `30`; allowed: integer in [1, 1440].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `device.clipboard.readMode`: Whether the agent can read what is on the phone's clipboard. grantable (stock): it asks every time and offers "always allow", like every other capability. ask-only: it asks every time, permissions.mode yolo included, and neither offers nor honours a durable grant. off: clipboard reads are refused; putting text ON the clipboard is unaffected.
  - type `enum`; default `"grantable"`; allowed: `off`, `ask-only`, `grantable`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `device.grants.auditRetentionDays`: How long the grants ledger keeps its record of grants given, used, revoked, and expired. This is what the grants surface shows you when you ask what a phone has been allowed to do and when.
  - type `number`; default `30`; allowed: integer in [1, 365].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `device.grants.expiryDays`: How long an "always allow" grant lasts before it expires and the capability starts asking again. Nothing is granted forever: an expired grant is removed by housekeeping and is never honoured in the meantime.
  - type `number`; default `90`; allowed: integer in [1, 3650].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `device.grants.maxPerNode`: How many "always allow" grants one phone may hold at once. Past this count the oldest grants for that phone are removed, so a paired device cannot accumulate authority indefinitely.
  - type `number`; default `64`; allowed: integer in [1, 512].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `device.location.precision`: How exact a location the phone will report. precise-grantable (stock): both approximate and street-level fixes are available, and either may be granted durably. ask-precise: street-level fixes are available but always ask, permissions.mode yolo included, and neither offer nor honour "always allow". coarse-only: street-level fixes are refused entirely; only city-scale approximate location is served.
  - type `enum`; default `"precise-grantable"`; allowed: `coarse-only`, `ask-precise`, `precise-grantable`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `device.nodes.maxPaired`: How many phones may be paired as device nodes at once. Each paired phone is a separate identity with its own grants; this bounds how many can be outstanding before an old one has to be unpaired.
  - type `number`; default `8`; allowed: integer in [1, 64].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

### diagnostics

- `diagnostics.postEdit`: Post-edit diagnostics: after a successful file write/edit, append cheap, in-process syntax diagnostics (errors only) for the touched file to the tool result so the model sees a broken edit immediately. on (default): run the tree-sitter syntax provider when a TS/JS project context is detectable (no process spawn, no type checking). off: never append diagnostics.
  - type `enum`; default `"on"`; allowed: `on`, `off`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

### fetch

- `fetch.allowLocalhost`: Allow the fetch tool to reach localhost/loopback dev servers (e.g. http://localhost:3000) in every project. Set by approving the localhost fetch ask and saved in your own settings, so it never re-asks; a project settings file cannot turn it on. Private-IP blocking is governed by fetch.allowedPrivateHosts; cloud-metadata blocking is absolute.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would open a listener, a remote entry point or local fetching counts as loosening security.

- `fetch.allowedPrivateHosts`: Comma-separated private-network hosts the fetch tool and the browser may reach: a LAN device (192.168.1.20), a container (172.17.0.2), a VPN peer (100.101.102.103), or a name that resolves to one (nas.lan). Patterns match as in fetch.trustedHosts. For the fetch tool it applies only to the host a call writes, never to a redirect target; the browser holds every request a page makes (navigation, redirect, frame, subresource, WebSocket) to it, and asks the owner before opening any other private or loopback address for a page. Cloud-metadata, link-local, loopback (see fetch.allowLocalhost) and other reserved addresses stay refused. A call in YOLO mode, or one the owner admitted, may also reach a private address written as an IP without this list. Your own settings only: a project settings file cannot set it.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would let fetch reach a private-network host counts as loosening security.

- `fetch.blockedHosts`: Comma-separated default blocked hosts for fetch trust-tier classification. Blocked hosts are always refused regardless of sanitize mode or permission mode. Per-call blocked_hosts are added on top of this default. Patterns match as in fetch.trustedHosts (* one label, ** across dots, * or ** alone every host), and a.example.com. is the same host as a.example.com. The built-in SSRF-risk block (private, link-local, metadata and other non-public addresses, and encoded IP forms) applies independently of this list, in every mode.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would remove a host from the fetch block list counts as loosening security.

- `fetch.sanitizeMode`: Default response sanitization mode applied by the fetch tool when the per-call sanitize_mode is omitted: none (no content sanitization), safe-text (strip active/script content, default), or strict (aggressive text-only reduction). A per-call sanitize_mode always overrides this default. Private-IP and cloud-metadata host blocking applies regardless of mode.
  - type `enum`; default `"safe-text"`; allowed: `none`, `safe-text`, `strict`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `fetch.trustedHosts`: Comma-separated trusted hosts for fetch sanitization/trust-tier classification (e.g. docs.example.com, *.internal.example.com). Trusted hosts relax sanitization. This list is the only source of trust: a fetch call cannot add to it. Empty means no host is trusted. In a pattern * matches one name label and ** matches across dots; an entry that is only * or ** matches every host. Hosts are compared lower-case, without a trailing dot, in their ASCII (punycode) form.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

### fleet

Externally-launched agents merely observed on the host never count. Renamed from orchestration.maxActiveAgents.
  - type `number`; default `8`; allowed: number in [1, 20].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

An app left in "Testing" is issued refresh tokens that expire after seven days; moving it to "In production" (self-certified, no Google review needed) removes that expiry. Empty until a setup or verification run has read it.
  - type `string`; default `""`.

### hostedSessions

- `hostedSessions.attachmentTtlMs`: How long a client stays attached to a daemon-hosted session without renewing, in milliseconds. Attaching again renews it, and a client whose control-plane connection is still open renews automatically. A client that crashed or closed its tab never detaches, so without this its attachment stands forever and a kill-policy session waits for a departure that never comes. When the last attachment lapses the session is treated as detached, and hostedSessions.detachPolicy decides what happens next. Between 30 seconds and a day.
  - type `number`; default `600000`; allowed: integer in [30000, 86400000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `hostedSessions.detachPolicy`: What happens to a daemon-hosted session when its last client detaches. kill (default): the session ends, which is what closing a client has always done. survive: the session stays alive and reattachable, so work continues while nothing is watching and you can pick it up again from any surface. A single session can override this when it is created.
  - type `enum`; default `"kill"`; allowed: `kill`, `survive`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `hostedSessions.maxMessagesPerSession`: How many of a hosted session's most recent messages are written to disk. The transcript in memory is unaffected; this bounds what a restart can restore, so one long conversation cannot grow its file without limit.
  - type `number`; default `500`; allowed: integer in [1, 100000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `hostedSessions.maxSessions`: How many daemon-hosted sessions may be live at once. Creating one past this is refused with the count and this setting named, rather than accepted and starved. Terminated sessions do not count.
  - type `number`; default `8`; allowed: integer in [1, 1000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `hostedSessions.promoteInboundConversations`: Hand inbound channel conversations to the daemon to host, instead of answering them inside the surface process that received them. Off (default): a message from Telegram, Slack, email or any other channel is answered by that process, and it stops when the process stops. On: the first message of a conversation creates a daemon-hosted session and every later message is steered into it, so the conversation keeps its context and keeps running while no surface is open. What happens when the last client leaves is still hostedSessions.detachPolicy.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `hostedSessions.routeConversationTurns`: Only goodvibes-agent reads this; the terminal product (goodvibes) always runs turns in its own process. Off (the default): the agent's conversation turns run in the agent process, with the agent's own prompt, persona, skills, memory and tools; work that must outlive the terminal goes to the daemon through /work, channels and schedules. On: with a connected daemon reachable, the first message of a conversation creates a daemon-hosted session rooted at this surface's working directory and every later message is steered into it, so the turn survives this process closing; that hosted turn is still an Agent turn, with the agent's operator policy, persona, skills, routines, memory and its profile, occasions, artifact, document, research-run, research-source, review-packet, media, notify and work-plan tools, while the agent tools that run only in this process are named to the model and refused there. With no connected daemon reachable the turn runs locally regardless, and the transcript says so in one line naming the reason.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `hostedSessions.terminatedRetentionMs`: How long a terminated hosted session's record and transcript are kept before they are retired, in milliseconds. Until then the session is still listable with its termination reason, and its transcript (its reply included) stays readable with sessions.hosted.history by the client that created it, also after a daemon restart.
  - type `number`; default `86400000`; allowed: integer in [0, 31536000000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

### httpListener

- `httpListener.host`: Bind host for the webhook HTTP listener.
  - type `string`; default `"127.0.0.1"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `httpListener.hostMode`: Network binding mode: local (127.0.0.1, default port), network (0.0.0.0, default port), custom (editable host and port)
  - type `enum`; default `"local"`; allowed: `local`, `network`, `custom`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `httpListener.port`: Bind port for the webhook HTTP listener.
  - type `number`; default `3422`; allowed: integer port in [1, 65535]; a port this machine listens on.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `httpListener.tls.certFile`: Certificate chain PEM path for direct webhook-listener TLS (empty = certs/fullchain.pem under this surface's settings directory)
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `httpListener.tls.keyFile`: Private key PEM path for direct webhook-listener TLS (empty = certs/privkey.pem under this surface's settings directory)
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `httpListener.tls.mode`: TLS mode for the webhook HTTP listener.
  - type `enum`; default `"off"`; allowed: `off`, `proxy`, `direct`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `httpListener.trustCloudflare`: Read the real client IP from CF-Connecting-IP, and only when the connecting peer is inside a published Cloudflare range. Requires httpListener.trustProxy: with it off, CF-Connecting-IP is ignored no matter what this says. The range check is the point, without it any peer could send a CF-Connecting-IP header and choose which address the rate limiter and the audit log recorded. Leave off unless this listener genuinely sits behind Cloudflare.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `httpListener.trustProxy`: Trust proxy forwarding headers such as x-forwarded-for for the webhook listener.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

### integrations

- `integrations.delivery.initialDelayMs`: Initial exponential-backoff delay (ms) between integration delivery retries. Delay grows as initialDelayMs * 2^(attempt-1) with jitter, capped at integrations.delivery.maxDelayMs.
  - type `number`; default `1000`; allowed: integer in [0, 3600000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `integrations.delivery.maxDelayMs`: Upper cap (ms) on the exponential-backoff delay between integration delivery retries.
  - type `number`; default `30000`; allowed: integer in [0, 86400000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `integrations.delivery.maxDlqSize`: Maximum entries retained in the integration delivery dead-letter queue; oldest entries are evicted first past this size.
  - type `number`; default `500`; allowed: integer in [1, 100000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `integrations.delivery.maxRetries`: Maximum retry attempts for a retryable integration delivery (Slack/Discord/webhook) before it moves to the dead-letter queue. A per-queue maxRetries option overrides this default.
  - type `number`; default `3`; allowed: integer in [0, 100].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `integrations.delivery.sloEnforced`: Enforce delivery service-level objectives for channel integrations: failures are classified retryable/terminal, retried with exponential backoff, and dead-letter events are logged at error level and surfaced in integration diagnostics; failed webhook notifications are listed with /notify failed and sent again with /notify resend <id|all>. When false, dead letters are warn-level only. An explicit per-queue sloEnforced option still overrides this default.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `integrations.deliveryTracking`: Track integration deliveries first-class: retries, dead letters, and per-surface delivery outcomes. Default on; it is inert until a channel surface is configured.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `integrations.routeBinding`: Durably bind and resolve external conversation routes, thread contexts, and reply targets across channel surfaces. Default on; it is inert until a channel surface is configured.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

### judgment

- `judgment.backend`: Optional adapter (system-one, cloudflare-workers-ai or laya), maxInputBytes, maxQuestions and responseModels for the primary deployment. Limits apply to the complete request; evidence is never silently shortened. Cloudflare run URLs select their adapter automatically.
  - type `object`; default `{}`; allowed: data object with optional adapter, positive maxInputBytes/maxQuestions and explicit responseModels.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change which decision model decides for you counts as loosening security.

- `judgment.decisionDeadlineMs`: How long a decision that a person or a tool call waits on may take, in milliseconds, before it takes its fallback (for example asking you, or the safe default). A decision target that misses this deadline three times in a row is skipped for a minute, so the next decisions take their fallback at once.
  - type `number`; default `1500`; allowed: integer in [1, 120000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `judgment.endpoint`: Address of the decision model server the engine asks for judgments (a server that answers the decision API, POST /v1/systemone, as the hosted Jev does); empty uses TYPESAFE_BASE_URL, then the hosted endpoint. A loopback address selects a local model. While judgment.keySource is not none, change or reset it only together with judgment.keySource or judgment.keyName in one update (keep or clear the credential), or it is refused; embedded credentials, query strings and fragments are refused.
  - type `string`; default `""`; allowed: empty, or an http(s) URL without embedded credentials, query or fragment.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change which decision model decides for you counts as loosening security.
  - Environment: `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` (used when the setting is empty).

- `judgment.fallbacks`: Ordered decision targets with endpoint, model, keySource, keyName and optional backend capabilities. Each target may use a different decision model or adapter. keySource is env, secret or none; none requires an empty keyName. Credentials are privately resolved from references, never inline values. An empty array disables inherited fallbacks. Each target is attempted with a finite timeout; when the chain is exhausted, a decision that has a fallback takes it and any other decision stops.
  - type `array`; default `[]`; allowed: array of { endpoint, model, keySource: "env" | "secret" | "none", keyName } (keyName empty for "none"); no credentials in URLs or inline keys.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change which decision model decides for you counts as loosening security.

- `judgment.keyName`: Primary decision credential reference, such as TYPESAFE_API_KEY or CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN; never an inline key value. Ignored when keySource is none.
  - type `string`; default `"TYPESAFE_API_KEY"`; allowed: a credential reference name.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change which decision model decides for you counts as loosening security.

- `judgment.keySource`: Where the decision model's key comes from: env reads an environment variable, secret reads the secret store, and none sends no key. This setting stores only one of those three words, never a credential or a credential reference.
  - type `enum`; default `"env"`; allowed: `env`, `secret`, `none`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change which decision model decides for you counts as loosening security.

- `judgment.model`: Judgment model or alias; empty uses TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL, then jev-latest.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change which decision model decides for you counts as loosening security.
  - Environment: `TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL` (used when the setting is empty).

- `judgment.policy`: Hybrid (default) uses the set decision model and, when none is set or it fails, continues without it: decisions take their fallbacks and a failure is shown once with the model, what failed and the next step. Decision Model Only stops the operation and reports when the set decision model fails. No Decision Model makes no decision-model calls. With no decision model set, every policy continues without one.
  - type `enum`; default `"Hybrid"`; allowed: `Hybrid`, `Decision Model Only`, `No Decision Model`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `judgment.timeoutMs`: Finite timeout per judgment target in milliseconds; legacy 0 uses the default 30000 ms. Cancellation may stop the operation sooner.
  - type `number`; default `30000`; allowed: integer in [0, 2147483647].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `judgment.volumeMonitor`: Local decision call-volume alerts. Set enabled:true and budgets:[{name:"All decisions",maxLogicalDecisions:1000,maxWireAttempts:2000}]. Optional battery/site restrict each budget; windowMs defaults to one hour, intervalMs to one minute, limit to 10000 log entries. Alerts report usage without calling models or stopping work. Disabled settings retain the optional GOODVIBES_JUDGMENT_MONITOR file override.
  - type `object`; default `{"budgets":[],"intervalMs":60000,"windowMs":3600000,"limit":10000,"enabled":false}`; allowed: object with enabled and up to 100 budgets; enabled monitoring needs at least one budget.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.
  - Environment: `GOODVIBES_JUDGMENT_MONITOR` (the setting, when enabled, wins).

### memory

- `memory.budgetMb`: How much memory the daemon plans to use, in MB. The governor sheds caches and pauses background jobs as RSS approaches this budget. 0 means auto: min(25% of system RAM, 4096 MB), resolved at daemon start. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: integer in [0, 1048576].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `memory.hardLimitPct`: The daemon restarts before its memory reaches this share of the most it may use: its own memory limit where it has one, else the computer's memory. If RSS holds at/above this percent of that ceiling for memory.tripwire.sustainSec, the governor writes a hard-limit receipt and exits so a supervisor restarts clean, catching a leak too slow for memory.tripwire.rateMbPerSec just before the kernel/cgroup OOM killer would strike. Default 90: fire at 90% of the real kill line, leaving a safety margin for the exit itself. Deliberately anchored to the kill ceiling and NOT to memory.budgetMb: the budget caps small by design (25% of RAM, max 4096 MB), and a large-but-stable working set above the budget on a big-RAM host is handled by the critical tier (refuse new expensive work, stay alive), anchoring the exit to the budget would put such a healthy daemon in a permanent restart loop. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `90`; allowed: integer in [1, 100].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `memory.projection.dir`: /memory sync-files writes one markdown file per standing (project/team-scope) memory record here, and commits the directory when it sits inside a git repository. Relative paths resolve against the project working directory. /recall files review reads user edits back from this directory as proposals; a file edit or deletion never mutates the store directly.
  - type `string`; default `".goodvibes/memory/projection"`.
  - Stored in the terminal app's own file only (`~/.goodvibes/tui/settings.json`); the daemon refuses it as not a settings key.
  - 
  - Only the terminal app's `/settings` screen lists it; the shared settings schema does not declare it.

- `memory.showProvenance`: Show a "used N memories" chip on turns that drew on your standing memories, with a drill-in listing them (Alt+M to expand). Off by default; when off, nothing is rendered and no metadata is read.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the terminal app's own file only (`~/.goodvibes/tui/settings.json`); the other programs do not have this setting.
  - A project file may not set it.

- `memory.tier.criticalPct`: At this share of the memory budget, the daemon refuses new heavy work and says why. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `95`; allowed: integer in [1, 100].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `memory.tier.elevatedPct`: At this share of the memory budget, the daemon trims what it keeps in memory. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `60`; allowed: integer in [1, 100].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `memory.tier.highPct`: At this share of the memory budget, the daemon empties what it keeps in memory and pauses background work that can wait. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `80`; allowed: integer in [1, 100].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `memory.tripwire.rateMbPerSec`: If memory use keeps growing faster than this, in MB per second, after the daemon has emptied what it keeps, it suspects a leak. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `25`; allowed: number in [1, 100000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `memory.tripwire.sustainSec`: How long, in seconds, that growth must last before the daemon records why and restarts itself cleanly. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `60`; allowed: integer in [1, 86400].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

### notifications

- `notifications.adaptiveSuppression`: When many notifications of one kind arrive close together, lists the first few and counts the rest in one entry instead of listing each. Critical, milestone, and alert notifications are always exempt. Turn off to record every one as its own entry. Read when the app starts.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `notifications.blockedEscalationFollowUpMs`: Time between reminders after that first push, while the agent is still waiting for you. Read live per reminder.
  - type `number`; default `300000`; allowed: integer in [0, 86400000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `notifications.blockedEscalationGraceMs`: How long an agent waiting for you may wait before your devices get a push, even while a screen is open. Presence (an open TUI, a heartbeat) suppresses only the immediate push, never this escalation, a process being attended is not a human answer. A real interaction that clears the block cancels the escalation. Read live when a block is first tracked.
  - type `number`; default `300000`; allowed: integer in [0, 86400000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `notifications.blockedEscalationMaxFollowUps`: Most reminders after that first push (0 sends the one push and no reminders). Keeps a long-unanswered block from becoming an unbounded stream of pushes.
  - type `number`; default `2`; allowed: integer in [0, 100].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `notifications.burstThreshold`: How many notifications of one kind are listed one by one in a short time before the rest are counted together. The window follows the print level (behavior.hitlMode: 5 s quiet, 2 s balanced, 0.5 s operator) and runs from the first notification, so a steady trickle cannot keep one open. Critical, milestone and alert notifications never collapse. Read when the app starts.
  - type `number`; default `3`; allowed: integer in [1, 10000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `notifications.pushApproval`: Sends a push to your paired devices when something is waiting for your approval. On by default, the toggle exists to silence the class, never as a prerequisite for it to work. Read live per event.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `notifications.pushCompletion`: Sends a push to your paired devices when a run you follow finishes, fails or is stopped. On by default with zero setup; the toggle only silences. Read live per event.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `notifications.pushNeedsInput`: Sends a push to your paired devices when an agent is waiting for you, unless you are already looking. On by default; the toggle only silences. Read live per event.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `notifications.webhookUrls`: Webhook URLs that receive the notifications this machine sends (turn ends, approvals waiting, budget alerts). Each URL carries its own key, so it is kept in the secret store and this list holds a goodvibes://secrets/ reference to each; add one with /notify add <url>. Screens show only each URL's host. Applies at the next start.
  - type `array`; default `[]`; allowed: list of goodvibes://secrets/ references to stored webhook URLs; add a URL with /notify add <url>.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a credential: the settings file holds only a `goodvibes://secrets/...` reference to it.

### occasions

- `occasions.activeHours`: The hours a nudge may arrive, HH:MM-HH:MM, reckoned in daemon.timezone. 08:00–22:00 because those hours are generally fine and anything outside them probably is not. Outside this window nothing is dropped, it waits. An empty or unreadable value means no restriction rather than permanent silence, so a typo cannot switch the feature off invisibly.
  - type `string`; default `"08:00-22:00"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `occasions.awayAdjust`: Let a plan that has you away from home move a nudge EARLIER, to the day before you leave. On because you cannot have something delivered to a house you are not in, so a reminder that arrives while you are abroad has already missed the window it existed to protect. When you have already left there is nothing earlier to move to and the nudge stands rather than waiting for your return.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `occasions.cadenceDays`: How often an unresolved CONFLICT in your dates, two lines recorded for the same thing (two different dates, or one date written twice), is raised again, in days. It no longer governs birthday reminders: those speak twice, when the date enters its runway and on the day itself, and never repeat beyond that. A conflict is a fact about your file that stays wrong until you fix it, so it does keep coming back.
  - type `number`; default `3`; allowed: integer in [1, 60].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `occasions.calendarMirror`: Write your occasions out to the connected calendar as well. Off by default because your profile is the record and the calendar is a copy, calendar entries are single occurrences that do not persist across years, which is exactly why these dates live in the profile instead. Nothing is ever read back the other way, and deleting a calendar entry never removes the occasion.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `occasions.enabled`: Raise your important dates on their own, before they matter. On by default because a feature that ships off ships dark, and because being told about your wife's birthday in time is the whole point. Turning it off does NOT forget anything: the dates stay in your profile, stay readable, and are still answered when you ask, it only stops the system raising them unprompted.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `occasions.giftHistoryYears`: How long the record of what you landed on is kept, in years. Ten, so year three is not steered by year one. This is the one part of the machine-owned state that deliberately outlives its occasion's answer, the answers expire with their date so next year asks fresh, the history does not.
  - type `number`; default `10`; allowed: integer in [1, 50].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `occasions.interviewQuestions`: How many questions are asked after you say yes to sorting a gift. Three, because it is meant to guide you to an idea rather than fill in a form, and a long one is a form. The questions open from what your profile already knows about the person and from what you landed on last time; none of them recommends anything.
  - type `number`; default `3`; allowed: integer in [1, 8].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `occasions.leadDays`: How many days ahead an occasion starts being raised. Ten because that is enough runway to order something and have it arrive. An individual entry overrides this by carrying "lead 21" on its line, so a date that needs longer does not force everything else earlier.
  - type `number`; default `10`; allowed: integer in [0, 365].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `occasions.nudgeChannel`: Where a nudge is delivered: a comma-separated list of channel destinations, each a surface or surface:address, "telegram", "agent", "telegram,agent", "telegram:12345,agent". Telegram by default, because an occasion nudge that waits to be asked for has already missed the date it existed to protect, the owner ruled that these push out of the box, to Telegram and to the agent. Naming "agent" puts the reminder in the Agent's conversation: the host tells a connected Agent to read it at once (when no turn is running; otherwise when the turn ends), and an Agent that was not connected reads it at its next turn or idle check, because the reminder stays outstanding until you answer it. Naming both means both get it, and a broken credential on one cannot silence the other. Set it to empty to make the feature pull-only instead: nothing is pushed or announced, and a surface picks up what is outstanding at the end of a turn. The TUI is refused as a destination whatever is set here: it is a get-work-done interface, and life admin does not belong in it.
  - type `string`; default `"telegram"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `occasions.suppressMirroredNudges`: Stay quiet about an occasion that is already in a calendar, so the calendar's own reminder is the only ping. On by default because two pings for one birthday is how a useful reminder becomes one you mute. Turn it off if you would rather have both, an occasion marked "mirrored" on its own line is covered by this too.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `occasions.sweepIntervalMinutes`: How often the daemon looks for dates entering their lead window, in minutes. Hourly by default, which is frequent enough that a nudge lands within an hour of the window opening and cheap enough to be invisible, the pass reads memory and touches one small file. It cannot over-nudge whatever this is set to: each occasion carries its own next-due date, so a shorter interval makes the FIRST nudge land sooner and changes nothing about the rhythm after it. Housekeeping runs on every pass, including the ones that are inside quiet hours or that raise nothing.
  - type `number`; default `60`; allowed: integer in [5, 1440].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

### orchestration

- `orchestration.maxDepth`: Optional recursive orchestration depth limit; 0 is unlimited. recursionEnabled controls whether recursion is allowed.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: non-negative safe integer; 0 means unlimited.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `orchestration.recursionEnabled`: Allow recursive agent orchestration under bounded policy controls.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

### payments

- `payments.billingAddress.city`: City or town. Part of the billing address the card issuer checks against (address verification). Stored in daemon-owned config rather than the secret store because surfaces must display and edit it, but note it sits beside stored card material, so anyone holding both has everything a card-not-present charge needs. A virtual card with a hard issuer cap is what bounds that. When left empty, the matching address field of the owner profile is used once it has been verified.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `payments.billingAddress.country`: Country, as the checkout expects it (an ISO two-letter code is safest). Part of the billing address the card issuer checks against (address verification). Stored in daemon-owned config rather than the secret store because surfaces must display and edit it, but note it sits beside stored card material, so anyone holding both has everything a card-not-present charge needs. A virtual card with a hard issuer cap is what bounds that. When left empty, the matching address field of the owner profile is used once it has been verified.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

  - type `string`; default `""`.
