  - A project file may not set it.

- `payments.billingAddress.region`: State, province or region; leave empty where the country has none (it is required only for countries whose addresses use one, such as US, CA, AU, IN). Part of the billing address the card issuer checks against (address verification). Stored in daemon-owned config rather than the secret store because surfaces must display and edit it, but note it sits beside stored card material, so anyone holding both has everything a card-not-present charge needs. A virtual card with a hard issuer cap is what bounds that. When left empty, the matching address field of the owner profile is used once it has been verified.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `payments.budget.dailyItem`: Most that may be spent on ITEM PRICES in one calendar day, written the way you would say it: 100 is a hundred, 19.99 is nineteen ninety-nine, in whatever payments.currency is set to. The item price alone is checked against this; tax, mandatory fees and delivery draw on the separate overage budget below. Resets at midnight in daemon.timezone (UTC when unset), the boundary is real, so 100 at 23:59 and 100 at 00:00 both go through. Default 0: until you set it every purchase asks you first, and the first time one does, your inbox offers to set it. While payments.budget.dailyOverage is also 0, a purchase with any tax, fee or paid delivery is refused, not asked about.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: a plain number like 100 or 19.99, no greater than 1000000; an amount in `payments.currency`, written as a person says it (`100`, `19.99`)
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would raise a spending limit counts as loosening security.

- `payments.budget.dailyOverage`: Daily allowance for charges that CANNOT BE AVOIDED on a purchase you already approved: sales tax, mandatory handling or booking fees, and the delivery option actually used. Written the way you would say it, 25 is twenty-five, 7.50 is seven fifty. Discretionary add-ons, expedited shipping beyond what the ladder picks, insurance, gift wrap, extended warranties, are purchase decisions, not delivery costs, and never draw on this. Default 0.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: a plain number like 100 or 19.99, no greater than 1000000; an amount in `payments.currency`, written as a person says it (`100`, `19.99`)
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would raise a spending limit counts as loosening security.

- `payments.budget.overageToleranceDailyAllowance`: Daily tolerance allowance, used only when overageToleranceEnabled is true. Written the way you would say it, 5 is five, 2.50 is two fifty. This is a third pool, drawn on only after the shipping ladder has stepped delivery all the way down and the unavoidable charges still do not fit. Every use is recorded in the purchase audit record.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: a plain number like 100 or 19.99, no greater than 1000000; an amount in `payments.currency`, written as a person says it (`100`, `19.99`)
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would raise a spending limit counts as loosening security.

- `payments.budget.overageToleranceEnabled`: When true, a purchase whose unavoidable charges cannot fit the overage budget even at the CHEAPEST delivery option may draw the shortfall from the tolerance allowance below instead of being refused. Default FALSE. Enabling it alone changes nothing, the allowance also starts at 0.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would let purchases draw on the overage tolerance counts as loosening security.

- `payments.budget.perPurchaseCeiling`: The most any single purchase may come to in total, items plus tax, fees and delivery, applied when perPurchaseCeilingEnabled is true. A purchase over it asks you first and names the ceiling and by how much. Written the way you would say it, 100 is a hundred, 19.99 is nineteen ninety-nine. Default 0, so with the ceiling on and this unset every purchase needs your explicit approval, the safe direction until you choose a number.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: a plain number like 100 or 19.99, no greater than 1000000; an amount in `payments.currency`, written as a person says it (`100`, `19.99`)
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would raise a spending limit counts as loosening security.

- `payments.budget.perPurchaseCeilingEnabled`: When true (DEFAULT), no single purchase may come to more than payments.budget.perPurchaseCeiling in total (items, tax, fees and delivery) without your explicit approval, no matter how much of the daily budget is left. A separate question from the daily budget: both must pass. Turn it off only if you want one purchase to be able to consume the whole day at once.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would turn the per-purchase spending ceiling off counts as loosening security.

- `payments.cardsOnFile`: Cards purchases can use. Enter closes Settings, lists the cards on the daemon, and starts "Add a card" (Esc stops it); /payments remove-card deletes one. Settings never takes a card number. The daemon keeps this setting (in ~/.goodvibes/daemon/settings.json), so it applies to every program, not just this one.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Not stored: it is a row of the terminal app's settings screen that opens a command, with no value of its own.
  - 
  - Only the terminal app's `/settings` screen lists it; the shared settings schema does not declare it.

- `payments.confirmEveryPurchase`: When true, every purchase needs your approval first, given with /payments approve (or payments.checkout.approve) naming the merchant, the item and the most it may cost, before the agent may start it; the approval lasts five minutes and is used once. Default FALSE: the agent buys on your behalf inside your budgets without asking first, and that standing answer is kept here until you change it. Either way, a purchase over a budget or at a shop nobody vouches for still asks you before it is bought, and an approval you give in advance answers that question for a total up to the amount you named.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would stop asking you before every purchase counts as loosening security.

- `payments.currency`: ISO-4217 code your budgets are denominated in. A checkout priced in any other currency is REFUSED rather than converted, the issuer converts at its own rate on its own date, so any number shown to you before the charge would not be the number you are charged.
  - type `string`; default `"USD"`; allowed: a three-letter ISO-4217 code such as USD, GBP or EUR.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change the currency your spending limits are counted in counts as loosening security.

- `payments.cvvHandling`: How the card verification value is handled at checkout. 'stored' (DEFAULT) keeps it in the daemon secret store beside the card number, encrypted at rest, so a purchase within budget completes while you are away, which is what autonomous action requires. Choosing 'prompt' stores nothing: when a purchase is approved and reaches payment, it stops and asks you to type the code in the terminal app (/payments pending) or the local web UI, waiting as long as an approval window, and nothing is bought if the code is not typed in time. So nothing completes while you are away. Never send the code in a chat; a likely code typed on a remote channel while one is awaited is refused there. Surfaces show CVV_PROMPT_TRADEOFF_WARNING at the moment you select it. Provisioning a virtual card with a hard issuer cap bounds what any leak of stored card material could cost; a real card number does not.
  - type `enum`; default `"stored"`; allowed: `stored`, `prompt`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would keep the card code so purchases complete while you are away counts as loosening security.

- `payments.defaultCardId`: A card id from payments.cards.list. A purchase that names no card is paid with this one; with this empty, every purchase must name its card. Deleting that card does not clear this setting, and a purchase that would use a deleted card is refused saying so. The card NUMBER, expiry and CVV live in the daemon secret store and never in config.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would choose the card a purchase is paid with counts as loosening security.

- `payments.ebayMinSellerFeedbackCount`: Minimum feedback ratings earned AS A SELLER before an eBay Buy It Now listing proceeds on silence. eBay's headline score combines buying and selling, so an account with a large number can have earned all of it buying, only the seller-side figure counts. Below this, or when the figure cannot be read from eBay's own seller widget, the purchase asks for your yes. The listing is read by code from the page the purchase runs on: its purchase controls and eBay's seller card, never the seller's text. Auctions and Best Offer listings are refused outright regardless, because there is no final price to show you before paying.
  - type `number`; default `100`; allowed: integer in [0, 1000000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would lower the eBay seller feedback a purchase needs counts as loosening security.

- `payments.ebayMinSellerPositivePercent`: Minimum positive feedback percentage AS A SELLER before an eBay Buy It Now listing proceeds on silence. Read from eBay's own feedback widget, never from the seller's listing text, if the figures cannot be attributed to eBay with confidence, the purchase asks for your yes rather than assuming.
  - type `number`; default `98`; allowed: integer in [0, 100].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would lower the eBay seller rating a purchase needs counts as loosening security.

- `payments.enabled`: Master switch for the payment capability. Default OFF. While false the daemon will not price, reserve, or charge anything, and the payments operator methods refuse. Turning it on does not by itself allow a purchase, the daily budgets below start at 0, so nothing goes through until you set an amount.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would turn payments on counts as loosening security.

- `payments.majorRetailersAdditional`: Comma-separated REGISTRABLE domains (eTLD+1, e.g. 'microcenter.com', not 'www.microcenter.com') to add to the recognised-retailer list. A purchase at a recognised retailer gets the veto window, you are told and it goes ahead unless you object. Everything else asks for your yes. The test is recourse: is there a real path to remedy if it goes wrong. Additions are yours alone, nothing is learned onto this list, inferred from a page, or added by an agent, because a page that could argue itself onto it could buy from itself unattended.
  - type `string`; default `""`; allowed: a comma-separated list of registrable domains.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would add a shop that buys without asking you counts as loosening security.

- `payments.majorRetailersExcluded`: Comma-separated registrable domains to REMOVE from the shipped recognised-retailer list, so purchases there ask for your yes instead of proceeding on silence. A domain listed in both this and the additions is excluded (it asks for your yes), because on a spending path the stricter instruction wins.
  - type `string`; default `""`; allowed: a comma-separated list of registrable domains.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would let an excluded shop buy without asking you counts as loosening security.

- `payments.notifyChannels`: Comma-separated, ordered list of channels that ALSO receive approval and veto prompts and may answer them. Every purchase notice, window and confirmation is always posted to your owner inbox (/questions in both terminal apps, and the web UI), where it can be answered, whatever this says; these channels reach you away from them. Today only 'telegram' has a delivery path. EMAIL IS NOT AND WILL NEVER BE ACCEPTED HERE, an inbound email is content anyone can write and cannot authorize spending. An unrecognised name is rejected rather than ignored, because a channel you believe will reach you and does not is worse than none. Empty means the owner inbox only: an in-budget purchase is announced there and waits its veto window, and an above-budget one is asked there.
  - type `string`; default `""`; allowed: a comma-separated list; only 'telegram' can deliver a notice today.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would let another channel answer purchase approvals counts as loosening security.

- `payments.shipping.preferredTier`: Preferred delivery tier, ordinal against WHAT THE CHECKOUT ACTUALLY OFFERS rather than delivery-day promises: its options are ranked cheapest-first and this indexes into that ranking. The chosen tier draws on the overage budget; when the budget cannot cover it, delivery steps down ONE tier at a time until it fits, stopping at the cheapest. A step-down needs no approval (it is within budget) but is recorded and shown to you, so you never learn about it from a late package. Default 'normal'.
  - type `enum`; default `"normal"`; allowed: `normal`, `fast`, `fastest`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `payments.shippingAddress.city`: City or town. Where purchases are delivered. A purchase is REFUSED while the shipping address is incomplete, there is nowhere to send it, and guessing an address is not a thing this should do. When left empty, the matching address field of the owner profile is used once it has been verified.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change where purchases are delivered counts as loosening security.

- `payments.shippingAddress.country`: Country, as the checkout expects it (an ISO two-letter code is safest). Where purchases are delivered. A purchase is REFUSED while the shipping address is incomplete, there is nowhere to send it, and guessing an address is not a thing this should do. When left empty, the matching address field of the owner profile is used once it has been verified.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change where purchases are delivered counts as loosening security.

- `payments.shippingAddress.line1`: Street address, first line. Where purchases are delivered. A purchase is REFUSED while the shipping address is incomplete, there is nowhere to send it, and guessing an address is not a thing this should do. When left empty, the matching address field of the owner profile is used once it has been verified.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change where purchases are delivered counts as loosening security.

- `payments.shippingAddress.line2`: Second address line (apartment, suite); leave empty when unused. Where purchases are delivered. A purchase is REFUSED while the shipping address is incomplete, there is nowhere to send it, and guessing an address is not a thing this should do. When left empty, the matching address field of the owner profile is used once it has been verified.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change where purchases are delivered counts as loosening security.

- `payments.shippingAddress.name`: Recipient name. Where purchases are delivered. A purchase is REFUSED while the shipping address is incomplete, there is nowhere to send it, and guessing an address is not a thing this should do. When left empty, the matching address field of the owner profile is used once it has been verified.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change where purchases are delivered counts as loosening security.

- `payments.shippingAddress.postalCode`: Postal or ZIP code. Where purchases are delivered. A purchase is REFUSED while the shipping address is incomplete, there is nowhere to send it, and guessing an address is not a thing this should do. When left empty, the matching address field of the owner profile is used once it has been verified.
  - type `string`; default `""`.

- `payments.shippingAddress.region`: State, province or region; leave empty where the country has none (it is required only for countries whose addresses use one, such as US, CA, AU, IN). Where purchases are delivered. A purchase is REFUSED while the shipping address is incomplete, there is nowhere to send it, and guessing an address is not a thing this should do. When left empty, the matching address field of the owner profile is used once it has been verified.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change where purchases are delivered counts as loosening security.

- `payments.windows.approvalMinutes`: How long an ABOVE-BUDGET purchase waits for your explicit approval, in minutes. This is the opposite of the veto window: if you say nothing, the purchase is DENIED. Denial is the recoverable outcome, ask again and it goes through, so a short window costs friction while a long one leaves a cart holding a price that may drift. Default 60, which survives a meeting or a commute; raise it if you are away for long stretches.
  - type `number`; default `60`; allowed: integer in [1, 10080].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `payments.windows.vetoMinutes`: How long you get to STOP an in-budget purchase, in minutes, starting once the final total is known and before payment. The notice is always in your owner inbox, and on the channels in payments.notifyChannels. This is a VETO, not an approval: if you say nothing, the purchase GOES AHEAD. One word (stop) cancels it. The window always runs its full length wherever you are, no presence, focus or activity signal shortens it, and an explicit acknowledgement buys immediately.
  - type `number`; default `10`; allowed: integer in [1, 1440].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would shorten the time you have to stop a purchase counts as loosening security.

### permissions

- `permissions.commandParser`: Shell parse before an exec command runs: ast (default) parses the command into segments and refuses one in which a segment has nothing to run, naming it; a command the parser cannot read runs as the permission gate decided. flat skips the parse. The permission gate decides risk, including the catastrophic-command block, identically in both modes.
  - type `enum`; default `"ast"`; allowed: `ast`, `flat`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would stop parsing shell commands before they run counts as loosening security.

- `permissions.divergenceDashboard`: Aggregate permission-evaluator divergence by tool/prefix/mode, expose trend history in diagnostics, and block enforce-mode transitions while the divergence rate exceeds permissions.divergenceThreshold. Turn off to fall back to warn mode (no gate enforcement).
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `permissions.divergenceThreshold`: While new permission rules are tried out beside the rules in force, how often they may disagree (0 to 1) before switching to them is refused. Default 0.05 = 5%. A per-simulator divergenceThreshold override still wins.
  - type `number`; default `0.05`; allowed: number in [0, 1].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `permissions.engine`: Permission evaluator: baseline (default) or policy-engine (the redesigned layered model with granular tool-level, path-level, and parameter-level rules). Restart to apply. Default baseline until divergence evidence from the shadow simulation clears the gate.
  - type `enum`; default `"baseline"`; allowed: `baseline`, `policy-engine`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `permissions.execEnvScrubAllowlist`: Comma-separated environment variable NAMES always kept in a spawned exec command's environment even when the name looks credential-bearing (case-insensitive). Names only: this never inspects or reports values. The scrub itself stays on; this only widens what it lets through, from the next command. Empty = the built-in credential-name scrub applies with no extra exceptions.
  - type `array`; default `[]`.
  - Stored in the terminal app's own file only (`~/.goodvibes/tui/settings.json`); the daemon refuses it as not a settings key.
  - 
  - Only the terminal app's `/settings` screen lists it; the shared settings schema does not declare it.

- `permissions.maxDivergenceRecords`: How many of those disagreements are kept for the comparison report. A per-simulator maxDivergenceRecords override still wins.
  - type `number`; default `500`; allowed: integer in [1, 1000000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `permissions.mode`: Who decides what ordinary work does not settle. Ask me: you are asked about dangerous actions and owner-only decisions. Jev decides (the default): Jev, the decision model, decides judgment calls and you are asked only owner-only decisions; with no working decision model it behaves as Ask me, and while it is only the default (not chosen) it also does until a calibration run has measured Jev's decisions on the configured decision model. Just vibes: does as much as it can without interrupting you; Jev decides judgment calls when a decision model works, and anything that needs you is held and listed at the end. YOLO: runs every action without safety denials (containment, secret storage and payment limits still apply). Plan: a separate read-only planning posture.
  - type `enum`; default `"jev-decides"`; allowed: `ask-me`, `jev-decides`, `just-vibes`, `yolo`, `plan`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it only to a stricter value; a change that would loosen the permission mode counts as loosening security.

- `permissions.simulation`: Run the candidate permission evaluator beside the active one, recording divergence without changing enforcement. Default on so divergence evidence accumulates before stricter enforcement is considered; it never blocks tool execution by itself. Restart to apply.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `permissions.tools.agent`: Permission for spawning subagents or delegating tasks. Deny refuses it in every mode but YOLO. Prompt sets no rule of its own: the permission mode decides each time, and Ask me allows a read, or a change to files inside the folder that can be undone, without asking. Allow also lets it run without asking when no decision model works, except for a decision only the owner makes.
  - type `enum`; default `"prompt"`; allowed: `allow`, `prompt`, `deny`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it only to a stricter value; a change that would loosen a per-tool permission counts as loosening security.

- `permissions.tools.analyze`: Permission for code/project analysis operations. Deny refuses it in every mode but YOLO. Prompt sets no rule of its own: the permission mode decides each time, and Ask me allows a read, or a change to files inside the folder that can be undone, without asking. Allow also lets it run without asking when no decision model works, except for a decision only the owner makes.
  - type `enum`; default `"allow"`; allowed: `allow`, `prompt`, `deny`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it only to a stricter value; a change that would loosen a per-tool permission counts as loosening security.

### planner

- `planner.adaptive`: Reserved for choosing an execution strategy (single/cohort/background/remote) on every conversation turn. No turn reads a strategy yet, so this setting changes nothing today. The planner that /work planner, planner-mode, planner-override and planner-explain work with is consulted when /workstream drafts a plan, whatever this setting says.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `planner.decomposition`: How /workstream decomposes a goal into work items: 'agent' spawns a read-only planning agent (with automatic fallback to the heuristic path on any failure); 'heuristic' forces the deterministic single-item path and never spawns an agent.
  - type `enum`; default `"agent"`; allowed: `agent`, `heuristic`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `planner.maxTurns`: Optional planner turn limit; 0 runs until completion or cancellation.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: non-negative safe integer; 0 means unlimited.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `planner.tokenCeiling`: Optional total planner token limit; 0 imposes no work budget.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: non-negative safe integer; 0 means unlimited.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `planner.wallTimeoutMs`: Optional planner wall-clock limit in milliseconds; 0 runs until completion or cancellation.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: non-negative safe integer; 0 means unlimited.

### policy

- `policy.bundlePath`: Filesystem path to the policy bundle JSON loaded at startup when policy.bundleSource is "file" and policy.registryEnabled is true. Empty disables file loading. The loaded bundle enters the registry as a candidate (subject to the divergence gate before promotion); once promoted, the same unchanged bundle is enforced again at every start.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `policy.bundleSource`: Where the policy bundle registry loads its initial bundle from at startup: none (no bundle loaded; bundles supplied programmatically or via commands), or file (load policy.bundlePath). Only consulted when policy.registryEnabled is true.
  - type `enum`; default `"none"`; allowed: `none`, `file`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `policy.registryEnabled`: Enable the versioned policy bundle registry with promote/rollback semantics and the /security load-policy, simulate-policy, compare-policy, enforce-policy and restore-policy actions. Enforcement requires passing divergence-gate evidence first; default off until that evidence exists.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `policy.requireSignedBundles`: Require a valid HMAC-SHA256 signature on every policy bundle: a bundle that is unsigned, altered or signed with another key is refused, and so is every bundle when no signing key is set. The key is read from the GOODVIBES_POLICY_SIGNING_KEY environment variable (hex, at least 16 bytes). Restart to apply. Default off until divergence evidence clears the governance gate.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.
  - Environment: `GOODVIBES_POLICY_SIGNING_KEY` (the key the setting checks against).

### power

- `power.inhibitWhileWorking`: Hold an idle/sleep inhibitor automatically while real work runs (a running turn, an active agent, a schedule about to fire), released when work drains. On by default so the host cannot sleep mid-work.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `power.keepAwake`: The owner keep-awake toggle: the daemon holds a sleep inhibitor INDEPENDENT of work state, so the host stays reachable after work finishes and after surfaces close. Covers idle + sleep + lid-switch inhibitor classes where the OS grants them; the served state names any refused class honestly. Every attached surface shows an always-visible "sleep disabled" chip while this is on, the chip, not a timer, is the safety mechanism.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `power.workInhibitMaxMinutes`: Hard cap in minutes on the automatic WORK inhibitor (never the keep-awake toggle): a wedged hold releases at the cap and the state reports the expiry honestly.
  - type `number`; default `180`; allowed: integer in [1, 1440].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

### pricing

- `pricing.modelPrices`: Manual model prices, keyed provider:model (e.g. "openrouter:deepseek/deepseek-chat"). Each entry: { input, output, cacheRead?, cacheWrite? } in USD per 1M tokens. A manual price always wins over provider-served and catalog pricing and applies live (no restart). Set one when registering a custom provider/model, or to pin a negotiated rate for any model.
  - type `object`; default `{}`; allowed: record keyed "provider:model" of { input, output, cacheRead?, cacheWrite? }, finite numbers >= 0, USD per 1M tokens.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

### profile

- `profile.autonomousWrites`: Lets GoodVibes save facts it learns from what you tell it about yourself, without asking each time. On by default because that was the owner's explicit choice over propose-first. Off leaves reads and your own hand edits working exactly as before, the honest "I will curate this myself" mode, not a disabled feature. Untrusted sources are barred either way.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `profile.consumerFallback`: Lets a setting you have not set take its value from your profile: quiet hours, where notifications go, and your shopping details. On because a profile nothing reads is a diary. A value you configured explicitly always wins; the profile only fills a gap, and only for a single keyed read, never in a settings listing or export.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `profile.conversationalCapture`: Let a conversation record what you say about yourself as you say it, a trip and its itinerary, a birthday, a preference, a person. On by default because the alternative is what shipped before it: you paste a flight itinerary, get a warm reply, and nothing is stored. Off leaves conversations working and every profile read unchanged; it only stops the writing, and a turn that would have recorded something says so instead of staying quiet.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `profile.discloseClosedTierReads`: Says so in the reply when a private detail from your profile is used, for example "Used your shipping address from your profile." On by default because using your address on an order should be visible to you at the moment it happens rather than discoverable afterwards in a log.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `profile.discloseWrites`: Say in one line what was recorded, e.g. "Noted, saved your office address to your profile." On by default because telling you what it recorded was a condition attached to autonomous learning. Editable because the receipts may read as noisy over time, but turning them off is your decision made knowingly rather than a default that hides writes.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `profile.enabled`: Keeps a profile about you: what you have told GoodVibes about yourself, in one file you can read and edit. On by default because the owner asked for it built, and a feature that ships off ships dark. Turning it off means the file is never opened and every profile verb answers "your profile is turned off", a stated state, not an empty profile that would read as "I know nothing about you". Applies when the daemon starts.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `profile.injectOpenTier`: Tells the model, each turn, what about you is not private: how you like to be addressed, your pronouns, city and timezone, your units and date format, and your style notes. On by default because otherwise the agent still guesses a metro area for a weather answer, which is the failure that started this. Closed-tier content (addresses, contact details, people, notes) is never bulk-injected regardless of this setting.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `profile.ownerChannels`: The channels whose incoming messages are you, comma-separated, each as a surface name or surface:address, the same form as occasions.nudgeChannel. Only these may record to your profile; anything arriving anywhere else is treated as someone else's words and is refused, which is the rule that keeps a forwarded email from editing what the system believes about you. Empty means no channel counts as you on a conversational turn: only a surface you are sitting at (the terminal, the web UI) can record to your profile, and the refusal names this setting. occasions.nudgeChannel is where reminders are sent and is not an owner grant, so the channel that sends you a birthday reminder cannot also record that your flight leaves at nine until you list it here.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `profile.path`: Where the profile file is kept (a full path). Empty means the default, owner-profile.md under the daemon home, which already honours GOODVIBES_DAEMON_HOME, so this override is only for keeping the file somewhere else entirely. Applies when the daemon starts.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `profile.reloadThrottleMs`: How often to look for your own edits to the profile file, on a computer that cannot report file changes. Used only on that fallback path and never on a read, so it costs nothing in the common case. 2000 sits under human edit-then-check latency: you save the file, look at the assistant, and it already knows. Applies when the daemon starts.
  - type `number`; default `2000`; allowed: integer in [50, 3600000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

### provider

- `provider.decisionRouter`: Which model answers which kind of decision, and how hard it thinks. Used only when decision-router:auto is selected. Empty categories use the required General target. Contains no credentials.
  - type `object`; default `{"categories":{"lookup-navigation":{"label":"Lookup / navigation","description":"Find a definition, locate a file or setting, or answer a narrow question about existing work.","target":null},"coding-implementation":{"label":"Coding / implementation","description":"Implement, modify or refactor code and configuration.","target":null},"analysis-decisions":{"label":"Analysis / decisions","description":"Reason through a problem, compare options, plan an approach or make a decision.","target":null},"documentation-writing":{"label":"Documentation / writing","description":"Write or edit documentation, explanations and other prose.","target":null},"summarization-extraction":{"label":"Summarization / extraction","description":"Summarize supplied material or extract its facts into a requested form.","target":null},"general":{"label":"General","description":"Catch-all for conversation and requests that do not fit a more specific category.","target":null},"debugging-diagnosis":{"label":"Debugging / diagnosis","description":"Identify the cause of an error, failing test, crash or unexpected behavior.","target":null},"review-verification":{"label":"Review / verification","description":"Review a change or verify claims, correctness, behavior or test evidence.","target":null},"research":{"label":"Research","description":"Find and synthesize information from external sources.","target":null},"data-analysis":{"label":"Data analysis","description":"Analyze datasets, calculate metrics, or interpret quantitative results.","target":null}},"initialContextChars":3000,"expandedContextChars":10000}`.
  - Stored in the shared file (one value, which wins over each program's own file).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `provider.embeddingProvider`: The provider that turns memories into a form GoodVibes can search.
  - type `string`; default `"hashed-local"`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `provider.fallbackModels`: Your fallback order: the models a turn moves to, in order, when the selected model fails on every sign-in of its provider (OpenAI tries the same model through the API key after the subscription first). Empty (default): the turn stops and says so; no other model is chosen for you. Applies from the next failure, in every program that runs a turn: the terminal app, `goodvibes run`, the Agent, the daemon's hosted sessions and its agents. The model that answers instead is named in a [Failover] line, and the next turn starts on the selected model again. A provider may be named by its id or display name.
  - type `array`; default `[]`; allowed: list of provider-qualified model ids, for example ["anthropic:claude-sonnet-5"].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `provider.localContextIngestion`: Uses the context size a local model's server reports, so the conversation is shortened at the right point for that model. Turn off to use only explicitly configured or static limits.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `provider.model`: The model new conversations use, written as provider:model.
  - type `string`; default `"openrouter:openrouter/free"`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `provider.optimizerMode`: How GoodVibes picks a provider for each request: off (the default), manual (it compares but never switches), auto (it picks the best provider that can do the request), or pinned (always the one model named in the next setting). Applies at once from any settings path; /provider-opt commands write this setting.
  - type `enum`; default `"off"`; allowed: `off`, `manual`, `auto`, `pinned`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `provider.optimizerPinnedModel`: The one model used while provider choice is pinned, written as provider:model (for example anthropic:claude-sonnet-4); a change applies at once. Empty leaves the optimizer unpinned (falls back to manual).
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `provider.reasoningEffort`: How much the model reasons before it answers, for models that can be told.
  - type `string`; default `"medium"`; allowed: a known reasoning effort level, run /effort for the current model choices.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `provider.systemPromptFile`: A file of standing instructions the model gets at the start of every conversation; empty for none.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `provider.visionFallbackModel`: Model (provider-qualified, e.g. openai:gpt-4o, or a unique bare id) that reads an image you attach when the current model cannot accept images. Empty (default): such an image is refused and sent nowhere, and the refusal names the models that can read it. Setting this sends those images to the named model's provider.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

### push

- `push.subscriptions.failureThreshold`: How many deliveries in a row a push service must refuse before the daemon treats that endpoint as dead and removes it. A 404 or 410 removes it immediately, that is the push service saying the subscription is gone, so this bound is for the murkier case of an endpoint that only ever errors or times out. Any single success resets the count to zero. Raise it if you have a flaky network and would rather keep retrying; lower it to clear out dead endpoints faster.
  - type `number`; default `5`; allowed: integer in [1, 100].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `push.subscriptions.sweepIntervalMinutes`: How often housekeeping re-reads the stored push subscriptions while the daemon is up, looking for records that are provably dead, unreadable key material, a torn record, or an endpoint past the refusal threshold. A sweep also runs at every start; this interval is what keeps a daemon that stays up for weeks from going that long without one. Each sweep writes what it removed and the evidence, so a removal is never indistinguishable from data loss. A change to the interval takes effect after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `60`; allowed: integer in [1, 1440].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `push.subscriptions.warnAbovePerPrincipal`: How many registered push devices one operator can hold before housekeeping starts saying so. This is a WARNING line, not a limit: passing it logs the count and writes it into the housekeeping disclosure, and every subscription is kept. A working device is NEVER removed to make room for a new one, registering a new phone always succeeds, even when that puts you over this number, because dropping a quiet-but-live device would stop its notifications with nothing to tell you and no way back but resubscribing. Devices leave only when something proves them dead (the push service reports the endpoint gone, or refuses it repeatedly).
  - type `number`; default `50`; allowed: integer in [1, 100000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `push.vapidSubject`: Who a push service contacts when it has a problem delivering your notifications. Every push the daemon sends is signed with this address in it (the VAPID "sub" claim), and it is the only way Apple, Google, or Mozilla can reach you about, say, a malformed payload or a rate limit. Set it to a mailto: address you read, or an https: page with contact details on it. Left empty it falls back to mailto:goodvibes-push@goodvibes.invalid, which is well-formed and accepted but reaches nobody, push still works, you just never hear about a problem. A change takes effect after the daemon restarts.
  - type `string`; default `""`; allowed: empty, or a mailto: address or an https: URL a push service can use to reach you.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

### relay

- `relay.enabled`: Connect the daemon OUTBOUND to a zero-knowledge relay for reachability from outside the LAN. Default on, but no connection is ever made without an explicitly configured relay.url, leave the URL empty to keep the daemon LAN-only.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `relay.label`: Human-facing daemon label carried in relay pairing payloads.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `relay.rendezvousId`: The rendezvous id the daemon registers under on the relay, derived from the daemon's relay identity key and recorded here by the daemon; setting it has no effect.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `relay.requireStepUpForMutations`: Require a recent WebAuthn step-up assertion on mutating operator calls arriving via relay (checked against a passkey registered through pairing or the step-up verbs)
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `relay.url`: Relay URL to dial (wss://…); empty disables the outbound relay connection.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

### runtime

- `runtime.companionChat.closedRetentionDays`: Days after a companion chat is closed before its saved files are deleted. 0 (the default) keeps closed chats forever. Read on every cleanup pass, so a change applies without a restart.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: integer in [0, 36500].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `runtime.companionChatLimiter.perSessionLimit`: Max companion chat messages per 60-second window per session. 0 (the default) means unset: the GOODVIBES_CHAT_LIMITER_THRESHOLD env var (read once at daemon startup) applies, else 10. A positive integer overrides the env var and is read on each check() call.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: integer in [0, 100000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.
  - Environment: `GOODVIBES_CHAT_LIMITER_THRESHOLD` (a positive setting wins over the variable).

- `runtime.eventBus.maxListeners`: Maximum number of listeners per event channel (per-type and per-domain) before a warning is emitted in production or a RangeError is thrown in development mode. Raise this only if you have verified there is no subscriber leak.
  - type `number`; default `100`; allowed: integer in [1, 100000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `runtime.maxParallelToolCalls`: Most tool calls of one model response that run at the same time. Reads run side by side, and so do writes to files that do not overlap; a command, an action the owner decides and a tool with undeclared effects always run alone, in the order the model asked. 1 runs every call one after another. Applies to the main session, sub-agents and companion chat; read once per response.
  - type `number`; default `8`; allowed: integer in [1, 64].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `runtime.mcpLifecycle`: Reconnect an MCP server automatically when its connect fails or its process exits: exponential back-off from 1 s to 30 s, at most 5 attempts, then the server stays disconnected and a call to it says why and to run /mcp reload. Each server's state (connecting, connected, degraded, reconnecting, disconnected) shows in /mcp servers, the MCP workspace, the mcp tool and the health view. Read each time a server drops, so a change applies to the next drop. Default on. Off: a server that drops stays disconnected until /mcp reload.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `runtime.pluginLifecycle`: Publishes each plugin's lifecycle (loading, loaded, active, error, unloading, disabled, with the reason) as plugin events: the runtime store's plugin view, automation triggers on plugin loaded or failed, and tracing read them. Read at each event, so a change applies at once. Off: plugins load, run and unload the same, and nothing is reported. Default on.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `runtime.toolBudget.enforced`: Enforce per-call budgets on tool execution: wall-clock, token, and cost limits (runtime.toolBudget.maxMs/maxTokens/maxCostUsd). The wall-clock limit stops a call when it is reached and tells the model what it was stopped by. A call that finishes anyway, or finishes over its token or cost limit (known only when the tool returns), is reported to the model as succeeded, with its output and a note naming the limit it went over; token and cost apply only to tools that report tokenCount or costUsd.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `runtime.toolBudget.maxCostUsd`: Cost budget (USD) for one tool call when runtime.toolBudget.enforced is true, checked when the tool returns against the costUsd the result reports. 0 = unlimited.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: number in [0, 1000000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `runtime.toolBudget.maxMs`: Wall-clock budget (ms) for one tool call when runtime.toolBudget.enforced is true: the call is stopped when it is reached. 0 = unlimited.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: integer in [0, 86400000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `runtime.toolBudget.maxTokens`: Token budget for one tool call when runtime.toolBudget.enforced is true, checked when the tool returns against the tokenCount the result reports. 0 = unlimited.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: integer in [0, 100000000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `runtime.unifiedTasks`: The unified RuntimeTask interface used for task tracking across all subsystems (exec, agent, acp, scheduler, daemon, mcp, plugin, integration), including the /tasks command and operator interventions (cancel/pause/resume/retry). Restart to apply. Default on. Set false to turn the runtime task manager off.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

### sandbox

- `sandbox.egressAllowlist`: Commands the exec sandbox lets reach the network, by base name; every other sandboxed command runs with the network off. The entry * lets every command reach the network. Applies from the next command.
  - type `array`; default `[]`; allowed: list of non-empty command names, for example ["git", "npm"].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would let another command reach the network from the sandbox counts as loosening security.

- `sandbox.enabled`: Master switch for the per-command exec sandbox (bubblewrap on Linux): the workspace is writable, the rest of the filesystem is read-only, /tmp is isolated, and network is disabled unless a command is on sandbox.egressAllowlist. Default ON where the host probe passes; honestly reported unavailable when bubblewrap is not present, leaving the exec path unchanged. Turning it on takes effect at the next start (the host is probed then); sandbox.egressAllowlist and sandbox.workspaceWritable apply from the next command.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it only to a stricter value; a change that would turn the sandbox off counts as loosening security.

- `sandbox.judgment`: Model-judgment pass on sandbox escalation asks: off (plain asks), annotate (default, a proposed verdict with stated reasons annotates the ask, the human still decides), or auto-approve (additionally auto-approves looks-safe verdicts; explicit opt-in). Never auto-denies and never touches the frozen catastrophic block; every judgment leaves a receipt.
  - type `enum`; default `"annotate"`; allowed: `off`, `annotate`, `auto-approve`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would let a model approve sandbox escalations counts as loosening security.

- `sandbox.mcpIsolation`: How stdio MCP servers start: disabled runs each as a host process; contained runs each inside its own bubblewrap boundary (workspace and sandbox.workspaceWritable writable, system files and the server's own install read-only, $HOME and /tmp private, host network shared). On a host without bubblewrap a contained server is not started and its status says why. Applies when a server next connects.
  - type `enum`; default `"disabled"`; allowed: `disabled`, `contained`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would change a safety-gate setting counts as loosening security.

- `sandbox.workspaceWritable`: Extra absolute paths the exec sandbox lets commands write besides the workspace. Applies from the next command.
  - type `array`; default `[]`; allowed: list of absolute paths.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it; a change that would let sandboxed commands write another path counts as loosening security.

### security

- `security.tokenAudit.enabled`: Audit API tokens for minimum-scope violations and overdue rotation, surfacing age, scope, and rotation warnings in diagnostics with typed security events. Default on in advisory mode: tokens are reported, never blocked, unless security.tokenAudit.managed is also true.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `security.tokenAudit.managed`: When true (and security.tokenAudit.enabled is on), tokens with excess scopes or overdue rotation are BLOCKED from use rather than only reported. Default false = advisory reporting only.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `security.tokenAudit.rotationCadenceDays`: Default rotation cadence (days) for the token audit: a token older than this is reported overdue. Per-policy rotationCadenceMs overrides this default. Only enforced (blocking) when security.tokenAudit.managed is also true.
  - type `number`; default `90`; allowed: integer in [1, 3650].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `security.tokenAudit.rotationWarningDays`: Default lead time (days) before the rotation-cadence due date at which a token is reported as a rotation warning. Per-policy rotationWarningThresholdMs overrides this default.
  - type `number`; default `14`; allowed: integer in [0, 3650].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

### service

- `service.autostart`: Whether the daemon's service starts on its own at login. The daemon applies every change, however it is set (a settings screen, /settings set in either terminal program, goodvibes-daemon config set, the API, or an edit of the daemon's settings file): on installs the service when it is not installed and enables it at login (systemd enable; a LaunchAgent with RunAtLoad); off disables it at login and leaves it installed and running. A value set while no daemon runs is applied when the daemon next starts. goodvibes-daemon install-service turns it on and uninstall-service off. A Windows logon task starts at login while installed whatever its value. A daemon setting, in the daemon's settings file.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `service.enabled`: Whether this machine runs the daemon as a service. On, a daemon started by hand installs the service at its first idle moment and doctor reports a missing or stopped service; off (the installers' --no-service, or goodvibes-daemon uninstall-service), nothing installs one and doctor does not ask for one. goodvibes-daemon install-service turns it on. A daemon setting: one value every program and installer reads, in the daemon's settings file.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `service.logPath`: File path for daemon/service logs (empty = platform default under the configured service directory)
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `service.platform`: Target service manager platform.
  - type `enum`; default `"auto"`; allowed: `auto`, `systemd`, `launchd`, `windows`, `manual`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `service.restartOnFailure`: Restart the service automatically after failure.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `service.serviceName`: Name of the daemon's service unit, used by the installer, the daemon's and the terminal apps' service commands and onboarding alike. Empty (the default) uses goodvibes (goodvibes.service under systemd) on Linux and Windows, and sh.goodvibes.daemon (the launchd label) on macOS.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.imap.secure`: Connect to IMAP over TLS.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.imap.user`: IMAP account name, overriding surfaces.email.user.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.accounts`: JSON array of configured mailbox account identifiers to watch for inbound mail, e.g. ["primary"]. The first names the daemon's own mailbox; empty labels it with the mail user. A list rather than a single switch because one address for signups and another for the owner's real mail is the expected shape. The first entry is the daemon's own mailbox (surfaces.email.*, or Gmail when Google is connected); every further entry is watched over IMAP with the connection surfaces.email.inbound.mailboxes gives it, and one without an entry there is reported in inbound mail status rather than watched.
  - type `string`; default `"[]"`; allowed: a JSON array of account names, e.g. ["primary"].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.capabilityRecheckMinutes`: How often a mailbox that reported it cannot do what inbound mail requires (for example a Gmail grant that authorizes listing but not reading message bodies, or a mailbox that does not exist) is re-probed. Long enough that a refused account is not hammered in a tight loop; short enough that fixing the underlying scope or account problem is noticed without a daemon restart.
  - type `number`; default `60`; allowed: integer in [5, 1440].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.dedupTtlMinutes`: How long an inbound message's identity is remembered, inside the running daemon, so an overlapping poll or a retried pass does not process it twice. This cache lives in memory only: a restart destroys it rather than expiring it, so no value here prevents a duplicate across a restart, the inbound record store does that, by remembering which messages were already announced. Seconds would be enough for what this covers; a larger value only costs a little memory.
  - type `number`; default `60`; allowed: integer in [5, 1440].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.enabled`: Turns on inbound notices: arriving mail is matched against open verification expectations, recorded and announced, and further accounts below are watched. Off by default. The daemon's own mailbox is read by one reader for the inbox as well whenever it is configured; this switch decides whether that mail is also announced.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.expectationWindowMinutes`: Default lifetime, in minutes, of a verification expectation opened for inbound-mail matching (for example an account signup awaiting its confirmation email). Raising it gives a slower-to-arrive confirmation more time to match; lowering it shrinks how long a stale expectation can be satisfied by a late message. Hard-capped at 60 to match MAX_VERIFICATION_WINDOW_MS. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `15`; allowed: integer in [1, 60].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.gmailPollSecondsExpecting`: How often the Gmail source asks Google what changed while something is actually being waited for, a signup mid-flight whose verification mail has not arrived yet. This is polling, not push: mail can sit unnoticed for up to this many seconds, and no setting makes Gmail faster than the interval. Five seconds is the floor worth having for a person watching a signup form; the underlying call costs 2 quota units against a daily budget in the billions, so a shorter interval buys latency rather than saving quota. Ignored entirely when the IMAP source is in use, which pushes instead.
  - type `number`; default `5`; allowed: integer in [2, 60].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.gmailPollSecondsIdle`: How often the Gmail source asks Google what changed when nothing is being waited for. Again polling, not push: with nothing pending, mail is noticed up to this many seconds after it arrives. A minute keeps the daemon from asking Google every five seconds all week for mail nobody is waiting on; lowering it narrows that gap at the cost of a request every few seconds around the clock. Ignored entirely when the IMAP source is in use.
  - type `number`; default `60`; allowed: integer in [10, 3600].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.idleReissueMinutes`: How often an open IDLE connection is torn down and re-issued. RFC 2177 advises re-issuing at least every 29 minutes, or the server may silently log the connection off; raising this toward 29 trims reconnect churn but leaves less margin against a slow round trip.
  - type `number`; default `27`; allowed: integer in [5, 29].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.mailboxes`: JSON object giving each account after the first in surfaces.email.inbound.accounts its own IMAP mailbox, e.g. {"signups":{"host":"imap.example.com","user":"signups@example.com"}}. Fields: host and user (required), port (default 993, or 143 when secure is false), secure (default true; false only for a loopback host), mailbox (default INBOX) and passwordRef, a goodvibes://secrets/goodvibes/<KEY> reference whose key contains EMAIL, MAIL or IMAP as a word. Without passwordRef the password is read from the secret GOODVIBES_EMAIL_INBOUND_<ACCOUNT>_PASSWORD (the account name upper-cased, other characters as _). Each mailbox is watched with the same inbound settings as the first, and a change here takes effect without a restart.
  - type `string`; default `"{}"`; allowed: a JSON object mapping account names to {"host":"…","user":"…"}, with optional port, secure, mailbox and passwordRef.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.maxRecords`: Hard cap on the number of inbound mail records kept regardless of age. Whichever of this and retentionDays is reached first wins, so this bounds worst-case storage even under a burst of mail. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `5000`; allowed: integer in [100, 100000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.mode`: How the IMAP source receives new mail: "idle" holds a persistent IMAP IDLE connection, "poll" checks on a timer, "auto" uses IDLE when the server advertises it and falls back to polling when it does not. Leave at auto unless a specific provider needs to be forced one way. Applies only to the IMAP source; the Gmail source has no IDLE to hold and is always polled, on the two intervals above.
  - type `enum`; default `"auto"`; allowed: `idle`, `poll`, `auto`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.notice.mode`: How much inbound mail generates an owner notice: "all" announces every message, "expected-only" announces only mail matching a registered expectation (quieter for a high-volume mailbox), "none" announces nothing. Choosing "none" means mail can arrive with no notice at all, a deliberate but silent choice.
  - type `enum`; default `"all"`; allowed: `all`, `expected-only`, `none`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.notice.route`: Where the owner is told about inbound mail: the literal "default" uses the owner's most recently used one-to-one conversation with the daemon (never a group or shared channel); a specific route binding id, shared or not, sends inbound-mail notices there instead. A second place to configure "where to reach me" is a second place to get it wrong, so most installations should leave this at default.
  - type `string`; default `"default"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.onInsufficientCapability`: "refuse-and-notify" stops the watcher for that account and tells the owner once, naming what is missing and the exact step to fix it, the account is not watched again until the recheck above finds it fixed. "notice-only" is a deliberate downgrade: it keeps announcing that mail arrived using envelope fields alone (sender, subject, delivery evidence), stating plainly in every notice that bodies are unavailable, and it can never satisfy a verification expectation while degraded, an account signup or order confirmation will not work under it. "notice-only" applies to exactly one condition: a Google grant that authorizes message headers and excludes message bodies (the gmail.metadata scope), which is the only case where mail can be seen arriving without being readable. Every other insufficient condition, no stored password, a refused sign-in, a mailbox that will not open, a lost cursor, a refused or unreadable fetch, leaves no envelope fields to announce, so "notice-only" behaves as "refuse-and-notify" there and the notice says which one is in force.
  - type `enum`; default `"refuse-and-notify"`; allowed: `refuse-and-notify`, `notice-only`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.pollIntervalSeconds`: How often the fallback poller checks the mailbox when IDLE is unavailable. Lower is more responsive but closer to a provider's rate limit; higher delays notice of new mail by up to this many seconds. Only applies when the connection is not using IDLE.
  - type `number`; default `120`; allowed: integer in [30, 3600].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.reconnect.maxBackoffSeconds`: Ceiling on the exponential reconnect backoff after a dropped connection or provider error. Raising it tolerates a longer provider outage without hammering it; lowering it shortens the worst-case silence after a disconnect at the cost of retrying a still-down server more often.
  - type `number`; default `300`; allowed: integer in [10, 3600].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.retentionDays`: How many days an inbound mail record (sender, subject, delivery evidence, link verdicts, never the full body) is kept before it is reaped. Longer keeps a longer history to explain "why did I get that message"; shorter bounds how much of the owner's mail metadata the daemon retains. Applies after the daemon restarts.
  - type `number`; default `30`; allowed: integer in [1, 365].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inbound.source`: Which mechanism reads the mailbox. "auto" uses Gmail when Google credentials have been adopted and the configured mail account is a Gmail account, and IMAP otherwise, so connecting Google is the whole of the setup and no IMAP host, username or app password has to be found. "gmail" and "imap" force one of them. The two are not equivalent and the difference is a real cost: IMAP holds an IDLE connection, which is true push and delivers in under a second, while Gmail has no push available to a daemon on a home machine and is POLLED on a timer, its worst-case delay is the whole poll interval below, never less. Forcing "gmail" without adopted Google credentials, or on an account that is not a Gmail account, is refused rather than quietly served over IMAP.
  - type `enum`; default `"auto"`; allowed: `auto`, `gmail`, `imap`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `surfaces.email.inboxTagging`: Write triage labels (GoodVibes/Spam, Priority, Normal) back to the mailbox as IMAP keywords on the messages they label. Off: labels stay in GoodVibes and channels.inbox.applyLabels refuses for this account.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.
