### telemetry

- `telemetry.decisionOtlpEnabled`: Export permission/policy decision-log records to an OTLP endpoint (export-only, no ingestion). Requires telemetry.decisionOtlpEndpoint.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `telemetry.decisionOtlpEndpoint`: OTLP/HTTP JSON endpoint base for decision-log export (empty = disabled). Spans POST to <base>/v1/traces, logs to <base>/v1/logs.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `telemetry.decisionOtlpSignal`: Which OTLP record shape each decision is emitted as: span, log, or both.
  - type `enum`; default `"span"`; allowed: `span`, `log`, `both`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `telemetry.includeRawPrompts`: Allow raw telemetry reads from this daemon while enabled. Default false rejects raw reads; safe views always redact content. HTTP raw reads also require read:telemetry and an admin session or read:telemetry-sensitive scope. Active raw streams stop after this opt-in is revoked. Raw prompts may contain private data. Enabling the setting at startup emits a WARN log.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `telemetry.otelMode`: OpenTelemetry instrumentation: off (default, no OTel SDK initialization; a daemon left at the default records spans in-process so its telemetry traces list answers, and setting off explicitly turns that off too), in-process (spans for LLM calls, turns, tool calls, agents, tasks, plugins, MCP servers, transport, permission checks, sessions, compaction and health cascades, recorded and exported in-process only; a turn span records the prompt length, not its text), or remote-export (additionally export spans as OTLP/HTTP JSON to the collector named by OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT, or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT with /v1/traces appended). Switching away from off requires a restart; in-process <-> remote-export applies live.
  - type `enum`; default `"off"`; allowed: `off`, `in-process`, `remote-export`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

### tools

- `tools.autoHeal`: When a write or edit fails validation, try the project's own formatter, then its linter fix, then a model repair, each from the content as written; a repair is kept only when it fixes the errors and changes nothing else. The formatter and linter run inside a bubblewrap boundary with no network and nothing writable but their own copy of the file; where none can be built they are skipped with a warning.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `tools.defaultTokenBudget`: Optional token budget for precision read operations; 0 includes the complete result.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: non-negative safe integer; 0 means unlimited.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `tools.hooksFile`: Hook configuration file name, relative to the project working directory (so the default is <project>/hooks.json, not a file under .goodvibes)
  - type `string`; default `"hooks.json"`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `tools.hostedResearchScreening`: Explicitly allow raw research report text and source URLs to be screened by Abacus route-llm and TypeSafe Jev. Providers manage retention; zero retention is unverified. Requires native ABACUSAI_API_KEY and TYPESAFE_API_KEY credentials. Covers research report preview, save, and the research editor only.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in Agent's own file only (`~/.goodvibes/agent/settings.json`); the other programs do not have this setting.
  - A project file may not set it.

- `tools.llmEnabled`: Uses a separate model for GoodVibes's own background work; off, that work uses the conversation's model when it needs one.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `tools.llmModel`: That separate model; empty uses the provider's fastest.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `tools.llmProvider`: The provider of that separate model; empty uses the conversation's provider.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `tools.outputSchemaFingerprints`: Append _meta.outputSchemaFingerprint (exact sorted result key names) and _meta.schemaShapeId to results from the find, analyze, and inspect tools, enabling schema drift detection. Default off.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `tools.overflowSpillBackend`: Where large tool-output overflow content spills: file (on-disk .overflow, default), ledger (execution ledger), or diagnostics. An injected custom backend still takes precedence.
  - type `enum`; default `"file"`; allowed: `file`, `ledger`, `diagnostics`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `tools.validators.build`: Command the write and edit tools run for validate "build" in a project that declares no build command of its own (no package.json script, Cargo or Go toolchain, Makefile target or pyproject tool), e.g. "pnpm -r build" for a monorepo whose scripts live in its packages. Split like a shell command line, without pipes or substitution, and run through the exec tool's own path. Your own settings only: a project settings file cannot set a command. Empty: the validator is refused with what the project does declare.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `tools.validators.lint`: Command the write and edit tools run for validate "lint" in a project that declares no lint command of its own (no package.json script, Cargo or Go toolchain, Makefile target or pyproject tool), e.g. "pnpm -r lint" for a monorepo whose scripts live in its packages. Split like a shell command line, without pipes or substitution, and run through the exec tool's own path. Your own settings only: a project settings file cannot set a command. Empty: the validator is refused with what the project does declare.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `tools.validators.test`: Command the write and edit tools run for validate "test" in a project that declares no test command of its own (no package.json script, Cargo or Go toolchain, Makefile target or pyproject tool), e.g. "pnpm -r test" for a monorepo whose scripts live in its packages. Split like a shell command line, without pipes or substitution, and run through the exec tool's own path. Your own settings only: a project settings file cannot set a command. Empty: the validator is refused with what the project does declare.
  - type `string`; default `""`.

  - type `enum`; default `"panel"`; allowed: `panel`, `conversation`, `both`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

- `ui.voiceEnabled`: Enable the optional local-first voice control surface.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may set it.

### update

- `update.alertAfterFailedChecks`: Consecutive failed update checks before the daemon tells the owner over a channel that still works that it can no longer update itself. Lower is louder; 1 reports the first failure. A repeat is held back for 12 hours so an ongoing outage is one message rather than one an hour.
  - type `number`; default `3`; allowed: integer in [1, 100].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `update.applyTimeoutMs`: Maximum milliseconds the terminal app and the Agent spend downloading, verifying and swapping in a new release at launch. Past it, an update that has not started replacing files is cancelled and tried at the next launch; one already replacing files finishes in the background and says so when it is done.
  - type `number`; default `45000`; allowed: integer in [5000, 300000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `update.auto`: While-running self-update of this installation (the daemon, and the Agent): check for a new release hourly, download and checksum-verify it, swap at a no-active-work moment, and restart (the previous binary is kept for one-command rollback). A daemon setting: one value for every program on this machine, kept in the daemon's settings file; a project settings file cannot set it. The release installer's --no-auto-update sets it false.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `update.autoUpdateAtLaunch`: The terminal app and the Agent check for and install a newer release at launch. Set false to disable launch updates; the Agent's while-running updates also stop unless update.auto is explicitly set. A daemon setting: one value for every program on this machine, kept in the daemon's settings file; a project settings file cannot set it. The release installer's --no-auto-update sets it false.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `update.firstCheckSeconds`: Seconds after daemon start before the FIRST update check (a boot-settle delay, so a daemon that was down while releases shipped does not stay stale for a whole interval). Capped at one check interval.
  - type `number`; default `30`; allowed: integer in [0, 3600].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `update.intervalMinutes`: Minutes between daemon update checks.
  - type `number`; default `60`; allowed: integer in [5, 1440].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `update.launchCheckTimeoutMs`: Maximum milliseconds spent checking for a terminal update at launch; the installed version starts if the check cannot complete.
  - type `number`; default `2500`; allowed: integer in [250, 30000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `update.releasesUrl`: GitHub releases/latest URL for a complete GoodVibes monorepo suite. Exact historical default feeds migrate to goodvibes. Native suite updates replace installed sibling programs and configured release WebUI/browser support together. Must be a release URL of the GoodVibes repository itself (https://github.com/mgd34msu/goodvibes/releases/...), or an http URL on this machine (loopback address) (empty turns the update loop off): the binaries and checksums are downloaded from this origin and are not signed, so any other repository or remote host would let a config write replace the installed programs.
  - type `string`; default `"https://github.com/mgd34msu/goodvibes/releases/latest"`; allowed: https://github.com/mgd34msu/goodvibes/releases/... (or http on 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1]) without credentials, or empty to turn the update loop off.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `update.rollbackAfterFailedStarts`: Consecutive rapid boots that fail to reach a fully-started daemon before the startup path automatically restores the kept previous binary and restarts onto it. 0 leaves a bad update in place for a hand-run rollback.
  - type `number`; default `3`; allowed: integer in [0, 10].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

### voice

- `voice.local.sttBinary`: Where the speech-to-text program is (a full path, for example whisper.cpp's whisper-cli). Managed setup installs the engine and sets this.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.local.sttEngine`: The program that turns your speech into text on this computer: whisper-cpp (the default; runs on the processor, fast enough for live speech) or faster-whisper (for NVIDIA graphics cards, through a wrapper script). Empty means not configured, and the machine says so honestly rather than erroring. Managed setup installs whisper-cpp and fills this in.
  - type `enum`; default `""`; allowed: ``, `whisper-cpp`, `faster-whisper`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.local.sttModelPath`: Where the speech-to-text model file is (a full path, for example ggml-tiny.en.bin). Managed setup downloads the model, checksum-verifies it and sets this path; a path you set yourself is kept unless it names an install the managed runtime replaces, which is reported when it happens.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.local.ttsBinary`: Where the text-to-speech program is (a full path, for example piper). Managed setup installs the engine and sets this.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.local.ttsEngine`: The program that reads answers aloud on this computer: piper (the default; starts speaking almost at once) or kokoro (a better-sounding voice, through a wrapper script). Empty means not configured. Managed setup installs piper and fills this in.
  - type `enum`; default `""`; allowed: ``, `piper`, `kokoro`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.local.ttsModelPath`: Where the voice model file is (a full path, for example en_US-lessac-low.onnx, with its .json file beside it). Managed setup downloads the voice, checksum-verifies it and sets this path; a path you set yourself is kept unless it names an install the managed runtime replaces, which is reported when it happens.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.activationSound`: Sound played the moment a wake is confirmed. "chime" by default because audible confirmation is how a user knows the microphone acted, a silent wake is the behaviour people distrust. "custom" plays voice.wake.activationSoundPath; "none" is silent and leaves voice.wake.indicator as the only feedback.
  - type `enum`; default `"chime"`; allowed: `none`, `chime`, `custom`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.activationSoundPath`: Absolute path to the audio file played on wake. Read only when voice.wake.activationSound is "custom"; ignored otherwise. A host surface plays the file through the same player local voice output uses. A browser tab cannot read a path on your machine, so it plays the built-in chime instead and reports that this row is not in force there, a wake stays audible either way.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.autoSubmit`: Submit the transcribed text as a turn automatically instead of placing it in the input for review. Applies to the utterance captured after a WAKE; push-to-talk always places its transcript in the composer, because a person who pressed a key is already looking at the screen. Off by default, matching the never-auto-send posture of the existing voice input: a misheard transcript must not become a submitted turn without a human seeing it first.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.browserBackend`: Execution backend for the detector inside a browser tab. "wasm" is the default and the measured configuration: the per-frame cost already beats real time by a wide margin, and WebGPU cannot run the front end without splitting the graph across devices, which costs more in transfers than it saves. "webgpu" is available for hosts that measure otherwise. Read by the browser tab when it creates its inference sessions; a host surface always runs WASM and ignores this row. BOTH VALUES LOAD THE SAME ENGINE BINARY, the WebGPU-capable build carries the CPU engine too, so switching costs no extra download, and a tab set to "webgpu" on a browser without navigator.gpu falls back to the CPU provider inside the binary it already has.
  - type `enum`; default `"wasm"`; allowed: `wasm`, `webgpu`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.captureCommand`: Which recorder feeds capture on a HOST surface, the terminal and the daemon child process. A browser tab ignores this row and uses getUserMedia. Feeds both consumers: wake detection and push-to-talk voice input. "auto" probes for pw-record, parecord, arecord, ffmpeg, then sox and uses the first present, mirroring how local audio playback discovers its player. Name one explicitly to pin the choice on a host where the probe picks a device-starved backend; a named recorder that is not installed reports that instead of quietly falling back, because pinning it was the point.
  - type `enum`; default `"auto"`; allowed: `auto`, `pw-record`, `parecord`, `arecord`, `ffmpeg`, `sox`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.captureMaxSeconds`: Hard ceiling on how long capture runs before it stops on its own. Bounds memory and guarantees a stuck or silent stream cannot hold the microphone open indefinitely. Applies to post-wake capture AND to push-to-talk, where a key-release event that never arrives would otherwise leave the device open. 0 REMOVES THE CEILING: speech-to-text imposes no length limit of its own, so the ceiling is policy rather than a technical bound, and a long dictated thought is a real thing to want. It still defaults to 10 because the ceiling is the backstop for the OTHER stop condition failing. Post-wake capture normally ends about voice.wake.silenceStopMs after you stop talking, which depends on frames reading as silence, with the ceiling off, a stream that goes stuck or a room the silence floor cannot resolve holds the microphone open with nothing left to close it. Turn it off alongside a silence-stop you have seen work in your room; voice.wake.silenceFloorRms is the row that makes that reliable.
  - type `number`; default `10`; allowed: integer in [0, 120].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.cooldownMs`: Milliseconds after a confirmed wake during which further detections are ignored, so one spoken phrase cannot fire twice as it passes through the detector's rolling window. Applied after patience confirms a hit. 0 disables the cooldown and lets every confirmed frame fire.
  - type `number`; default `2000`; allowed: integer in [0, 60000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.crashWindowSeconds`: Rolling window in which repeated crashes count toward voice.wake.maxRestarts. Exceeding the ceiling inside this window latches the supervisor off so a detector that cannot stay up stops consuming the device; a clean run past the window resets the count.
  - type `number`; default `60`; allowed: integer in [1, 3600].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.customModelDir`: Directory searched for wake models whose ids are not the pinned default. Empty uses the managed wake model directory under the surface storage root. Set it to keep your own models outside the managed tree; files there are loaded as-is and are not checksum-pinned, unlike the managed download.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.enabled`: Listens all the time for the wake phrase on the chosen microphone. Turning it on starts a supervised capture process and a persistent listening indicator; turning it off stops it and releases the device immediately. WHERE IT LISTENS depends on the voice.wake.surfaces.* rows: the terminal captures through a recorder subprocess and is on by default, the agent captures the same way and is opted in per surface, and a browser tab captures through getUserMedia and is opted in per origin. Off by default because an always-on microphone must be an explicit act, not something a user discovers after the fact. THE MODEL IS ALREADY THERE: installing goodvibes downloads and checksum-verifies the pinned classifier, and a daemon retries at boot if the install could not reach the network, so turning this on normally needs no setup step at all. Turning it on in the terminal app or Agent (settings, /settings, a model's settings call) runs the same setup as /voice wake-setup: it turns the wake rows on, fetches any missing wake-word model files and shows the plan; installing a speech-to-text engine is only proposed.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.indicator`: How the surface shows that the microphone is live. "statusline" keeps a persistent listening marker for as long as the detector runs, not only at the moment of a wake, so an always-on microphone is never invisible: a footer row in the terminal, a status-strip chip in the web UI. "banner" is more prominent; "off" removes the marker entirely and is not the default for that reason.
  - type `enum`; default `"statusline"`; allowed: `off`, `statusline`, `banner`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.inputDevice`: Capture device to listen on. Empty means the operating system default source. Shared by BOTH microphone consumers: wake detection and push-to-talk voice input open the same device through the same path, so this row moves both rather than only the always-on one. Device identifiers are host-specific, list real ones with `pactl list short sources` or `arecord -L`, or use a navigator.mediaDevices deviceId in a browser tab. Note pw-record takes a PipeWire node serial or node name here, not a PulseAudio device name, and sox cannot target a device at all (it reads AUDIODEV from the environment), which the surface reports rather than silently ignoring.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.maxRestarts`: How many times the supervisor restarts a crashed detector process inside voice.wake.crashWindowSeconds before it stops trying and reports the failure. Matches the restart ceiling used for MCP clients. 0 disables restarts, so any crash is terminal and immediately visible.
  - type `number`; default `3`; allowed: integer in [0, 20].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.models`: The wake-word models to listen with, by name, separated by commas. Default "hey_goodvibes" is the model the platform pins, hosts, and verifies by checksum. Additional ids resolve against voice.wake.customModelDir. Each model costs one classifier inference per 80 ms frame, the shared melspectrogram and speech-embedding front end is computed once regardless of how many models are listed, so a second model is far cheaper than a second detector. An empty list disables detection without stopping the service. Ids are letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen only, since each becomes a file name.
  - type `string`; default `"hey_goodvibes"`; allowed: comma-separated ids made of letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen (no path separators)
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.noiseSuppression`: Noise suppression applied to captured audio before anything reads it, the wake classifier scores filtered frames, and the utterance recorded after a wake (and push-to-talk voice input) is filtered audio too. "speex" is SpeexDSP's own denoiser, carried in the platform as a WebAssembly module and applied on every surface that has WebAssembly, which is both shipped ones: nothing to install, nothing to download, no per-host library. It attenuates the estimated noise floor by about 15 dB, measured at 13.2 dB against a synthetic tone-plus-white-noise set, for 0.24 ms of work per 80 ms frame beside the detector's own 3.46 ms. "none" ships as the default and is a true passthrough: the captured bytes reach the detector exactly as the device produced them. Choose "speex" on a noisy input (a fan, an air conditioner, street noise through an open window), and "none" on a quiet one, where a denoiser only has speech to work on.
  - type `enum`; default `"none"`; allowed: `none`, `speex`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.patienceFrames`: Consecutive 80 ms frames that must all score above voice.wake.threshold before the wake fires. Two frames is about 160 ms of agreement, which removes most single-frame false accepts for one extra frame of latency. Set to 1 for the fastest possible trigger at the cost of more spurious wakes.
  - type `number`; default `2`; allowed: integer in [1, 10].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.preRollMs`: Milliseconds of audio kept from BEFORE the wake fired and prepended to the speech-to-text request, so a phrase run straight into the command ("hey goodvibes, what's—") is not clipped at the front. 500 ms covers the detector's own confirmation latency plus a fast speaker. 0 starts capture at the moment of detection.
  - type `number`; default `500`; allowed: integer in [0, 2000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.restartBackoffMs`: Base delay before restarting a crashed detector, multiplied by the attempt number for linear backoff (2 s, 4 s, 6 s). Stops a process that fails instantly from becoming a restart storm.
  - type `number`; default `2000`; allowed: integer in [0, 60000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.retainAudio`: Whether captured audio is written to disk. "none" by default, nothing is stored, which is the only setting under which the microphone leaves no recording behind. "session-temp" keeps clips in a session-scoped directory that is deleted when the session ends and swept on recovery, and exists to debug a bad transcript, not as a recording feature. A browser tab has no filesystem to retain into: it reports that this row is not in force rather than appearing to store clips it is not storing.
  - type `enum`; default `"none"`; allowed: `none`, `session-temp`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.silenceFloorRms`: The audio level at or below which a frame counts as silence, on the int16 magnitude scale the capture path uses (full scale 32768, so 180 is about -45 dBFS). 0, the default, MEASURES IT PER UTTERANCE from the audio captured just before the wake fired, and places the floor 12 dB above the room's own noise. That measurement is what makes voice.wake.silenceStopMs work at all in a room that is not quiet: with a fixed floor, steady background noise above it means no frame is ever silent, silence never accumulates, and every capture runs to the voice.wake.captureMaxSeconds ceiling however long ago you stopped talking. The floor then FOLLOWS the room for the rest of the capture, tracking the quiet moments in the last second and a half, because a headset with automatic gain control raises the input once you stop talking and the room comes back louder than the number measured before it. It is never raised over a third of the speech being heard at the same time, so it cannot end up above your own voice. Set a number to pin the floor instead, which is worth doing if the measurement guesses wrong in your room: raise it if capture keeps running after you stop, lower it if capture cuts off while you are still speaking. A number you set here is used exactly as given AND frozen, it stays where you put it for the whole capture, with no following. The first measured value is never allowed below 180 or above 1440; the following that comes after it may reach 5760.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: integer in [0, 8000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.silenceStopMs`: Milliseconds of silence that end post-wake capture, so the request is sent when the user stops talking rather than at the voice.wake.captureMaxSeconds ceiling. Raise it if capture cuts off mid-sentence during natural pauses. Post-wake only: push-to-talk ends when the key is released, because someone holding it through a pause has not finished talking.
  - type `number`; default `1200`; allowed: integer in [100, 10000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.speechRetriggerMs`: How long a run of sound above the silence floor has to last before it counts as you talking again. Shorter runs are counted as part of the silence they interrupted rather than starting the voice.wake.silenceStopMs wait over. This is what a close-worn or in-ear microphone needs: a breath, a lip tick or a chair creak is loud and lasts one or two frames, and treating each one as speech means the wait never completes and capture runs to the voice.wake.captureMaxSeconds ceiling every time however long ago you stopped. 150 ms sits under the shortest syllable anyone ends a sentence on and over the longest of those noises. Raise it if capture still will not end in a room full of short noises; lower it if the first word of a resumed sentence gets clipped. 0 turns it off, so every loud frame resets the wait, the behaviour before this row existed.
  - type `number`; default `150`; allowed: integer in [0, 2000].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.surfaces.agent`: Listen for the wake phrase on the agent surface, through a recorder subprocess on the host, the same capture path the terminal uses. Turning this on with voice.wake.enabled opens the microphone on the agent, and a confirmed wake sends the utterance that follows to speech-to-text and puts the transcript into the agent conversation input, or submits it when voice.wake.autoSubmit is on. Off by default because two surfaces on one machine both acting on a single spoken utterance is a confusing default, not because it does not work: turn it on when the agent is the surface you actually talk to, and consider turning voice.wake.surfaces.tui off when you do.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.surfaces.app`: Listen for the wake phrase in the desktop companion app, which runs the detector inside its embedded webview on a WASM backend, the same runtime and download path the web UI uses. Off by default because webview capture is a separate stack with its own microphone permission prompt, it is opted into per install, not inherited from the host. While it is off the webview never calls getUserMedia at all, so no permission prompt appears.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.surfaces.tui`: Listen for the wake phrase on the terminal, through a recorder subprocess on the host. On by default: once wake detection is enabled the terminal is the primary surface, and a wake that reaches no surface is a detector that appears broken. A confirmed wake plays the activation sound, shows the listening indicator, captures the utterance that follows and sends it to speech-to-text, then places the transcript in the composer, or submits it when voice.wake.autoSubmit is on.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.surfaces.webui`: Listen for the wake phrase in the web UI, which runs the detector inside the browser tab on a WASM backend and downloads the pinned model through the daemon. This daemon's setting: once it is on, every browser that opens this daemon's web UI listens, each only after its own microphone permission prompt is accepted. Off by default because browser capture is a separate stack from the terminal's. While it is off a tab never calls getUserMedia at all, so no permission prompt appears. A plain-http origin cannot capture and says so instead of failing silently.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.threshold`: How sure, from 0 to 1, the listener must be before the wake phrase counts as heard. DELIBERATELY 0.9, NOT openWakeWord's upstream default of 0.5 and not the 0.5 originally accepted for this row: measurement on the shipped hey_goodvibes model showed 0.5 fires on 34.5% of never-trained minimal-pair phrases ("hey good vibe check", "hey goodbye vibes", ordinary English a user will actually say) at 99.2% recall, while 0.9 cuts that to 24.7% for 96.8% recall. Trading 2.4 points of recall to remove roughly a third of the wrong wakes is the better default for a microphone that is always on. Lower it toward 0.5 if the detector misses you; raise it above 0.9 if it fires when you did not speak to it. Recall figures here are synthetic-only, no human has recorded the phrase.
  - type `number`; default `0.9`; allowed: number in [0, 1].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `voice.wake.vadThreshold`: Speech-probability floor, 0 to 1, from the speech gate run ahead of the wake classifier; frames below it are withheld from scoring instead of being classified. The gate is our own speech/non-speech head over the SAME embedding the wake classifier consumes, so it costs one extra inference of 0.025 ms per 80 ms frame, beside the detector's own 3.46 ms, and no extra front end. It provisions with the wake models. Measured on 106,390 held-out frames: at 0.3 it passes 96.0% of speech frames and withholds 95.7% of non-speech ones, which is the recommended value; lower passes more speech and screens less, higher screens more and starts costing wakes. 0 is the shipped default and turns the stage off entirely, it is the configuration that has been exercised longest, and a gate can only ever cost you a detection. A surface that has not loaded the gate REFUSES TO START with any value above 0, rather than running unscreened frames through a stage you have configured.
  - type `number`; default `0`; allowed: number in [0, 1].
  - Stored in each program's own file (the terminal app, Agent and the daemon each keep their own value).
  - A project file may not set it.

### watchers

- `watchers.ciPollIntervalMs`: Cadence (ms) for the daemon's recurring CI-watch poll; the poller enforces a 15s floor to respect the status source's rate limits. Read once when the daemon starts: a new value applies after the next restart.
  - type `number`; default `60000`; allowed: integer in [1000, 86400000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.enabled`: Enable managed watcher/listener services (checkpointing and recovery for long-running external sources). Default on: with no watchers configured the framework idles.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.heartbeatIntervalMs`: Heartbeat interval for watcher services in milliseconds.
  - type `number`; default `15000`; allowed: integer in [1000, 3600000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.pollIntervalMs`: Default polling interval in milliseconds for new watchers registered through the API; existing watchers and other registration paths keep their own interval.
  - type `number`; default `60000`; allowed: integer in [1000, 86400000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.recoveryWindowMinutes`: Recovery window for watcher restart and missed-event catch-up.
  - type `number`; default `10`; allowed: integer in [0, 1440].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.backoffLadderMs`: Comma-separated retry ladder in milliseconds, walked one rung per consecutive failure of a trigger check. The default climbs 30s, 60s, 5m, 15m, 60m so a briefly unreachable endpoint recovers fast while a genuinely broken one stops hammering. The last rung repeats until the breaker opens. Read once when the daemon starts; restart to apply a change.
  - type `string`; default `"30000,60000,300000,900000,3600000"`; allowed: comma-separated integers, each 1000..86400000 ms.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.breakerStrikes`: Consecutive check failures that open the trigger's breaker. An open breaker parks the trigger in a visible circuit-open state with the last error attached instead of retrying forever; the operator resets it explicitly. Raise it for a flaky-but-recoverable source, lower it to fail fast. Read once when the daemon starts; restart to apply a change.
  - type `number`; default `5`; allowed: integer in [1, 50].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.defaultCheckIntervalMs`: Cadence used by a condition trigger that does not declare its own interval. This is the steady-state polling rate; the backoff ladder overrides it while a trigger is failing.
  - type `number`; default `60000`; allowed: integer in [1000, 86400000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.enabled`: Enable the trigger family: stream watchers over long-lived commands, model-free condition checks, and one-shot on-exit process triggers. Off by default because a trigger launches and supervises real processes on your machine without a person watching, turning it on is a deliberate choice, not a fallback. With it on and no triggers defined, the supervisor idles and consumes nothing.
  - type `boolean`; default `false`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.eventLogLimit`: Entries retained in the shared event log that cross-watcher correlation rules read. This log is the only channel through which one trigger can observe another, and it is bounded so correlation cannot grow without limit. Read once when the daemon starts; restart to apply a change.
  - type `number`; default `500`; allowed: integer in [10, 50000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.eventLogTtlHours`: Age ceiling in hours on the shared correlation event log. Correlation windows longer than this cannot see the older side of the pair, so raise it together with any long correlation window. Read once when the daemon starts; restart to apply a change.
  - type `number`; default `24`; allowed: integer in [1, 2160].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.maxConcurrentChecks`: How many condition checks may execute at the same moment. Checks beyond this wait their turn, so a large trigger set cannot saturate the machine or a rate-limited API.
  - type `number`; default `4`; allowed: integer in [1, 64].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.observationRingSize`: Observations kept per trigger in its persisted ring buffer. Every rule, change, transition, rate-of-change, windowed aggregation, is a pure function over this buffer, so this is the memory depth available to them. Larger windows need a larger ring. Read once when the daemon starts; restart to apply a change.
  - type `number`; default `200`; allowed: integer in [2, 10000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.onExitMaxDurationMs`: Hard ceiling on a supervised on-exit child. When it is reached the child is terminated and the trigger fires with an explicit timed-out termination state, so a process waiting on a prompt that will never come cannot hang forever. The six-hour default is sized for a long build.
  - type `number`; default `21600000`; allowed: integer in [1000, 604800000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.onExitStdin`: Standard input handed to a supervised on-exit child. "none" closes stdin so a password-prompting process gets EOF and exits instead of blocking forever; "empty" attaches an immediately-closed empty pipe for programs that require a readable stdin handle. There is deliberately no interactive option, nobody is at the keyboard.
  - type `enum`; default `"none"`; allowed: `none`, `empty`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.outputTailBytes`: Bytes of trailing child output carried in an on-exit termination payload. Exit is not success, so the payload always includes this tail for the agent prompt to inspect alongside the exit code and signal.
  - type `number`; default `8192`; allowed: integer in [0, 1048576].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.probeTimeoutMs`: Ceiling on one probe execution (http request, file read, command run, or platform-tool call) before it is abandoned and counted as a failed check. Keeps a hung endpoint from stalling the whole check queue.
  - type `number`; default `15000`; allowed: integer in [250, 600000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.runHistoryLimit`: Run records kept per trigger (when it ran, what it observed, whether it fired, what the action returned). Bounded on purpose: an append-only history is a disk leak with a nicer name. Read once when the daemon starts; restart to apply a change.
  - type `number`; default `50`; allowed: integer in [1, 5000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.runHistoryTtlHours`: Age ceiling in hours on retained run history. Records older than this are reaped by the recovery sweep even when the count limit has not been reached, and the sweep reports how many it removed. Read once when the daemon starts; restart to apply a change.
  - type `number`; default `168`; allowed: integer in [1, 8760].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.streamBatchIntervalMs`: How long a partially filled stream batch waits before it is flushed anyway, so a slow trickle of matches still reaches an agent promptly instead of waiting for the batch to fill.
  - type `number`; default `1000`; allowed: integer in [50, 3600000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.streamBatchLines`: Matched lines gathered into one payload before an agent is invoked. Batching is what keeps a stream watcher from starting one agent turn per log line.
  - type `number`; default `25`; allowed: integer in [1, 10000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.streamQueueLimit`: Matched lines a stream watcher may hold before the oldest are dropped. The queue is bounded so a chatty log cannot exhaust memory; every drop is counted and reported on the trigger record rather than being silent.
  - type `number`; default `1000`; allowed: integer in [1, 1000000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.supervisionTickMs`: How often the supervisor checks whether a supervised on-exit child has terminated and whether any condition check is due. This is the floor on how quickly an on-exit trigger notices its process ended; raise it to trade detection latency for less polling on a machine running long builds. Read once when the daemon starts; restart to apply a change.
  - type `number`; default `1000`; allowed: integer in [250, 300000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `watchers.triggers.sweepIntervalMs`: Cadence of the recurring housekeeping sweep: reap records whose owning process or session is gone, retire fired one-shot triggers, enforce the count and age bounds, and re-validate persisted state by content. A daemon that only sweeps at boot never sweeps. Read once when the daemon starts; restart to apply a change.
  - type `number`; default `300000`; allowed: integer in [10000, 86400000].
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

### web

- `web.enabled`: Declare the browser-based operator surface as switched on (its channel status and delivery policy). Where the web UI is, and every link to it, does not depend on it. This does not bind a listener: the bundle is served by the control-plane listener when controlPlane.webui.serve is true, so who can reach it follows controlPlane.hostMode and controlPlane.host.
  - type `boolean`; default `true`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `web.host`: Host the web UI's development server binds (with web.hostMode custom). Nothing else listens on web.host:web.port, and no link uses it; the served bundle follows controlPlane.host and controlPlane.port.
  - type `string`; default `"127.0.0.1"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `web.hostMode`: Where the web UI's development server listens (local, network or custom), with web.host and web.port; the development server reads it through goodvibes-daemon webui status --json. It is never the web UI's address: the bundle the daemon serves, and every link to it, follow controlPlane.hostMode.
  - type `enum`; default `"local"`; allowed: `local`, `network`, `custom`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `web.port`: Port the web UI's development server binds. The daemon does not bind it and no link, pairing address, goodvibes web or tailscale serve uses it: the bundle the daemon serves is at the control-plane address (controlPlane.port).
  - type `number`; default `3423`; allowed: integer port in [1, 65535]; a port this machine listens on.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `web.publicBaseUrl`: Public base URL for web links and notification deep links, for a web app served somewhere the daemon cannot describe (a tunnel or reverse proxy). Empty (the default) means links are derived: the daemon's own reachable address when it serves the web app (controlPlane.webui.serve), otherwise there is no web app and no link; a link only reachable on this machine is left out of messages read on other devices.
  - type `string`; default `""`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

- `web.staticAssetsDir`: Static asset directory for the embedded web surface (index.html + assets), served when controlPlane.webui.serve is true. Used when controlPlane.webui.bundleDir is empty; that more specific key wins when it names a directory.
  - type `string`; default `"dist/web"`.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

### worktree

- `worktree.setup.carryOverGlobs`: Untracked files copied from the main checkout into a new worktree, as glob patterns. auto (the default, an empty list) copies .env and .env.* when the repository root has them. none copies nothing. A list copies exactly the files those patterns match. Copies stay in the worktree until it is removed.
  - type `array`; default `[]`; allowed: a list of glob patterns such as [".env", "config/*.local.json"], [] for auto, or {"mode":"none"}.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may set it.

- `worktree.setup.commands`: Commands run in a new worktree before an isolated agent starts in it. auto (the default, an empty list) runs the install command each lockfile in the repository names (bun install, npm ci, pnpm, yarn, uv sync, cargo fetch, go mod download; pip install -r requirements.txt only inside an active virtual environment). none runs nothing. A list runs exactly those commands, in order; one that exits non-zero marks the worktree setup failed.
  - type `array`; default `[]`; allowed: a list of shell commands, [] for auto, or {"mode":"none"}.
  - Stored in the daemon file (one value, which all three programs read).
  - A project file may not set it.

## Command line: `goodvibes`

The terminal app's top-level help, then the help page of every command, exactly as `goodvibes --help` and `goodvibes help <command>` print them. Usage lines use `<name>` for a value you supply, `[x]` for something optional and `a|b` for a choice.

### `goodvibes --help`

```
Usage: goodvibes [OPTIONS] [PROMPT]
       goodvibes [OPTIONS] <COMMAND> [ARGS]

Commands:
  tui [path]                 Start the interactive TUI (default)
  run|exec [prompt]          Run non-interactively with text/json/stream-json output
  web                        Show browser surface bind URL and enablement
  service                    Inspect/manage daemon service lifecycle
  status                     Print config, provider, service, and onboarding posture
  doctor                     Print status plus setup warnings
  doctor explain <target>    Explain why a tool/command would be allowed/asked/denied
  doctor routing             Print which model/provider serves which role
  doctor hooks               List registered hooks, their source, and validation status
  onboarding [status]        Open onboarding in the TUI, or print onboarding status
  models [provider]          List/use/pin selectable models and recent model history
  providers                  List/inspect/use provider config/auth posture
  auth                       Inspect and manage local users, sessions, and bootstrap auth
  subscription               Start/finish/logout provider subscription sessions
  secrets                    List, set, link, delete, and test GoodVibes secret refs
  sessions                   List, show, export, or resume saved sessions
  tasks                      List/show in-process tasks or submit a non-interactive task
  acp                        Run as an Agent Client Protocol agent over stdio (for editors)
  host pair|unpair          Review explicit TUI host pairing (--bootstrap-shared; --apply), or forget it
  pair|qrcode                Mint a named device token on the connected host; print its link and QR code
  surfaces                   Inspect/check/enable/disable browser/listener/external surfaces
  listener test              Test HTTP listener/webhook readiness
  control-plane status       Inspect daemon auth, local admin, tokens, and ports
  support-bundle export|inspect|import
                             Move a support snapshot (config + diagnostics + posture)
  remote|bridge              Inspect remote runner/node posture
  hooks validate             Validate hooks.json against the hook loader schema
  plugin init|validate|trust Scaffold, validate, or set what a plugin may do
  plugin bundles ...         Browse/install/uninstall/list SHA-256-pinned capability bundles
  completion <shell>         Generate shell completion script
  help [command]             Print this help or command-specific help
  version                    Print version

Options:
  -m, --model <registryKey>       Override model. provider:model infers --provider
      --provider <id>            Override provider
  -C, --cd <dir>                 Set working directory for this launch
      --working-dir <dir>        Alias for --cd
      --daemon-home <dir>        Override daemon home for daemon-backed commands
  -c, --config <key=value>       Override a config value for this launch
      --enable <feature>         Enable a platform feature for this launch
      --disable <feature>        Disable a platform feature for this launch
  -p, --prompt <text>            Run a non-interactive prompt
      --print                    Alias for non-interactive run mode
  -o, --output <format>          text, json, or stream-json
      --output-format <format>   Alias for --output
      --json                     Alias for --output-format json
      --just-vibes               Work without interrupting you; anything that needs you is held for the end
      --yolo                     Run every action without safety denials for this launch
      --no-alt-screen            Keep output in normal terminal scrollback
      --port <port>              Port for server/web commands
      --hostname <host>          Hostname for server/web commands (--host is an alias)
      --open                     Open browser when supported
  -r, --resume [id|latest]       Resume saved session when supported
  -s, --session <id>             run: attach to a specific session
      --continue                 Continue the latest session when supported
      --fork [id]                Fork session (current or specific id) when supported
      --timeout <duration>       run: stop after this long (90, 90s, 5m, 1h); exits 124
      --max-turns <n>            run: stop after n model answers that still ask for tools; exits 1
      --omit-accumulated         run: with stream-json, leave `accumulated` out of STREAM_DELTA
      --answer-permissions       run: with stream-json, read PERMISSION_ANSWER lines on stdin for owner prompts
  -y, --yes                      Auto-confirm prompts (non-interactive)
      --non-interactive          Disable all interactive prompts (implies --yes)
      --strict                   doctor: also fail on advisory findings, for CI
  -h, --help                     Print help
  -v, --version                  Print version

Examples:
  goodvibes
  goodvibes --no-alt-screen
  goodvibes --cd ~/work/project --model openai:gpt-5.2
  goodvibes onboarding
  goodvibes onboarding status
  goodvibes status
  goodvibes models current
  goodvibes models use openai:gpt-5.2
  goodvibes providers inspect openai
  goodvibes surfaces
  goodvibes surfaces check
  goodvibes surfaces enable web
  goodvibes service check
  goodvibes listener test
  goodvibes control-plane status
  goodvibes subscription providers
  goodvibes subscription login openai start --open
  goodvibes-daemon --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 3421
```

### `goodvibes acp`

```
GoodVibes acp

Run GoodVibes as an Agent Client Protocol agent on stdin/stdout so an ACP editor (Zed and others) can drive it. Stdout carries only protocol frames; messages go to stderr. Ends when the editor closes stdin. Prompt input is text only and session restore (loadSession) is not supported. For an MCP client use `goodvibes-daemon mcp serve`.

Usage:
  goodvibes acp

Examples:
  goodvibes acp
```

### `goodvibes auth`

```
GoodVibes auth

Inspect and manage local admin users, bootstrap auth, and local sessions. Changes are written to the user store; a running host picks them up when it restarts, and its in-memory sessions are not reachable from this command.

Usage:
  goodvibes auth status
  goodvibes auth users
  goodvibes auth sessions
  goodvibes auth add-user <username> [--password <value>|--password-stdin] [--role <role>]
  goodvibes auth delete-user <username>
  goodvibes auth rotate-password <username> [--password <value>|--password-stdin]
  goodvibes auth revoke-session <session-id-or-token>
  goodvibes auth revoke-sessions <username>
  goodvibes auth clear-bootstrap

Examples:
  goodvibes auth
  goodvibes auth add-user admin --password-stdin
  goodvibes auth rotate-password admin --password-stdin
  goodvibes auth clear-bootstrap
```

```
GoodVibes doctor
```

```
GoodVibes host

Usage:

  goodvibes host unpair [--url <exact-origin>]

  goodvibes host unpair
```

### `goodvibes plugin`

Also answers to: `goodvibes plugins`.

```
GoodVibes plugin

Scaffold a minimal valid plugin (manifest.json + entry file), validate a plugin directory against the plugin loader checks, browse/install/uninstall/list SHA-256-pinned capability bundles from a governed marketplace index (--ref picks a git ref when the bundle source is a git remote; without --yes, install prints the activation plan and changes nothing), or set and inspect a plugin's trust tier (what it may register), which every GoodVibes app on this machine applies the next time it starts the plugin. Bundle installs are never unpinned; a missing or mismatched --sha256 is refused, not overridable. Marking a plugin trusted when its signature does not verify needs --yes.

Usage:
  goodvibes plugin init <name> [directory]
  goodvibes plugin validate <path>
  goodvibes plugin bundles browse <index-url-or-file>
  goodvibes plugin bundles install <ref> --sha256 <pin> [--ref <git-ref>] [--yes]
  goodvibes plugin bundles uninstall <id>
  goodvibes plugin bundles list
  goodvibes plugin trust <name> <untrusted|limited|trusted> [note]
  goodvibes plugin verify <name>
  goodvibes plugin capabilities <name>

Examples:
  goodvibes plugin init my-plugin
  goodvibes plugin validate .goodvibes/plugins/my-plugin
  goodvibes plugin bundles browse ./marketplace-index.json
  goodvibes plugin bundles install ./bundle.json --sha256 <64-hex> --yes
  goodvibes plugin bundles uninstall my-bundle
  goodvibes plugin trust my-plugin limited
```

### `goodvibes run`

Also answers to: `goodvibes e`, `goodvibes exec`.

```
GoodVibes run

Run one prompt non-interactively and print the result; the prompt goes straight to the local model. The --intake-* modes work on a prompt captured through native daemon admission: status is read-only and recovery reuses the saved input. Use -- before literal prompt tokens.

Usage:
  goodvibes run [prompt] [--output text|json|stream-json]
  goodvibes exec [prompt]
  goodvibes run --intake-status|--intake-retry|--intake-resume|--intake-cancel
  goodvibes run [prompt] [--timeout <duration>] [--max-turns <n>] [--omit-accumulated] [--answer-permissions]

Examples:
  goodvibes run "summarize the current project"
  goodvibes run --output json "list risks"
  goodvibes exec --output stream-json "fix lint"
```

## Command line: `goodvibes-agent`

Agent's top-level help, then the help page of every command, exactly as `goodvibes-agent --help` and `goodvibes-agent help <command>` print them.

### `goodvibes-agent --help`

```
Usage: goodvibes-agent [OPTIONS] [PROMPT]
       goodvibes-agent [OPTIONS] <COMMAND> [ARGS]

Primary use:
  goodvibes-agent                 Launch the interactive Agent TUI
  goodvibes-agent setup           Open the Agent workspace

Inside the TUI:
  /agent                    Open the operator workspace
  /setup                    Open the Agent workspace
  /model                    Choose provider and model
  /knowledge                Use isolated Agent Knowledge
  /notes                    Open Agent-local scratchpad notes
  /personas, /my-skills     Tune how the Agent talks and what it can do (VIBE.md too)
  /routines                 Run local routines in the main conversation
  /schedule                 Schedule something to run, see, pause, resume, change or remove schedules
  /agents                   Your agents; hand build, fix or review work to the terminal app
  /about-me                 What the platform knows about you
  /agent-home               Separate Agent homes and their starters

Scriptable mirrors:
  run|exec [prompt]          Run non-interactively with text/json/stream-json output
  status                     Print config, provider, auth, and setup posture
  doctor                     Print status plus setup warnings
  setup|onboarding [status]  Open the Agent workspace, or print setup status
  models [provider]          List/use/pin selectable models and recent model history
  providers                  List/inspect/use provider config/auth posture
  profiles                   Manage isolated Agent profile homes
  personas                   Manage local Agent personas
  skills                     Manage local Agent skills and skill bundles
  memory                     Manage Agent-owned durable memory records
  routines                   Inspect local routines and explicitly promote one to a connected schedule
  ci                         Check connected-host CI status and manage standing CI watches
  principals                 Manage the connected-host cross-channel principal identity registry
  owner-profile              Read, trace, correct, and delete what the platform knows about you
  channel-profiles           Manage per-channel model/provider/permission-mode defaults
  workspaces                 Manage which workspaces get automatic checkpoints
  browser                    Drive a real browser from the shell (status|provision|open <url>|read <url>)
  plugin bundles ...         Browse/install/uninstall/list SHA-256-pinned capability bundles
  relay                      Show the connected host's relay registration and pairing (status|pair)
  fleet                      Review and resolve the connected host's best-of-N attempt groups
  auth                       Inspect Agent auth posture and connection token state
  compat                     Inspect connected-host compatibility and Agent Knowledge route readiness
  knowledge                  Use isolated Agent Knowledge routes
  ask|search                 Shortcuts for isolated Agent Knowledge ask/search
  delegate                   Explicitly delegate build/fix/review work to GoodVibes TUI
  subscription               Start/finish/logout provider subscription sessions
  secrets                    List, set, link, delete, and test GoodVibes secret refs
  sessions                   List, show, export, or resume saved sessions
  tasks                      Inspect connected-host task summaries (submission is blocked)
  pair|qrcode                Mint a named device token on the connected host; print its link and QR code
  bundle export|inspect|import
                             Export/inspect bundles; import restores config only
  import openclaw [path]     Migrate an OpenClaw workspace (dry-run default, --apply to write)
  completion <shell>         Generate shell completion script
  help [command]             Print this help or command-specific help
  version                    Print version

Options:
  -m, --model <registryKey>       Override model. provider:model infers --provider
      --provider <id>            Override provider
      --agent-profile <name>     Use an isolated Agent profile home
      --runtime-url <url>        Connected GoodVibes API root
  -C, --cd <dir>                 Set working directory for this launch
      --working-dir <dir>        Alias for --cd
  -c, --config <key=value>       Override a config value for this launch
      --enable <feature>         Enable a feature flag for this launch
      --disable <feature>        Disable a feature flag for this launch
  -p, --prompt <text>            Run a non-interactive prompt
      --print                    Alias for non-interactive run mode
  -o, --output <format>          text, json, or stream-json
      --output-format <format>   Alias for --output
      --json                     Alias for --output-format json
      --no-alt-screen            Keep output in normal terminal scrollback
      --just-vibes               Work without interrupting you; anything that needs you is held for the end
      --yolo                     Run every action without safety denials for this launch
  -r, --resume [id|latest]       Resume saved session when supported
  -s, --session <id>             run: attach to a specific session
      --continue                 run: continue the latest session
      --yes                      Confirm a command that changes state
      --port <n>, --hostname <h> pair: endpoint to print in the pairing payload
      --timeout <duration>       run: stop after this long (90, 90s, 5m, 1h); exits 124
      --max-turns <n>            run: stop after n model answers that still ask for tools; exits 1
      --omit-accumulated         run: with stream-json, leave `accumulated` out of STREAM_DELTA
      --answer-permissions       run: with stream-json, read PERMISSION_ANSWER lines on stdin for owner prompts
  -h, --help                     Print help
  -v, --version                  Print version

Examples:
  goodvibes-agent
  goodvibes-agent --no-alt-screen
  goodvibes-agent --cd ~/work/project --model openai:gpt-5.2
  goodvibes-agent setup
  goodvibes-agent setup status
  goodvibes-agent status
  goodvibes-agent --runtime-url http://127.0.0.1:3421 status
  goodvibes-agent models current
  goodvibes-agent models use openai:gpt-5.2
  goodvibes-agent providers inspect openai
  goodvibes-agent profiles create household --template household --yes
  goodvibes-agent --agent-profile household
  goodvibes-agent personas create --name "Travel Planner" --description "Plan trips" --body "Compare options before booking"
  goodvibes-agent skills create --name "Daily Brief" --description "Summarize operator state" --procedure "Review Agent Knowledge, work plans, approvals, and routines" --requires-env GOODVIBES_AGENT_TOKEN --requires-command gh --enabled
  goodvibes-agent memory add fact "Prefers concise morning briefings" --scope project --tags preference
  goodvibes-agent memory search "morning briefings"
  goodvibes-agent routines promote daily-operations-sweep --cron "0 9 * * *" --timezone America/Chicago --yes
  goodvibes-agent ci status my-org/my-repo --ref main
  goodvibes-agent ci watches create my-org/my-repo --ref main --delivery-channel slack:C123 --yes
  goodvibes-agent principals resolve --channel slack --value U123
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile read
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile provenance commerce.shippingAddress
  goodvibes-agent channel-profiles set slack --model openai:gpt-5.4 --permission-mode plan --yes
  goodvibes-agent fleet attempts list
  goodvibes-agent compat

  goodvibes-agent routines list
```

### `goodvibes-agent fleet`

```
GoodVibes Agent fleet

Review and resolve the best-of-N attempt groups held by the connected host's running contracts (a connected-host call; groups of contracts an open Agent is running are reviewed in that Agent): siblings that ran in isolated worktrees and are held for a winner pick instead of auto-merging. judge runs the optional judge model and PROPOSES a winner (clearly labeled as a model proposal, never an auto-decision); pick is the confirm-gated action that actually merges the winner and cleans losing worktrees.

Usage:
  goodvibes-agent fleet attempts list [--workstream <workstreamId>]
  goodvibes-agent fleet attempts pick <groupId> <winnerItemId> --yes
  goodvibes-agent fleet attempts judge <groupId>

Examples:
  goodvibes-agent fleet attempts list
  goodvibes-agent fleet attempts list --workstream workstream-1
  goodvibes-agent fleet attempts judge group-1
  goodvibes-agent fleet attempts pick group-1 item-2 --yes
```

### `goodvibes-agent import`

```
GoodVibes Agent import

Migrate an OpenClaw workspace into the Agent registries. Dry-run is the default; it prints the personas, memory records, skills, and permission allowlist categories that would be created, plus any skipped files with reasons. Re-run with --apply to write the memory records (to the connected host store when it answers, else to this machine), personas and skills; records already imported are reported as unchanged. Permission categories are granted only with --apply-permissions: each pre-allows every tool in the category for this Agent profile, so the output lists what each grant covers and the /settings reset commands that undo it. Reads ~/.openclaw by default, or a supplied path.

Usage:
  goodvibes-agent import openclaw [path] [--apply] [--apply-permissions]

Examples:
  goodvibes-agent import openclaw
  goodvibes-agent import openclaw ~/.openclaw
  goodvibes-agent import openclaw ~/.openclaw --apply
  goodvibes-agent import openclaw ~/.openclaw --apply --apply-permissions
```

### `goodvibes-agent owner-profile`

```
GoodVibes Agent owner-profile

Read, trace, correct, and delete the owner profile the daemon keeps: one Markdown file holding your name, contact, location, commerce, preferences, people, places, work, and notes. read prints the whole document with the provenance suffix on every learned line; get prints one field; person prints one person by name; provenance answers "where did you get that" for one field, including the values it superseded; set supersedes a field and keeps the old one; undo puts the previous value back; note adds a line to a prose section; forget deletes a line and its kept history, and reports that a field was not there rather than reporting success; a prose line is named by its section and exact text, never by position, because you edit this file yourself and a position from an earlier read can point at a different line by now; status prints load state, path, counts, and any field whose value did not parse: never values. On a terminal read lists the People section; when stdout is captured (a pipe, or a model driving a shell tool) it only counts the people.

Usage:
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile read
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile get <fieldId>
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile person <name>
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile provenance <fieldId>
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile set <fieldId> <value> [--said "<your words>"] --yes
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile note --section <section> --text "<the line>" [--said "<your words>"] --yes
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile undo <fieldId> --yes
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile forget <fieldId> --yes
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile forget --section <section> --text "<the line, exactly>" --yes
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile status

Examples:
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile read
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile provenance commerce.shippingAddress
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile person Sarah
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile undo location.timezone --yes
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile set location.timezone America/Detroit --yes
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile forget contact.phone --yes
  goodvibes-agent owner-profile status
```

### `goodvibes-agent plugin`

```
GoodVibes Agent plugin

Browse a governed marketplace index, install a SHA-256-pinned capability bundle, remove one, or list the installed ones. An install is never unpinned: a missing or mismatched --sha256 is refused, not overridable. Without --yes, install prints the activation plan (granted, withheld and quarantined capabilities) and changes nothing; with --yes it installs that plan and writes the receipt the plugin loader enforces. /plugin-trust trust <plugin> <tier> sets what an installed plugin may register.

Usage:
  goodvibes-agent plugin bundles browse <index-url-or-file>
  goodvibes-agent plugin bundles install <ref> --sha256 <pin> [--ref <git-ref>] [--yes]
  goodvibes-agent plugin bundles uninstall <id>
  goodvibes-agent plugin bundles list

Examples:
  goodvibes-agent plugin bundles browse ./marketplace-index.json
  goodvibes-agent plugin bundles install ./bundle.json --sha256 <64-hex>
  goodvibes-agent plugin bundles install ./bundle.json --sha256 <64-hex> --yes
  goodvibes-agent plugin bundles list
```

### `goodvibes-agent relay`

```
GoodVibes Agent relay

Ask the connected GoodVibes host for its live relay registration (status) and mint the pairing payload one device scans to reach it through the relay (pair: relay URL, rendezvous id, the daemon's public key and a relay code for that device alone, labelled with the name). codes lists the devices' relay codes; revoke cuts one device off the relay at its next request while every other keeps working.
```
