## Command line: `goodvibes-daemon`

The daemon's top-level help, then the help page of every command, exactly as `goodvibes-daemon --help` and `goodvibes-daemon help <command>` print them. Commands that read their own flags list them after the page.

The pages below are rendered for Linux, where the service is a systemd user service. On macOS the same commands manage a launchd user agent.

### `goodvibes-daemon --help`

```
Usage: goodvibes-daemon [COMMAND] [OPTIONS]

The GoodVibes daemon: the one long-running host for the control plane, the
channels, cluster membership, scheduled work, the knowledge and memory stores,
and the verb families every GoodVibes client calls.

Run with no command it starts serving in the foreground. Run `goodvibes-daemon
install-service` to have it start on its own as a systemd user service
(at login; at boot on Linux with lingering).

Commands:
  install-service               Install the daemon as a host service and start it.
  refresh-service               Rewrite the service definition to the current launch without starting it.
  uninstall-service             Stop the daemon service and remove its definition.
  service-status                Report whether the daemon service is installed and running.
  start-service                 Start the installed daemon service.
  stop-service                  Stop the daemon service without removing it.
  restart-service               Restart the daemon service.
  status                        Ask a running daemon what it is doing.
  pair                          Print the pairing link and QR code again, or mint one on a remote daemon.
  sessions                      List or end the sessions a running daemon is hosting.
  mcp                           Serve the operator surface of a running daemon to an MCP client over stdio.
  config                        Read and write this daemon's settings.
  update                        Report whether this daemon is keeping itself current, or check now.
  send                          Send a message to one of your configured channels.
  cluster                       Share inbound channel work with your other machines.
  webui                         Serve the browser operator surface from this daemon.
  provision-wake-model          Fetch any missing wake-word model files.
  completion                    Print a shell completion script.
  help                          Print help for the binary, or for one command.
  check-install-reader          Check whether this release can read an installation’s saved data.
  version                       Print the version.

Run `goodvibes-daemon help <command>` for a command's own arguments and flags.
Run `goodvibes-daemon --help --json` for the versioned machine command catalog.

Global options (accepted by every command):
      --daemon-home <dir>       Run this daemon entirely out of <dir>: its identity (operator tokens, daemon settings, secrets) in <dir>, and everything else it keeps (users, device tokens, memory, sessions) under <dir>/.goodvibes/, unless GOODVIBES_HOME names that tree. Shares nothing with another daemon.
  -C, --working-dir, --cd <dir> The directory the daemon treats as its workspace.
  -h, --help                    Print help and exit 0.
  -v, --version                 Print the version and exit 0.

The commands send, cluster, webui, provision-wake-model, check-install-reader read every word after their name as their own arguments, so give them global options before the command.

Serving options (a bare invocation, or `serve`):
      --hostname, --host <host> Bind address for the control plane. 0.0.0.0 means every interface.
      --port <n>                Control-plane port to bind.
      --provider <id>           Run with this provider instead of the configured one. Not written to settings.
  -m, --model <registryKey>     Run with this model. A provider:model key also sets the provider.
  -c, --config <key=value>      Override one settings key for this run only. Repeatable. Never written to disk.
      --enable <feature>        Switch a capability on for this run through its real settings key. Repeatable.
      --disable <feature>       Switch a capability off for this run. Repeatable.

Exit codes:
  0                             the command did what it says
  1                             it ran and failed: the reason is printed; cluster also exits 1
                                for a word or flag it does not understand after its name
  2                             the command line was wrong: an unknown command, an unknown flag,
                                a flag this command does not take, or a missing value
  3                             service-status: installed, but not running;
                                install-service: installed, but it did not start
  4                             service-status, start-service, stop-service, restart-service,
                                uninstall-service: no service is installed
  5                             install-service, refresh-service, uninstall-service: the definition
                                at the service's path was not written by GoodVibes; nothing was changed
```

### `goodvibes-daemon check-install-reader`

```
Usage: goodvibes-daemon check-install-reader <installed-executable> | --describe

Read the selected installation’s data-reader requirements without loading settings, starting services or changing files.
The release installer invokes its verified staged binary before replacing installed programs.
--describe reports the readers compiled into this binary for the native CI artifact producer.

Options `check-install-reader` reads itself (`--help` only right after `check-install-reader`):
      --describe                Report the readers compiled into this binary.

Every word after `check-install-reader` is its own argument; give global options before the command: `goodvibes-daemon --daemon-home <dir> check-install-reader …`.

Global options:
      --daemon-home <dir>       Run this daemon entirely out of <dir>: its identity (operator tokens, daemon settings, secrets) in <dir>, and everything else it keeps (users, device tokens, memory, sessions) under <dir>/.goodvibes/, unless GOODVIBES_HOME names that tree. Shares nothing with another daemon.
  -C, --working-dir, --cd <dir> The directory the daemon treats as its workspace.
  -h, --help                    Print help and exit 0.
  -v, --version                 Print the version and exit 0.
```

### `goodvibes-daemon cluster`

```
Usage: goodvibes-daemon cluster status|create|join|key|nodes|forget|rotate|leave|rename|groups|publish|accept

Manage the group of machines on this network that share inbound channel work.

  status            what this machine is doing in its group
  create            start a group here
  join              join one (interactively, or with --group and --key)
  key               print the join key for another machine to use
  nodes             every machine in the group
  groups            groups advertising themselves on this network
  forget <machine>  drop a machine from the group
  rotate [--now]    change the shared key
  rename <name>     rename the group
  leave             leave the group
  publish <setting> send this machine's value of a shared setting to the group
                    (user:<name>: make this machine's account of that name the group's)
  accept <setting>  take the group's value of a shared setting here
                    (user:<name>: give up this machine's account of that name for the group's)
                    (status lists the shared settings that differ here)

Talks to a running daemon over the same --host/--port/--token convention
`status` uses; --json gives a scriptable answer.

Exit codes: 0 done; 1 failed or refused, and also for an unknown flag, an
unknown subcommand, or `cluster <sub> --help` (this page is `cluster --help`, exit 0).

Options `cluster` reads itself (`--help` only right after `cluster`):
      --group <value>           The group to join.
      --key <value>             The join key.
      --name <value>            A name for the group.
      --passphrase <value>      The group passphrase.
      --host <value>            The machine whose daemon to ask.
      --port <value>            That daemon's port.
      --token <value>           The operator token for that daemon.
      --now                     Rotate immediately.
      --qr                      Print the join key as a QR code.
  -y, --yes                     Answer yes to confirmations.
      --json                    Print one JSON document instead of prose.
  -h, --help                    Print help and exit 0.

Every word after `cluster` is its own argument; give global options before the command: `goodvibes-daemon --daemon-home <dir> cluster …`.

Global options:
      --daemon-home <dir>       Run this daemon entirely out of <dir>: its identity (operator tokens, daemon settings, secrets) in <dir>, and everything else it keeps (users, device tokens, memory, sessions) under <dir>/.goodvibes/, unless GOODVIBES_HOME names that tree. Shares nothing with another daemon.
  -C, --working-dir, --cd <dir> The directory the daemon treats as its workspace.
  -h, --help                    Print help and exit 0.
  -v, --version                 Print the version and exit 0.
```

### `goodvibes-daemon completion`

Also answers to: `goodvibes-daemon completions`.

```
Usage: goodvibes-daemon completion bash|zsh|fish

Print a completion script for the named shell on stdout. It completes this
binary's commands, their sub-words and their flags, generated from the same
catalog the parser and the help text use; so it cannot drift from what the
binary accepts.

Install it by writing it somewhere the shell reads, for example:
  goodvibes-daemon completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/goodvibes-daemon
  goodvibes-daemon completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_goodvibes-daemon
  goodvibes-daemon completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/goodvibes-daemon.fish

Global options:
      --daemon-home <dir>       Run this daemon entirely out of <dir>: its identity (operator tokens, daemon settings, secrets) in <dir>, and everything else it keeps (users, device tokens, memory, sessions) under <dir>/.goodvibes/, unless GOODVIBES_HOME names that tree. Shares nothing with another daemon.
  -C, --working-dir, --cd <dir> The directory the daemon treats as its workspace.
  -h, --help                    Print help and exit 0.
  -v, --version                 Print the version and exit 0.
```

### `goodvibes-daemon config`

```
Usage: goodvibes-daemon config list|get <key>|set <key> <value>|unset <key> [--json]

config list            every setting with its current value; the settings file it names
                       is the global one, not the file every key lives in.
config get <key>       one setting.
config set <key> <v>   write one setting to disk. The value is checked against the
                       schema first, and a daemon-owned key lands in the daemon's
                       own settings file rather than the shared one. A credential
                       key is never written as plain text: it is stored in the
                       secret store and the settings file keeps a reference.
config unset <key>     remove the global, daemon and shared value of one setting. A
                       project settings value is untouched and can still apply.

Values are read and written on this machine's settings files directly, so this
works whether or not a daemon is running. A running daemon picks up most
changes live, including a move to another control-plane port; a setting that is
only read at startup applies the next time the daemon starts. A host change that
keeps the same port (between loopback and all interfaces) needs a restart: the old
listener holds the port, so the daemon keeps serving the old address until then.

Anything that reads like a credential (a token, a password, an API key) is
printed as <redacted>, so a settings dump pasted into an issue carries none.

Options:
      --json                    Print one JSON document instead of prose, for scripting.

Global options:
      --daemon-home <dir>       Run this daemon entirely out of <dir>: its identity (operator tokens, daemon settings, secrets) in <dir>, and everything else it keeps (users, device tokens, memory, sessions) under <dir>/.goodvibes/, unless GOODVIBES_HOME names that tree. Shares nothing with another daemon.
  -C, --working-dir, --cd <dir> The directory the daemon treats as its workspace.
  -h, --help                    Print help and exit 0.
  -v, --version                 Print the version and exit 0.
```

### `goodvibes-daemon mcp`

```
Usage: goodvibes-daemon mcp serve [--categories <list|all>] [--allow-write] [--allow-destructive] [--host <http(s)://name>] [--port <n>] [--token <t>]

mcp serve              speak the Model Context Protocol on stdin/stdout, with one tool
                       per operator method of the daemon it connects to (session
                       lifecycle first), so an MCP client can drive GoodVibes.

By default it serves the agent slice: the sessions, tasks, contracts and approvals
methods that read, plus creating a session, sending it a message and steering it
(the exact number is printed at start). --categories picks other operator families (comma separated or
repeated; `all` for every family), --allow-write adds the methods that change
state, and --allow-destructive adds the methods the contract marks dangerous.
The number of tools served is printed on stderr at start.

A client that cancels a tool call (notifications/cancelled) stops the request to
the daemon.

It connects the way status and sessions do: with no flags to the daemon on this
machine using this machine's operator token; --host/--port/--token pick another (--host needs http:// or https://).
The daemon is checked before the first frame. When it is not running, or the token
is missing or refused, the command prints one line naming the prerequisite on
stderr and exits 1; nothing is written to stdout.

Stdout carries only protocol frames; every message for a person goes to stderr.
The command ends, exit 0, when the client closes stdin.

Client configuration: { "command": "goodvibes-daemon", "args": ["mcp", "serve"] }.

Options:
      --categories <list>       Operator families to serve, comma separated or repeated; `all` for every family.
      --allow-write             Also serve the methods that change state.
      --allow-destructive       Also serve the methods marked dangerous.
      --host <name>             The machine to ask, as a name or a URL (https://name, https://name:3421). Defaults to this one. A URL without a port means 443 for https and 80 for http.
      --port <n>                That daemon's control-plane port. Defaults to the port in a --host URL, else its scheme's (443, 80), else the configured one.
      --token <t>               Operator token for that daemon. Defaults to this machine's own.

Global options:
      --daemon-home <dir>       Run this daemon entirely out of <dir>: its identity (operator tokens, daemon settings, secrets) in <dir>, and everything else it keeps (users, device tokens, memory, sessions) under <dir>/.goodvibes/, unless GOODVIBES_HOME names that tree. Shares nothing with another daemon.
  -C, --working-dir, --cd <dir> The directory the daemon treats as its workspace.
  -h, --help                    Print help and exit 0.
  -v, --version                 Print the version and exit 0.
```

### `goodvibes-daemon pair`

Also answers to: `goodvibes-daemon qr`, `goodvibes-daemon qrcode`.

```
Usage: goodvibes-daemon pair [--json] [--host <http(s)://name>] [--port <n>] [--token <t>] [-y]

LOCAL FORM (no --host, or one naming this machine): print the same pairing
block a daemon prints once at startup: the web origin, the offers a new
device can accept, what it will be able to do, and a QR code encoding the
deep link that opens the web app already signed in.

It reprints the EXISTING shared token rather than minting a new one, so a link
printed here and one printed at boot are the same link. Scrolling the startup
banner off the screen therefore costs nothing.

It asks the running daemon first: whether it accepts the token, and the address
and scheme it is really bound to, so the QR carries what the daemon serves. A
daemon that refuses the token is reported (pass the right one with --token) and
no link is printed. When no daemon answers, the link is built from the settings
and the token file, and the output says so. A daemon started on a port other than
its settings is found with --port.

REMOTE FORM (--host http(s)://name of another machine): ask THAT daemon to MINT A NEW
per-device pairing token and print the pairing block for it. Minting is a
different act than reprinting: it is a fresh token, and every token that
daemon already issued, its shared token included, is left untouched.

Because it changes state on a daemon that may not be this process's own, it
states the plan and asks for confirmation before acting: -y (or --yes) is the
non-interactive answer. Without -y
nothing is changed. An unreachable daemon, a rejected token, and a daemon too
old to serve the mint verb are each refused by name, never a stack trace.

Options:
      --json                    Print one JSON document instead of prose, for scripting.
      --host <name>             The machine to ask, as a name or a URL (https://name, https://name:3421). Defaults to this one. A URL without a port means 443 for https and 80 for http.
      --port <n>                That daemon's control-plane port. Defaults to the port in a --host URL, else its scheme's (443, 80), else the configured one.
      --token <t>               Operator token for that daemon. Defaults to this machine's own.
  -y, --yes, --non-interactive  Answer the confirmation prompt with yes. Nothing destructive happens without it.

Global options:
      --daemon-home <dir>       Run this daemon entirely out of <dir>: its identity (operator tokens, daemon settings, secrets) in <dir>, and everything else it keeps (users, device tokens, memory, sessions) under <dir>/.goodvibes/, unless GOODVIBES_HOME names that tree. Shares nothing with another daemon.
  -C, --working-dir, --cd <dir> The directory the daemon treats as its workspace.
  -h, --help                    Print help and exit 0.
  -v, --version                 Print the version and exit 0.
```

### `goodvibes-daemon send`

```
Usage: goodvibes-daemon send [message] [--channel <id>] [--to <address>] [--title <text>] [--list]

Send a message through Telegram, ntfy, Discord, Slack, Google Chat, Signal,
WhatsApp, iMessage, Teams, BlueBubbles, Mattermost, Matrix or a webhook. The
message is an argument or stdin, so it composes with other tooling.

--channel <id> picks the channel; with none named it uses your one configured
channel and says which. --to <address> targets a topic, chat or room inside it,
--title <text> sets a title, and --list shows every channel with where it would

with no daemon running, which is much of the point: the reason to message

Global options:
      --daemon-home <dir>       Run this daemon entirely out of <dir>: its identity (operator tokens, daemon settings, secrets) in <dir>, and everything else it keeps (users, device tokens, memory, sessions) under <dir>/.goodvibes/, unless GOODVIBES_HOME names that tree. Shares nothing with another daemon.

### `goodvibes-daemon sessions`

Also answers to: `goodvibes-daemon session`.

```
Usage: goodvibes-daemon sessions list|kill <id> [--json] [--all] [--host <name>] [--port <n>] [--token <t>]

sessions list          every session this daemon hosts, most recently used first.
sessions kill <id>     end one: its in-flight turn is interrupted and its loop
                       taken apart, whoever is attached and whatever its detach
                       policy says.

they ended, until the retention window retires them.

      --port <n>                That daemon's control-plane port. Defaults to the port in a --host URL, else its scheme's (443, 80), else the configured one.
      --token <t>               Operator token for that daemon. Defaults to this machine's own.

Shares nothing with another daemon.
  -C, --working-dir, --cd <dir> The directory the daemon treats as its workspace.

### `goodvibes-daemon webui`

```
Usage: goodvibes-daemon webui enable|disable|status [--bundle-dir <dir>] [--lan|--loopback]

The web UI is a built bundle of static files served by the daemon's own
control-plane listener, on the same origin as the API; so the URL to open is
the control-plane one, not the declared web port.

  enable [--bundle-dir <dir>]  serve the bundle at that directory
  disable                      stop serving it; the bundle stays on disk
  status                       what is served, from where, and who can reach it
  status --json                configured web.* binding for development clients
                               (not proof that a listener is running)

`enable` changes no network exposure on its own: a daemon bound to loopback
keeps serving to this machine only. --lan binds every interface and turns
controlPlane.enabled on so other devices are served, --loopback takes the
binding back, and both are stated in the receipt.

Options `webui` reads itself (`--help` only right after `webui`):
      --bundle-dir <value>      The directory holding the built web UI.
      --lan                     Bind every interface and serve other devices (controlPlane.enabled).
      --loopback                Take the binding back to this machine only.
      --json                    Print the configured web.* binding as JSON.
  -h, --help                    Print help and exit 0.

Every word after `webui` is its own argument; give global options before the command: `goodvibes-daemon --daemon-home <dir> webui …`.

Global options:
      --daemon-home <dir>       Run this daemon entirely out of <dir>: its identity (operator tokens, daemon settings, secrets) in <dir>, and everything else it keeps (users, device tokens, memory, sessions) under <dir>/.goodvibes/, unless GOODVIBES_HOME names that tree. Shares nothing with another daemon.
  -C, --working-dir, --cd <dir> The directory the daemon treats as its workspace.
  -h, --help                    Print help and exit 0.
  -v, --version                 Print the version and exit 0.
```

## Slash commands: terminal app

Every slash command typed in the terminal app's prompt, in alphabetical order. Each entry gives the command and its argument pattern, what it does, its category in the command palette, its aliases, whether it changes anything, whether it asks before acting, and its subcommands with their argument hints. Type `/help` in the app for the same list.

- `/about-me` `/about-me show | field <fact> | person <person...> | where <fact> | status | set <fact> <value...> | note [<section>] <line...> | undo <fact> | forget <fact> | forget-line <section> <line...>`: What the platform knows about you: read it, see where a fact came from, correct it, or forget it.
  - Category Owner Profile; depends on the subcommand (`show`, `field`, `person`, `where`, `status` only read)
  - `/about-me field` `<fact>   See one fact about you`
  - `/about-me forget` `<fact>   Forget a fact`
  - `/about-me forget-line` `<section> <line...>   Forget a line`
  - `/about-me note` `[<section>] <line...>   Add a line about you`
  - `/about-me person` `<person...>   See what is known about a person`
  - `/about-me set` `<fact> <value...>   Record or correct a fact`
  - `/about-me show` `See what is known about you`
  - `/about-me status` `Check that your profile loads`
  - `/about-me undo` `<fact>   Put back a fact's earlier value`
  - `/about-me where` `<fact>   See where a fact came from`
- `/accounts` `/accounts review | show <provider> | routes <provider> | repair <provider> | open | sign-in <service> <address> [--user <user name>] [--password <password>] [--key <kept as>] | sign-out <service> <address> [--key <kept as>]`: Your model provider accounts, and signing in to a GoodVibes daemon or listener.
  - Category Provider Accounts; depends on the subcommand (`review`, `show`, `routes`, `repair`, `open` only read)
  - `/accounts open` `Open the providers screen`
  - `/accounts repair` `<provider>   See how to fix a provider's account`
  - `/accounts review` `See your provider accounts`
  - `/accounts routes` `<provider>   See how a provider is reached`
  - `/accounts show` `<provider>   See one provider's account`
  - `/accounts sign-in` `<service> <address> [--user <user name>] [--password <password>] [--key <kept as>]   Sign in to a daemon or listener`
  - `/accounts sign-out` `<service> <address> [--key <kept as>]   Sign out of a daemon or listener`
- `/agents` `/agents open [--target <select>] | hostable | host <coding agent> [<folder>] | team | start <kind of agent> <what to do...> | recipe <recipe> <what to do...> | archetypes | archetype <archetype> | start-archetype <archetype> <what to do...> | hand-off [--review] [--reason <why>] [--success <done when>] [--workspace <where>] [--priority <priority>] <the work...> | handed-off [<hand-off>] | contract [<contract>] | contracts-view | stop-group <group> | stop-branch <agent>`: What your agents are doing: open the live view, start agents, host a coding agent, hand work on, and stop work.
  - Category Agents; depends on the subcommand (`open`, `hostable`, `team`, `archetypes`, `archetype`, `handed-off`, `contract`, `contracts-view` only read)
  - `/agents archetype` `<archetype>   See one archetype`
  - `/agents archetypes` `See agent archetypes`
  - `/agents contract` `[<contract>]   See a work contract`
  - `/agents contracts-view` `Open the work contracts view`
  - `/agents hand-off` `[--review] [--reason <why>] [--success <done when>] [--workspace <where>] [--priority <priority>] <the work...>   Hand coding work to the terminal app`
  - `/agents handed-off` `[<hand-off>]   See work you handed off`
  - `/agents host` `<coding agent> [<folder>]   Host a coding agent`
  - `/agents hostable` `See coding agents you can host`
  - `/agents open` `[--target <select>]   Open Your agents`
  - `/agents recipe` `<recipe> <what to do...>   Run a recipe of agents`
  - `/agents start` `<kind of agent> <what to do...>   Start an agent in a team mode`
  - `/agents start-archetype` `<archetype> <what to do...>   Start an agent from an archetype`
  - `/agents stop-branch` `<agent>   Stop an agent and the agents it started`
  - `/agents stop-group` `<group>   Stop a group of agents`
  - `/agents team` `See team modes and recipes`
- `/approval` `/approval kinds [<kind>] | waiting`: What each kind of approval asks about, and the approvals waiting on you.
  - Category Experience; reads only.
  - `/approval kinds` `[<kind>]   See the kinds of approval`
  - `/approval waiting` `Open the approvals waiting on you`
- `/auth` `/auth review | show <provider> | repair <provider> | export <file> [--replace] | inspect <file>`: See how you are signed in to model providers and how to fix a sign-in.
  - Category Platform Access; depends on the subcommand (`review`, `show`, `repair`, `inspect` only read)
  - `/auth export` `<file> [--replace]   Save a sign-in summary to a file`
  - `/auth inspect` `<file>   Read a saved sign-in summary`
  - `/auth repair` `<provider>   See how to fix a provider's sign-in`
  - `/auth review` `See your provider sign-ins`
  - `/auth show` `<provider>   See one provider's sign-in`
- `/calendar` `/calendar upcoming [--days <how many days>] | get <event> | add [--title <title>] [--start <starts>] [--end <ends>] [--location <where>] [--notes <notes>] [--again] | change <event> [--title <title>] [--start <starts>] [--end <ends>] | delete <event> | status | all | import <file> | export [<file>] | accounts | connect <account> [--with <sign in with>] [--code <address or code>] | use-app <account> <client id> [--secret <client secret>] | disconnect <account> | subscriptions | subscribe <feed address> [--name <name>] [--every <read every>] [--allow-private-host] | refresh [<feed>] | unsubscribe <feed>`: See what is coming up, add, change and remove events, and the feeds and accounts your calendar reads.
  - Category Mail & Calendar; depends on the subcommand (`upcoming`, `get`, `status`, `all`, `accounts`, `subscriptions` only read)
  - `/calendar accounts` `See your calendar accounts`
  - `/calendar add` `[--title <title>] [--start <starts>] [--end <ends>] [--location <where>] [--notes <notes>] [--again]   Add an event`
  - `/calendar all` `See every event`
  - `/calendar change` `<event> [--title <title>] [--start <starts>] [--end <ends>]   Change an event`
  - `/calendar connect` `<account> [--with <sign in with>] [--code <address or code>]   Sign in to a calendar account`
  - `/calendar delete` `<event>   Remove an event`
  - `/calendar disconnect` `<account>   Sign out of a calendar account`
  - `/calendar export` `[<file>]   Export events to a file`
  - `/calendar get` `<event>   See one event`
  - `/calendar import` `<file>   Import events from a file`
  - `/calendar refresh` `[<feed>]   Read the feeds again now`
  - `/calendar status` `See whether the calendar is connected`
  - `/calendar subscribe` `<feed address> [--name <name>] [--every <read every>] [--allow-private-host]   Subscribe to a calendar feed`
  - `/calendar subscriptions` `See the feeds you subscribe to`
  - `/calendar unsubscribe` `<feed>   Stop subscribing to a feed`
  - `/calendar upcoming` `[--days <how many days>]   See what is coming up`
  - `/calendar use-app` `<account> <client id> [--secret <client secret>]   Use your own calendar app to sign in`
- `/changes` `/changes [<which changes>]`: Changed files with their diff: stage hunks, comment for the model, mark reviewed.
  - Category Diff & Review; reads only.
- `/channels` `/channels status | readiness [--show <show>] | configured <channel> | guide [<channel>] | setup <channel> | doctor <channel> | test <channel> | accounts | rules [<channel>] | set-rules <channel> [--enabled <accept messages>] [--require-mention <only when mentioned>] [--commands-without-mention <commands without a mention>] [--allow-dms <direct messages>] [--allow-groups <group messages>] [--allow-threads <thread messages>] [--dm-policy <direct messages from others>] [--group-policy <groups not on the list>] [--open <open to anyone>] [--allow-users <users>] [--allow-channels <conversations>] [--allow-group-ids <groups>] [--allowed-commands <commands>] | profiles | profile <channel> [<one conversation>] | set-profile <channel> [<one conversation>] [--model <model>] [--provider <provider>] [--permission-mode <permission mode>] | remove-profile <channel> [<one conversation>] | triage [--limit <how many>] | send [--channel <to>] [--title <title>] [--route <route>] [--webhook <webhook address>] [--link <link>] <message...> | deliveries [--limit <how many>] | overview | routes | delivery | open | telegram-cursor`: Your channels (Slack, Telegram, ntfy, ...): their state and setup, who may reach the assistant, and what each one's sessions get.
  - Category Channels; depends on the subcommand (`status`, `readiness`, `configured`, `guide`, `setup`, `doctor`, `accounts`, `rules`, `profiles`, `profile`, `triage`, `deliveries`, `overview`, `routes`, `delivery` only read)
  - `/channels accounts` `See the accounts behind your channels`
  - `/channels configured` `<channel>   See how one channel is configured`
  - `/channels deliveries` `[--limit <how many>]   See what was sent to channels`
  - `/channels delivery` `See how outbound messages are delivered`
  - `/channels doctor` `<channel>   Check a channel that isn't working`
  - `/channels guide` `[<channel>]   Walk through setting up channels`
  - `/channels open` `Open the routes view`
  - `/channels overview` `See what the channels carry`
  - `/channels profile` `<channel> [<one conversation>]   See what one channel's sessions get`
  - `/channels profiles` `See channel profiles`
  - `/channels readiness` `[--show <show>]   See which channels are set up`
  - `/channels remove-profile` `<channel> [<one conversation>]   Remove a channel's profile`
  - `/channels routes` `See the active routes`
  - `/channels rules` `[<channel>]   See who may reach the assistant`
  - `/channels send` `[--channel <to>] [--title <title>] [--route <route>] [--webhook <webhook address>] [--link <link>] <message...>   Send a message to a channel`
  - `/channels set-profile` `<channel> [<one conversation>] [--model <model>] [--provider <provider>] [--permission-mode <permission mode>]   Give a channel its own model or permission mode`
  - `/channels set-rules` `<channel> [--enabled <accept messages>] [--require-mention <only when mentioned>] [--commands-without-mention <commands without a mention>] [--allow-dms <direct messages>] [--allow-groups <group messages>] [--allow-threads <thread messages>] [--dm-policy <direct messages from others>] [--group-policy <groups not on the list>] [--open <open to anyone>] [--allow-users <users>] [--allow-channels <conversations>] [--allow-group-ids <groups>] [--allowed-commands <commands>]   Change who may reach the assistant`
  - `/channels setup` `<channel>   See what a channel needs to be set up`
  - `/channels status` `See your channels`
  - `/channels telegram-cursor` `Pick up Telegram where it left off`
  - `/channels test` `<channel>   Send a test message through a channel`
  - `/channels triage` `[--limit <how many>]   See what came in on your channels`
- `/checkin` `/checkin status | run`: The proactive check-in: its settings and what each one did, or one now.
  - Category Check-in; depends on the subcommand (`status` only read)
  - `/checkin run` `Check in now`
  - `/checkin status` `See check-in settings and what they did`
- `/checkpoint` `/checkpoint list | make [<name...>] | restore <checkpoint> | rewind <turn> [<what goes back>]`: Snapshots of the workspace's files: see them, make one, put the files back, or go back to an earlier turn.
  - Category Checkpoints; depends on the subcommand (`list` only read)
  - `/checkpoint list` `See your checkpoints`
  - `/checkpoint make` `[<name...>]   Make a checkpoint now`
  - `/checkpoint restore` `<checkpoint>   Put the files back to a checkpoint`
  - `/checkpoint rewind` `<turn> [<what goes back>]   Go back to an earlier turn`
- `/ci` `/ci watches | status <repository> | watch <repository> <tell me on> [--fix-session] | run <watch> | unwatch <watch>`: See a repository's CI job by job, and keep standing watches that tell you when it fails.
  - Category CI; depends on the subcommand (`watches`, `status` only read)
  - `/ci run` `<watch>   Check a watch now`
  - `/ci status` `<repository>   Check a repository's CI now`
  - `/ci unwatch` `<watch>   Stop watching a repository`
  - `/ci watch` `<repository> <tell me on> [--fix-session]   Watch a repository's CI`
  - `/ci watches` `See your CI watches`
- `/clear`: Start a fresh conversation; the current one is saved as its own session.
  - Category Shell & Session; depends on the subcommand.

## Slash commands: Agent

Every slash command typed in Agent's prompt, in alphabetical order, read the same way as the list above.

- `/about-me` `/about-me show | field <fact> | person <person...> | where <fact> | status | set <fact> <value...> | note [<section>] <line...> | undo <fact> | forget <fact> | forget-line <section> <line...>`: What the platform knows about you: read it, see where a fact came from, correct it, or forget it.
  - Depends on the subcommand (`show`, `field`, `person`, `where`, `status` only read)
  - `/about-me field` `<fact>   See one fact about you`
  - `/about-me forget` `<fact>   Forget a fact`
  - `/about-me forget-line` `<section> <line...>   Forget a line`
  - `/about-me note` `[<section>] <line...>   Add a line about you`
  - `/about-me person` `<person...>   See what is known about a person`
  - `/about-me set` `<fact> <value...>   Record or correct a fact`
  - `/about-me show` `See what is known about you`
  - `/about-me status` `Check that your profile loads`
  - `/about-me undo` `<fact>   Put back a fact's earlier value`
  - `/about-me where` `<fact>   See where a fact came from`

## Model tools

Every tool the model can call. A tool is called by the model, not typed by a person; the permission mode and the decision model decide whether each call runs. Each tool gives its name, what it does, its permission category (which permission rules apply: `read`, `write`, `execute` or `delegate`), and every input with its type and whether it is required.

### Tools of the terminal app, the daemon's hosted sessions and helper agents

These 28 tools are the platform's own. Each line under a tool names one input: its type, whether it is required, and what it means. Nested inputs are indented under their parent.
Not in Agent: `work_plan`.

### `agent`

Manages in-process subagents. Modes: spawn (create a new agent task), batch-spawn (hand several tasks over at once: the tasks without outsideContract become the proposed units of one contract, and tasks with outsideContract run as separate agents), status (check agent progress by ID), cancel (stop a running agent), list (show all agents and their status), templates (list available agent templates with default tool sets), get (detailed agent info including messages), budget (token usage for an agent), plan (execution plan: task + template + tools), wait (returns current status immediately if terminal, or waits up to timeoutMs, returning as soon as the agent ends; one wait is capped at contract.heartbeatTimeoutMs, default 10 minutes, and says so when it was), message (send a message to an agent), contracts (list the contracts of the current session with their status, goal, units and criteria met), contract-history (the decisions, checks and escalations of one contract, by contractId), cohort-status (JSON summary of all agents in a named cohort), cohort-report (markdown table report for all agents in a named cohort). A team is a cohort: spawn its members with one cohort name, each with its template as its role and its communicationLane, brief each with context and successCriteria, and track the work items in the work plan; cohort-status and cohort-report read the team back, and the fleet view shows the cohort on each agent. Discovery: use mode=list to see all agents and their status, mode=templates to see available agent templates. Work handed to this tool with mode=spawn or batch-spawn runs as a contract: a planner splits it into units, and each unit is checked against its acceptance criteria while it works and told what to fix until it passes. The result carries contractStarted, contractId and the owner agent id; the owner agent reports the contract's answer when it ends. Use contracts for requested deliverables and work with multiple functional parts: their criteria link each part to the original objective, and the host checks completed parts before integration. Set outsideContract only for a bounded helper whose complete result can be checked as one part. Standalone agents still require native Jev completion and output checks. Do not use outsideContract to avoid a rejected plan or move the same unfinished work past its required checks.

Permission category `delegate`; side effects: `agent`, `workflow`, `state`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"spawn"`, `"batch-spawn"`, `"status"`, `"cancel"`, `"list"`, `"templates"`, `"get"`, `"budget"`, `"plan"`, `"wait"`, `"message"`, `"contracts"`, `"contract-history"`, `"cohort-status"`, `"cohort-report"`, required): Operation mode.
- `task` (string, optional): Task description (mode: spawn). Without outsideContract it becomes the proposed unit of a new contract; with outsideContract it is the agent's own task. Describe the deliverable itself.
- `template` (one of `"orchestrator"`, `"planner"`, `"engineer"`, `"reviewer"`, `"tester"`, `"researcher"`, `"integrator"`, `"general"`, optional): Agent template to use (mode: spawn). Default: general. Each template includes a pre-selected tool set.
- `model` (string, optional): Model for the spawned agent (mode: spawn). A bare model id (e.g. "claude-fable-5") resolves automatically; use the provider:model form only when the id exists on more than one provider. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
- `provider` (string, optional): Provider override for the spawned agent (mode: spawn). Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
- `fallbackModels` (array of string, optional): Ordered models to try if the primary model fails (mode: spawn). Bare ids resolve automatically, same as model. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
- `executionIntent` (object, optional): Explicit execution-intent hints for policy-aware runtimes (mode: spawn). Needs outsideContract=true: on a contract this is refused, because the contract planner chooses the tools and write scope of each unit.
  - `riskClass` (one of `"safe"`, `"elevated"`, `"dangerous"`, optional): Execution risk classification hint for downstream policy/evaluation surfaces.
  - `requiresApproval` (boolean, optional): Whether the spawned agent should be treated as requiring approval-sensitive execution.
  - `networkPolicy` (one of `"inherit"`, `"allow"`, `"deny"`, `"scoped"`, optional): Requested network posture for downstream execution surfaces.
  - `filesystemPolicy` (one of `"inherit"`, `"workspace-write"`, `"read-only"`, `"isolated"`, optional): Requested filesystem posture for downstream execution surfaces.
- `reasoningEffort` (one of `"none"`, `"instant"`, `"minimal"`, `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, `"xhigh"`, `"max"`, optional): Reasoning effort override for providers/models that support it (mode: spawn). Which levels the spawned agent's model actually accepts is per-model. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
- `tools` (array of string, optional): Explicit tool subset for the agent (mode: spawn). Defaults to template defaults. The "agent" tool is never included. Needs outsideContract=true: on a contract this is refused, because the contract planner chooses the tools and write scope of each unit.
- `context` (string, optional): Additional context to provide to the spawned agent (mode: spawn). On a contract it is passed only as continuation evidence, not as a requirement.
- `successCriteria` (array of string, optional): Concrete success criteria the spawned agent must satisfy (mode: spawn). Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
- `requiredEvidence` (array of string, optional): Evidence the spawned agent must return before completion (mode: spawn). Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
- `writeScope` (array of string, optional): Expected file or path scope for writes owned by the spawned agent (mode: spawn). Needs outsideContract=true: on a contract this is refused, because the contract planner chooses the tools and write scope of each unit.
- `executionProtocol` (one of `"direct"`, `"gather-plan-apply"`, optional): Execution discipline the spawned agent should follow (mode: spawn). Default: gather-plan-apply. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
- `reviewMode` (one of `"none"`, `"contract"`, optional): Whether the agent uses contract unit checks (mode: spawn). Default: contract, or none when outsideContract is set. Mandatory Jev completion and output checks apply in either mode.
- `communicationLane` (one of `"parent-only"`, `"parent-and-children"`, `"cohort"`, `"direct"`, optional): Permitted communication lane for the spawned agent (mode: spawn). Default: parent-only for children, direct for root workers. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
- `orchestrationGraphId` (string, optional): Explicit orchestration graph id to attach the spawned worker to (mode: spawn). Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
- `orchestrationNodeId` (string, optional): Explicit orchestration node id for the spawned worker (mode: spawn). Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
- `parentNodeId` (string, optional): Parent orchestration node id for the spawned worker (mode: spawn). Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
- `restrictTools` (boolean, optional, default `false`): If true, use ONLY the specified tools (override mode). If false or omitted, specified tools are merged with template defaults (additive mode). Only applies when tools is also provided (mode: spawn). Needs outsideContract=true: on a contract this is refused, because the contract planner chooses the tools and write scope of each unit.
- `outsideContract` (boolean, optional, default `false`): If true, run a bounded helper directly instead of using contract units (mode: spawn, batch-spawn). Native Jev completion and output checks remain mandatory. Use the default contract for requested deliverables or multi-part work. Default: false.
- `tasks` (array of object, optional): Tasks to hand over at once (mode: batch-spawn). Max 20. The tasks without outsideContract become the proposed units of one contract, whose planner decides the units that run; tasks with outsideContract run as separate agents, up to the active-agent cap.
  - `task` (string, required): Task description for the agent.
  - `template` (one of `"orchestrator"`, `"planner"`, `"engineer"`, `"reviewer"`, `"tester"`, `"researcher"`, `"integrator"`, `"general"`, optional): Agent template.
  - `model` (string, optional): Model for this task. A bare model id resolves automatically; use provider:model only when the id exists on more than one provider. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
  - `provider` (string, optional): Provider override. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
  - `fallbackModels` (array of string, optional): Ordered models to try if the primary model fails. Bare ids resolve automatically. Without them the owner's provider.fallbackModels applies; routing.providerFailurePolicy "fail" tries none. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
  - `executionIntent` (object, optional): Explicit execution-intent hints for downstream runtimes. Needs outsideContract=true: on a contract this is refused, because the contract planner chooses the tools and write scope of each unit.
    - `riskClass` (one of `"safe"`, `"elevated"`, `"dangerous"`, optional): Execution risk classification hint.
    - `requiresApproval` (boolean, optional): Whether approval-sensitive execution is required.
    - `networkPolicy` (one of `"inherit"`, `"allow"`, `"deny"`, `"scoped"`, optional): Requested network posture.
    - `filesystemPolicy` (one of `"inherit"`, `"workspace-write"`, `"read-only"`, `"isolated"`, optional): Requested filesystem posture.
  - `reasoningEffort` (one of `"none"`, `"instant"`, `"minimal"`, `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, `"xhigh"`, `"max"`, optional): Reasoning effort override. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
  - `tools` (array of string, optional): Tool subset. Needs outsideContract=true: on a contract this is refused, because the contract planner chooses the tools and write scope of each unit.
  - `restrictTools` (boolean, optional): If true, use ONLY the specified tools (override mode). Default: false. Needs outsideContract=true: on a contract this is refused, because the contract planner chooses the tools and write scope of each unit.
  - `context` (string, optional): Additional context.
  - `successCriteria` (array of string, optional): Concrete success criteria. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
  - `requiredEvidence` (array of string, optional): Evidence the spawned agent must return. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
  - `writeScope` (array of string, optional): Expected write ownership scope. Needs outsideContract=true: on a contract this is refused, because the contract planner chooses the tools and write scope of each unit.
  - `executionProtocol` (one of `"direct"`, `"gather-plan-apply"`, optional): Execution discipline. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
  - `reviewMode` (one of `"none"`, `"contract"`, optional): Whether the work is checked as a contract. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
  - `communicationLane` (one of `"parent-only"`, `"parent-and-children"`, `"cohort"`, `"direct"`, optional): Permitted communication lane. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
  - `orchestrationGraphId` (string, optional): Graph id to attach the worker to. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
  - `orchestrationNodeId` (string, optional): Explicit node id for the worker. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
  - `parentNodeId` (string, optional): Parent node id for the worker. Applies only with outsideContract=true; without it the work runs as a contract and this is not carried.
  - `outsideContract` (boolean, optional): Run a bounded helper as a standalone agent with mandatory Jev completion/output checks, instead of contract units. Default: the batch's outsideContract.
- `cohort` (string, optional): Cohort name to group agents together (mode: spawn, batch-spawn; applies to agents run with outsideContract=true, not to a contract's owner). Filter by cohort (mode: list, cohort-status, cohort-report).
- `agentId` (string, optional): Agent ID to query, cancel, get, budget, plan, wait, or message (mode: status, cancel, get, budget, plan, wait, message).
- `detail` (one of `"summary"`, `"contract"`, `"messages"`, `"full"`, optional): Detail level for inspection/reporting modes. Summary keeps the core execution state; contract adds capability/ownership data; messages adds recent bus traffic; full returns everything.
- `timeoutMs` (number, optional): Timeout in milliseconds for the wait action (mode: wait). Default: 0 (non-blocking, returns immediately). Returns as soon as the agent ends. One wait is capped at contract.heartbeatTimeoutMs (default 600000, 10 minutes; 30 minutes when that is 0); a reduced wait reports requestedMs and limitMs. If the agent is still running at the timeout, returns its current status with waitedMs and a hint to wait again.
- `message` (string, optional): Message content to send to an agent (mode: message). Sent to the id a delegation returned (a contract), it goes to the agents working that contract's units now, and the result lists them.
- `kind` (one of `"directive"`, `"status"`, `"question"`, `"finding"`, `"review"`, `"handoff"`, `"escalation"`, `"completion"`, optional): Structured communication kind for the message (mode: message). Default: directive.
- `includeTerminal` (boolean, optional): Include contracts that already ended (mode: contracts). Default: true.
- `contractId` (string, optional): The contract to read (mode: contract-history).

### `analyze`

Multi-mode code analysis tool. Modes: impact (change blast radius), dependencies (import graph / circular detection), dead_code (unreferenced exports), security (hardcoded secrets/env audit), coverage (lcov parse), surface (public API exports), preview (diff without writing), diff (git ref diff), bundle (stats.json parse), breaking (API breaking changes between refs), semantic_diff (LLM-powered diff summary), upgrade (npm registry version check), permissions (dangerous pattern scan), env_audit (.env file key comparison), test_find (locate test files for source files).

Permission category `read`; side effects: `read_fs`, `network`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"impact"`, `"dependencies"`, `"dead_code"`, `"security"`, `"coverage"`, `"bundle"`, `"preview"`, `"diff"`, `"surface"`, `"breaking"`, `"semantic_diff"`, `"upgrade"`, `"permissions"`, `"env_audit"`, `"test_find"`, required): Analysis mode to run.
- `files` (array of string, optional): Target files or directories for analysis.
- `projectRoot` (string, optional): Project root directory. Defaults to current working directory.
- `changes` (string, optional): Description of planned changes (mode: impact).
- `submode` (one of `"analyze"`, `"circular"`, `"upgrade"`, optional): Sub-mode for dependencies analysis. analyze: the import graph. circular: import cycles. upgrade: lists the external packages the scanned files import, with no version check (mode upgrade checks versions). Default: analyze.
- `securityScope` (one of `"secrets"`, `"permissions"`, `"env"`, `"all"`, optional): Security check scope (mode: security). Default: all.
- `before` (string, optional): Git ref (branch, tag or commit; must not start with '-') for the before state (modes: diff, breaking, semantic_diff). Not a file path; use files to narrow the diff to paths.
- `after` (string, optional): Git ref (branch, tag or commit; must not start with '-') for the after state (modes: diff, breaking, semantic_diff). Not a file path.
- `find` (string, optional): String to find (mode: preview). Used with replace.
- `replace` (string, optional): Replacement string (mode: preview).
- `packages` (array of string, optional): Package names to check (mode: upgrade). Defaults to all packages in package.json.
- `output` (object, optional): Output options.
  - `format` (one of `"summary"`, `"detailed"`, `"json"`, optional): Output format. Default: json.
  - `max_tokens` (integer, optional, at least 0): Approximate token budget for the response.

### `channel`

Inspect and operate channel surfaces. Modes: accounts, account_action, directory, resolve_target, capabilities, tools, agent_tools, run_tool, actions, run_action, authorize. run_action refuses actions marked dangerous and edit-allowlist, and account_action refuses the actions that write or remove credentials (setup, connect, login, wait_login, disconnect, logout); the owner runs those. authorize checks that the account is enabled and the action is available; actorId is the value you pass, not an identity, and is evaluated against an allowlist only when result.metadata.actorEvaluated is true.

Permission category `delegate`; side effects: `state`, `network`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"accounts"`, `"account_action"`, `"directory"`, `"resolve_target"`, `"capabilities"`, `"tools"`, `"agent_tools"`, `"run_tool"`, `"actions"`, `"run_action"`, `"authorize"`, required): What to do; see the tool description. Every mode but accounts, capabilities, tools, agent_tools and actions needs surface.
- `surface` (string, optional): The channel surface, such as slack, discord or telegram; for the listing modes, omitted means every surface.
- `accountId` (string, optional): The account on the surface: accounts shows that one; account_action, resolve_target and authorize act for it.
- `accountAction` (string, optional): account_action: the account action to run (actions that write or remove credentials are refused).
- `query` (string, optional): directory: the text to look up; resolve_target: the target when target is not given.
- `target` (string, optional): resolve_target: the user, chat or channel to resolve, as a name or id; authorize: the target the action would reach.
- `preferredKind` (string, optional): resolve_target: the kind of conversation to prefer: direct, group, channel, thread or service.
- `threadId` (string, optional): resolve_target: the thread within the target.
- `createIfMissing` (boolean, optional): resolve_target: when nothing matches, return the target as given instead of failing.
- `live` (boolean, optional): directory, resolve_target: also ask the provider, not only the routes already known.
- `scope` (string, optional): directory: which entries: all, self, users, peers, groups, channels, threads, services or members.
- `groupId` (string, optional): directory: the group whose members or threads to list.
- `limit` (number, optional): directory: at most this many entries.
- `toolId` (string, optional): run_tool: the channel tool, by id or name, as mode tools lists it.
- `actionId` (string, optional): run_action, authorize: the operator action, as mode actions lists it.
- `actorId` (string, optional): authorize: the sender to check; it is a value you pass, not a proven identity.
- `input` (object, optional): account_action, run_tool, run_action, authorize: the arguments the action or tool takes.

### `context_accounting`

Report the current session's context composition honestly: what was passively injected this turn (memory record ids, sources, and why), recall-contract outcomes (relevance floor, budget exclusions, degraded/lexical fallback, index-unavailable reasons), compaction state, and token-budget state. Measured token counts are reported as fact; estimated values are flagged. Call this to tell "no memory exists" apart from "recall was floored" apart from "the index is unavailable". Read-only.

Permission category `read`; side effects: `read_fs`.

Inputs: none.

### `contract_self_check`

Read how your contract unit's acceptance criteria read now, from the last check, without ending your turn. Read-only; it passes nothing and describes the last check, not work done since.

Permission category `read`; side effects: `read_fs`.

Inputs: none.

### `control`

List this product's own slash commands (name and one-line description) and panels, the built-in subscription providers, and the sandbox presets. A session without a command surface answers available: false.

Permission category `delegate`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"commands"`, `"panels"`, `"subscriptions"`, `"sandbox-presets"`, required): What to list: commands (slash commands), panels, subscriptions (built-in subscription providers) or sandbox-presets.

### `edit`

Edit files by finding and replacing text. Supports exact, fuzzy, and regex matching. Handles multiple edits in one call with atomic or partial transaction semantics. Read a file before editing it: an edit is refused (OCC conflict) when the file changed since your last read, and stays refused until you read it again. Also supports Jupyter notebook (.ipynb) cell operations via notebook_operations field.

Permission category `write`; side effects: `write_fs`.

Inputs:

- `edits` (array of object, optional, at least items: 1): The text replacements to make, each a path with a find and a replace; give either edits or notebook_operations.
  - `path` (string, required): File path to edit (relative to project root or absolute within it)
  - `find` (string, optional): Text to find in the file. Required unless find_base64 is sent; must not be empty.
  - `find_base64` (string, optional): Base64-encoded text to find, used instead of find for binary-safe transport. Send one of find or find_base64; if both are sent they must decode to the same text.
  - `replace` (string, optional): Replacement text. Required unless replace_base64 is sent; an empty string deletes the match.
  - `replace_base64` (string, optional): Base64-encoded replacement text, used instead of replace for binary-safe transport. Send one of replace or replace_base64; if both are sent they must decode to the same text.
  - `id` (string, optional): Optional identifier for this edit, used in result tracking.
  - `occurrence` (one of `"first"`, `"last"`, `"all"` or integer, optional): Which occurrence to replace. Default: error if 0 or 2+ matches (ambiguity guard). Set to first/last/all/N to override.
  - `hints` (object, optional): Narrow which occurrence of find is meant.
    - `near_line` (integer, optional, at least 1): Prefer the occurrence closest to this line number.
    - `in_function` (string, optional): Only match within a function with this name.
    - `in_class` (string, optional): Only match within a class with this name.
    - `after` (string, optional): Only match occurrences that appear after this text anchor in the file.
    - `before` (string, optional): Only match occurrences that appear before this text anchor in the file.
- `match` (object, optional): How find is matched, for every edit of the call.
  - `mode` (one of `"exact"`, `"fuzzy"`, `"regex"`, `"ast"`, `"ast_pattern"`, optional, default `"exact"`): Match mode. exact: literal string match (whitespace differences are tolerated); text not in the file fails at once with the closest lines to copy. fuzzy: whitespace-insensitive, and when nothing matches the single closest run of lines is applied if a decision-model check reads it as the intended code. regex: treat find as regex. ast: structural match using tree-sitter; if unavailable, exact fallback is reported as a warning. ast_pattern: pattern matching using @ast-grep/napi metavariables like $VAR or $$$ARGS; if unavailable, exact fallback is reported as a warning.
  - `case_sensitive` (boolean, optional, default `true`): Whether matching is case-sensitive. Default: true.
  - `whitespace_sensitive` (boolean, optional, default `true`): Whether whitespace differences matter. When false in exact mode, delegates to fuzzy matching algorithm. Default: true.
  - `multiline` (boolean, optional, default `false`): When true and mode is regex, adds the s (dotAll) and m (multiline) flags. s flag: . matches newlines, enabling patterns that span multiple lines. m flag: ^ and $ match at line boundaries. Default: false.
- `transaction` (object, optional): Whether the edits of the call succeed or fail together.
  - `mode` (one of `"atomic"`, `"partial"`, `"none"`, optional, default `"atomic"`): atomic: all edits succeed or all fail (default). partial: apply succeeding edits, report failures, roll nothing back. none: older name for partial.
- `output` (object, optional): How much the result reports.
  - `format` (one of `"count_only"`, `"minimal"`, `"with_diff"`, `"verbose"`, optional, default `"minimal"`): count_only: only total edits applied. minimal: per-edit success/failure summary (default). with_diff: include unified diff per edit. verbose: untruncated diffs plus each changed file's content before and after (20,000 characters each, longer content says how much was left out). Results include status field: applied | not_found | ambiguous | conflict | failed, decided by the matcher that refused the edit. Failed results include hint field with actionable suggestions (count_only lists failed edits by path and status).
  - `diff_context` (integer, optional, at least 0, default `3`): Number of context lines to include around each change in unified diffs. Default: 3. Reduce to 0 for minimal diffs, increase for more context.
- `dry_run` (boolean, optional, default `false`): Compute all replacements and return diffs without writing to disk. Default: false.
- `validate` (object, optional): Run validators (the project's own typecheck, lint, test or build command: its package.json script through its package manager, the Cargo/Go toolchain, a Makefile target or a pyproject-configured pytest/mypy/ruff, else the owner's tools.validators.<name> setting) before and/or after applying edits. One the project does not declare is refused before anything changes. They run through the exec tool's path, under the same sandbox, containment and credential rules as an exec command; a session without one refuses validate.
  - `before` (array of one of `"typecheck"`, `"lint"`, `"test"`, `"build"`, optional): Validators to run before applying edits. If any fail, edits are not applied.
  - `after` (array of one of `"typecheck"`, `"lint"`, `"test"`, `"build"`, optional): Validators to run after applying edits. If any fail in atomic mode, edits are rolled back.
- `notebook_operations` (object, optional): Jupyter notebook (.ipynb) cell operations. Alternative to edits, provide either edits or notebook_operations, not both. match, transaction and validate do not apply to notebook operations and are refused when sent with them.
  - `path` (string, required): Path to .ipynb notebook file.
  - `operations` (array of object, required, at least items: 1): The cell operations, applied in order.
    - `op` (one of `"replace"`, `"insert"`, `"delete"`, required): Cell operation: replace existing cell content, insert a new cell, or delete a cell. Any other op is refused by name and nothing is written.
    - `cell` (integer, optional, at least 0): 0-based cell index in the notebook as it was before any operation of this call (used by replace/delete when cell_id is not provided). Inserts and deletes earlier in the same call do not renumber it.
    - `cell_id` (string, optional): Cell ID targeting, takes precedence over cell index for all operations.
    - `after` (integer, optional, at least -1): For insert: insert after this 0-based index, numbered as before any operation of this call (-1 = insert at beginning). Omit to append at end.
    - `source` (string, optional): Cell source content (required for replace and insert operations)
    - `cell_type` (one of `"code"`, `"markdown"`, `"raw"`, optional): Cell type (required for insert; optional for replace, if provided, changes the cell type)
    - `clear_outputs` (boolean, optional): Clear cell outputs on replace (default: false)

### `exec`

Execute shell commands. Supports batch, parallel, background, retry, timeout, expectation-checking, until-pattern, and pre-command file operations.

Permission category `execute`; side effects: `exec`, `read_fs`, `write_fs`.

Inputs:

- `commands` (array of object, required, at least items: 1): Commands to execute. Run sequentially by default, parallel if parallel=true.
  - `cmd` (string, optional): Shell command to execute via sh -c. Special values manage background processes started with background: true: "bg_list", "bg_status <process_id>", "bg_output <process_id> [tail=<bytes>|from=<byte>]", "bg_stop <process_id>". bg_output reads the saved output: tail= the last bytes, from= onward from a byte offset.
  - `cmd_base64` (string, optional): Base64-encoded command. Use when cmd contains special characters. Give cmd or cmd_base64, not both; entries that give both with different text are refused.
  - `working_dir` (string, optional): Per-command working directory override. Prefer the top-level working_dir for the project root. For a single-command call with no top-level working_dir, it is used as the working_dir.
  - `timeout_ms` (integer, optional, at least 0): Optional per-command timeout in milliseconds. Omitted or 0 waits for completion or cancellation.
  - `env` (object, optional): Additional environment variables merged with the current process env.
  - `expect` (object, optional): Expectations to validate after the command completes.
    - `exit_code` (integer, optional): Expected exit code.
    - `stdout_contains` (string, optional): Substring that stdout must contain.
    - `stderr_contains` (string, optional): Substring that stderr must contain.
  - `background` (boolean, optional): Run detached, returns immediately with a process_id. Manage it with later exec calls whose cmd is "bg_list", "bg_status <id>", "bg_output <id> [tail=<bytes>|from=<byte>]" or "bg_stop <id>".
  - `retry` (object, optional): Retry configuration for transient failures.
    - `max` (integer, optional, at least 1): Maximum retry attempts. Default: 3.
    - `delay_ms` (integer, optional, at least 0): Base delay between retries in ms. Default: 1000.
    - `max_delay_ms` (integer, optional, at least 0): Max jitter cap for exponential backoff in ms. Default: 30000.
    - `backoff` (one of `"fixed"`, `"exponential"`, optional): Backoff strategy. Default: exponential.
    - `on` (array of one of `"network"`, `"lock"`, `"busy"`, `"oom"`, optional): Error categories to retry on. Default: ["network", "lock", "busy"].
  - `until` (object, optional): Pattern-based early termination. Watch stdout/stderr for a regex match.
    - `pattern` (string, required): Regex to watch for in combined stdout/stderr.
    - `timeout_ms` (integer, optional, at least 0): Optional pattern-wait timeout in ms. Omitted uses the command timeout; 0 waits until cancellation.
    - `kill_after` (boolean, optional): Kill the process when pattern matches. Default false (promotes to background).
  - `progress` (boolean, optional): Stream stdout lines to a pollable progress file at .goodvibes/.overflow/{id}-progress.txt. true: the file is created when the command starts and kept. Unset (with no timeout or timeout_ms > 30000): a file is created only once the command has run 30 s, and removed when it finishes; a stopped command keeps it. false: no file. The result includes a progress_file path when one is kept.
  - `interactive` (boolean, optional): Run under a PTY so terminal prompts (host-key confirmations, credential asks) can be detected and answered instead of hanging. Without it a command runs with piped output; a plain sudo, doas or su that fails only for want of a terminal is run once more under a PTY (when the host has one) and the result says so; any other command that needed a terminal is not repeated and the result says to rerun it with interactive: true. Set false to keep the plain pipe path. PTY output merges stderr into stdout (result notes pty: true).
- `parallel` (boolean, optional): Run all commands in parallel. Default: false (sequential). A parallel run starts every command, so stop_on_error does not apply.
- `working_dir` (string, optional): Global working directory applied to all commands unless overridden per-command. Optional, defaults to the session's working directory when omitted. A sandboxed command must use a directory inside the session's project root.
- `timeout_ms` (integer, optional, at least 0): Optional timeout in ms applied to all commands. Omitted or 0 waits for completion or cancellation.
- `verbosity` (one of `"count_only"`, `"minimal"`, `"standard"`, `"verbose"`, optional): count_only: exit codes only (plus process_id, timed_out, cancelled, expectation_error, warnings and other notices that explain or act on the result); minimal: exit codes + first line stdout/stderr; standard: full stdout/stderr + exit code (default); verbose: everything + timing, env, cwd.
- `stop_on_error` (boolean, optional): Sequential runs only (ignored with parallel: true): stop at the first failed command (non-zero exit, timed_out, or expectation_error). Unexecuted commands appear as {skipped: true} entries. Default: false.
- `file_ops` (array of object, optional): File operations to execute BEFORE commands run, on the host and outside any sandbox. Every path, absolute or relative, must be inside the project root; delete refuses the root itself and .git. If one fails, the earlier ones stay applied (listed in the result), no commands run, and nothing is undone. Refused in sessions that require the exec boundary.
  - `op` (one of `"copy"`, `"move"`, `"delete"`, required): Operation type.
  - `source` (string, required): Source path (relative or absolute), which must be inside the project root.
  - `destination` (string, optional): Destination path. Required for copy and move.
  - `recursive` (boolean, optional): Copy/delete directories recursively. Deleting a path that does not exist fails and names the path.
  - `overwrite` (boolean, optional, default `false`): Overwrite destination if it already exists (copy/move only). Default: false. When false and destination exists, the operation returns an error.
  - `dry_run` (boolean, optional, default `false`): Preview what would be deleted without deleting (delete only). Default: false. Returns a list of files that would be deleted.
  - `update_imports` (boolean, optional, default `false`): After a move of a TypeScript/JavaScript file or of a directory, rewrite every relative import of a moved file (written with or without an extension, or as a directory index) in the files that import it, and re-base each moved file's own relative imports for its new directory. All moves of one call share one pass over the project. Non-relative imports (aliases, packages) are not touched. A warning says when nothing changed. Default: false.

### `fetch`

Fetch one or more URLs via HTTP. Supports batch parallel/sequential requests, per-URL method/headers/body/params, extraction modes (raw, text, json, markdown, readable, code_blocks, links, metadata, structured, tables, pdf, summary), per-URL timeouts, caching, rate limiting, auth refresh, content-length limits, redirect tracking, timing metrics, token estimation, and verbosity control.

Permission category `read`; side effects: `network`.

Inputs:

- `urls` (array of object, required, at least items: 1): URLs to fetch. Processed as a batch in one call.
  - `url` (string, required): The URL to fetch.
  - `method` (one of `"GET"`, `"POST"`, `"PUT"`, `"DELETE"`, `"PATCH"`, `"HEAD"`, `"OPTIONS"`, optional): HTTP method. Defaults to GET.
  - `params` (object, optional): Query parameters to append to the URL as a query string.
  - `headers` (object, optional): HTTP headers to include in the request.
  - `body` (string, optional): Request body string.
  - `body_base64` (string, optional): Base64-encoded request body, decoded to bytes and sent as binary. Content-Type defaults to application/octet-stream unless body_type is json or form. Precedence: body_data (with form or multipart) wins over body_base64, which wins over body.
  - `body_type` (one of `"json"`, `"form"`, `"raw"`, `"multipart"`, optional): How to encode the body. json: sets Content-Type application/json; form: URL-encodes body_data or sends body as application/x-www-form-urlencoded; multipart: builds a FormData body from body_data (object of key-value pairs); raw: sends body as-is with no default Content-Type (set one in headers).
  - `body_data` (object, optional): Key-value pairs for structured request bodies. For form, entries are URL-encoded into the request body. For multipart, each entry becomes a FormData field.
  - `extract` (one of `"raw"`, `"text"`, `"json"`, `"markdown"`, `"readable"`, `"code_blocks"`, `"links"`, `"metadata"`, `"structured"`, `"tables"`, `"pdf"`, `"summary"`, optional): Extraction mode for this URL. Overrides the global extract. raw: raw response body; text: plain text, strips HTML tags; json: ask for JSON (Accept: application/json unless headers set Accept), parse and format it (a body that is not JSON comes back as written, with json_parse_error); markdown: convert HTML to markdown; readable: extract main content, strip nav/sidebar/footer; code_blocks: extract <pre>/<code> blocks; links: extract all URLs; metadata: extract title/og-tags; structured: extract text of elements matching simple selectors: tag, #id, .class, tag.class (requires selectors field); tables: parse <table> elements into JSON arrays; pdf: extract the text of a PDF response, page by page (no OCR; pdf_error says why when nothing could be read); summary: extractive summary (the paragraph that says what the page is about + headings).
  - `selectors` (array of string, optional): Selectors for structured extraction mode: tag, #id, .class, or tag.class with any number of classes (for example "h2", "#main", ".note", "div.card.big"). Combinators, attribute selectors and comma lists are not supported and are reported as an error. Each matched element text is returned as an array item.
  - `timeout_ms` (integer, optional, at least 1): Per-URL timeout in milliseconds. Default 30000.
  - `max_content_length` (integer, optional, at least 1): Maximum response body size in bytes. Responses exceeding this are truncated (truncated: true). Overrides global max_content_length. Default 5000000.
  - `retry_on_auth` (boolean, optional): When a service is specified and a 401 is returned, attempt to refresh auth and retry once. Defaults to true when service is specified.
  - `service` (string, optional): Named service for automatic credential lookup from the service registry. The credential is sent only to the service's own origin (its baseUrl); a URL on another origin is refused with nothing sent. Services are configured in the host services.json file. Use the registry tool or inspect that registry to discover available service names.
  - `auth` (object, optional): Inline auth configuration. Applied directly without registry lookup.
    - `type` (one of `"bearer"`, `"basic"`, `"api-key"`, required): Auth type.
    - `token` (string, optional): Bearer token (for type bearer).
    - `username` (string, optional): Username (for type basic).
    - `password` (string, optional): Password (for type basic).
    - `header` (string, optional): Header name (for type api-key). Defaults to X-API-Key.
    - `key` (string, optional): API key value (for type api-key).
- `extract` (one of `"raw"`, `"text"`, `"json"`, `"markdown"`, `"readable"`, `"code_blocks"`, `"links"`, `"metadata"`, `"structured"`, `"tables"`, `"pdf"`, `"summary"`, optional): Global extraction mode applied to all URLs unless overridden per-URL. Defaults to raw.
- `parallel` (boolean, optional): Fetch URLs in parallel. Default true. Setting rate_limit_ms runs them one after another instead.
- `verbosity` (one of `"count_only"`, `"minimal"`, `"standard"`, `"verbose"`, optional): count_only: totals only; minimal: URL + status + byte size; standard: URL + status + content (default); verbose: all metadata, with the value of credential headers (set-cookie, authorization and the like) withheld.
- `cache_ttl_seconds` (integer, optional, at least 0): Cache successful GET responses (status below 400) by URL+params for this many seconds. Error statuses are never cached. 0 disables caching (default).
- `rate_limit_ms` (integer, optional, at least 0): Minimum delay in milliseconds between requests. Any value above 0 runs the URLs one after another with this pacing, whatever parallel says. 0 disables rate limiting (default).
- `max_content_length` (integer, optional, at least 1): Global maximum response body size in bytes. Responses exceeding this are truncated (truncated: true). Default 5000000. Can be overridden per-URL.
- `sanitize_mode` (one of `"none"`, `"safe-text"`, `"strict"`, optional): Response sanitization mode applied to all URL responses. none: content returned verbatim (trusted hosts only); safe-text: strips script/style blocks, control characters and invisible Unicode (default); strict: strips all HTML and every non-ASCII character (untrusted hosts). Both modes alter the content, so structured data can change; a result whose content was altered carries sanitized: true and sanitized_removed (characters removed by kind), and sanitize_note when more than a tenth of the text went. Tags are stripped only from content that is still HTML or XML (extract raw); extracted text keeps a literal < or >.
- `blocked_hosts` (array of string, optional): Hostnames or glob patterns explicitly blocked. Denied pre-request regardless of other config.

### `find`

Search the codebase using glob patterns, regex content search, or symbol extraction. Supports multiple queries in one call. Modes: files (glob), content (grep), symbols (regex).

Permission category `read`; side effects: `read_fs`.
