Inputs:

- `queries` (array of object, required, at least items: 1): One or more search queries to execute.
  - `id` (string, required): Unique identifier for this query. Results are keyed by this id.
  - `mode` (one of `"files"`, `"content"`, `"symbols"`, `"references"`, `"structural"`, required): Search mode: files (glob), content (grep; files over 8 MiB are skipped and counted), symbols (declarations from the tree-sitter parser; a language without a grammar uses line patterns and a warning says so), references (the language server's answer when one is attached, an empty answer included, scoped to path; otherwise a word match on the symbol name with fallback_reason saying why), structural (AST pattern matching via ast-grep).
  - `patterns` (array of string, optional): Glob patterns (mode: files).
  - `exclude` (array of string, optional): Glob patterns to exclude (mode: files).
  - `min_size` (integer, optional, at least 0): Minimum file size in bytes (mode: files).
  - `max_size` (integer, optional, at least 0): Maximum file size in bytes (mode: files).
  - `modified_after` (string, optional): ISO date string, include only files modified after this date (mode: files).
  - `modified_before` (string, optional): ISO date string, include only files modified before this date (mode: files).
  - `respect_gitignore` (boolean, optional): Exclude files matched by .gitignore and .ignore patterns (mode: files). Default: true. Note: only reads the project root .gitignore and .ignore, nested ones are not applied.
  - `sort_by` (one of `"name"`, `"size"`, `"modified"`, optional): Sort results by name, size, or modified date (mode: files). Default: name.
  - `sort_order` (one of `"asc"`, `"desc"`, optional): Sort direction (mode: files). Default: asc.
  - `has_content` (string, optional): Regex pattern, include only files whose content matches (mode: files).
  - `is_empty` (boolean, optional): When true include only empty files; when false exclude empty files (mode: files).
  - `follow_symlinks` (boolean, optional): Follow symbolic links when collecting files (mode: files). Default: false.
  - `include_hidden` (boolean, optional): Include hidden files and directories (dot-prefixed) (mode: files). Default: false.
  - `pattern` (string, optional): Regex search pattern (mode: content).
  - `pattern_base64` (string, optional): Base64-encoded regex pattern, alternative to pattern (mode: content).
  - `glob` (string, optional): File filter glob pattern (mode: content).
  - `path` (string, optional): Directory to search (modes: files, content, symbols, references, structural). Defaults to project root.
  - `case_sensitive` (boolean, optional): Case-sensitive matching (mode: content). Default: true.
  - `whole_word` (boolean, optional): Match whole words only (mode: content).
  - `multiline` (boolean, optional): No effect: content mode matches each line on its own, so a pattern cannot span lines (the call warns when this is set). Search for one line of the text instead.
  - `negate` (boolean, optional): Return files that do NOT match the pattern (mode: content).
  - `ranked` (boolean, optional): Sort results by relevance (mode: content). Each matched file is judged against the pattern; files where what the pattern names is defined, declared, exported or implemented come first, files that only mention it come after. Every match is still returned.
  - `preview_replace` (string, optional): Replacement string (mode: content). When provided, shows what each matched line would look like after replacement WITHOUT writing to disk. Adds original and replaced fields to each match.
  - `relationships` (boolean, optional): Include import/export relationships (mode: content). For each matched file, shows which files import it and which files it imports.
  - `symbol` (string, optional): Symbol name to search for references to (mode: references).
  - `file` (string, optional): File path containing the symbol (mode: references).
  - `line` (integer, optional, at least 1): One-based line number of the symbol, as find results report lines (mode: references).
  - `column` (integer, optional, at least 0): Zero-based column offset of the symbol on that line (mode: references). Used only by a language server.
  - `query` (string, optional): Symbol name pattern to filter by (mode: symbols).
  - `kinds` (array of one of `"function"`, `"class"`, `"interface"`, `"type"`, `"variable"`, `"constant"`, `"enum"`, optional): Symbol kinds to include (mode: symbols).
  - `exported_only` (boolean, optional): Only return exported symbols (mode: symbols). Default: false.
  - `include_private` (boolean, optional): Include non-exported (private) symbols (mode: symbols). When true, overrides exported_only and includes all symbols regardless of export status.
  - `group_by` (one of `"file"`, `"kind"`, `"none"`, optional): Group symbol results (mode: symbols). file: group by file path, kind: group by symbol kind, none: flat list (default).
  - `lang` (one of `"ts"`, `"tsx"`, `"js"`, `"jsx"`, `"css"`, `"html"`, optional): Language for AST parsing (mode: structural). Omitted: each file is parsed by its extension. Set without glob: only files with this language's extensions are searched. Set with glob: every file the glob names is parsed as this language. Supported: ts, tsx, js, jsx, css, html. Files with other extensions are skipped and counted.
- `output` (object, optional): Output format options.
  - `format` (one of `"count_only"`, `"files_only"`, `"locations"`, `"matches"`, `"context"`, `"with_stats"`, `"with_preview"`, `"signatures"`, `"full"`, optional): Progressive disclosure format. count_only < files_only < locations < matches < context. The format is shared by every query of the call; a format that does not belong to a query's mode is replaced by the nearest one for that mode and the result warns. with_stats returns file size and modified date per file (mode: files). with_preview returns first N lines of each file (mode: files, controlled by preview_lines). signatures: include full function/method signature with params+return type (mode: symbols). full: include signature + JSDoc comment + container class/namespace (mode: symbols).
  - `preview_lines` (integer, optional, at least 1): Number of lines to include in preview (format: with_preview). Default: 3.
  - `context_before` (integer, optional, at least 0): Lines before each match (format: context).
  - `context_after` (integer, optional, at least 0): Lines after each match (format: context).
  - `expand_to` (one of `"line"`, `"block"`, `"function"`, `"class"`, optional): Expand each content match to its enclosing scope. 'function' expands to the enclosing function/method, 'class' to the enclosing class. Adds startLine and endLine fields to each match. Requires tree-sitter grammar for the file language; results remain unexpanded when unavailable. 'line' and 'block' are accepted but currently behave the same as no expansion.
  - `offset` (integer, optional, at least 0): Zero-based result offset for pagination. Use next_offset from the previous page.
  - `max_results` (integer, optional, at least 1): Results per page, at least 1. Default: 100. Searches all eligible files and reports the full count and next_offset.
  - `max_per_item` (integer, optional, at least 0): Optional per-file display limit. By default all matches are eligible for pagination.
  - `max_total_matches` (integer, optional, at least 1): Matches per page across all files. Default: 100. Does not stop the search scan.
  - `max_tokens` (integer, optional, at least 0): Approximate token budget for the whole call's results (about 4 characters per token), shared equally among its queries. A page that would exceed its share is shortened; continue with next_offset. Default: about 10,000 tokens per query, less when several queries share the call.
  - `max_line_length` (integer, optional, at least 1): Truncate matched lines longer than this value (mode: content). Adds "..." suffix when truncated.
- `parallel` (boolean, optional): Execute queries concurrently. Default: true.
- `timeout_ms` (integer, optional, at least 1): Deadline for the whole call. A query still running then returns timed_out with no results while finished queries keep theirs. Default: 60000.

### `goodvibes_context`

Inspect the current GoodVibes runtime and host harness. Use before answering questions about settings, configured integrations, surfaces, providers, models, tools, Home Assistant, Cloudflare, ntfy, Slack, companion apps, or daemon/TUI capabilities. Returns redacted config only.

Permission category `read`; side effects: `state`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"summary"`, `"config_get"`, `"config_schema"`, `"integrations"`, `"tools"`, `"cloudflare_status"`, `"cloudflare_token_requirements"`, required): summary of the runtime; config_get current setting values (redacted); config_schema the settings' definitions; integrations the channel surfaces; tools the registered tools; cloudflare_status; cloudflare_token_requirements the token permissions a Cloudflare setup needs.
- `key` (string, optional): config_get, config_schema: one setting key, exactly.
- `category` (string, optional): config_get, config_schema: only settings whose key starts with this domain (the part before the first dot).
- `prefix` (string, optional): config_get, config_schema: only settings whose key starts with this text.
- `surface` (string, optional): integrations: only this channel surface (for example slack).
- `includeSchema` (boolean, optional): config_get: also return each setting's type, default and description (default true).
- `includeParameters` (boolean, optional): tools: also return each tool's input schema (default false).
- `includeBootstrap` (boolean, optional): cloudflare_token_requirements: also list the permission the temporary bootstrap token needs to create the narrower operational token.
- `components` (object, optional): cloudflare_token_requirements: the Cloudflare components to plan for, each true or false.
- `limit` (number, optional): config_get: at most this many settings (every match when unset); tools: at most this many tools (default 250, at most 1000).

### `goodvibes_settings`

Apply a GoodVibes setting. When the user supplies a concrete configuration value, a bot username, a chat id, a host, a port, a model, a path, that is a request to set it: call this tool, then tell the user the key and the persistedTo store it landed in. A value only mentioned in your reply has not been set. The write is routed to the runtime that owns the key: daemon-owned settings (surfaces.*, control-plane binding, watchers, device pairing, provisioning, retention) go to the daemon's config, client-owned settings stay in this client's config. The value is then re-read from that store, so a write that did not land is reported as a failure rather than as success. If you cannot tell which key a stated value belongs to, ask one short question instead of guessing, and do not set anything the user did not ask for. Raw secret/token/password values are rejected: store the secret separately and set the key to a goodvibes:// secret reference. A key the project overlay sets to something else is refused before anything is written, naming the overlay file to change instead.

Permission category `write`; side effects: `state`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"set"`, `"reset"`, required): set writes value; reset returns the key to its default.
- `key` (string, required): The setting key, as the settings list names it.
- `value` (any, optional): The value to set, of the setting's type; a credential is given as a goodvibes:// secret reference, never the secret itself.

### `inspect`

Inspect and analyze a project or file. Modes: project (structure), api (routes), api_spec (generate OpenAPI 3.0 spec), api_validate (compare spec to code), api_sync (detect frontend/backend drift), database (schema), components (React), layout (CSS/Tailwind), accessibility (a11y issues), scaffold (module skeleton generator).

Permission category `read`; side effects: `read_fs`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"project"`, `"api"`, `"api_spec"`, `"api_validate"`, `"api_sync"`, `"database"`, `"components"`, `"layout"`, `"accessibility"`, `"scaffold"`, `"component_state"`, `"render_triggers"`, `"hooks"`, `"overflow"`, `"sizing"`, `"stacking"`, `"responsive"`, `"events"`, `"tailwind"`, `"client_boundary"`, `"error_boundary"`, required): Analysis mode. project: detect project type and structure; api: scan route definitions; api_spec: generate OpenAPI 3.0 spec from discovered routes; api_validate: compare existing OpenAPI spec against discovered routes; api_sync: detect frontend/backend type drift via fetch() call analysis; database: parse schema models; components: extract React components; layout: analyze CSS/Tailwind layout; accessibility: detect a11y issues; scaffold: generate module skeleton; component_state: trace useState/useReducer/useContext; render_triggers: find re-render causes; hooks: analyze hook dependency arrays; overflow: find CSS overflow issues; sizing: analyze sizing strategy; stacking: z-index and stacking context; responsive: Tailwind breakpoint analysis; events: event handling analysis; tailwind: detect class conflicts; client_boundary: Next.js directive analysis; error_boundary: error boundary coverage.
- `projectRoot` (string, optional): Root directory for the analysis. Defaults to the current working directory. Must be inside the working directory unless access outside the project is allowed; scaffold files are written under it by the write tool, which keeps its own rule for where it may write.
- `file` (string, optional): Path to a specific file. Required for the single-file modes: components, layout, accessibility, component_state, render_triggers, hooks, overflow, sizing, stacking, responsive, events, tailwind, client_boundary and error_boundary.
- `specPath` (string, optional): Path to an OpenAPI spec (JSON). Required for api_validate mode.
- `framework` (one of `"auto"`, `"nextjs"`, `"express"`, `"fastify"`, `"hono"`, optional): Web framework for api mode. auto detects from package.json. Default: auto.
- `schemaPath` (string, optional): Path to a Prisma schema file. For database mode. Defaults to prisma/schema.prisma. Other schema formats (for example Drizzle) are not parsed.
- `moduleName` (string, optional): Module name for scaffold mode. Used to name generated files.
- `dryRun` (boolean, optional): scaffold mode: true (default) returns the file plan without writing. false creates the files through the write tool: asked and recorded as a write (undo, changed files), only new files (nothing is written when one exists), refused for an agent that has no write tool.
- `output` (object, optional): Output formatting options.
  - `format` (one of `"summary"`, `"detailed"`, `"json"`, optional): summary: condensed overview; detailed: full analysis; json: raw JSON. Default: detailed.
  - `max_tokens` (integer, optional, at least 1): Hard token cap for the response.

### `mcp`

Call tools on connected MCP servers (mode "call"), and inspect servers, tools, schemas and trust state. set-trust, set-role and approve-quarantine change what a server is allowed to do.

Permission category `delegate`; side effects: `state`, `network`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"call"`, `"servers"`, `"tools"`, `"schema"`, `"security"`, `"auth"`, `"approve-quarantine"`, `"set-trust"`, `"set-role"`, required): call runs a tool on a connected server (qualifiedName and input); tools lists the callable names; schema shows one tool's arguments.
- `view` (one of `"descriptor"`, `"preview"`, `"full"`, optional): How much of each server servers and security return: descriptor (a summary, the default), preview, or full (the whole record).
- `qualifiedName` (string, optional): mcp:<server>:<tool>, as mode:"tools" lists it.
- `input` (object, optional): Arguments for mode:"call", shaped by the tool's own schema (read it with mode:"schema").
- `serverName` (string, optional): The server to act on: required for approve-quarantine, set-trust and set-role; for servers, tools and security it narrows the list to that server.
- `trustMode` (one of `"constrained"`, `"ask-on-risk"`, `"allow-all"`, `"blocked"`, optional): The trust mode set-trust gives the server.
- `role` (one of `"general"`, `"docs"`, `"filesystem"`, `"git"`, `"database"`, `"browser"`, `"deploy"`, `"automation"`, optional): The role set-role gives the server, which decides how its tools are treated (deploy is stored as ops).

### `profile`

Record what the owner tells you about themselves: trips and other dated plans, birthdays and anniversaries, declared profile fields, and free-text facts. Also reads back what is stored, and records that the owner has an upcoming occasion in hand so the reminders stop. Use it in the same turn the thing is said, recording is part of answering, not an offer to make.

Permission category `delegate`; side effects: `state`.

Inputs:

- `action` (one of `"record_trip"`, `"record_date"`, `"set_field"`, `"note"`, `"list"`, `"acknowledge_occasion"`, required): record_trip: a trip or any dated plan, with a start and end date. record_date: a birthday, anniversary or other date that recurs or matters on one day. set_field: one of the declared profile fields, by id. note: a free-text fact under a profile section. list: read back the dates and plans already stored. acknowledge_occasion: the owner has this one in hand, so stop reminding them about it. Use it whenever the owner responds to a reminder by saying they know, they have it covered, they are already sorting it, or that they do not want to hear about it again. It stops the reminders for that occurrence only; the date stays on the profile, every other date is untouched, and next year asks fresh.
- `said` (string, optional): The owner's own words that this came from, quoted verbatim. Required for every write. This is what makes "where did you get that?" answerable later, so quote the owner rather than paraphrasing.
- `title` (string, optional): (record_trip, record_date) What to call it, e.g. "Trip to Picayune" or "Mum's birthday".
- `from` (string, optional): (record_trip) Start date as YYYY-MM-DD.
- `to` (string, optional): (record_trip) End date as YYYY-MM-DD.
- `destination` (string, optional): (record_trip) Where the trip goes, e.g. "Picayune MS".
- `away` (boolean, optional): (record_trip) True when this takes the owner away from home. Travel is away; a week of building work at the house is a real dated plan that is not. Default false.
- `details` (array of string, optional): (record_trip) Everything else the owner gave, one detail per entry: confirmation number, each flight with its number and times, who is travelling, and why they are going. Keep the figures exactly; these are the reason the itinerary was pasted.
- `date` (string, optional): (record_date) MM-DD for something that comes round every year, or YYYY-MM-DD for a single day.
- `kind` (one of `"gift-giving"`, `"remember-only"`, `"neither"`, optional): (record_date) Whether this is something to sort a gift for, something to simply remember, or neither. Never guess it, no rule tells a birthday from a death anniversary. Ask the owner if they did not say.
- `person` (string, optional): (record_date) Whose date it is, when it belongs to someone else.
- `self` (boolean, optional): (record_date) True when the date is about the OWNER: their own birthday, their own anniversary of something. The owner knows their own dates, so one they only have to remember is kept and answerable but never pushed at them. Set it when the owner says "my birthday" rather than putting their name in `person`.
- `occasionId` (string, optional): (acknowledge_occasion) Which occasion, by the id `list` gives back. Its title normalised, lower case, single spaces.
- `occurrence` (string, optional): (acknowledge_occasion) The specific date as YYYY-MM-DD, when the owner means one that is not the next one. Omit for the upcoming occurrence, which is almost always what is meant.
- `recurrence` (one of `"annual"`, `"once"`, optional): (record_date) Whether it repeats every year. Inferred from the date format when omitted.
- `leadDays` (number, optional): (record_date) How many days ahead to raise it, when the owner asked for something other than the default.
- `fieldId` (string, optional): (set_field) The declared field id, e.g. "location.city", "location.timezone", "commerce.shippingAddress", "style.verbosity". A list of valid ids comes back if this one is unknown.
- `value` (string, optional): (set_field) The value to store.
- `section` (string, optional): (note) The profile section to file it under, e.g. "People", "Places", "Work", "Preferences", "Notes".
- `text` (string, optional): (note) The fact, as one sentence.

### `query`

Leave the owner a question and carry on working. The question goes to the owner's inbox, which he reads and answers later from either terminal app, the web UI or a push notification on his phone when push is on. When he answers, the answer is put on your next model request while you are still running, or when your session is next opened; show (or list) reads it at any time. Nothing waits for it.

Permission category `read`; side effects: `state`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"ask"`, `"show"`, `"list"`, `"withdraw"`, required): ask posts a question and returns its id at once; show reads one question and its answer; list reads this session's questions; withdraw takes back a question that no longer matters.
- `question` (string, optional): (ask) The question, one line the owner can answer; at most 200 characters.
- `detail` (string, optional): (ask) Context the owner needs to answer: what you found, what each choice means.
- `options` (array of string, optional, at most items: 8): (ask) Short answers the owner can pick from; he can always answer in his own words instead.
- `key` (string, optional): (ask) Your own name for the question; asking again under the same key while it is open returns the first question instead of a second one.
- `questionId` (string, optional): (show, withdraw) The id ask returned.
- `status` (one of `"open"`, `"closed"`, `"all"`, optional): (list) Default: all.
- `reason` (string, optional): (withdraw) Why the question no longer needs an answer.

### `read`

Read one or more files from disk. Supports extract modes (content, outline, symbols, lines, ast) for token-efficient reading, per-file caching, pagination via token_budget, and batch processing.

Permission category `read`; side effects: `read_fs`.

Inputs:

- `files` (array of object, required, at least items: 1): Files to read. Processed as a batch in one call.
  - `path` (string, required): Relative or absolute path to the file.
  - `extract` (one of `"content"`, `"outline"`, `"symbols"`, `"ast"`, `"lines"`, optional): Extraction mode. Overrides the global extract for this file. content: full text; outline: signatures without bodies; symbols: exported names only; lines: specific line range; ast: the syntax tree from tree-sitter, each structural node (declarations, blocks) with its type, name and line range, indented by depth (falls back to a line-pattern outline, with a note saying why, when the file has no grammar).
  - `range` (object, optional): Line range to read (1-based, inclusive). Used with extract=lines.
    - `start` (integer, required, at least 1): First line to read, counting from 1.
    - `end` (integer, required, at least 1): Last line to read, included.
  - `force` (boolean, optional): Bypass cache and re-read the file from disk.
  - `force_text` (boolean, optional): Read a file as UTF-8 text even though it contains a NUL byte (otherwise it is skipped as binary).
  - `pages` (string, optional): Accepted for PDF files but not applied: PDF text is returned for the whole document and labelled approximate, because page boundaries are not available.
  - `image_mode` (one of `"default"`, `"unoptimized"`, `"metadata-only"`, `"thumbnail-only"`, optional): Image handling mode. default: resize to 1568px max edge (token-efficient). unoptimized: full resolution. metadata-only: dimensions/format/size only, no image data. thumbnail-only: aggressive 256px resize for previews.
- `extract` (one of `"content"`, `"outline"`, `"symbols"`, `"ast"`, `"lines"`, optional): Global extraction mode applied to all files unless overridden per-file. Defaults to content.
- `output` (object, optional): Output formatting options.
  - `format` (one of `"count_only"`, `"minimal"`, `"standard"`, `"verbose"`, optional): count_only: file count + totals; minimal: paths + line counts; standard: full content with line numbers (default); verbose: full content + metadata.
  - `include_line_numbers` (boolean, optional): Include line numbers in content output. Default true.
  - `max_per_item` (integer, optional, at least 1): Maximum lines to return per file.
  - `max_tokens` (integer, optional, at least 1): Token cap across the entire response; use this to bound a read. Files clipped by it are listed in summary.truncated with next_start_line to continue from (extract=lines with range). Default: 25000 unless token_budget is set.
- `token_budget` (integer, optional, at least 1): Splits a large multi-file batch into pages of whole files that fit the budget; fetch later pages with page=N (pagination.pending_files lists the rest). Use only for batches too large for one response; to cap one response use output.max_tokens. When omitted, the owner's tools.defaultTokenBudget setting applies if it is above 0.
- `page` (integer, optional, at least 1): Page number to return when using token_budget pagination. Default 1.
- `image_mode` (one of `"default"`, `"unoptimized"`, `"metadata-only"`, `"thumbnail-only"`, optional): Global image handling mode. Per-file image_mode overrides this. Default: default.
- `max_image_size` (integer, optional, at least 1): Maximum image file size in bytes. Images exceeding this return metadata only. Default: 5242880 (5MB).

### `registry`

Discover and inspect skills, agents, and tools. Modes: search finds items by keyword; recommend lists items sorted by relevance; dependencies reads a skill's dependency chain; content returns full markdown file.

Permission category `read`; side effects: `read_fs`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"search"`, `"recommend"`, `"dependencies"`, `"preview"`, `"content"`, required): Operation mode: search finds skills/agents/tools by query; recommend lists items sorted by relevance to a task; dependencies reads a skill's depends_on; preview returns metadata, references, and preview text without materializing linked content; content returns the materialized markdown body and parsed metadata. Discovery: use mode=search with no query to list all available items; use mode=search type=skills to list skills, type=agents for agents, type=tools for tools.
- `query` (string, optional): (mode: search) Search words, matched against each item's name and description; matching items are returned best first. An exact name is returned at once; otherwise the top few matches are ordered in one ranking step.
- `type` (one of `"skills"`, `"agents"`, `"tools"`, `"all"`, optional): (mode: search) Filter by item type. Default: "all".
- `task` (string, optional): (mode: recommend) Task description; items judged to fit it come first, best first, then the rest alphabetically.
- `scope` (one of `"skills"`, `"tools"`, optional): (mode: recommend) Whether to recommend skills or tools. Default: "skills".
- `skillName` (string, optional): (mode: dependencies) Name of the skill to inspect for dependencies: the name search lists, or its file or directory name. Not a path.
- `path` (string, optional): (mode: preview/content) Absolute or relative path to a skill/agent markdown file inside .goodvibes/skills or .goodvibes/agents (project or home). Paths that resolve outside those directories are refused.

### `remote`

Manage remote runner pools, contracts, and portable artifacts.

Permission category `delegate`; side effects: `workflow`, `state`, `read_fs`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"create-pool"`, `"pools"`, `"assign"`, `"unassign"`, `"contracts"`, `"artifacts"`, `"review"`, `"import-artifact"`, required): create-pool makes a runner pool; pools, contracts and artifacts list them; assign and unassign add or remove a runner in a pool; review summarizes one artifact; import-artifact reads one from a file in the project.
- `view` (one of `"summary"`, `"full"`, optional): For pools, contracts and artifacts: summary (the default) or each full record.
- `poolId` (string, optional): The pool: required for create-pool, assign and unassign.
- `label` (string, optional): A display name for the pool create-pool makes.
- `runnerId` (string, optional): The runner to assign or unassign, as mode contracts lists it.
- `artifactId` (string, optional): The artifact review summarizes, as mode artifacts lists it.
- `path` (string, optional): The artifact file import-artifact reads; it must be inside the project.

### `repl`

Evaluate one snippet inside the command sandbox and return its printed value and output. runtime: javascript or typescript (Bun), python (the contained python3), sql (a fresh in-memory SQLite database; prints the last result rows as JSON; bindings are named parameters $name), graphql (parses, prints the normal form and operations; a schema binding with SDL text also validates; nothing is executed). Each eval is stateless (no shared variables); bindings are JSON values exposed as globals. history lists this session's eval attempts.

This tool is offered only where the command sandbox is available on the machine; elsewhere the model does not see it.

Permission category `delegate`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"eval"`, `"history"`, required): eval runs expression; history lists this session's eval attempts.
- `runtime` (one of `"javascript"`, `"typescript"`, `"python"`, `"sql"`, `"graphql"`, optional): Default: javascript.
- `expression` (string, optional): The code to evaluate in the chosen runtime (for sql, the statements). Required for eval.
- `timeout_ms` (integer, optional, at least 0): Optional execution timeout in ms. Omitted: 120000. 0 waits for completion or cancellation.
- `offset` (integer, optional, at least 0): History page offset, oldest first. Omitted: the newest page.
- `limit` (integer, optional, at least 0): History page size. Default: 20.
- `bindings` (object, optional): Named JSON values the snippet can use: globals for javascript, typescript and python, $name parameters for sql, and a schema entry (SDL text) for graphql.

### `repo_map`

Return a map of the repository: a per-directory source-file count plus the most central source files (ranked by how many other files import them, size as a tie-break) with their top-level exported symbols, within about 25000 tokens by default; it says how many files it left out. Call this to orient in an unfamiliar codebase before reading files; narrow it with path. Use detail="structure" for directories and source paths without reading bodies or building an import graph. Read-only; covers TypeScript/JavaScript source files.

Permission category `read`; side effects: `read_fs`.

Inputs:

- `path` (string, optional): Subdirectory to map, relative to the project root (default: the whole project).
- `budgetTokens` (number, optional): Approximate token budget for symbol detail. Default 25000; the map says how many files it left out. 0 includes every indexed source file and its exported symbols.
- `detail` (one of `"symbols"`, `"structure"`, optional): Default symbols: files ranked by how many others import them, with exported symbols, within the budget. Structure lists directories with source-file counts without reading source bodies (every file name for a path, or a project of up to 400 files); use it for initial orientation.

### `state`

Access and manipulate session state. Modes: get/set/list/clear operate on KVState; budget reports this session's measured token usage and turns, context its context window (last request size, window size, compaction), both with the files this product has read or written in this workspace; telemetry reports this tool's call counts and how many of them failed or were refused; hooks lists registered hooks and, with the same approval running their command would need, changes them (enable/disable/add/remove); mode reads or sets how much the terminal app prints: quiet, balanced or operator (get/set/list). Discovery: use mode=list to see existing KV keys, mode=hooks hookAction=list to see registered hooks, mode=mode modeAction=get to see the current print level. mode=analytics analyticsAction=summary shows the tool calls this process ran (name, status, duration, result size).

Permission category `read`; side effects: `state`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"get"`, `"set"`, `"list"`, `"clear"`, `"budget"`, `"context"`, `"telemetry"`, `"hooks"`, `"mode"`, `"analytics"`, required): Operation mode: get/set/list/clear manipulate KVState; budget reports the session's measured token usage and turns; context reports the context window (last request size, window size, compaction); memory reads and writes project memories by key (the records prompts retrieve); telemetry returns this tool's call counts; hooks manages registered hooks (list/enable/disable/add/remove); mode reads or sets how much the terminal app prints (quiet/balanced/operator; get/set/list); analytics reads the tool calls this process ran (query/summary/export/dashboard).
- `keys` (array of string, optional): (mode: get) Keys to retrieve from KVState.
- `values` (object, optional): (mode: set) Key-value pairs to write into KVState.
- `prefix` (string, optional): (mode: list) Optional prefix filter. Returns only keys starting with this string.
- `view` (one of `"summary"`, `"full"`, optional): (modes: list, memory, hooks, mode, analytics) Output detail level. Default: summary, except mode=mode modeAction=list and mode=memory memoryAction=get, which default to full.
- `clearKeys` (array of string, optional): (mode: clear) Keys to remove from KVState.
- `memoryAction` (one of `"get"`, `"set"`, `"list"`, `"delete"`, optional): (mode: memory) Sub-action: get reads a key, set saves a key (replacing its value), list shows all keys, delete removes a key.
- `memoryKey` (string, optional): (mode: memory, action: get/set/delete) The memory key: letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.
- `memoryValue` (string, optional): (mode: memory, action: set) JSON string or plain text to save. It is embedded for retrieval, so a value holding a credential is refused.
- `hookAction` (one of `"list"`, `"enable"`, `"disable"`, `"add"`, `"remove"`, optional): (mode: hooks) Sub-action: list all hooks; enable/disable by name; add a new hook; remove by name.
- `hookName` (string, optional): (mode: hooks, action: enable/disable/remove) Name of the hook to target.
- `hookDefinition` (object, optional): (mode: hooks, action: add) Hook definition object with eventPattern and hook fields. name is required and must be unused; the hook for its type (command, url or path) is required. The hook lasts for this session only.
  - `eventPattern` (string, optional): Event path pattern (e.g. Pre:tool:*)
  - `name` (string, optional): Required. Unique name for the hook; enable, disable and remove address it by this name.
  - `type` (one of `"command"`, `"http"`, `"ts"`, optional): Hook type.
  - `match` (string, optional): Event path to match.
  - `command` (string, optional): (type: command) Shell command to run.
  - `url` (string, optional): (type: http) URL to POST to.
  - `path` (string, optional): (type: ts) Path to TypeScript file.
  - `description` (string, optional): Human-readable description.
- `modeAction` (one of `"get"`, `"set"`, `"list"`, optional): (mode: mode) Sub-action: get returns the current print level; set saves a new one; list returns the levels.
- `modeName` (string, optional): (mode: mode, action: set) The print level: quiet (only warnings and errors toast), balanced (the default) or operator (everything toasts).
- `analyticsAction` (one of `"query"`, `"summary"`, `"export"`, `"dashboard"`, optional): (mode: analytics) Sub-action: query recorded calls by filter; summary aggregation; export as JSON/CSV; dashboard top-level view. Calls are kept in memory for this process, the newest 10,000.
- `analyticsFilter` (object, optional): (mode: analytics, action: query) Filter object: { tool?, status? (ok, error or cancelled), since?, until?, limit? }.
- `analyticsFormat` (one of `"json"`, `"csv"`, optional): (mode: analytics, action: export) Export format.

### `task`

Manage durable cross-session task refs, dependencies, cancellations, and handoffs shared by every session of this project. A handoff blocks the task until its destination session accepts it with mode=acknowledge handoffId=<id>; the source session can take it back with mode=withdraw handoffId=<id>. Results list handoffs waiting for this session under handoffsAwaitingThisSession.

Permission category `delegate`; side effects: `workflow`, `state`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"create"`, `"list"`, `"show"`, `"status"`, `"depend"`, `"cancel"`, `"handoff"`, `"handoffs"`, `"acknowledge"`, `"withdraw"`, required): create a task ref; list or show refs; status moves one; depend records that it waits on another; cancel; handoff passes one to another session; handoffs lists the pending ones; acknowledge accepts one; withdraw takes one back.
- `view` (one of `"summary"`, `"full"`, optional): For list, show and handoffs: summary (the default) or each full record.
- `sessionId` (string, optional): READ-ONLY selector, used by list and show to view another session's task refs. Defaults to the current session. It does NOT set ownership: refs created or modified by this tool are always owned by the current session, and this field is ignored by create, status, depend, cancel, handoff, acknowledge and withdraw.
- `taskId` (string, optional): The task ref, chosen at create: required for create, show, status, depend and handoff; for cancel, the task to start from.
- `title` (string, optional): create: what the task is.
- `label` (string, optional): create: an optional short label.
- `status` (one of `"queued"`, `"running"`, `"blocked"`, `"completed"`, `"failed"`, `"cancelled"`, optional): create: the starting status (default queued). status: the status to move the task to; it is refused when the task cannot move there.
- `dependsOnSessionId` (string, optional): depend: the session that owns the task waited on (default this session).
- `dependsOnTaskId` (string, optional): depend: the task waited on.
- `reason` (string, optional): depend, cancel, handoff: why, recorded with the change.
- `toSessionId` (string, optional): handoff: the session the task is passed to.
- `handoffId` (string, optional): acknowledge: the handoff (from mode=handoffs) this session, its destination, accepts. withdraw: the handoff this session, its source, takes back.
- `scope` (one of `"task"`, `"subtree"`, `"session"`, optional): cancel: the task alone (the default), the task and every task that depends on it, or every task of this session.

### `trigger`

Watch for something and act when it happens, without holding this turn open. The daemon supervises the watcher; when it fires, an agent turn starts with what was seen. Kinds (definition.spec.kind): "on-exit" runs a command and fires once when it ends (exit code, signal and output tail included); "stream" runs a long-lived command and fires on output lines matching a pattern (batched); "condition" checks a URL, file, command or a reading platform tool (probe {"kind":"platform-tool","tool":"read","input":{...}}) on an interval and fires when a rule holds (change, value, threshold, debounce-n, ...). Commands are argv: command plus args, never a shell line. Actions: create (definition), list, history (id), cancel (id), reset (id, after its breaker opened). Example: {"action":"create","definition":{"id":"build","label":"Build finished","spec":{"kind":"on-exit","command":"npm","args":["run","build"]}}}.

Permission category `execute`; side effects: `exec`, `agent`, `state`.

Inputs:

- `action` (one of `"create"`, `"list"`, `"history"`, `"cancel"`, `"reset"`, required): create (with definition), list, history (id), cancel (id), or reset (id, after its breaker opened).
- `id` (string, optional): The trigger id, for history, cancel and reset.
- `definition` (object, optional): For create: { id, label, description?, spec, action? }. spec.kind is on-exit | stream | condition. action defaults to an agent turn ({"kind":"agent-turn","prompt"?,"deliverTo"?}); its answer goes to the channel deliverTo names ("telegram", "slack:C123"), else to the owner inbox. {"kind":"action-grant","grantId","digest"} runs a command the owner registered.
- `limit` (number, optional): For history: how many of the newest runs to return (default 20).

### `web_search`

Search the web through a provider-backed search layer. Returns normalized ranked results, optional instant-answer data, and optional fetched evidence. metadata.ignoredFilters names any region, safeSearch or timeRange filter the answering provider could not apply.

Permission category `delegate`; side effects: `network`.

Inputs:

- `query` (string, required): Web search query to execute.
- `providerId` (string, optional): Optional provider id. Defaults to the built-in default provider.
- `maxResults` (integer, optional, at least 1, at most 25): Maximum number of ranked results to ask for. Default 10. A provider returns at most its own limit: Brave, Firecrawl and Tavily 20, Perplexity 10, the others 25.
- `verbosity` (one of `"urls_only"`, `"titles"`, `"snippets"`, `"evidence"`, `"full"`, optional): urls_only returns ranked URLs, titles adds titles, snippets adds descriptions, evidence fetches bounded excerpts from the top results, and full fetches fuller readable excerpts.
- `region` (string, optional): Region: a country code such as us, or DuckDuckGo's country-language form such as us-en. A provider that cannot filter by region names it in metadata.ignoredFilters.
- `safeSearch` (one of `"strict"`, `"moderate"`, `"off"`, optional): Safe-search posture. Default provider behavior is moderate. A provider without the filter names it in metadata.ignoredFilters.
- `timeRange` (one of `"any"`, `"day"`, `"week"`, `"month"`, `"year"`, optional): Optional recency filter. A provider that cannot apply it (or this range) names it in metadata.ignoredFilters, so the results are not date-filtered.
- `includeInstantAnswer` (boolean, optional): When supported, include provider instant-answer enrichment.
- `includeEvidence` (boolean, optional): Attach fetched evidence from the top ranked pages.
- `evidenceTopN` (integer, optional, at least 1, at most 10): How many top results to fetch for evidence when evidence is enabled.
- `evidenceExtract` (one of `"raw"`, `"text"`, `"json"`, `"markdown"`, `"readable"`, `"code_blocks"`, `"links"`, `"metadata"`, `"structured"`, `"tables"`, `"pdf"`, `"summary"`, optional): Fetch extraction mode to use for evidence fetches.

### `work_plan`

Keep the project work plan: a checklist of work items with status, owner and notes that the user sees in the work plan view and that lasts across sessions. Use it to plan multi-step work and to track who is doing what (owner: an agent id, a cohort name or the user); give spawned workers their brief through the agent tool (context and successCriteria). Statuses: pending, in_progress, blocked, done, failed, cancelled.

Permission category `write`; side effects: `workflow`, `state`.

Inputs:

- `action` (one of `"list"`, `"add"`, `"update"`, `"set_status"`, `"remove"`, `"clear_completed"`, required): list the items; add one; update its title, owner or notes; set_status; remove one; clear_completed removes done and cancelled items.
- `id` (string, optional): (update, set_status, remove) The item id, or a unique prefix of it.
- `title` (string, optional): (add, update) What the item is, in a short line.
- `status` (one of `"pending"`, `"in_progress"`, `"blocked"`, `"done"`, `"failed"`, `"cancelled"`, optional): (add, set_status) The item status. add defaults to pending. (list) Show only items in this status.
- `owner` (string, optional): (add, update) Who is doing it: an agent id, a cohort name or the user.
- `notes` (string, optional): (add, update) Detail, acceptance notes or what is blocking it.

### `workflow`

Automation control plumbing. To run work, use the agent tool instead. This tool manages: hook actions (a command run when a hook event fires), schedule (recurring background commands on intervals), and workflow state tracking (does not execute anything). Hook actions and schedules run in the project root with credential variables withheld and inside the exec sandbox when it is on; their command is judged as a shell command once, when added, exactly as an exec call is (a refusal says why), and list shows its boundary. and last until this process exits; list shows each one's last run, exit code and error. For routines that survive restarts use /schedule. Modes: hook-actions (manage hook actions), schedule (manage recurring commands), start/status/transition/cancel/list (state tracking only, no execution), except start with definition=contract, which hands the task to a new contract whose units are checked against acceptance criteria while they work.

Permission category `delegate`; side effects: `workflow`, `state`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"start"`, `"status"`, `"transition"`, `"cancel"`, `"list"`, `"hook-actions"`, `"schedule"`, required): Operation mode.
- `definition` (one of `"contract"`, `"fix_loop"`, `"test_then_fix"`, `"review_only"`, optional): Workflow definition to instantiate (mode: start). contract starts a contract instead of a tracked state machine.
- `task` (string, optional): Task description for the workflow (mode: start).
- `workflowId` (string, optional): Workflow instance ID (mode: status, transition, cancel).
- `targetState` (string, optional): State to transition to (mode: transition).
- `hookAction` (one of `"list"`, `"add"`, `"remove"`, `"enable"`, `"disable"`, optional): Hook action management (mode: hook-actions).
- `hookActionId` (string, optional): Hook action ID for remove/enable/disable (mode: hook-actions).
- `hookActionDefinition` (object, optional): Hook action to add (mode: hook-actions, hookAction: add).
  - `event` (string, required): Hook event pattern to match (e.g. Pre:tool:*, Post:file:write).
  - `condition` (string, optional): Optional condition over event.* and payload.* paths with ===, !==, ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=, &&, ||, ! and parentheses, e.g. payload.tool === 'exec'. One that cannot be parsed is refused when added.
  - `action` (string, required): Command to run when the event fires, split into words with no shell (POSIX quoting and backslash escapes). Killed after 60 s.
- `scheduleAction` (one of `"list"`, `"add"`, `"remove"`, `"enable"`, `"disable"`, optional): Schedule management action (mode: schedule). disable stops the timer and keeps the schedule; enable starts it again.
- `scheduleName` (string, optional): Unique name for the schedule entry.
- `scheduleInterval` (string, optional): Repeat interval: a number followed by s, m, h or d, from 1s up to 24d, e.g. '5m', '1h', '30s' (mode: schedule, action: add).
- `scheduleCommand` (string, optional): Command to run on each interval tick, split into words with no shell (POSIX quoting and backslash escapes) (mode: schedule, action: add). A tick is skipped (and counted) while the previous run is still going; a run longer than its interval (at least 60 s) is killed.

### `write`

Write one or more files to disk. Supports batch writes, automatic parent directory creation, and modes fail_if_exists (default), overwrite, backup, and restore (puts the newest backup back). Use content_base64 for content containing special characters.

Permission category `write`; side effects: `write_fs`.

Inputs:

- `files` (array of object, required, at least items: 1): Array of files to write.
  - `path` (string, required): Path to the file to write, relative to project root or absolute.
  - `content` (string, optional): Text file content to write. Exactly one of content or content_base64 is required (content may be an empty string), except with mode restore, which takes neither.
  - `content_base64` (string, optional): Base64-encoded file bytes, written exactly as decoded (use it for binary files, or when content contains single quotes, backticks, or ${} patterns). Exactly one of content or content_base64 is required.
  - `encoding` (one of `"utf-8"`, `"utf8"`, `"ascii"`, `"latin1"`, `"binary"`, optional, default `"utf-8"`): How the text in content is encoded on disk. Default: utf-8. Text with a character the chosen encoding cannot hold is refused. content_base64 and mode restore write exact bytes and take no other encoding.
  - `mode` (one of `"fail_if_exists"`, `"overwrite"`, `"backup"`, `"restore"`, optional, default `"fail_if_exists"`): Behaviour when the file already exists. fail_if_exists (default): return an error. overwrite: replace existing content. backup: copy the existing file to .goodvibes/.backups/ before overwriting (the newest 5 copies per file are kept; the result names the copy). restore: put back the newest backup of this file (send no content).
- `verbosity` (one of `"count_only"`, `"minimal"`, `"standard"`, `"verbose"`, optional, default `"count_only"`): Output detail level. Default: count_only (recommended, you provided the content). At every level the result lists backup copies made, backups restored, and files auto-heal rewrote (healed), whose content then differs from what you sent.
- `dry_run` (boolean, optional, default `false`): If true, validate and plan writes but do not write any files.
- `validate` (object, optional): Run validators after all files have been written.
  - `after` (array of one of `"typecheck"`, `"lint"`, `"test"`, `"build"`, optional): Validators to run after writing: the project's own typecheck, lint, test or build command (its package.json script through its package manager, the Cargo/Go toolchain, a Makefile target or a pyproject-configured pytest/mypy/ruff, else the owner's tools.validators.<name> setting). One the project does not declare is refused before anything is written. A failure makes the call unsuccessful but does NOT undo writes.
- `transaction` (object, optional): Batch transaction behaviour when one or more file writes fail.
  - `mode` (one of `"atomic"`, `"partial"`, `"none"`, optional, default `"none"`): atomic: if any write fails, undo all previously written files (restores originals). partial: skip failed writes but continue. none (default): same as partial, no rollback.

- `processId` (string, optional): Background process id for process inspect or lifecycle modes.
- `processSessionId` (string, optional): Process session id alias for background process modes.
- `processAction` (one of `"start"`, `"spawn"`, `"run"`, `"stop"`, `"kill"`, `"cancel"`, `"wait"`, `"list"`, `"status"`, `"poll"`, `"log"`, `"output"`, `"write"`, `"capabilities"`, `"doctor"`, `"parity"`, optional): Background process lifecycle action or process-style alias.
- `action` (one of `"start"`, `"spawn"`, `"run"`, `"stop"`, `"kill"`, `"cancel"`, `"wait"`, `"list"`, `"status"`, `"poll"`, `"log"`, `"output"`, `"write"`, `"capabilities"`, `"doctor"`, `"parity"`, `"preview"`, `"import"`, `"apply"`, optional): Process-style action alias, or preview/import/apply for settings-import workspace actions.
- `cwd` (string, optional): Workspace-relative cwd for a background process start.
- `timeoutMs` (number, optional): Wait timeout in ms (0 = check once, capped at 600000); for a background start, 0 = no automatic deadline; also the local model smoke probe timeout.
- `lifetime` (one of `"task"`, `"detached"`, optional): Background start: task (default) ends with the Agent and at timeoutMs; detached keeps running after the Agent exits, logs to a file, and is listed and stoppable from later sessions.
- `pty` (boolean, optional): Request PTY mode; reports unsupported unless the process capability report lists a PTY contract (process action:"capabilities").
- `data` (string, optional): Input data for process action:write to a running tracked process with native stdin; requires current recorded effect admission (process action:"capabilities" shows whether stdin write is supported).
- `recoveryAction` (one of `"undo"`, `"redo"`, optional): File recovery action for run_file_recovery mode.
- `laneId` (string, optional): Lane id for personal_ops_lane or document_ops_lane mode.
- `queueItemId` (string, optional): Queue item id for autonomy_queue_item mode.
- `candidateId` (string, optional): Candidate id for learning_candidate mode.
- `sourceId` (string, optional): Research source id for research_source mode.
- `runId` (string, optional): Research run id for research_run mode.
- `pairingRouteId` (string, optional): Pairing route id for pairing_route mode.
- `delegationRouteId` (string, optional): Delegation route id for delegation_route mode.
- `findingId` (string, optional): Security finding id for security_finding mode.
- `bundlePath` (string, optional): Workspace-relative bundle JSON path for support_bundle mode.
- `mediaProviderId` (string, optional): Voice or media provider id for media_provider mode.
- `sessionId` (string, optional): Saved session id (session mode), or process session id (process modes).
- `categoryId` (string, optional): Workspace category id. For open_ui_surface with surfaceId "agent-workspace", the workspace tab to open.
- `surfaceId` (string, optional): UI surface id for ui_surface or open_ui_surface modes.
- `actionId` (string, optional): Workspace action id or keybinding action id.
- `fields` (object, optional): Values for a workspace action's blanks (by input id) for run_workspace_action, or combo fields (key, ctrl, shift, alt) for set_keybinding. For run_setup_smoke only agentBinaryOutput, statusJson, connectedHostStatusOutput, setupPostureOutput, firstAssistantTurn and notes are saved (8000 characters each, longer values are cut with a marker); other keys are listed as ignoredFields.
- `combo` (object, optional): Single key combo for set_keybinding.
  - `key` (string, required): The key, such as g, enter, tab or up.
  - `ctrl` (boolean, optional): Ctrl is held.
  - `shift` (boolean, optional): Shift is held.
  - `alt` (boolean, optional): Alt is held.
- `combos` (array of object, optional): Multiple key combos for set_keybinding.
  - `key` (string, required): The key, such as g, enter, tab or up.
  - `ctrl` (boolean, optional): Ctrl is held.
  - `shift` (boolean, optional): Shift is held.
  - `alt` (boolean, optional): Alt is held.
- `recordId` (string, optional): Selected Agent-local record id.
- `knowledgeSpaceId` (string, optional): Agent Knowledge space id for memory_refinement or run_memory_refinement.
- `sourceIds` (array of string, optional): Agent Knowledge source ids for scoped semantic refinement.
- `gapIds` (array of string, optional): Agent Knowledge semantic gap ids for scoped refinement.
- `maxRunMs` (number, optional): Maximum semantic refinement run budget in milliseconds.
- `force` (boolean, optional): Force semantic refinement reprocessing where supported.
- `key` (string, optional): Agent setting key, or a key-combo lookup such as "Ctrl+G" for keybinding, run_keybinding, set_keybinding and reset_keybinding.
- `value` (string or number or boolean, optional): Setting value, a combo label such as "Ctrl+G" for set_keybinding, or visible search text for shortcut routes.
- `target` (string, optional): Generic lookup target for single-item modes.
- `methodId` (string, optional): Public operator or Agent Knowledge method id.
- `endpointId` (string, optional): Connected service endpoint id.
- `artifactId` (string, optional): Release evidence artifact id.
- `itemId` (string, optional): Release readiness item id for mode release_readiness_item.
- `capabilityId` (string, optional): Connected-host capability id.
- `toolName` (string, optional): First-class model tool name.
- `tool` (string, optional): Alias for toolName in policy_explain mode.
- `commandName` (string, optional): Alias for command in command and run_command modes.
- `cliCommand` (string, optional): Alias for command in cli_command mode.
- `session_id` (string, optional): Alias for processId on background-process routes.
- `toolArgs` (object, optional): Model tool arguments for policy_explain mode.
- `category` (string, optional): Setting category filter.
- `prefix` (string, optional): Setting key prefix filter such as surfaces.slack.
- `includeHidden` (boolean, optional): Include hidden settings in settings mode.
- `includeParameters` (boolean, optional): Include optional detail for discovery modes.
- `limit` (number, optional): Maximum catalog entries to return. settings, workspace_actions and operator_methods page 50 rows by default, at most 100. inbox_triage: messages to label, at most 100.
- `offset` (number, optional): Row to start a settings, workspace_actions or operator_methods page at; a short page names the next offset.
- `confirm` (boolean, optional): Optional annotation only; grants no authority. An effect runs only under the owner's current recorded effect admission. Without admission the call is refused and names the missing approval.
- `explicitUserRequest` (string, optional): Optional: the owner's request in their own words; grants no authority.
- `peerId` (string, optional): Remote peer or backend id for remote_peers_invoke, remote_backends_register and remote_backends_remove (target is an accepted alias).
- `requestId` (string, optional): Pair request id for remote_pair_approve or remote_pair_reject (target is an accepted alias).
- `workId` (string, optional): Remote work item id for remote_work_cancel (target is an accepted alias).
- `payload` (object, optional): Command payload for remote_peers_invoke. For a registered backend: stdin and timeoutMs (put arguments, environment and directory in command, not payload.args, payload.env or payload.cwd).
- `displayName` (string, optional): Display name for remote_backends_register; defaults to peerId.
- `backendKind` (one of `"docker"`, `"ssh"`, `"cloud-terminal"`, `"local-process"`, optional): Backend kind for remote_backends_register.
- `backendConfig` (object, optional): Backend settings for remote_backends_register. docker: containerName, dockerHost; ssh: sshHost, sshPort, sshUser, identityRef; cloud-terminal: provider (gcp|aws|azure), credentialRef, projectId, location, instance; local-process: cwd, allowedCommands. Credentials are goodvibes://secrets/ references only.
- `note` (string, optional): Optional note for remote pair request approve/reject.
- `confirmReplace` (boolean, optional): For remote_pair_approve: set true only when the request names an existing peer and it is the same device re-pairing; approving replaces that peer's capabilities, commands and tokens.
- `reason` (string, optional): Optional cancellation reason for remote_work_cancel.
- `draftId` (string, optional): Channel draft id for channel_drafts, channel_draft_send.
- `draftStatus` (one of `"draft"`, `"queued"`, `"sent"`, `"failed"`, optional): Status filter for channel_drafts list.
- `draftTitle` (string, optional): Optional title for channel_draft_save.
- `draftMessage` (string, optional): Message body for channel_draft_save.
- `draftChannel` (string, optional): Channel target for channel_draft_save.
- `draftRoute` (string, optional): Channel route id for channel_draft_save and channel_routing_assign; with surfaceKind, the channel route whose assignment channel_routing_remove removes.
- `assignmentId` (string, optional): Routing assignment id (as channel_routing_assign returned it) for channel_routing_remove.
- `draftWebhook` (string, optional): Webhook URL for channel_draft_save.
- `draftLink` (string, optional): Link target for channel_draft_save.
- `draftTags` (array of string, optional): Tags for channel_draft_save.
- `surfaceKind` (string, optional): Channel surface kind for channel_routing or channel_routing_assign.
- `profileId` (string, optional): Profile id for channel_routing_assign.
- `routeLabel` (string, optional): Optional label for channel_routing_assign.
- `itemIds` (array of string, optional): Inbox item ids (from unified_inbox or channels.inbox.list) for inbox_labels_apply; up to 100.
- `labels` (array of string, optional): Labels for inbox_labels_apply: GoodVibes/Spam, GoodVibes/Priority or GoodVibes/Normal (writing one takes the other two off), or a custom label name.
- `provider` (string, optional): Inbox account for inbox_triage: slack, discord or email.
- `cursor` (string, optional): Page cursor for inbox_triage: nextCursor from channels.inbox.list or an earlier inbox_triage answer.
- `dryRun` (boolean, optional): inbox_triage: return the readings without storing them.

### `agent_local_registry`

Inspect or update Agent-local records by domain. Actions per domain: memory, note: list, search, get, create, update, review, stale, delete. persona adds use and clear_active. skill and skill_bundle add enable and disable. routine adds enable, disable and start. Create needs: memory summary; note title and body; persona name, description and body; skill name, description and procedure; skill_bundle name, description and skillIds; routine name, description and steps. Writes need current recorded admission. Marking a persona, skill, skill bundle or routine reviewed, and enabling one nobody reviewed, are the owner's: refused here with the command the owner types.

Permission category `delegate`; side effects: `state`.

Inputs:

- `domain` (one of `"memory"`, `"note"`, `"persona"`, `"skill"`, `"skill_bundle"`, `"routine"`, required): Which kind of record to work on.
- `action` (one of `"list"`, `"search"`, `"get"`, `"create"`, `"update"`, `"enable"`, `"disable"`, `"review"`, `"stale"`, `"use"`, `"clear_active"`, `"start"`, `"delete"`, required): What to do; each domain accepts only some actions (see the tool description).
- `id` (string, optional): Record id for get, update, review, stale, delete, use, enable, disable and start.
- `query` (string, optional): Search text for action search.
- `limit` (number, optional): Memory list or search: maximum rows (search default 10, at most 50).
- `semantic` (boolean, optional): Memory search: semantic by default; false forces literal matching.
- `cls` (one of `"decision"`, `"constraint"`, `"incident"`, `"pattern"`, `"fact"`, `"risk"`, `"runbook"`, `"architecture"`, `"ownership"`, optional): Memory class when domain is memory.
- `scope` (one of `"session"`, `"project"`, `"team"`, optional): Memory scope when domain is memory.
- `summary` (string, optional): Memory summary when domain is memory.
- `detail` (string, optional): Memory detail when domain is memory.
- `confidence` (number, optional): Memory review confidence from 0 to 100.
- `title` (string, optional): Note title when domain is note.
- `name` (string, optional): Name of a persona, skill, skill_bundle or routine.
- `description` (string, optional): Description of a persona, skill, skill_bundle or routine.
- `body` (string, optional): Note body or persona body/instructions.
- `sourceUrl` (string, optional): Optional source URL when domain is note.
- `procedure` (string, optional): Skill procedure.
- `steps` (string, optional): Routine steps.
- `skills` (array of string, optional): Skill ids for skill_bundle create/update.
- `skillIds` (array of string, optional): Skill ids for skill_bundle create/update.
- `requiresEnv` (array of string, optional): Required environment variable names.
- `requiresCommands` (array of string, optional): Command names required by a skill or routine.
- `triggers` (array of string, optional): Trigger phrases for a persona, skill or routine.
- `tags` (array of string, optional): Tags on any record.
- `reason` (string, optional): Why a record is marked stale.
- `enabled` (boolean, optional): Skill, skill_bundle or routine: initial state on create, or the new state on update.
- `activate` (boolean, optional): Persona create or update: true makes it the active persona, false clears it if it is active.
- `provenance` (string, optional): Where the record came from.
- `confirm` (boolean, optional): Optional annotation only; grants no authority. An effect runs only under the owner's current recorded effect admission.
- `explicitUserRequest` (string, optional): Optional: the owner's request in their own words; grants no authority.

### `agent_model_compare`

Blind-compare models on a prompt or artifact (run, reveal, review, sideBySide), save a judgment (judge), then apply the winner route or record a route decision (apply, routeDecision), and export, hand off, archive or diff reviews (export, handoff, handoffArchive, handoffDiff) or summarize saved judgments (analytics, synthesis).

Permission category `delegate`; side effects: `network`, `state`.

Inputs:

- `mode` (one of `"run"`, `"reveal"`, `"review"`, `"sideBySide"`, `"judge"`, `"apply"`, `"routeDecision"`, `"export"`, `"handoff"`, `"handoffArchive"`, `"handoffDiff"`, `"analytics"`, `"synthesis"`, required): Select compare workflow mode.
- `prompt` (string, optional): Exact prompt sent identically to every candidate model.
- `modelRefs` (array of string, optional): Optional registry keys or model ids. Omit to auto-select candidates.
- `candidateCount` (number, optional): Number of candidates to auto-select when modelRefs is omitted. 2 to 4; default 2.
- `rubric` (string, optional): Optional judging rubric shown with the blinded results.
- `systemPrompt` (string, optional): Optional system prompt sent identically to every candidate model.
- `maxTokens` (number, optional): Optional per-candidate output cap. Omit or use 0 for the selected model’s supported output limit.
- `reveal` (boolean, optional): For run, review, side-by-side, export and handoff: include model identities (and a judged winner model) in this output; without it none is printed, even when the judgment stored one. For judge: also write the winner model into the judgment. apply and routeDecision read the winner model from the judged comparison either way, so a blind judgment can be applied; a judgment of a comparison that was not saved needs reveal:true to be applied.
- `saveArtifact` (boolean, optional): Defaults true; save the local JSON review artifact.
- `benchmarkKind` (string, optional): Optional benchmark tag for saved comparisons or analytics filters. A tag beginning with "local" (local-model-route) makes a blank modelRefs list fill from local routes only, and refuses with fewer than two; name a remote baseline in modelRefs to include one.
- `taskType` (string, optional): Optional task type tag for saved comparisons or analytics filters.
- `documentId` (string, optional): Optional document id tag for saved comparisons or analytics filters.
- `comparisonId` (string, optional): Stored comparison id for reveal, review and judge (or pass a saved comparison artifactId).
- `artifactId` (string, optional): Run source artifact (a text artifact inlined into the prompt; the prompt, document and request together may hold at most 1,000,000 characters), or the saved comparison or judgment artifact id for apply, routeDecision, export, handoff, handoffArchive, sideBySide and review.
- `leftArtifactId` (string, optional): Left saved reviewer handoff artifact id for handoffDiff.
- `rightArtifactId` (string, optional): Right saved reviewer handoff artifact id for handoffDiff.
- `sectionId` (string, optional): Optional handoffDiff jump: all, metadata, policy, related, comparison.
- `winnerBlindId` (string, optional): Candidate label to save as winner, such as A or Candidate B.
- `winner` (string, optional): Alias for winnerBlindId.
- `reasons` (string, optional): User-visible reasons for the saved judgment.
- `notes` (string, optional): Optional extra judgment notes.
- `decision` (one of `"left-unchanged"`, `"leave-unchanged"`, `"keep-current"`, `"no-change"`, optional): routeDecision receipt choice; defaults to left-unchanged. To apply the winner use mode:"apply".
- `limit` (number, optional): Max saved judgments for analytics and synthesis. 1 to 100; default 20.
- `includeReasons` (boolean, optional): If true, include short reason excerpts.
- `relatedArtifactIds` (array of string, optional): Related artifact ids for sideBySide (optional) and handoff (required, at least one).
- `previewBytes` (number, optional): Max bytes per related artifact preview.
- `confirm` (boolean, optional): Optional annotation only; grants no authority. An effect runs only under the owner's current recorded effect admission.
- `preview` (boolean, optional): For mode:run, inspect a comparison request without metered provider calls or result writes.
- `explicitUserRequest` (string, optional): Optional: the owner's request in their own words, kept with route-decision receipts; grants no authority.

### `agent_model_compare_candidate`

Run one metered blind-comparison candidate using an exact model and bounded output.

Permission category `delegate`; side effects: `network`.

Inputs:

- `registryKey` (string, required): The model's registry key; with modelId and providerId it must name a model that can still be selected.
- `modelId` (string, required): The exact model id to run.
- `providerId` (string, required): The provider that serves the model.
- `blindId` (string, required): The label this candidate's answer is shown under in the blind comparison.
- `prompt` (string, required): The prompt every candidate of the comparison is sent.
- `systemPrompt` (string, required): The system prompt every candidate of the comparison is sent.
- `maxTokens` (integer, required, at least 0): The most output tokens the candidate may produce.
- `metered` (exactly `true`, required): Must be true: the call is a paid model request.
- `comparisonRequest` (object, required): The comparison request this candidate belongs to, checked against the screening.
- `screeningId` (string, required): The screening agent_model_compare mode "run" made of the request; a candidate without a current one is held.

### `browser`

Drive a real browser: open, read, click, type, and sign in.

Permission category `delegate`; side effects: `network`, `write_fs`, `state`.

Inputs:

- `action` (one of `"status"`, `"provision"`, `"launch"`, `"attach"`, `"release"`, `"close"`, `"navigate"`, `"snapshot"`, `"click"`, `"type"`, `"select"`, `"press"`, `"scroll"`, `"wait_for"`, `"read_text"`, `"screenshot"`, `"tabs"`, `"new_tab"`, `"switch_tab"`, `"close_tab"`, `"back"`, `"forward"`, `"extract"`, required): What to do. status reports availability and open sessions.
- `url` (string, optional): URL for navigate or new_tab (http, https, file, or about only; file: must be a path the read tool may open), or the address action:"wait_for" waits to reach.
- `ref` (string, optional): Element ref from the latest snapshot of this page.
- `selector` (string, optional): CSS selector for extract. Reaches into open shadow DOM.
- `text` (string, optional): Required for action:"type": the text to enter (an explicit empty string clears the field). For action:"wait_for": the text to wait for; with neither text nor url, wait_for waits for the network to go idle.
- `key` (string, optional): Key name for action:"press", such as Enter or Escape.
- `values` (array of string, optional): Required for action:"select": the option values to choose.
- `fields` (array of one of `"text"`, `"html"`, `"value"`, `"attributes"`, optional): What to read for action:"extract": any of text, html, value, attributes. Defaults to text; an unknown name is skipped and listed in ignoredFields.
- `all` (boolean, optional): For action:"extract": read every match rather than the first.
- `sessionId` (string, optional): Browser session to act on. Defaults to the open session, except action:"release" and action:"close", which require it.
- `pageId` (string, optional): Page/tab to act on. Defaults to the active tab.
- `cdpEndpoint` (string, optional): Remote debugging endpoint of a running browser, for attach.
- `profileName` (string, optional): Saved profile to launch with. Keeps logins across runs.
- `headless` (boolean, optional): Launch with no visible window. Sign-ins need a visible one.
- `submit` (boolean, optional): Press Enter after typing.
- `replace` (boolean, optional): Replace the field contents rather than appending. Default true.
- `fullPage` (boolean, optional): Capture the whole scrollable page instead of the visible area.
- `path` (string, optional): File name or path inside the screenshot folder to write to. Defaults to a generated name there. An existing file is never overwritten.
- `direction` (one of `"up"`, `"down"`, optional): Scroll direction when no ref is given.
- `amount` (number, optional): Scroll distance in pixels.
- `limit` (number, optional): Maximum elements to include in a snapshot.
- `maxChars` (number, optional): Maximum characters to return from action:"read_text".
- `timeoutMs` (number, optional): Deadline for this one call, in milliseconds (up to 600000). Defaults: navigate, back, forward, new_tab, wait_for and screenshot 30000; click, type, select, press, scroll and read_text 15000. A call that passes its deadline fails and says what to do next. Never affects the browser.
- `repair` (boolean, optional): For provision: reinstall even if a browser is cached.
- `button` (one of `"left"`, `"right"`, `"middle"`, optional): Mouse button for action:"click".

- `expectationId` (string, optional): For mail.verification: the expectation id accounts action:"alias" returned. Waits up to 30 s for the daemon to receive the verification mail and returns its link or code.
- `to` (string, optional): Recipient address for mail.send.
- `subject` (string, optional): Subject for mail.send.
- `body` (string, optional): Plain-text body for mail.send.
- `summary` (string, optional): Event title for calendar.create.
- `start` (string, optional): RFC3339 start time for calendar.create.
- `end` (string, optional): RFC3339 end time for calendar.create.
- `location` (string, optional): Optional event location for calendar.create.
- `description` (string, optional): Optional event description for calendar.create.
- `timeMin` (string, optional): RFC3339 lower bound for calendar.list. Defaults to now when neither bound is given.
- `timeMax` (string, optional): RFC3339 upper bound for calendar.list.
- `maxResults` (number, optional): How many items to return. Defaults to 10.
- `clientId` (string, optional): OAuth client id the user pasted, for connect.client.

### `occasions`

Occasions/trips: raise, answer yes/no/later, gift interview, capture.

Permission category `delegate`; side effects: `network`, `state`.

Inputs:

- `action` (one of `"list"`, `"pending"`, `"state"`, `"gifts"`, `"plans"`, `"answer"`, `"interview"`, `"interview_answer"`, `"interview_record"`, `"propose"`, `"confirm"`, `"remove"`, `"resolve_conflict"`, `"plan_propose"`, `"plan_confirm"`, `"sweep"`, optional): Which action to run. propose/plan_propose return a proposal token; confirm/plan_confirm take it.
- `occasionId` (string, optional): Which occasion. action:"pending" and action:"list" both name it.
- `answer` (one of `"yes"`, `"no"`, `"later"`, `"acknowledged"`, optional): His answer. "later" is its own answer, not a no, never send it as one.
- `occurrence` (string, optional): YYYY-MM-DD; only for an occurrence other than the next one.
- `interviewId` (string, optional): The interview in flight. action:"pending" lists them.
- `stepId` (string, optional): Which question he just answered.
- `text` (string, optional): His answer to one interview question, in his words.
- `landedOn` (string, optional): What he actually settled on. Closes the interview.
- `proposal` (string, optional): confirm/plan_confirm: the token propose/plan_propose returned for the line he agreed to. Exactly that line is written.
- `title` (string, optional): propose/plan_propose: what the occasion or plan is called, in his words.
- `date` (string, optional): propose: MM-DD for something annual, YYYY-MM-DD for a one-off.
- `kind` (one of `"gift-giving"`, `"remember-only"`, `"neither"`, optional): HE picks this: gift-giving offers a gift, remember-only does not. On confirm, the kind he chose.
- `person` (string, optional): Who it is about, as a plain label. Omit when the title already says.
- `recurrence` (one of `"once"`, `"annual"`, optional): Omit to let the date decide: MM-DD is annual, YYYY-MM-DD is a one-off.
- `leadDays` (number, optional): Override the default runway for this one occasion only.
- `self` (boolean, optional): propose: true when the date is his own (his birthday). Recorded as "for me"; a remember-only date of his own is never pushed at him.
- `from` (string, optional): A plan's first day, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `to` (string, optional): A plan's last day, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `away` (boolean, optional): True when the plan takes him away from home. Feeds reminder timing.
- `destination` (string, optional): Where, when he said. Omit when he did not.
- `details` (array of string, optional): plan_propose: everything else he gave about the plan, one detail per entry (a confirmation number, a flight and its times, who is travelling), exactly as given.
- `keep` (string, optional): resolve_conflict: the date he says is right, as recorded (MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD). The other lines for that title are removed. Omit to get the recorded dates to ask him about.
- `confirmed` (boolean, optional): action:"remove" only: true after you asked him once to confirm the removal. Never grants write authority.
- `authority` (one of `"owner-direct"`, `"web-page"`, `"email"`, `"channel-message"`, `"document"`, `"calendar-event"`, optional): Optional source provenance; external-source labels further restrict profile writes.
- `said` (string, optional): His verbatim words. Required for confirm and plan_confirm when `authority` is an external-source label; ignored otherwise. Never grants write authority.
