The same route also serves the settings clients' lanes, which answer with that lane's own object: `{ settingsPrecondition }` takes action `capture` (read the facts a change would act on) or `write` (make it, optionally only while `ifServing` and `ifIncarnation` still hold; a repeated `requestId` returns the first answer), and `{ settingsImportPrecondition }` takes the same two actions plus `apply`, which spends a captured `reference`; a settings import is refused (403 OWNER_ONLY) for a token minted for automation. A change that loosens a security, permission, judgment or payment setting is the owner's own act: asked with a token minted for automation (one minted through the API by another token, such as pairing.tokens.create or pairing.tokens.migrate, or with narrowed scopes or for a named client; pairing.tokens.list shows it as origin automation) it is not made, but put to the owner as an approval only his own credential answers, and the answer is 202 with code OWNER_APPROVAL_PENDING and the `approvalId`; the change is applied when he approves it, and lapses after a day unanswered or if the daemon restarts first. The operator token, an admin sign-in, the apps on the daemon's machine and a device the owner paired himself (origin owner-pairing) make it at once. |
| `config.setMany` | `POST /config/many` | admin | `write:config` | write (dangerous) | safe with the header `Idempotency-Key` | Write several config values on the daemon as one update: `{ entries: [{ key, value }] }`. Every entry is admitted before anything is written, each settings file is written once and the configuration revision moves once, so a pair of settings that only make sense together never lands half-applied. A refusal names the setting, the reason and the next step, and says what was saved (nothing, unless a later settings file could not be written after an earlier one was). The answer lists, per key, the value the host now holds and which file and tier it is in; when a key does not hold the value asked for (a higher tier overrides it, or it was coerced), the answer is 409 CONFIG_SET_NOT_APPLIED naming those keys in `notApplied`, with the revision written and every entry's held value. A key that holds a credential takes only a goodvibes://secrets/ reference; runtime.workingDir is set on its own with config.set. A change that loosens a security, permission, judgment or payment setting is the owner's own act: asked with a token minted for automation (one minted through the API by another token, such as pairing.tokens.create or pairing.tokens.migrate, or with narrowed scopes or for a named client; pairing.tokens.list shows it as origin automation) it is not made, but put to the owner as an approval only his own credential answers, and the answer is 202 with code OWNER_APPROVAL_PENDING and the `approvalId`; the change is applied when he approves it, and lapses after a day unanswered or if the daemon restarts first. The operator token, an admin sign-in, the apps on the daemon's machine and a device the owner paired himself (origin owner-pairing) make it at once. |
| `credentials.delete` | invoke only | admin | `write:config` | write (owner only, dangerous) | safe to repeat | Remove a credential: the stored secret first, then the config reference pointing at it. That order is deliberate, clearing the config first would strand a secret nothing points at and nothing reaps, while this order leaves, for an instant, a reference resolving to nothing, which every reader already treats as configured-but-broken (the honest state for a credential mid-removal). `cleared: false` means nothing was stored under that key: a miss, not an error, because asking for a credential to be gone when it already is has succeeded. ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding. Mutating, so a relay call is covered by relay.requireStepUpForMutations exactly as config.set is. |
| `credentials.get` | `GET /config/credentials` | admin | `read:config` | read | safe to repeat | Return secret-free credential status (configured/usable) for the shared store. Never returns raw secret bytes. Optional ?key= narrows to one credential. |
| `credentials.set` | invoke only | admin | `write:config` | write (owner only, dangerous) | safe to repeat | Store a credential for a secret-bearing config key THROUGH the daemon, so a surface no longer has to write it into its own on-disk secret store, the write counterpart to credentials.get, and the reason a client on another machine can now finish a settings modal at all. `key` is the config path (e.g. surfaces.telegram.botToken); the secret-store name is derived from it. The value goes into the encrypted store at the scope the ownership rules resolve (a daemon-needed credential lands in the daemon tier whoever asked), is read BACK and compared, and only then does the config key take its goodvibes://secrets/goodvibes/<KEY> reference. A read-back mismatch fails the call and leaves the setting exactly as it was, because a reference resolving to nothing reads as a configured-but-broken credential. The response is secret-free: key names, the resolved scope, the reference now in config, and two plain sentences about where the setting and the credential are filed, never the value. Refuses a key that is not credential-bearing (use config.set) and refuses a value that is itself a goodvibes:// reference. ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding. Mutating, so a relay call is covered by relay.requireStepUpForMutations exactly as config.set is. |

### contracts

| Method | HTTP route | Access | Scopes | Effect | Retry | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `contracts.budget` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:fleet` | write | safe to repeat | Replace a running contract's token and cost ceiling (`maxCostUsd`, `maxTokens`, or both); a limit left out keeps its current value. | `contracts.cancel` | `POST /api/contracts/{contractId}/cancel` | authenticated | `write:fleet` | write | safe to repeat | Stop a contract and every unit agent it runs; its status line records how many files were already changed and where. `cancelled` is false when the contract had already ended. 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id; 409 with CONTRACT_NATIVE for native work (stop it through its own execution, or answer its open question with `cancel`); 409 with CONTRACT_NOT_RUNNING when this runner holds the contract only for inspection. | `contracts.dispatch` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:fleet` | outward | safe with the body `idempotencyKey`: A repeat by the same caller with the same `idempotencyKey` returns the first dispatch's contract while that contract runs, instead of starting a second one. | Start a contract for `ask` (the person's words verbatim) in a hosted session created for it, in `workspaceRoot` (absolute, inside the daemon's working directory or a registered workspace, the folders sessions.hosted.workspaces lists) or the daemon's working directory. | `contracts.list` | `GET /api/contracts` | authenticated | `read:fleet` | read | safe to repeat | Every contract this daemon holds, newest first, each with its whole tree: the ask, the goal, the acceptance criteria with every Jev reading, the groups and units with their checks and nudges, open and answered owner escalations, decisions, usage, and the answer or status line once it ends. `sessionId` narrows the list to one session's contracts (a hosted session's, or a shared session's); ended contracts are left out unless `includeTerminal` is set. Contracts of another caller are left out here and read as CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND everywhere else. |
| `contracts.remove` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:fleet` | write (cannot be undone) | safe to repeat | Delete the record of a contract that has ended (passed, failed or cancelled): its checkpoint and summary. Its branch and worktree, if any, are left to the worktree retention rules. Ended contracts are also removed automatically 30 days after they end, and beyond the newest 100 per project. `removed` is true when it was deleted. 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id; 409 with CONTRACT_NOT_ENDED while it runs (cancel it first); 409 with CONTRACT_NATIVE for native work, whose record its native execution keeps. |
| `contracts.reply` | `POST /api/contracts/{contractId}/reply` | authenticated | `write:fleet` | outward | safe with the header `Idempotency-Key` | The owner's free-text reply to an open escalation of a contract, read by Jev as approve, reject, amend or unclear. Returns how it was read and what the runner did: approved, amended, stopped, asked again (with the new escalation id), or refused when the escalation is no longer open. Approval never passes a criterion Jev read as unmet; the requirement changes only through an amendment. A failed-work question (a native work contract's failed turn, a failed unit, a result that could not be published) is not read by Jev: it accepts exactly `retry` or `cancel`. 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id; 409 with CONTRACT_NOT_RUNNING when this runner holds the contract only for inspection, 409 with CONTRACT_ENDED when the contract has ended, 409 with ESCALATION_NOT_OPEN when the escalation is already answered or another reply to it is being read, 400 with INVALID_ARGUMENT when the text is not an answer the question accepts. |
| `contracts.retryUnit` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:fleet` | write | safe with the header `Idempotency-Key` | Run one unit of a running contract again: a unit that is working gets a fresh agent with its brief and previous checks, a unit that failed (the contract waits on its retry-or-cancel question, the units depending on it held) runs again with a fresh agent, the same as replying `retry`, and a passed unit whose commit failed has its changes committed again. `outcome` is `restarted`, `committed`, or `refused` with `reason` naming why and what to do instead (a unit that has not started, is being fixed, or ended with its contract). 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id; 409 with CONTRACT_ENDED once the contract has ended; 409 with CONTRACT_NATIVE for native work. |
| `contracts.start` | `POST /api/contracts` | authenticated | `write:fleet` | outward | safe with the header `Idempotency-Key`: A retry with the same key and the same body returns the first contract (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true response header) instead of starting a second one; the same key with a different body is refused with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Keys are kept with the contract store per caller, so a retry after a daemon restart, or through another process on the same project, still returns the first contract; the body is compared field by field, in any order. A start whose key cannot be recorded is refused with CONTRACT_KEY_UNRECORDED and starts nothing; a repeat while another process is still starting the first is refused with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again in a few seconds). The key may also be sent as `idempotencyKey` in the body; the header wins when both are given. A replayed result carries `replayed: true`. | Start a contract for `ask`, the person's words verbatim, which every stated acceptance criterion must trace to. Returns at once with the new contract and its owner agent id; the contract shapes, plans and runs on its own, and its progress arrives on the `contracts` event domain. When `sessionId` names a live session this daemon hosts, the contract starts in that session (origin `hosted`): its turns receive the contract's questions and a following turn answers them. Otherwise it starts on the daemon's own runner (origin `external`) under `sessionId`, or the `operator` session when none is given, in `workspaceRoot` (absolute), or the daemon's working directory. `isolation` overrides `contract.isolation` for this contract. 400 with INVALID_ARGUMENT when `ask` is empty, `workspaceRoot` is relative or outside the daemon's workspace, or differs from the hosted session's; 403 with SESSION_NOT_OWNED when the session belongs to another caller; 409 with SESSION_NOT_LIVE when `sessionId` names a hosted session that is no longer live. |
| `contracts.status` | invoke only | authenticated | `read:fleet` | read | safe to repeat | One contract's summary (as `contracts.summaries` gives it), for polling. A stored contract this daemon holds without running carries `held` with `code` (`input-unavailable`: its recorded input could not be restored, and `contracts.cancel` ends it; `claim-unavailable`: no run claim could be taken) and the `reason`. 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND when no runner on this daemon holds the id. |
| `contracts.summaries` | invoke only | authenticated | `read:fleet` | read | safe to repeat | The contracts `contracts.list` returns (same `sessionId` and `includeTerminal`), newest first, each as a small summary: id, session, owner agent, origin, ask, goal, status and status line, failure, group and unit counts, open owner question ids and the newest open question, usage, created, ended and last-changed times, and a `revision` that changes whenever any of these does. Nothing of the evidence, readings or history is sent; read one contract's tree with `contracts.get`. |

| `update.check` | invoke only | admin | `write:control-plane` | write | safe to repeat | Run one update check immediately instead of waiting for the next interval, and return the status afterwards. This is the same tick the schedule runs, so an on-demand check and the hourly one cannot reach different conclusions. It never forces an install: a downloaded-and-verified release still waits for a moment when no work is in flight, which the returned `pendingVersion` reports. A check that fails is reported in `failedCheckCount` and `lastCheckFailure` rather than refused, the caller asked what the state is, and "the check failed" is the answer. `check` says what the call did: `ran` (a check ran now), `already-in-flight` (another check was still running, none was started, and the rest of the answer is as of now) or `loop-off` (no loop is armed, `offReason` says why, and nothing ran). |
| `update.status` | invoke only | authenticated | `read:control-plane` | read | safe to repeat | Whether this daemon is keeping itself current, and, when it is not, the reason in one line. `armed` is false whenever no loop is running and `offReason` says which gate stopped it: update.auto not set, no artifact identity (a host that manages its own updates), or no release URL to resolve tags from. `failedCheckCount` with `lastCheckFailure` is the case that used to be invisible: checks running on schedule and failing every time, which looks exactly like having nothing to update to. `pendingVersion` is a release already downloaded and verified, waiting for a moment when no work is in flight; `pendingSince` says since when a release has waited and `pendingBlockedBy` names the fleet ids of the work it waits behind (the owner is told once after 24 hours). `rejectedVersion` is a release that was installed here, failed to start, and was rolled back, it is deliberately not reinstalled. `recoveryRequired` (true) and `transactionRecovery` appear only while an interrupted update or rollback fences the loop: `transactionRecovery.recoveryPaths` lists the retained files to inspect, `recoveryErrors` what went wrong, and the loop stays off until they are dealt with. |

| `email.inbox.list` | `GET /api/email/inbox` | authenticated | `read:email` | read | safe to repeat | Return inbox message summaries fetched live from the configured IMAP account, newest first (ordered by server-assigned UID, never by the sender-written Date header). When the server answered for a message and the daemon could not read the answer, the page is short and `unreadable` says so, an omitted message is not by itself evidence that it was deleted. A message the daemon's inbox mirror has labelled carries `triageLabel` (spam, priority or normal); one not labelled yet has none. A message the mirror holds carries `screening`: `screened`, or `not-screened` when only code checked it for credential and card text, with `screeningReason`. `uidValidity` is the mailbox generation the page's UIDs belong to (absent only when the server reports none); email.inbox.update needs it. |
| `email.inbox.read` | `GET /api/email/inbox/{uid}` | admin | `read:email` | read | safe to repeat | Return the full body and attachment metadata for a single inbox message by IMAP UID, with `uidValidity`, the mailbox generation it was read under (email.inbox.update needs it). Read-only (BODY.PEEK; does not mark as read). |
| `email.inbox.update` | invoke only | admin | `write:email` | write | safe to repeat | Change one inbox message by IMAP UID: action seen or unseen sets or clears its read flag; archive moves it to the folder the server marks Archive (or All Mail); delete moves it to the folder the server marks Trash, so it can be recovered there. A server with no such folder is refused and nothing changes; nothing here expunges permanently. uidValidity is required: the mailbox generation email.inbox.list or email.inbox.read returned with the uid, so a reset mailbox refuses instead of changing whichever message now holds that UID. Answers { uid, action, movedTo? }. |
| `email.send` | `POST /api/email/send` | admin | `write:email` | outward (dangerous) | safe with the body `clientSendId`: A repeat with the same `clientSendId` and the same message within ten minutes returns the first answer instead of sending again; the same id with a different message is 409 CLIENT_SEND_ID_REUSED. | Send a composed email via the configured SMTP account. Irreversible external send; requires confirm: true and explicit user review of recipients and body. Pass a clientSendId (8-128 letters, digits, - or _) chosen when the message was composed: a repeat with the same id and the same message within ten minutes returns the first answer instead of sending again (the id also becomes the Message-ID), and the same id with a different message is refused (409 CLIENT_SEND_ID_REUSED). A send whose final server reply was lost fails with EMAIL_DELIVERY_UNCONFIRMED: it may have gone, and repeating it with the same id will not send it twice. |

| `flags.graduation.report` | invoke only | authenticated | `read:config` | read | safe to repeat | Return the feature defaults report: every platform capability with its current default, default-disposition state (dark = default-off with no evidence, soaking = accumulating evidence, graduate-candidate = judged ready and awaiting a release decision, graduated = default on, blocked = held off with a dated reason), and its validation evidence. | `fleet.attempts.pick` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:fleet` | write (dangerous) | safe to repeat | Accept one attempt as the winner of its best-of-N group. With `confirm: true` its worktree branch is merged through the existing sequential integration lane and every losing sibling's worktree is cleaned; `losers` reports each clean-up as observed: `done` (worktree seen gone), `pending` (still cleaning after ten seconds; `check` names what to run), or `failed` (kept or not cleaned, with its refusal). | `fleet.conflicts.list` | invoke only | authenticated | `read:fleet-content` | read | safe to repeat | Return every work item whose integration merge CONFLICTED and is waiting on a human: the kept worktree path, item branch, the STRUCTURED conflicting-file list, and the resolution session id once one was spawned. | `fleet.conflicts.resolve` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:fleet` | write | safe with the header `Idempotency-Key` | The conflict row's one action: spawn a resolution session INSIDE the kept worktree, seeded with the structured conflict list and tree path (the same seeded-session machinery as the CI fix flow), and stamp the REAL session id back onto the item. When the resolution session ends with success, the merge is retried automatically (also after a daemon restart) and a clean merge reclaims the kept tree; otherwise fleet.conflicts.retry retries it. An item with no unresolved conflict is an honest 409, as is an item whose merge is being retried. When the conflict ends while the session starts (its merge landed meanwhile), the session is stopped and the call is refused with 409 CONFLICT_RESOLVED_ELSEWHERE. |
| `fleet.conflicts.retry` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:fleet` | write | not safe | Attempt the integration merge of a conflicted item again, for a conflict resolved by hand in the kept worktree or by a resolution session that ended without a clean re-merge. Answers outcome merged (the kept tree is reclaimed), conflict (still conflicted; the row stays) or not-conflicted (nothing to retry). Refused with 409 while that item's resolution session is still running or being started, or while another retry of it runs. |
| `fleet.graph.get` | `GET /api/fleet/workstreams/{workstreamId}/graph` | authenticated | `read:fleet-content` | read | safe to repeat | The dependency-graph view of one workstream: nodes (id, title, state, cluster, files, merge state, blocked reason, orphaned flag, deepest-remaining-path depth, stalled tell, agent), edges (from depends on to), and the elastic-pool state (ready/running counts, at-cap, cap key + size, any spawn refusal). Surfaces render the task graph under the chain from this, the fleet/observability idiom. 404 when the workstream is unknown to this daemon. |

| `voice.local.install` | `POST /api/voice/local/install` | admin | `write:config` | write (dangerous) | safe to repeat | Starts the one-act setup and answers at once with the run it started (or the run already in progress it joined); the install runs on in the daemon, voice.local.status serves its live progress as installInProgress and, when it ends, its receipt as lastInstall. The setup: download + checksum-verify the piper TTS engine, a default voice, and (where a pinned goodvibes-built bundle exists) the whisper.cpp STT engine with its default model into the goodvibes-managed directory, then point the voice.local.* config keys at the managed install, never overwriting a key you already set to a custom value (skipped keys are reported). The install ends by speaking a test phrase and reading it back: the transcript is compared word by word in code, allowing one differing word, and the receipt carries the transcript and the comparison. Downloads only when you ask; a failed or checksum-mismatched download keeps nothing. |
| `voice.local.status` | `GET /api/voice/local/status` | authenticated | `read:health` | read | safe to repeat | Whether the managed local voice runtime (piper TTS + a default voice) is installed: not-provisioned (with a size-labeled offer), partial, provisioned, or unsupported-platform. STT (whisper.cpp) reports its own managed state: goodvibes builds and pins the whisper.cpp bundle per platform (no official prebuilt exists; provisioning never compiles on your machine), so where a pinned bundle exists STT provisions like TTS, and elsewhere it reports unsupported honestly. While a voice.local.install run is active, the response also carries installInProgress, the live per-component progress (phase, byte sizes where known) of that run, so surfaces poll this read during the install to render real progress; the section is absent when no install is running. Once a run ends, lastInstall carries its receipt (or the reason it stopped without one) with the run's start and finish times; a surface that started an install reads its result here. Read-only. |
| `voice.setup` | `POST /api/voice/setup` | admin | `write:config` | write (dangerous) | safe to repeat | Sets voice up for what was asked: intent wake (this surface listens for the wake word; implies speech-to-text), stt, tts or voice (all of it), for the surface named (tui, agent, webui, app), which is the one that ends up listening. The plan is decided from this host's own facts (wake rows, wake models on disk, the managed speech runtimes, the input device); steps that need no answer are done at once (the wake rows are set, missing wake models are fetched), and the answer lists each step: do (done, or why it could not be), propose (acceptProposals: true does it) and ask (ttsChoice answers the text-to-speech question: local or a cloud provider this host holds a credential for). An install the plan needs is started and not waited for: installStarted names the run, and voice.local.status serves its progress and receipt. rendered is the plan as one reply a surface prints as-is; complete is true when nothing is left to answer and every step that ran finished. |
| `voice.wake.model.get` | `GET /api/voice/wake/model` | authenticated | `read:health` | read | safe to repeat | Read one provisioned wake artifact in bounded chunks, for a surface that cannot fetch it itself, a browser tab, whose cross-origin fetch of the release asset is refused because that asset answers with no CORS header. Each chunk carries the offset, the whole artifact's size, and its PINNED sha256, so a client reassembles the file and verifies it against the pin: a truncated transfer fails at the consumer instead of loading as a model that silently never detects. Both classifier formats are served, "classifier" is the onnx build a browser tab loads, "tflite" the same classifier for a runtime that cannot, as is the speech gate voice.wake.vadThreshold runs ("vad"), and so is the attribution NOTICE of each redistributable artifact ("notice" for the classifier, "embedding-notice" for the front end, "vad-notice" for the gate), because a client that can fetch the bytes but not the NOTICE cannot satisfy the terms it received them under. Serves what is on disk and does not download; installation puts it there, and voice.wake.provision is the recovery path when it is missing. |
| `voice.wake.provision` | `POST /api/voice/wake/provision` | authenticated | `write:config` | write | safe to repeat | Download and checksum-verify the pinned wake-word classifier in both runtime formats (onnx and tflite), the speech-embedding front end, the speech gate voice.wake.vadThreshold runs, and the attribution NOTICE of each, into the goodvibes-managed directory, about 6.1 MB. Installing goodvibes already does this, and a daemon retries at boot, so this verb is the RECOVERY path: an install that was offline, an artifact that failed verification, or a re-provision after the pinned model changes. Resumable by re-running: an artifact that already matches its pin is skipped, and one that is present but fails verification is replaced rather than used. A failed or mismatched download keeps nothing at the destination. Single-flight: two surfaces asking at once, or a boot attempt and a user asking, join one download instead of racing for the same files. |
| `voice.wake.status` | `GET /api/voice/wake/status` | authenticated | `read:health` | read | safe to repeat | Whether the pinned wake-word artifacts are on disk and VERIFIED BY CONTENT: the "hey goodvibes" classifier, the tflite form of the same classifier, the speech-embedding front end the classifier sits behind, the speech gate voice.wake.vadThreshold runs, and the attribution NOTICE belonging to each of the three redistributable artifacts (the classifier's, the front end's and the gate's). Each reports verified, corrupt (present but failing its checksum, a truncated or swapped file, distinct from missing) and its byte size, with the total a fresh provision would download. Installing goodvibes provisions these, and a daemon retries at boot whatever the install could not fetch, so on a normal machine this reads ready without anyone having run a setup command; an offline install reports not-provisioned here until it is retried. The overall ready flag covers the classifier, the front end and both of THEIR NOTICEs, an artifact whose attribution is missing is not one this daemon may serve, and excludes two things: the tflite twin, which nothing here loads, so a host missing just that can still detect; and the speech gate, reported as vadReady instead, because voice.wake.vadThreshold defaults to 0 and the detector runs without it. Also restates that the model's published recall figures are measured on synthesised speech only, which any surface describing the model must carry. Never downloads. Read-only. |

### memory

| Method | HTTP route | Access | Scopes | Effect | Retry | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `memory.consolidation.decide` | invoke only | admin | `write:memory` | write | safe to repeat | Answer one pending consolidation proposal (memory.consolidation.receipts lists them with their `id`). The actions each kind accepts, `first`/`second` being the proposal's ids in order: contradiction keep-first \| keep-second \| both-stand; cross-scope-duplicate keep-first \| keep-second \| keep-both; stale-delete delete \| keep. Keeping one record marks the other stale (recoverable); delete removes the record; both-stand and keep-both mark the records reviewed and record the decision, so the proposal is not raised again. Answers decided:true with the records changed and removed, or decided:false with a refusal (code, state, reason, next) and nothing changed. ws-only invoke verb. |
| `memory.consolidation.receipts` | `GET /api/memory/consolidation/receipts` | authenticated | `read:memory` | read | safe to repeat | Return the retained memory-consolidation run receipts (what each idle/scheduled pass scanned, merged, archived, decayed) and the pending judgment PROPOSALS they carry (contradictions, cross-scope duplicates), the records a proposal references are already marked into the review queue, and a human resolves them through the confirmation-gated review route. A runtime without the consolidation scheduler answers an honest 501. |
| `memory.doctor` | `GET /api/memory/doctor` | authenticated | `read:memory` | read | safe to repeat | Return sqlite-vec and memory embedding-provider diagnostics. |
| `memory.embeddings.default.set` | `POST /api/memory/embeddings/default` | admin | `write:memory` | write | safe to repeat | Set the active default memory embedding provider. |
| `memory.projections.get` | `GET /api/memory/projections/{id}` | authenticated | `read:memory` | read | safe to repeat | Return one standing record's projection by id: its metadata entry plus the exact markdown the file projection would write (front-matter + content, with the live temporal status labelled). Returns 404 when no standing (project/team) record has that id, a session-scope or unknown id is an honest miss, never an empty projection. |
| `memory.projections.list` | `GET /api/memory/projections` | authenticated | `read:memory` | read | safe to repeat | Return the live projection of standing (project/team-scope) memory records, one metadata entry per record (id, filename, scope, class, summary, tags, confidence, review state, temporal validity + status), oldest first. This is the read view over the same standing memory the file projection writes as markdown; session-scope records are excluded (they are not standing memory). Computed live from the store, never read from disk, so it always matches the current records. An expired record is present with status:"expired" rather than silently dropped. |
| `memory.records.add` | `POST /api/memory/records` | admin | `write:memory` | write | safe with the body `id`: An add that names a caller-generated `id` (mem_<base36 time>_<8 hex>) stores the memory once: a repeat with the same id and the same record returns the stored row, and the same id with a different record is refused. Without an id each call stores a new memory. | Add a memory record to the daemon-owned canonical store. The daemon is the single writer for its store; a client surface routes its writes here instead of opening the store file, so two processes never write the same sql.js file. New records default to confidence 60 (the recall floor) and reviewState fresh unless the review block overrides them. An optional caller-generated id (mem_<base36 time>_<8 hex>) makes the add safe to resend: the same id with the same record returns the stored row, the same id with a different record is refused. |
| `memory.records.delete` | `DELETE /api/memory/records/{id}` | admin | `write:memory` | write (cannot be undone) | safe to repeat | Permanently delete a memory record and its links from the canonical store. Delete means delete: the record is removed from the store and the semantic index, not merely flagged. Returns { deleted: false } when no record with that id existed, an honest boolean, never a 200 that pretends a phantom row was removed. |
| `memory.records.export` | `POST /api/memory/records/export` | authenticated | `read:memory` | read | safe to repeat | Export a no-loss bundle (records + links) for the given filter from the canonical store. The bundle round-trips through import id-keyed, so it is the wire form of the cross-surface fold/reconcile seam. Read-only. |
| `memory.records.get` | `GET /api/memory/records/{id}` | authenticated | `read:memory` | read | safe to repeat | Return a single memory record by id from the canonical store, or 404 when no record with that id exists. |
| `memory.records.import` | `POST /api/memory/records/import` | admin | `write:memory` | write | safe to repeat | Import a bundle into the canonical store as an id-keyed union: an id already present is left untouched (counted skipped), a new id is added; a link is added only when both its endpoints exist. Never overwrites, never deletes, idempotent on re-run. The daemon is the single writer, so a client imports here instead of writing the store file. |
| `memory.records.links.add` | `POST /api/memory/records/{id}/links` | admin | `write:memory` | write | safe to repeat | Create a directed relation (e.g. "supersedes", "caused") from the path record to a target record. Returns 404 when either endpoint does not exist, never a 200 that pretends a link was made between records that do not both exist. |
| `memory.records.links.list` | `GET /api/memory/records/{id}/links` | authenticated | `read:memory` | read | safe to repeat | Return every link where the record is the source or the target. Returns 404 when no record with that id exists, an honest not-found, distinct from a record that exists but has no links (an empty array). |
| `memory.records.list` | `POST /api/memory/records/list` | authenticated | `read:memory` | read | safe to repeat | Bulk read from the canonical store: a literal (non-semantic) search returning the matching records as a plain array. An empty filter returns every record (getAll). This is the read a client surface uses instead of opening the store file for its browse/list and knowledge-injection paths. |
| `memory.records.search` | `POST /api/memory/records/search` | authenticated | `read:memory` | read | safe to repeat | Search the canonical store, literal or semantic. When semantic is requested but the semantic index cannot be consulted, the search falls back to a literal scan and states the reason in indexUnavailableReason rather than returning a silent empty result that reads as "nothing was ever stored". With recall=true the cross-surface recall-honesty contract is applied: flagged (stale/contradicted) records are excluded outright and records below the 60% confidence floor are dropped, each exclusion counted honestly. |
| `memory.records.search-semantic` | `POST /api/memory/records/search-semantic` | authenticated | `read:memory` | read | safe to repeat | Rank records by semantic similarity against the query, returning scored results (distance, similarity, score). When the query has no vector match the store falls back to a lexical ranking rather than a silent empty. distance is null for a fallback (non-vector) result. Read-only against the daemon's canonical index. |
| `memory.records.update` | `POST /api/memory/records/{id}/update` | admin | `write:memory` | write | safe to repeat | Edit a record's content fields (scope, summary, detail, tags) and its temporal validity window (validFrom, validUntil) in the canonical store. This is distinct from the review update: it changes the record itself, e.g. moving scope project→team promotes a record to the shared surface. For validFrom/validUntil a number sets the bound, null clears it, and an omitted field leaves it unchanged, so a proposal that changes only the window can be applied. Returns 404 when no record with that id exists. |
| `memory.records.update-review` | `POST /api/memory/records/{id}/review` | admin | `write:memory` | write | safe to repeat | Update a record's review signal (reviewState, confidence, reviewer, staleReason) in the canonical store. Marking a record stale or contradicted flags it so the recall-honesty contract will never inject it into a prompt again regardless of confidence. Returns 404 when no record with that id exists. |
| `memory.review-queue` | `GET /api/memory/review-queue` | authenticated | `read:memory` | read | safe to repeat | Return memory records prioritised for review. Accepts optional limit (?limit=N) and scope filter (?scope=session\|project\|team). A scope query parameter that is present but not one of the three valid values returns 400. |
| `memory.snapshots.list` | `GET /api/memory/snapshots` | authenticated | `read:memory` | read | safe to repeat | The memory store's point-in-time copies, newest first: the daily copy, the copy taken before a schema migration, the copy every restore takes of the records it replaced, and the tripwire copy. Each with its name (what memory.snapshots.restore takes), why it was taken, when, its size on disk and how many records it holds (null when the copy could not be read). Only the records store is copied; the semantic index is rebuilt from the records. Empty for a store that lives in memory only. |
| `memory.snapshots.restore` | `POST /api/memory/snapshots/restore` | admin | `write:memory` | write (owner only, dangerous) | safe to repeat | Replace every memory record, link, consolidation proposal and store fact with those of one copy (its exact name from memory.snapshots.list, `latest`, or the start of one name such as a date). The owner's act only: requires confirm: true on an explicit request from the owner's own session, device or machine; an agent is refused. A copy of the records being replaced is taken first and named in `undoSnapshot`, so restoring it undoes this restore. One SQLite write transaction: processes that share the store (terminal app, Agent, daemon) see the restored records on their next read, and a failure part way leaves the store as it was. The semantic index then re-embeds only records whose text differs from what it holds (`vectorIndex: updating`). Answers which copy, records before and after, and links after. |
| `memory.vector.rebuild` | `POST /api/memory/vector/rebuild` | admin | `write:memory` | outward | safe with the header `Idempotency-Key` | Rebuild the sqlite-vec vector index. |
| `memory.vector.stats` | `GET /api/memory/vector` | authenticated | `read:memory` | read | safe to repeat | Return the current sqlite-vec vector-store posture. |

### occasions

| Method | HTTP route | Access | Scopes | Effect | Retry | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `occasions.acknowledge` | `POST /api/occasions/acknowledge` | admin | `write:occasions` | write | safe to repeat | Record that the owner has one occurrence in hand, so nothing is pushed at them about it again. This is not a yes and not a no: the open item STAYS OPEN and stays enumerable, so occasions.pending still lists it, under acknowledged[] rather than in the nudge, and asking what is coming up still answers with it. Only the push stops. The record expires with its occurrence, so next year asks fresh. An occurrence already answered yes or no is left as it is: changed is false and reply says so. source names how it was recorded: conversation when the owner said so in a reply, explicit when a surface offered the action, gift-flow when the owner is already answering gift questions about it. |
| `occasions.answer` | `POST /api/occasions/answer` | admin | `write:occasions` | write | safe to repeat | Record yes, no, later or acknowledged for one occurrence. A no goes silent for the rest of this cycle and expires with the date, so next year asks fresh carrying no memory of the refusal. A later is NOT a decline, it comes back roughly halfway to the date. A yes on a gift-giving occasion opens the short interview and returns its first question. A yes or a no RESOLVES the open item and removes it. A later keeps the item open and moves it to its return date with its pushes available again. An answer of acknowledged leaves the item standing and quiet (the same as occasions.acknowledge); on an occurrence already answered yes or no it changes nothing and ok is false with the reason. |
| `occasions.confirm` | `POST /api/occasions/confirm` | admin | `write:occasions` | write | not safe | Write the confirmed occasion as one line in the owner profile, under Important dates, carrying its provenance. self:true marks the owner's own date (written as for me), so a remember-only one is never pushed at them. This is the ONE confirmation: nothing re-confirms at nudge time, because for an annual date a silent write means the mistake surfaces up to eleven months later. Refused without a kind rather than defaulting one. Goes through the owner-profile write gate, so authority, surface and a verbatim quote of what the owner said are all required. |
| `occasions.conflict.resolve` | `POST /api/occasions/conflict/resolve` | admin | `write:occasions` | write | safe to repeat | Apply the owner's answer to "which date is right?": keep names the date to keep, the other lines for that title are removed from the owner profile through the profile write gate (so authority is required with keep), answers and gift history stay, and the conflict is not raised again. Without keep nothing changes and dates lists what is recorded, to put to the owner. A conflict is never resolved automatically: only the owner knows which date was right. Two lines for one occasion are a conflict even when they name the same date (their kind, person or lead time can differ); then keep may be left out, and every line but the first is removed. When the file already holds one line (the owner fixed it by hand) the reminder is closed and resolved is true. |
| `occasions.gifts` | `POST /api/occasions/gifts` | authenticated | `read:occasions` | read | safe to repeat | Return what the owner landed on for one occasion in previous years, newest first. | `occasions.interview.answer` | `POST /api/occasions/interview/answer` | admin | `write:occasions` | write | safe to repeat | Record one answer and return the next question, if there is one. The interview guides the owner to their own idea and never recommends a gift, that judgement is the owner's, which is also why the outcome recorded is what the owner landed on rather than what was suggested. |
| `occasions.interview.get` | `POST /api/occasions/interview` | authenticated | `read:occasions` | read | safe to repeat | Return one gift interview and the question that has not been answered yet. A thread the owner walked away from resumes here rather than restarting: the next step is the one the owner did not get to. Over a channel the steps are asked one at a time; in the agent they can be one exchange. |
| `occasions.interview.record` | `POST /api/occasions/interview/record` | admin | `write:occasions` | write | safe to repeat | Close the interview with what the owner settled on and write it to the gift history. Recording the outcome rather than merely that the owner said yes is the point: "said yes in 2026" cannot stop year three steering where year one did. |
| `occasions.list` | `GET /api/occasions` | authenticated | `read:occasions` | read | safe to repeat | Return every occasion declared in the owner profile, with its next occurrence, how many days away it is, the lead it uses, whether it is inside its lead window, and what was answered for that occurrence. Also returns lines under the heading that could not be typed, each with the reason, and any occasion recorded on two lines (two different dates, or the same date written twice). This carries the dates: it is the owner asking their own system what it holds, which is the explicit ask that unlocks a closed-tier read. A nudge never does. |
| `occasions.pending` | `GET /api/occasions/pending` | authenticated | `read:occasions` | read | safe to repeat | Return everything unresolved, without delivering anything: the batched nudge, any date conflict still open, and any interview left mid-thread. This is how a surface that is not a push destination receives a nudge, it pulls at the start of a turn rather than being pushed at, and a stored date is the prior scheduling that permits raising something unprompted. A nudge a push has already landed on the agent is left out while the agent is a configured push destination, so the push and the pull cannot raise the same thing twice; an item no push has ever landed there is still returned, so a missing sender or a failed send loses nothing. An occurrence inside its window is listed even before any sweep has opened it, so a machine that was just started still answers. Composed in code, the same with or without a decision model. The nudge names the occasion and the person and NEVER the date: proximity is a word, not a count of days. |
| `occasions.plans.confirm` | `POST /api/occasions/plans/confirm` | admin | `write:occasions` | write | not safe | Write the confirmed plan as one line in the owner profile, under Plans, carrying its provenance and every entry of details (a confirmation number, flights and times, who is travelling), which occasions.plans.list returns in extras. | `occasions.plans.list` | `GET /api/occasions/plans` | authenticated | `read:occasions` | read | safe to repeat | Return every plan declared in the owner profile, a dated range with attributes, plus whichever one has the owner away today. | `occasions.plans.propose` | `POST /api/occasions/plans/propose` | authenticated | `write:occasions` | write | safe to repeat | Work out what would be written for a plan heard in conversation, and return the one-line confirmation. Writes nothing. Away is opt-in rather than assumed: "the kitchen is being redone, 3rd to the 10th" is a real dated range that is not the owner leaving the house. |
| `occasions.plans.remove` | `POST /api/occasions/plans/remove` | admin | `write:occasions` | write (cannot be undone, dangerous) | safe to repeat | Remove one plan from the owner profile, chosen by planId (its normalised title) and planFrom when two plans share a name. One confirmation: confirmed:false returns the sentence to put to the owner and removes nothing. Goes through the owner-profile write gate, so authority is required. |
| `occasions.plans.update` | `POST /api/occasions/plans/update` | admin | `write:occasions` | write | safe to repeat | Change one recorded plan in place, chosen by planId (its normalised title) and planFrom when two plans share a name: any of title, from, to, away, destination and details (details replaces the list); a field left out keeps its value. With confirmed:false nothing is written and proposal carries the exact line and the sentence to put to the owner; with confirmed:true the new line is written and the old one removed, through the owner-profile write gate (authority, surface and said required). |
| `occasions.propose` | `POST /api/occasions/propose` | authenticated | `write:occasions` | write | safe to repeat | Work out what would be written for a date heard in conversation, and return the one-line confirmation to put to the owner. Any date already recorded for the same name that disagrees comes back in conflictsWith. |
| `occasions.remove` | `POST /api/occasions/remove` | admin | `write:occasions` | write (cannot be undone, dangerous) | safe to repeat | Remove one occasion and every record the machine kept against it, answers, gift history, open items, interviews and calendar mirrors. A confirmed:false call returns the sentence to put to the owner, naming the line (removedLine), and removes nothing. The line removed is the occasion's first; when other lines still declare the same occasion (stillDeclaredBy above 0) only that line goes and its records are kept, since the next line is now the occasion. |
| `occasions.state` | `GET /api/occasions/state` | authenticated | `read:occasions` | read | safe to repeat | What the machine-owned store is holding, counts of answers, gift records, open items, interviews and calendar mirrors, plus what the last housekeeping pass removed and why, and whether the file was found unreadable. | `occasions.sweep` | `POST /api/occasions/sweep` | admin | `write:occasions` | write | safe with the header `Idempotency-Key` | Run one pass immediately: reap expired and orphaned state, find the occasions entering their lead window, batch them into a single message, mirror to the calendar if that is on, and deliver. Housekeeping runs first and unconditionally, so a machine with nudging turned off still reaps. It runs the same with or without a decision model; with decision models off, provenance:"classic" says who each date is about was taken from the line's own for-me marker only. A push a destination accepted is recorded as sent even if settings or the profile changed during the send, so it is not pushed again next pass. |
| `occasions.update` | `POST /api/occasions/update` | admin | `write:occasions` | write | safe to repeat | Change one recorded occasion in place: any of date, kind, person, recurrence, leadDays (null returns to the default) and self; a field left out keeps its value. ### pairing

| Method | HTTP route | Access | Scopes | Effect | Retry | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pairing.handoff.complete` | invoke only | admin | `write:control-plane`, `write:relay` | write (owner only) | safe to repeat | Apply the surface's per-offer decisions in ONE pass: an accepted notifications offer registers the browser push subscription (endpoint + keys, optional deviceId), an accepted passkey offer registers the WebAuthn credential, an accepted relay offer is acknowledged. Each offer returns an honest per-offer result (completed / declined / unavailable / failed); an omitted or false offer is reported as declined, never silently half-applied. Because it can register a step-up passkey it needs what stepup.credentials.register needs (admin, write:relay, never the Agent's credential), and a passkey is accepted only when pairing.handoff.create offered one to this very pairing (the caller is the device that paired with that hand-off's token), once, within 30 minutes; otherwise the passkey offer fails and nothing is registered. A pairing minted narrower than full authority is not offered a passkey. |
| `pairing.handoff.create` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:control-plane` | write (owner only) | not safe | The owner's pairing flow. Mint a per-device token AND assemble the set-up OFFER SET this daemon can satisfy (notifications, carrying the VAPID public key; relay; passkey step-up), so a freshly-paired surface can complete them in one pass. Returns the offer set, the `#pair=<token>` deep-link fragment (the exact URL-fragment shape the web app consumes, token in `pair=`, offers in `offers=`), a full deep link when a web origin is configured, and that origin's honest TLS/capability POSTURE: the one plain-http-on-LAN notice line (stated here, never a nag) plus per-capability availability labels so surfaces render "needs https, available via tailscale" instead of dead buttons. The token secret is returned exactly once. When a paired device asks, the new token records that device (mintedBy) and is revoked with it; a device whose own pairing is gone is refused with 403 PAIRING_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND. Each offer is independently declinable at completion. The device it pairs is recorded as the owner's own (origin owner-pairing) when the caller holds the owner's own credential (the operator token, an admin sign-in, an app on his machine, or a device he paired himself) with full authority; from a token minted for automation, the Agent's credential or a narrowed caller it is recorded as automation. `fromSharedToken: true` is how a client signed in with the shared operator token (the owner's own browser) moves onto its own token: it pairs itself here, exempt from device.nodes.maxPaired as pairing.tokens.migrate is, and the token it gets is an owner device; only a caller on the shared token may send it (400 INVALID_ARGUMENT otherwise). |
| `pairing.posture.get` | invoke only | authenticated | `read:control-plane` | read | safe to repeat | The honest TLS/capability posture of a web origin, pass your surface's current origin (or omit it to read the configured web origin). Plain http on a private-network origin (LAN IP, .local, localhost) is a supported posture reported with its ONE notice line; browser-gated capabilities (service worker/PWA install, push, microphone) are each labeled available or "needs https, available via tailscale" so surfaces render labels instead of dead buttons. Localhost keeps all three. The daemon never mints certificates. |
| `pairing.tokens.create` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:control-plane` | write (owner only) | safe with the body `attemptId`: Sending the same attemptId again while the token that attempt produced is still unused returns that token (same id) under a new secret, and the secret of the lost reply stops working; once the token has been used, the same attemptId mints a new token. | Mint a new named per-device operator token and return its plaintext secret EXACTLY ONCE (for a QR / pairing hand-off). Only a hash is persisted; the secret is never listed or returned again. The name is user-visible and editable. When a paired device asks, the new token records that device (mintedBy) and is revoked with it; a device whose own pairing is gone is refused with 403 PAIRING_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND. client "agent" mints the GoodVibes Agent's credential for the calls it makes on the owner's behalf: the daemon reports it as credential "agent" and judges every call made with it; it is listed with client "agent" and does not count toward device.nodes.maxPaired. Send an attemptId and send the same one again when a reply is lost: while the token that attempt produced is unused, the repeat returns that token (same id) under a new secret. scopes limits the device to that list of operator scopes (for example read:sessions, read:transcripts and write:sessions for a phone that only chats); left out, the device holds full operator authority. A caller grants only scopes it holds: a narrowed caller's token inherits its list when scopes is left out, and naming a scope the caller does not hold is 403 MISSING_SCOPE. A token minted here is automation (origin automation): it does not make the owner's own acts, such as loosening a security, permission, judgment or payment setting. A device the owner pairs himself is paired with pairing.handoff.create. |
| `pairing.tokens.delete` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:control-plane` | write (owner only) | safe to repeat | Revoke (permanently delete) one paired device token. Revocation is immediate: the token fails the very next request with a 401, and every token this device minted is revoked with it (listed in alsoRevoked); every other paired device keeps working. An unknown id is a 404 PAIRING_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND, never a 200-noop. |
| `pairing.tokens.list` | invoke only | authenticated | `read:pairing` | read | safe to repeat | List the per-pairing operator tokens (paired devices/browsers) as redacted views: id, user-visible name, created timestamp, last-seen timestamp, mintedBy (the paired device that minted it, when one did), scopes (the operator scopes it holds, when it was paired with a narrower list; absent means full operator authority) and origin: `owner-pairing` for a device the owner paired himself through the pairing flow (pairing.handoff.create or the pairing screen, from the operator token, an admin sign-in, an app on his machine or another owner device, with full authority), which makes the owner's own acts (loosening a security, permission, judgment or payment setting; answering a change put to him), or `automation` for every other token (pairing.tokens.create, pairing.tokens.migrate, a narrowed list, the Agent's credential, and every token minted before origin was recorded), which does not. Origin is recorded at the mint and never changes; to make a device an owner device, pair it again from the pairing screen and revoke the old token. The token secret is never stored in listable form and is never returned. |
| `pairing.tokens.migrate` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:control-plane` | write (owner only) | safe with the body `attemptId`: Sending the same attemptId again while the token that attempt produced is still unused returns that token (same id) under a new secret, and the secret of the lost reply stops working; once the token has been used, the same attemptId mints a new token. | A client currently authenticated with the legacy single shared token mints its OWN named per-device token and receives the plaintext secret once. A token minted here is automation (origin automation), for a script; the owner's own browser or app moves off the shared token with pairing.handoff.create and `fromSharedToken: true`, which makes it an owner device. Send an attemptId and send the same one again when a reply is lost: while the token that attempt produced is unused, the repeat returns that token (same id) under a new secret instead of minting a second one. This does NOT revoke the shared token; that is a separate explicit step (pairing.tokens.revokeShared). |
| `pairing.tokens.rename` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:control-plane` | write | safe to repeat | Change the user-visible name of a paired device token. An unknown id is a 404 PAIRING_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND. |
| `pairing.tokens.revokeShared` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:control-plane` | write (owner only) | not safe | Revoke the shared operator token by replacing it: every copy handed to another device stops working immediately, and the daemon writes the new value to its operator-tokens.json, where the apps on its own machine read it, so they stay signed in. Other devices use per-device pairing tokens (or user sessions). Refused with SHARED_TOKEN_NOT_REPLACEABLE (409) when the daemon serves a token set by GOODVIBES_DAEMON_TOKEN. Not safe to repeat: each call replaces the shared token again. |

### payments

| Method | HTTP route | Access | Scopes | Effect | Retry | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `payments.budget.status` | `GET /api/payments/budget` | authenticated | `read:payments` | read | safe to repeat | Today's spending pools: the daily item budget, the separate overage budget that covers only unavoidable charges (tax, mandatory fees, and the delivery option actually used), and the tolerance allowance. Each reports its limit, what today has spent, what purchases in flight are holding, and what is left. Includes the calendar day and the timezone it was computed in, the day resets at midnight in daemon.timezone, UTC when unset, and whether this node is the one currently allowed to spend. Each spend keeps the day it was made on, in the zone then in force, and counts until that day is over, so changing the timezone cannot hand back a spent budget. The pools are in `currency` and count only what was spent in it: changing payments.currency starts a new pool for the rest of the day, and what was spent earlier that day in the old currency is listed in earlierSpend, in its own currency, never converted. |
| `payments.cards.create` | `POST /api/payments/cards` | admin | `write:payments` | write (owner only) | not safe | Store a card. The number, expiry, CVV and cardholder name go to the daemon secret store, encrypted at rest, under keys derived from the config path; only the label, brand, last four digits, kind and declared issuer cap are kept as config. The response carries the metadata record and never echoes what was submitted, because an echo would be a read path and no read path exists. A virtual card with a hard issuer cap is the recommended configuration: it bounds what any leak could cost to one killable number, which a real card number does not. |
| `payments.cards.delete` | `DELETE /api/payments/cards/{id}` | admin | `write:payments` | write (cannot be undone) | safe to repeat | Delete a card: its config metadata and every secret derived from its config path, reporting how many secret entries were cleared so a partial deletion is visible rather than silent. payments.defaultCardId is not cleared by a delete; payments.cards.list shows a stale id as empty, and every purchase must name its card anyway. |
| `payments.cards.list` | `GET /api/payments/cards` | authenticated | `read:payments` | read | safe to repeat | Configured cards, as METADATA ONLY: id, label, brand, last four digits, whether it is a virtual or a real card, expiry month and year, and the issuer spend cap the owner declared for a virtual card (declared, unverifiable by us, and never treated as an enforcement layer of ours). materialComplete reports whether every required secret field is present without revealing any of them. The card number, expiry, CVV and cardholder name live in the daemon secret store and there is no method that returns them. |

Status retains processing, refusal, cancellation, verification and uncertain-submission outcomes. Disconnecting the caller does not cancel the operation; stopping or shutdown drains its actual work. ### profile

| Method | HTTP route | Access | Scopes | Effect | Retry | What it does |

| `profile.forget` | `POST /api/profile/forget` | admin | `write:profile` | write (dangerous) | safe to repeat | Delete a mechanical field and every retained history comment for it, or one prose line addressed by its section plus its exact text. Text that no longer matches removes nothing and says so, rather than deleting the nearest thing. No tombstone, no deleted flag, no retention window, delete means delete. Forgetting something that was not there reports that honestly instead of returning success. Authority-gated exactly like a write: an injection that cannot add a fact must not be able to remove one. |

| `profile.read` | `GET /api/profile` | authenticated | `read:profile-document` | read | safe to repeat | Return the whole owner profile, by section, with each section's tier and every mechanical field's validity. | `push.subscriptions.delete` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:push` | write | safe to repeat | Permanently remove one of the authenticated operator's push subscriptions: the stored record (endpoint + keys) is dropped and cannot be listed afterward, and the removal is a terminal entry on the authority record, so no machine of the group pushes to that device again. | `push.subscriptions.list` | invoke only | authenticated | `read:push` | read | safe to repeat | List the authenticated operator's registered push devices as redacted subscription views (id, deviceId when the record has one, endpoint origin, timestamps, last delivery outcome; two records on the same push service share an origin, so tell them apart by id or deviceId), plus lastRemoval: the most recent device the daemon removed and why (reason gone: the push service answered 404/410; failure-threshold: the push service rejected the endpoint push.subscriptions.failureThreshold times in a row; unusable or malformed: the stored record could never receive a push). | `push.subscriptions.reconcile` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:push` | write | safe to repeat | Reconcile-on-open: the client presents its device identity (deviceId) and its CURRENT endpoint + p256dh/auth keys, and the daemon heals the record for that device in place, updating a stale endpoint the daemon had been holding, then reports what drifted (created / endpoint-updated / keys-updated / unchanged) so the client learns whether the daemon was out of date. | `push.subscriptions.verify` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:push` | write | safe with the header `Idempotency-Key` | Send a live test notification to one of the authenticated operator's subscriptions and return an honest delivery receipt (delivered / pruned / failed). An unknown id, or one owned by another principal, is a 404 SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND. |
| `push.vapid.get` | invoke only | authenticated | `read:push` | read | safe to repeat | Return the daemon's public VAPID key (base64url application-server key) that a browser client passes to pushManager.subscribe(). | `tailscale.get` | invoke only | authenticated | `read:control-plane` | read | safe to repeat | READ-ONLY detection of a usable tailscale environment: binary present, logged-in status, MagicDNS name, and the https URL `tailscale serve` would yield. | `tailscale.serve.run` | invoke only | admin | `write:control-plane` | write (owner only) | safe to repeat | The one-action https affordance: run `tailscale serve --bg <port>` so tailscale fronts the web UI at its https MagicDNS URL, the port being the one the web UI is served on: the control-plane port while the daemon serves the bundle (controlPlane.webui.serve), web.port for a web UI it does not serve (web.enabled). With no web UI served it is refused with 409 WEB_UI_NOT_SERVED and nothing runs. Run only from this explicit user-initiated verb. The serve persists in tailscaled, also after the daemon stops or restarts, until tailscale.serve.stop runs. The attempt is recorded with an honest receipt either way (when tailscale prints a link to turn Serve on for the tailnet, the receipt carries it as enableUrl); on success web.publicBaseUrl is updated to the https URL from the same resolution and the value it replaced is kept for the stop. The daemon never mints certificates, TLS is terminated by tailscale. |
| `tailscale.serve.stop` | invoke only | admin | `write:control-plane` | write | safe to repeat | Stop publishing the daemon to the tailnet: run `tailscale serve --https=443 off`, which removes what tailscale.serve.run started. The attempt is recorded with an honest receipt either way. On success, when web.publicBaseUrl still names the tailnet URL, it is put back to the value it had before the serve (cleared when none was recorded); publicBaseUrlDetail says what happened to it. |

### rewind

| Method | HTTP route | Access | Scopes | Effect | Retry | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rewind.apply` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:checkpoints` | write (dangerous) | safe to repeat | Apply a unified rewind to a session turn anchor, restoring files and/or conversation. DESTRUCTIVE: requires the confirmToken minted by rewind.plan (single-use, ~2 min), which is bound to the session, turn, scope, previewed checkpoint and the conversation as it was counted (its message count and last message). Called without it, it returns a non-error refusal (refused:true) naming rewind.plan, never a silent no-op; an unknown or expired token is a 400; a token whose target changed since the plan (a message arrived, another checkpoint now resolves) is a 409 TARGET_CHANGED naming each change, and nothing is changed. Every apply records an undo point (the workspace restore takes a pre-restore safety checkpoint; the conversation store captures its pre-rewind snapshot) so the rewind is itself reversible, and returns a receipt whose `undo` block carries how to reverse it: checkpoints.restore with undo.files.restoreCheckpointId for the files, rewind.undo with undo.conversation.undoSnapshotId for the conversation. undo.conversation.expiresAfter states how long that undo point lasts, as the process holding the conversation keeps it (the newest 32 rewinds; on disk where that process keeps its sessions). Emits a REWIND_APPLIED receipt event. |
| `rewind.conversation.host.register` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:sessions` | write | not safe | Register the conversation this surface is running for a session, so a conversation-scope rewind of it can actually be served. Only the process holding the messages can count or drop them: without this, rewind.plan for a session hosted anywhere but the daemon reports the conversation half unavailable, and files rewind is unaffected either way. Re-registering with the hostId returned here RENEWS the offer; registering without one claims the session and replaces whoever held it, answering that surface's outstanding requests as unavailable. The registration is a lease, not a reservation, it lapses unless the surface keeps taking its requests, and nothing about it survives a daemon restart, because a claim about a live process is worthless once the process on either end may be gone. |
| `rewind.conversation.host.release` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:sessions` | write | safe to repeat | Withdraw this surface's offer to serve a session's conversation, when the session ends, or the surface is going away. Outstanding requests put to it are answered unavailable rather than left to time out. Only the registered host may release its own session; anyone else is refused. |
| `rewind.conversation.hosts.list` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:sessions` | write | safe to repeat | Which sessions have a surface offering their live conversation right now, how each surface names itself, and when its lease runs out. This is what makes "conversation rewind is unavailable for that session" checkable rather than something a person has to take on trust. |
| `rewind.conversation.requests.answer` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:sessions` | write | safe to repeat | Report what this surface found or did. Which fields are expected follows from the REQUEST, which already says whether it was a preview, a rewind or an undo, an answer that restated that could only disagree with it, silently. For a preview: messagesToDrop and messagesRemaining. For a rewind: droppedMessages and the undoSnapshotId that restores them, optionally undoExpiresAfter saying how long this surface keeps it. For an undo: undone:true once the pre-rewind conversation is back and its save was tried, with notSaved saying why when that save failed. For any kind, a non-empty unavailableReason instead, which is the honest answer when the conversation is gone or this surface cannot serve it, and saying so beats staying silent, because silence becomes a timeout and a timed-out rewind cannot tell whether the messages were dropped; an undo refusal adds unavailableCode UNDO_POINT_GONE, CONVERSATION_CHANGED, or TARGET_CHANGED when the snapshot is of another session. A preview may add revision, the conversation's message count and last message key, which a rewind plan binds. Only the surface a request was put to may answer it. |
| `rewind.conversation.requests.take` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:sessions` | write | not safe | Collect the conversation questions waiting for this host, how many messages a rewind to an anchor would drop, a request to actually drop them, or a request to undo a rewind from its undoSnapshotId, and renew its lease, because a surface that is polling is a surface that is alive. With nothing waiting, pass waitMs to hold the call open until something arrives; an empty result is a normal answer, not an error. Answer each request with rewind.conversation.requests.answer before its expiresAt, or the caller waiting on it is told, honestly, that this surface did not answer in time. |
| `rewind.plan` | invoke only | authenticated | `read:checkpoints` | read | safe to repeat | Dry-run preview of a unified rewind to a session turn anchor: exactly what restoring files (the nearest workspace checkpoint), conversation (truncating session state to the anchor), or both would change, and a short-lived single-use confirm token authorizing the matching rewind.apply. Read-only, nothing is changed. A part with no store wired on this runtime is reported unavailable in a warning, never faked. |
| `rewind.undo` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:checkpoints` | write (dangerous) | safe to repeat | Put a session's conversation back to how it was before a rewind, from the undo.conversation.undoSnapshotId of the rewind.apply receipt. The pre-rewind copy replaces the whole conversation, so the undo is refused while the conversation has newer messages than the rewind left it with. Answers undone:true, or undone:false with a refusal (code, state, reason, next) and nothing changed: the snapshot is gone (see the receipt's undo.conversation.expiresAfter), the conversation changed since, the snapshot is of another session than sessionId (TARGET_CHANGED, naming that session), or the surface holding the conversation did not answer. When the undo took effect but the conversation's store could not save it, `notSaved` says so and what to do: a restart would bring back the rewound transcript. A conversation a surface is hosting is restored by that surface, asked over its rewind.conversation.requests channel; one this daemon holds is restored here. Files are reversed separately with checkpoints.restore. |

| `sessions.hosted.attach` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:sessions`, `read:transcripts` | write | safe to repeat | Join a hosted session and receive its transcript so far, so a client that was never connected, or one reconnecting after the daemon restarted, renders what it missed instead of an empty screen. An attachment carries a LEASE, `hostedSessions.attachmentTtlMs`, ten minutes by default, or `leaseMs` for this attachment alone, because a client that crashed or closed its tab never calls detach, and a claim nothing expires would hold a kill-policy session open forever. | `sessions.inputs.deliver` | `POST /api/sessions/{sessionId}/inputs/{inputId}/deliver` | admin | `write:sessions` | outward | safe to repeat | A live registered surface reports that it collected a queued input (moves it to `delivered`) or finished acting on it (`consumed:true` moves it to `completed`). Only queued/delivered inputs advance; a report on an input that already ended (cancelled, failed, answered by a daemon agent) is refused with 409 `INPUT_NOT_DELIVERABLE` naming its state, binds no agent and forwards no answer. One exception: an input a daemon restart cancelled while a surface in another process was answering it completes on that surface's `consumed:true` report. `agentId` names the agent the surface is running for this input: it binds the reply so a message that arrived over a channel gets its answer routed back to that conversation, the same binding the daemon makes for the executors it spawns itself. `surfaceInstance`, sent with `agentId`, names the surface process running that agent; it is kept in the input's `metadata.deliveringSurfaceInstance` (cleared by a report that names none), so a surface that restarted can fail the inputs a process that is gone was answering. `answer` (sent with `consumed:true`, optionally with `status`) is the output that agent finished with, the daemon writes it into the session and delivers it to the channel. `claim:true` is how a surface takes an input before it starts work on it: it succeeds for one caller only, for a `queued` input, or for a `delivered` one with no agent bound for at least two minutes (a claimant that died before starting it). Any other caller is refused with 409 `INPUT_NOT_CLAIMABLE` naming the state, and nothing changes. A granted claim is recorded as the input's `metadata.claimEpoch` (1 for the first claimant, one more for each later one): that number is the claimant's token. `claim:true` with `claimEpoch` renews the caller's own claim (restarts the two-minute lease, epoch unchanged) while no agent is bound; a surface holds its claim this way while its work waits for capacity. Every other report on a claimed input must carry the current `claimEpoch`: a report from a claimant that was superseded is refused with 409 `INPUT_NOT_CLAIMABLE` and binds nothing. |

Without `state` or `since` the newest `limit` inputs are listed. |
| `sessions.integration.snapshot` | `GET /api/session` | authenticated | `read:transcripts` | read | safe to repeat | Return the session integration snapshot. It carries the conversation's title, which is drawn from what was said, so it needs read:transcripts. |
| `sessions.list` | `GET /api/sessions` | authenticated | `read:transcripts` | read | safe to repeat | Return shared-session integration state. `unreadable`, present only when there are any, names each stored session, message or input this build could not read at start (kind, id, why); they stay in the store untouched and load again under a build that knows them. | `sessions.messages.create` | `POST /api/sessions/{sessionId}/messages` | admin | `write:sessions` | outward | safe with the body `messageId`: Sending the same messageId again to the same session (1 to 255 letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-", chosen by the caller) returns the input already recorded (the same input id, with its current state, and mode continued-live; the reply carries no duplicate flag) instead of recording a second one; an input that failed is run again in that session. | `sessions.permissionMode.get` | `GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/permission-mode` | authenticated | `read:sessions` | read | safe to repeat | Return the session execution mode in force (`mode`): ask-me, jev-decides, just-vibes, yolo, or the read-only plan posture, read the way the gate decides calls. `chosenMode` is the mode the session chose, or the saved one; when they differ, `reason` says why (for example jev-decides runs as ask-me while no decision model is set or while the set one is not answering). `words` says the same in plain words for a person: `chosen` (the label of the chosen mode, "Jev decides"), `inForce` ("asking you for now") and `because` ("decision model unreachable") when the mode in force differs, `sentence` (what the mode in force does, the explanation behind a mode chip) and `asksBefore` (what GoodVibes asks you before). | `sessions.permissionMode.set` | `POST /api/sessions/{sessionId}/permission-mode` | admin | `write:sessions` | write (owner only) | safe with the header `Idempotency-Key` | Set ask-me, jev-decides, just-vibes, or yolo execution, or enter the read-only plan posture. Admin only, because it can loosen security: yolo runs every action without safety denials, and for the local runtime session (no hosted or channel mode of its own) it rewrites the daemon-wide permissions.mode. A hosted session and a channel session with its own mode change only that session; a web chat (companion-chat) has no mode of its own, so setting it rewrites the daemon-wide permissions.mode. Emits runtime.gate (PRESET_CHANGED) so every surface stays in sync. Other session ids answer 404 SESSION_NOT_LOCAL. A looser mode asked with a token minted for automation is not set (a device the owner paired himself sets it at once): it is put to the owner as an approval only his own credential answers, the answer is 202 with code OWNER_APPROVAL_PENDING, the unchanged `mode` and the `approvalId`, and the mode changes when he approves it. |

| `sessions.queuedMessages.edit` | `POST /api/sessions/{sessionId}/queued-messages/{messageId}` | authenticated | `write:sessions` | write | safe to repeat | Replace the text of a message still waiting in the mid-turn queue. | `sessions.register` | `POST /api/sessions/register` | admin | `write:sessions` | write | safe with the body `sessionId`: Registering the same sessionId again is a heartbeat, not a second session; it returns the existing record. | Idempotently register (or heartbeat) a session keyed on a caller-supplied id, carrying its kind, project, and participant identity.
