### tasks

| Method | HTTP route | Access | Scopes | Effect | Retry | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tasks.cancel` | `POST /api/tasks/{taskId}/cancel` | admin | `write:tasks` | write | safe to repeat | Cancel an in-flight runtime task. |
| `tasks.create` | `POST /task` | admin | `write:tasks` | outward | safe with the header `Idempotency-Key` | Start an agent on `task`. Without `sessionId`, `routeId` or `surfaceKind` the agent runs on its own and the answer (202) carries `agentId`, `status`, `task`, `model` and `tools`. With `sessionId` the task goes to that existing session: an id this daemon does not hold is 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND and nothing is recorded or started, a closed session is 409 SESSION_CLOSED; leave `sessionId` out (with `routeId` or `surfaceKind`) to start a new session, whose id the answer carries. In a session the answer (202) carries `mode`: `spawn` (an agent was started, `agentId`), `continued-live` or `queued-follow-up` (handed to the agent already running, `inputId`), `queued-for-surface` (queued for the live surface that runs the session's turns, `inputId`, `agentId: null`; no daemon agent starts), or 409 with `mode` `rejected` and `acknowledged: false`. `tools` or routing's `tools` sent as `[]` is 400: an empty list selects no tool; leave it out for the default tools. `model`, `provider` and `tools` choose what the agent runs on, and win over the same choice in `routing`; routing's `modelId`, `providerId`, `tools`, `fallbackModels`, `providerSelection`, `providerFailurePolicy`, `executionIntent` and `reasoningEffort` are applied. An unknown or ambiguous model is 400 MODEL_NOT_FOUND or MODEL_AMBIGUOUS and nothing starts. |
| `tasks.get` | `GET /api/tasks/{taskId}` | authenticated | `read:transcripts` | read | safe to repeat | Return a single runtime task record, as `{ task }`. |
| `tasks.list` | `GET /api/tasks` | authenticated | `read:tasks` | read | safe to repeat | Return the integration snapshot for runtime tasks. `limit` returns only the newest that many tasks (the totals stay whole), so a long-lived daemon does not send its whole history. An agent task's title and description are its prompt, so a caller without read:transcripts gets each row with its kind as the title and no description or error, and `withheld` says so; counts and states are whole. |
| `tasks.retry` | `POST /api/tasks/{taskId}/retry` | admin | `write:tasks` | outward | safe with the header `Idempotency-Key` | Retry a failed or cancelled agent task: a new agent runs the same task on the model, provider, tools, routing (fallback models, provider selection and failure policy, reasoning effort), execution limits and contract settings the task was started with, in the session that started it. The task keeps its id and its `owner` becomes the new agent, returned as `agentId`. When the record of the agent that ran it is no longer held, nothing is started (409 TASK_SETTINGS_UNAVAILABLE). |
| `tasks.status` | `GET /task/{agentId}` | authenticated | `read:transcripts` | read | safe to repeat | Return lightweight runtime task status by agent id. `status` is pending, running, completed, failed or cancelled. |

After a lost response, use workLedger.submission.get with the same requestId. | Persist one bounded explicit-source goal and ordered criteria on the selected authoritative host. Exact request replay returns the immutable submission receipt. Does not start execution or grant verification authority. Complete encoded input is limited to 262144 bytes without truncation. |
| `workLedger.turn.cancel` | `POST /api/work-ledger/turn/cancel` | admin | `read:work-ledger`, `write:work-ledger`, `write:sessions` | write | safe to repeat | Persist cancellation of the exact native hosted dispatch and drain its owned turn. Cancellation does not undo effects already performed. |
| `workLedger.turn.session` | `POST /api/work-ledger/turn/session` | admin | `read:sessions` | read | safe to repeat | Read authoritative native session ownership. Only an explicit legacy result permits ordinary session ingress. Native sessions additionally require their current paired owner and native delivery scopes. |
| `workLedger.turn.start` | `POST /api/work-ledger/turn/start` | admin | `read:work-ledger`, `write:work-ledger`, `write:sessions` | outward | safe with the body `inputId`: An admitted input (inputId with its sourceRevision) is delivered at most once: a repeat joins or reports the first dispatch instead of starting a second turn. An ambiguous dispatch is never replayed; read it with workLedger.turn.status. | Deliver an already admitted native conversation input at most once through a host-owned broker identity and durable dispatch claim bound to the WebUI settings owner. An optional execution mode initializes only a new session; continuation and replay retain the current session mode. Cross-surface replay is refused. Ambiguous dispatch requires inspection and is never replayed. |
| `workLedger.turn.startAgent` | `POST /api/work-ledger/turn/startAgent` | admin | `read:work-ledger`, `write:work-ledger`, `write:sessions` | outward | safe with the body `inputId`: An admitted input (inputId with its sourceRevision) is delivered at most once: a repeat joins or reports the first dispatch instead of starting a second turn. An ambiguous dispatch is never replayed; read it with workLedger.turn.status. | Deliver an already admitted native conversation input at most once through a host-owned broker identity and durable dispatch claim bound to the Agent settings owner. An optional execution mode initializes only a new session; continuation and replay retain the current session mode. Cross-surface replay is refused. Ambiguous dispatch requires inspection and is never replayed. |
| `workLedger.turn.status` | `POST /api/work-ledger/turn/status` | admin | `read:work-ledger`, `write:work-ledger`, `write:sessions` | write | safe to repeat | Read native hosted dispatch status. Does not admit, claim, retry or execute. |

### workspaces

| Method | HTTP route | Access | Scopes | Effect | Retry | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaces.registrations.add` | `POST /api/workspaces/registrations` | authenticated | `write:workspaces` | write (owner only) | safe to repeat | Register a workspace root so the whole subtree beneath it is covered. Refuses an absurdly broad root (the home directory, the filesystem root, or the daemon state directory) with a 400, coverage flows down the entire subtree, so a root that broad would sweep far more than a project. Idempotent: re-registering the same normalized root returns alreadyRegistered:true. A root registered before native work existed has no native scope; re-registering it grants that scope and answers nativeScopeGranted:true (false otherwise), which is the step a native-work refusal asks for. Registering a root clears any remembered decline recorded at exactly that root. |
| `workspaces.registrations.list` | `GET /api/workspaces/registrations` | authenticated | `read:workspaces` | read | safe to repeat | Return every registered workspace root (coverage flows down each root's subtree) and every remembered subtree-scoped decline. Read-only. |
| `workspaces.registrations.remove` | `DELETE /api/workspaces/registrations` | authenticated | `write:workspaces` | write | safe to repeat | Remove a registered workspace root. Returns { removed: false } when no root with that normalized path was registered, an honest boolean, never a 200 that pretends a phantom root was removed. |
| `workspaces.resolve` | `POST /api/workspaces/resolve` | authenticated | `read:workspaces` | read | safe to repeat | Resolve a path against the registry: covered (by which nearest registered root), declined (at which root), or unknown. Coverage flows DOWN a registered root's subtree and is inherited through the git worktree→main-repo link, a linked worktree outside any registered root still resolves to the main repo's registration. When mainWorktreeRoot is omitted the daemon probes the link itself. Read-only. |

### worktrees

| Method | HTTP route | Access | Scopes | Effect | Retry | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `worktrees.discard` | invoke only | authenticated | `write:worktrees` | write (dangerous) | safe to repeat | Remove a worktree per the eviction-preserving rules: any uncommitted state is first committed onto the worktree's branch (a preservation failure REFUSES the removal rather than losing work), the directory is removed, and the branch is KEPT. Returns an honest receipt (ok, branch kept, preservation commit, detail) either way. |

A failed setup is a visible worktree state, never silent. |

## Operator scopes

Every scope an operator token or user can carry, grouped by what it covers, with how many methods and event streams need it.

A token or user carries scopes; a method or event stream needs every scope it lists (see "Operator API methods" for each method's scopes and access). `read:` scopes read and `write:` scopes change. "Read-only grant" says whether a token minted for reading gets the scope. A scope with no methods or streams is checked by an HTTP route directly (the telemetry routes check `read:telemetry`, and `read:telemetry-sensitive` for the raw view).

## Events

The event streams a client can subscribe to over the operator API, then every runtime event the platform emits, by domain, with its fields.

### Event streams a client subscribes to

Open the stream with `GET /api/control-plane/events?domains=<comma list>`. "SSE name" is the `event:` name each frame carries on the stream; the catalog name is the id the operator contract lists. Access `authenticated` means any credential holding the scopes; `admin` also needs an admin credential (an admin user's session, the daemon's operator token, or a token with no scope list). A stream asked for domains the credential may not receive opens with the allowed ones and names the rest in `withheldDomains` on its `ready` frame; when none is allowed the request is refused with `403` and code `EVENT_ACCESS_DENIED`.

| Catalog name | SSE name | Domains | Access | Scopes | What it carries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `control.approval_update` | `approval-update` | `gate` | admin | `read:events` | Every approval record transition, pushed the moment the broker records it: an ask RAISED (status pending, this is the prompt arriving), claimed by a surface, approved, denied, cancelled, or expired. The payload is the whole `approval` record plus the `createdAt` of the notice, so a subscriber renders the prompt from the event and never needs a follow-up read to draw it. This is the channel that makes approvals.raise usable from a surface that is not in the daemon process: raise returns the pending record and the DECISION arrives here, so a client gets keystroke-fast prompt delivery instead of polling approvals.list on a timer. Domain-tagged `gate` (gateway-scope-enforcement.ts EVENT_DOMAIN), so a client that opened the stream with ?domains=… must include `gate` to receive it; a client that opted into no domain narrowing receives it as before. The record is the daemon's, not the subscriber's: several surfaces see the same transition and the daemon remains the single source of the applied result, a surface renders what the record says rather than what it locally decided. The payload also carries `reading`, the record's reading for an admin who may answer (what is waiting, on whom, the deadline, the decision and whether the asker received it), and every record carries `revision`. A subscriber applies a frame only when its revision is higher than the one it holds, so a late or repeated frame never makes a settled approval actionable again; after a gap or a reconnect it reads approvals.list once, because frames are not replayed. |
| `control.heartbeat` | `heartbeat` |  | authenticated | `read:events` | Keepalive event emitted by the SSE control-plane transport. |
| `control.hosted_session_update` | `hosted-session-update` | `session` | admin | `read:sessions` | Every lifecycle transition of a session whose loop runs INSIDE the daemon: created, attached, detached, turn started, turn ended, terminated, and restored after a restart, plus a contract started in the session and a line the session said for one of its contracts (a question for the owner, or the outcome). The payload carries the whole hosted-session record plus the transition name, the client it is about (attach/detach) and a short detail, so a subscriber renders the change from the event and needs no follow-up read. This channel is LIFECYCLE ONLY. The turn itself, streamed tokens, tool calls, tool results, turn transitions, is already on the `turn` and `tools` runtime domains, stamped with the hosted session id, because a hosted session runs the ordinary orchestrator; a client watches those exactly as it does for a local session and filters on the id it was handed. A second copy of that stream is not published here. Domain-tagged `session`, so a client narrowing with ?domains=… must include `session` to receive it. The record is the daemon's: `effectiveDetachPolicy` says what leaving would do right now, and `terminatedReason` says why a session ended, a hosted session never simply disappears. |
| `control.own_session_activity` |  |  | authenticated | `read:own-sessions` | What a credential without the admin role holding `read:own-sessions` receives of the sessions its own principal created or an owner shared with it (sessions.hosted.create, sessions.hosted.share): their `turn`, `tools`, `gate` and `session` runtime frames (streamed text, tool calls and results, permission decisions, turn transitions), their `approval-update` events and their `hosted-session-update` notices. Frames of every other session, and frames naming no session, are withheld; the admin-only domains stay admin-only for everything else. Open the stream with `?domains=turn,tools,gate,session` (or subscribe to those domains on the socket) and filter on the session id. Ownership is saved with the session, so it holds across a daemon restart. |
| `control.owner_inbox_update` | `owner-inbox-update` | `gate` | admin | `read:events` | A question, claim, purchase window or queued action in the owner inbox was posted, answered or withdrawn. The payload is the whole `item` plus the `createdAt` of the notice, so a surface renders the change and an agent waiting on its question reads the answer without a follow-up inbox.list. Approvals are not repeated here; they arrive on control.approval_update. Domain-tagged `gate`, like approvals: a client narrowing with ?domains=… must include `gate`. |
| `control.ready` | `ready` |  | authenticated | `read:events` | Initial SSE/WebSocket handshake event emitted after a control-plane subscription is opened. `domains` is what the stream delivers; `withheldDomains` names requested domains this credential may not read; `unrecognisedDomains` names requested `?domains=` values that are not runtime event domains, so nothing will arrive for them (a request naming only unknown domains is refused with 400 UNKNOWN_EVENT_DOMAIN). |
| `control.remote_update` | `remote-pair-requested`, `remote-pair-approved`, `remote-pair-rejected`, `remote-pair-verified`, `remote-peer`, `remote-peer-heartbeat`, `remote-peer-disconnected`, `remote-token-rotated`, `remote-token-revoked`, `remote-work-queued`, `remote-work-claimed`, `remote-work-settled`, `remote-work-cancelled` |  | authenticated | `read:events`, `read:remote` | Distributed-runtime notices about paired peers and the work they run: a pair request and its approval, rejection or verification, a peer connecting, its heartbeat and disconnect, a peer token rotated or revoked, and remote work queued, claimed, settled or cancelled. The wire event name is the notice; the payload carries the sanitized peer and, for work, the work record. Requires read:remote, the scope remote.peers.list and remote.work.list require. |
| `control.session_update` | `session-update` | `session` | admin | `read:sessions` | Shared-session lifecycle broadcast. Every session created / closed / deleted / reopened / agent-bound / agent-completed / message-appended / message-forwarded / route-attached and every input & follow-up lifecycle transition is published on the single `session-update` wire event; the specific lifecycle name is the discriminated `payload.event` field. Cross-surface invalidation mapping (webui/TUI): created ⇐ session-created; updated ⇐ session-permission-mode-changed / session-message-appended / session-agent-completed / session-route-attached / session-detached / session-reopened; steered ⇐ session-input-queued-for-surface / session-input-delivered / session-message-forwarded; closed ⇐ session-closed; deleted ⇐ session-deleted. A deleted session is a hard removal: the record is gone, not merely closed. Domain-tagged `session` (gateway-scope-enforcement.ts EVENT_DOMAIN), the same tag control.hosted_session_update carries: both are session lifecycle, so a client that narrows with ?domains=… must include `session` to receive EITHER of them, and one that opted into no narrowing receives both. It is dropped entirely when the control-plane-gateway flag is turned off (no phantom buffering). |
| `control.surface_message` | `surface-message` |  | authenticated | `read:events`, `read:transcripts` | Out-of-band control-plane surface messages for operators and connected clients. Each carries the message text, so it needs read:transcripts, as control.messages.list does. |
| `runtime.agents` | `agents` | `agents` | admin | `read:events` | Agent lifecycle, planning, and completion events. |
| `runtime.automation` | `automation` | `automation` | authenticated | `read:events` | Automation job, schedule, and run events. |
| `runtime.communication` | `communication` | `communication` | admin | `read:events` | Agent communication and policy events. |
| `runtime.compaction` | `compaction` | `compaction` | authenticated | `read:events` | Context compaction and summary events. |
| `runtime.config` | `config` | `config` | admin | `read:events` | Key-level settings-change notices (CONFIG_KEY_CHANGED), carrying the dotted key, its ownership scope (daemon/client/user) and the new value, EXCEPT for a secret-bearing key, which travels by name only with secret:true and no value field at all. The poll-free counterpart to config.get for a client whose settings live in the daemon: an in-process ConfigManager.subscribe cannot see a write that happened on another machine, so a client without this stream keeps running on whatever it read at startup. |
| `runtime.contracts` | `contracts` | `contracts` | admin | `read:events` | Contract runner events: a contract from creation through shaping, planning and the plan checks, each unit and group status, every Jev check with its per-criterion readings, nudges and their consumption, regressions, stalls, planned fixes, owner escalations and replies, gates, commit, and the pass, failure or cancellation. |
| `runtime.control-plane` | `control-plane` | `control-plane` | admin | `read:events` | Control-plane client, auth, and subscription events. |
| `runtime.deliveries` | `deliveries` | `deliveries` | admin | `read:events` | Delivery queue and outcome events. |

| `runtime.gate` | `gate` | `gate` | admin | `read:events` | Gate events: each call through the deterministic boundary, its Jev stakes reading, the preset decision, approvals and preset changes. |

### Runtime events by domain

Each event is a JSON object whose `type` is the name below. The fields after the name are the rest of the object; a `?` marks an optional field.

Domain `agents` (access: admin):

- `AGENT_AWAITING_MESSAGE` { agentId: string, taskId?: string }: Agent is waiting to send a message to the LLM.
- `AGENT_AWAITING_TOOL` { agentId: string, taskId?: string, callId: string, tool: string }: Agent is waiting for a tool call to complete.
- `AGENT_CANCELLED` { agentId: string, taskId?: string, reason?: string }: Agent was cancelled before completion.
- `AGENT_COMPLETED` { occurrenceId?: string, agentId: string, taskId?: string, durationMs: number, output?: string, toolCallsMade?: number, usage?: object }: Agent completed successfully.
- `AGENT_FAILED` { occurrenceId?: string, agentId: string, taskId?: string, error: string, durationMs: number }: Agent failed with an error.
- `AGENT_PROGRESS` { agentId: string, taskId?: string, progress: string, audience?: "operator"|"owner", parentAgentId?: string, contractId?: string, contractRole?: "owner"|"planner"|"unit", contractUnitId?: string }: Agent emitted a textual progress update.
- `AGENT_RUNNING` { agentId: string, taskId?: string, parentAgentId?: string, contractId?: string, contractRole?: "owner"|"planner"|"unit", contractUnitId?: string, wake?: boolean }: Agent is actively running and processing.
- `AGENT_SPAWNING` { agentId: string, taskId?: string, task: string, parentAgentId?: string, contractId?: string, contractRole?: "owner"|"planner"|"unit", contractUnitId?: string, orchestrationGraphId?: string, parentNodeId?: string, taskContract?: object }: Agent is being initialised and configured.
- `AGENT_STREAM_DELTA` { agentId: string, taskId?: string, content: string, accumulated: string }: Agent streamed a chunk of output.

Domain `automation` (access: authenticated):

- `AUTOMATION_JOB_AUTO_DISABLED` { jobId: string, reason: string, consecutiveFailures: number }: A run failed and its job turned itself off after too many failures in a row: `consecutiveFailures` is the count and `reason` why it was paused (`failure-threshold-reached` unless the job gave its own).
- `AUTOMATION_JOB_CREATED` { jobId: string, name: string, scheduleKind: "at"|"cron"|"every", enabled: boolean }: A scheduled job was created. `name` is its display name, `scheduleKind` how it repeats (`at` once, `every` an interval, `cron` an expression), and `enabled` whether it will run.
- `AUTOMATION_JOB_DISABLED` { jobId: string, reason: string }: A scheduled job was turned off; `reason` is why it was paused (`disabled` when none was given).
- `AUTOMATION_JOB_ENABLED` { jobId: string }: A scheduled job was turned on and will run at its next due time.
- `AUTOMATION_JOB_UPDATED` { jobId: string, changedFields: string[] }: A scheduled job's definition changed; `changedFields` names the fields that differ. A change of `enabled` is also announced by AUTOMATION_JOB_ENABLED or AUTOMATION_JOB_DISABLED.
- `AUTOMATION_RUN_COMPLETED` { jobId: string, runId: string, startedAt: number, completedAt: number, durationMs: number, outcome: "cancelled"|"failed"|"partial"|"success", error?: string, retryable?: boolean }: The one terminal event: every run that ends announces it once, whatever the outcome. A subscriber that needs "the run is over" listens for this type only.
- `AUTOMATION_RUN_FAILED` { jobId: string, runId: string, startedAt: number, failedAt: number, error: string, retryable: boolean }: Detail of a failed run (its retry reading); the run's end is announced by AUTOMATION_RUN_COMPLETED.
- `AUTOMATION_RUN_STARTED` { jobId: string, runId: string, startedAt: number, attempt: number }: A run of a scheduled job began. `runId` names the run, `startedAt` is its start time (milliseconds since the epoch) and `attempt` counts retries of the same run, from 1.

Domain `communication` (access: admin):

- `COMMUNICATION_BLOCKED` { messageId: string, fromId: string, toId: string, scope: "broadcast"|"direct", kind: "completion"|"directive"|"escalation"|"finding"|"handoff"|"question"|"review"|"status"|"steer", reason: string, fromRole?: string, toRole?: string, cohort?: string, contractId?: string, parentAgentId?: string }: A message was not sent: the sender is not a registered agent, the recipient is unknown, or the communication policy refused it (an agent may only talk along its communication lane). `reason` says which.
- `COMMUNICATION_CONSUMED` { messageId: string, agentId: string, turn: number }: The agent `agentId` took a queued message into its conversation at turn `turn`. Emitted once, where the agent's inbox is drained at a turn boundary (orchestrator-runner's per-turn inbox drain).
- `COMMUNICATION_DELIVERED` { messageId: string, fromId: string, toId: string, scope: "broadcast"|"direct", kind: "completion"|"directive"|"escalation"|"finding"|"handoff"|"question"|"review"|"status"|"steer" }: The recipient took a sent message into one of its turns. A message waiting for a long turn to end has been sent, not yet delivered.
- `COMMUNICATION_SENT` { messageId: string, fromId: string, toId: string, scope: "broadcast"|"direct", kind: "completion"|"directive"|"escalation"|"finding"|"handoff"|"question"|"review"|"status"|"steer", content: string, fromRole?: string, toRole?: string, cohort?: string, contractId?: string, parentAgentId?: string }: An agent sent a message to another agent (`scope: 'direct'`, `toId` the recipient) or to every agent (`scope: 'broadcast'`, `toId` `*`). `kind` says what it is (a directive, a question, a finding, a handoff...), and `content` is its text. Role, cohort, contract and parent fields carry the routing the message was sent under.

Domain `compaction` (access: authenticated):

- `COMPACTION_AUTOCOMPACT` { sessionId: string, strategy: string, tokensBefore: number, tokensAfter: number }: Auto-compaction: automatic compaction triggered by threshold breach.
- `COMPACTION_BOUNDARY_COMMIT` { sessionId: string, checkpointId: string }: Compaction boundary commit: the compacted state has been persisted.
- `COMPACTION_CHECK` { sessionId: string, tokenCount: number, threshold: number }: A compaction threshold check was triggered.
- `COMPACTION_COLLAPSE` { sessionId: string, messageCount: number, tokensBefore: number, tokensAfter: number }: Collapse: full context collapsed into a single summary message.
- `COMPACTION_DONE` { sessionId: string, strategy: string, tokensBefore: number, tokensAfter: number, durationMs: number }: Compaction completed successfully.
- `COMPACTION_FAILED` { sessionId: string, strategy: string, error: string }: Compaction failed.
- `COMPACTION_MICROCOMPACT` { sessionId: string, turnCount: number, tokensBefore: number, tokensAfter: number }: Micro-compaction: lightweight summary of recent turns only.
- `COMPACTION_REACTIVE` { sessionId: string, tokenCount: number, limit: number }: Reactive compaction: triggered by an imminent context overflow.
- `COMPACTION_RECEIPT` { sessionId: string, trigger: "auto"|"manual", strategy: string, tokensBefore: number, tokensAfter: number, messagesBefore: number, messagesAfter: number, qualityScore: number, qualityGrade: string, lowQuality: boolean, instructionsReinjected: boolean, validationPassed: boolean, sectionsIncluded: string[], requestedStrategy?: string, strategyFallbackReason?: string, outcome: "applied"|"failed"|"kept-original", detail?: string }: Mandatory post-compaction receipt: emitted after every automatic (and the manual) compaction path so a compaction is never silent. Carries what was compacted, token/message counts before and after, the strategy, the quality score/grade the guard computed, whether the standing instruction chain was re-injected, and the outcome, `applied` (compacted context committed), `kept-original` (quality guard rejected it, conversation retained), or `failed` (compaction threw before producing a usable result).

Domain `config` (access: admin):

- `CONFIG_KEY_CHANGED` { key: string, scope: "client"|"daemon"|"user", secret: boolean, value?: unknown, changedAt: number }: One config key now holds a different value. Emitted for an in-process write (including every `config.set` a client makes) and for an external edit the file watcher picked up, the bridge rides `ConfigManager.subscribe`, which both paths already fire.

Domain `contracts` (access: admin):

- `CONTRACT_ATTEMPTS_SELECTED` { contractId: string, unitId: string, candidateIds: string[], chosen: string|null, outcome: "act"|"confirm"|"escalate", decisionId?: string, occurrenceId?: string }: A unit run as several attempts had the passing attempts compared: `candidateIds` are the attempts that passed, `chosen` the one kept (null when none could be chosen) and `outcome` what code does with the choice.
- `CONTRACT_CANCELLED` { contractId: string, reason: string, filesModified: number, occurrenceId?: string }: The contract was cancelled; `reason` says why and `filesModified` how many files it had changed.
- `CONTRACT_CHECKED` { contractId: string, scope: "deliverable"|"group"|"unit", targetId: string, checkId: string, trigger: "agent-failed"|"completion"|"fix-passed"|"owner-amend"|"resume"|"turn-end", result: "await-owner"|"native-decision"|"nudge"|"pass"|"recorded"|"stall", criteria: object[], goal: object, quality: object[], gates: object[], claims?: "files_verified"|"git_corroborated"|"unverifiable_no_claims"|"unverified"|"verified_empty", decisionIds: string[], occurrenceId?: string }: A unit, group or the whole deliverable was checked against its criteria. `trigger` is what started the check (a turn ended, the agent finished or failed, a fix passed, a resume, an owner amendment); `result` what came of it (pass, nudge, await-owner, a native decision, stall, recorded). It carries the reading of each criterion, the goal, the quality items, the gate commands and the verification of the agent's claims.
- `CONTRACT_COMMITTED` { contractId: string, status: "applied"|"committed"|"failed"|"skipped", hash?: string, note: string, occurrenceId?: string }: The finished work was published to the project: `committed` (as a git commit, `hash` given), `applied` (as uncommitted changes), `skipped` (nothing to publish) or `failed`; `note` says what was done.
- `CONTRACT_CREATED` { contractId: string, sessionId: string, origin: "agent-tool"|"cli"|"external"|"hosted"|"proposal"|"turn", ask: string, ownerAgentId: string, gateProblems?: string[], occurrenceId?: string }: A contract was created for a piece of work. `ask` is the request as given, `origin` where it came from (a turn, the agent tool, the command line, a hosted session, an outside client or a proposal), `sessionId` the session it belongs to and `ownerAgentId` the agent record its parent waits on.
- `CONTRACT_CRITERION_REGRESSED` { contractId: string, unitId: string, criterionId: string, metAtCheckId: string, checkId: string, occurrenceId?: string }: A criterion that read met at check `metAtCheckId` reads unmet at check `checkId`; a nudge always follows.
- `CONTRACT_ESCALATED` { contractId: string, escalationId: string, scope: "deliverable"|"group"|"plan"|"shape"|"unit", targetId: string, reason: "attempts-undecided"|"fix-rounds-exhausted"|"owner-decision-needed"|"plan-unresolved"|"stalled"|"unsettled"|"writing-unclear", question: string, unmetCriterionIds: string[], occurrenceId?: string }: The contract needs the owner: `question` is what the owner is asked, `reason` why (an unresolved plan, a stall, an unsettled reading, fix rounds used up, unclear writing permission, undecided attempts, an owner-only decision), and the contract waits in `awaiting-owner` for the reply.
- `CONTRACT_FAILED` { contractId: string, reason: string, failureKind: "budget"|"judgment-unavailable"|"max_turns"|"other"|"owner-rejected"|"planning"|"transport"|"zombie", membersSettled: boolean, turnLimit?: number, turnLimitSource?: "default"|"policy-bound"|"spawn-override", occurrenceId?: string }: The contract failed. `failureKind` names the cause (transport, max_turns, planning, budget, owner-rejected, judgment-unavailable, zombie, other) and `reason` says it in words; `turnLimit` and its source are given for a max_turns failure.
- `CONTRACT_FIX_PLANNED` { contractId: string, scope: "deliverable"|"group"|"unit", targetId: string, groupId: string, unitIds: string[], round: number, occurrenceId?: string }: A fix group was planned for a stalled or failing target: `unitIds` are its units and `round` counts fix rounds.
- `CONTRACT_GATE_RESULT` { contractId: string, targetId: string, gate: string, passed: boolean, skipped: boolean, durationMs: number, outcome?: "failed"|"passed"|"unverified", required?: boolean, reason?: string, occurrenceId?: string }: One gate command from the `contract.gates` setting ran against a target: whether it passed or was skipped, how long it took, its outcome, whether it is required, and why when it did not pass.
- `CONTRACT_GROUP_STATUS_CHANGED` { contractId: string, groupId: string, from: "awaiting-owner"|"blocked"|"cancelled"|"failed"|"fixing"|"judging"|"passed"|"pending"|"running", to: "awaiting-owner"|"blocked"|"cancelled"|"failed"|"fixing"|"judging"|"passed"|"pending"|"running", occurrenceId?: string }: A group of units moved from one status to another.
- `CONTRACT_MERGE_CONFLICT` { contractId: string, unitId: string, branch: string, path: string, files: string[], occurrenceId?: string }: Merging a unit's branch back conflicted: `branch` and `path` name the unit's worktree and `files` the conflicting files.
- `CONTRACT_NUDGED` { contractId: string, unitId: string, nudgeId: string, checkId: string, kinds: "claims"|"gate"|"quality"|"regression"|"unmet"|"unshown", criterionIds: string[], delivery: "bus"|"hold"|"wake", agentId: string, occurrenceId?: string }: A unit's agent was told what is still wrong (`kinds`: unmet or unshown criteria, a regression, quality, a gate, claims) so it fixes it and is checked again. `delivery` is how it reached the agent: `hold` (kept for the end of its current turn), `bus` (sent while it runs) or `wake` (a finished or failed agent was woken with it).
- `CONTRACT_NUDGE_CONSUMED` { contractId: string, unitId: string, nudgeId: string, agentId: string, turn?: number, occurrenceId?: string }: The nudged agent took the nudge into its conversation, at turn `turn`.
- `CONTRACT_OWNER_REPLIED` { contractId: string, escalationId: string, reading: "amend"|"approve"|"reject"|"unclear", outcome: "act"|"confirm"|"escalate", action: "amended"|"approved"|"asked-again"|"refused"|"stopped", occurrenceId?: string }: The owner answered an escalation. `reading` is how the reply was read (approve, reject, amend, unclear) and `action` what the runner did with it (approved, amended, stopped, asked again, refused).
- `CONTRACT_PASSED` { contractId: string, criteriaMet: number, criteriaJudged: number, excluded: number, nudges: number, occurrenceId?: string }: The contract passed: `criteriaMet` of `criteriaJudged` criteria met, `excluded` criteria not judged, after `nudges` nudges.
- `CONTRACT_PLANNED` { contractId: string, goal: string, criteria: object[], groups: object[], units: object[], repair: number, occurrenceId?: string }: The planner produced a plan (or repaired one): the goal, the acceptance criteria, the groups of units and the units themselves. `repair` is 0 for the first plan and n for the nth repair.
- `CONTRACT_PLAN_CHECKED` { contractId: string, check: "criterion-shape"|"criterion-trace"|"plan-coverage"|"structure"|"unit-shape", targetId?: string, passed: boolean, problems: object[], decisionIds: string[], occurrenceId?: string }: One check of the plan ran: `structure` and `criterion-trace` by code, the others by the decision model. `passed` says whether it held; `problems` lists what is wrong, by code and target.
- `CONTRACT_SHAPED` { contractId: string, forbidsDelegation: object, requestsParallelAgents: object, forbidsWriting: object, asksForAttempts: object, decisionIds: string[], occurrenceId?: string }: The request was read for its shape before planning: whether it forbids delegating, asks for parallel agents, forbids writing, or asks for several attempts. Each reading carries its verdict, probability and what code does with it; `decisionIds` are the decision-log records.
- `CONTRACT_SPAWN_GUARD_TRIGGERED` { contractId?: string, agentId: string, depth: number, activeAgents: number, reason: string, occurrenceId?: string }: A request to start an agent was refused: a contract's unit agent or planner may not start agents of its own (the contract plans sub-work), or the spawn would pass the nesting depth or active-agent limits. `depth` and `activeAgents` are the values at the refusal.
- `CONTRACT_STALLED` { contractId: string, scope: "deliverable"|"group"|"unit", targetId: string, route: "fresh"|"owner"|"split", unmetCriterionIds: string[], reason: string, decisionId?: string, occurrenceId?: string }: A unit, group or deliverable stopped making progress on its unmet criteria. `route` is what happens next: `split` (a planned fix of smaller units), `fresh` (a new agent starts it over) or `owner` (the owner is asked).
- `CONTRACT_STATUS_CHANGED` { contractId: string, from: "awaiting-owner"|"cancelled"|"checking-plan"|"committing"|"failed"|"fixing"|"judging"|"passed"|"planning"|"queued"|"running"|"shaping", to: "awaiting-owner"|"cancelled"|"checking-plan"|"committing"|"failed"|"fixing"|"judging"|"passed"|"planning"|"queued"|"running"|"shaping", occurrenceId?: string }: A contract moved from one lifecycle status to another (queued, shaping, planning, running, judging, fixing, committing, awaiting-owner, passed, failed, cancelled).
- `CONTRACT_UNIT_SILENT` { contractId: string, unitId: string, agentId: string, silentMs: number, action: "failed"|"retried", occurrenceId?: string }: A unit's agent produced nothing for `silentMs`; `action` says whether it was retried with a new agent or the unit failed.
- `CONTRACT_UNIT_SPAWNED` { contractId: string, unitId: string, agentId: string, route: object, purpose: "fresh-unit"|"resume"|"silence-retry"|"transport-retry"|"unit", occurrenceId?: string }: An agent was started to work a unit. `route` is the model, provider and reasoning effort chosen and why; `purpose` says whether it is the unit's first agent, a fresh start, or a retry after a transport failure, a silence or a resume.
- `CONTRACT_UNIT_STATUS_CHANGED` { contractId: string, groupId: string, unitId: string, from: "awaiting-owner"|"blocked"|"cancelled"|"checking"|"failed"|"fixing"|"held"|"held-merge"|"nudged"|"passed"|"pending"|"running", to: "awaiting-owner"|"blocked"|"cancelled"|"checking"|"failed"|"fixing"|"held"|"held-merge"|"nudged"|"passed"|"pending"|"running", agentId?: string, occurrenceId?: string }: A unit of work moved from one status to another; `agentId` is the agent working it, when one is.

Domain `control-plane` (access: admin):

- `CONTROL_PLANE_AUTH_GRANTED` { clientId: string, principalId: string, principalKind: "bot"|"service"|"token"|"user", scopes: string[] }: A connected client was authenticated: `principalId` and `principalKind` say who it acts as and `scopes` what it may do.
- `CONTROL_PLANE_CLIENT_CONNECTED` { clientId: string, clientKind: "bluebubbles"|"daemon"|"discord"|"google-chat"|"homeassistant"|"imessage"|"matrix"|"mattermost"|"msteams"|"ntfy"|"service"|"signal"|"slack"|"telegram"|"telephony"|"tui"|"web"|"webhook"|"whatsapp", transport: "http"|"local"|"sse"|"webhook"|"websocket"|"ws" }: A client opened a live connection to the daemon (a web UI, a terminal app, a service): `clientKind` is what it is and `transport` how it is connected.
- `CONTROL_PLANE_CLIENT_DISCONNECTED` { clientId: string, reason: string }: A connected client went away; `reason` says why (it closed, it timed out, it was dropped).
- `CONTROL_PLANE_SUBSCRIPTION_CREATED` { clientId: string, subscriptionId: string, topics: string[] }: A connected client subscribed to runtime events; `topics` are the event domains it receives.
- `CONTROL_PLANE_SUBSCRIPTION_DROPPED` { clientId: string, subscriptionId: string, reason: string }: A client's event subscription ended; `reason` says why.

Domain `deliveries` (access: admin):

- `DELIVERY_DEAD_LETTERED` { deliveryId: string, jobId: string, runId: string, surfaceKind: "bluebubbles"|"discord"|"google-chat"|"homeassistant"|"imessage"|"matrix"|"mattermost"|"msteams"|"ntfy"|"service"|"signal"|"slack"|"telegram"|"telephony"|"tui"|"web"|"webhook"|"whatsapp", targetId: string, reason: string, attempts: number }: A delivery used every attempt it had and was set aside as a dead letter; `attempts` is how many were made and `reason` the last failure.
- `DELIVERY_FAILED` { deliveryId: string, jobId: string, runId: string, surfaceKind: "bluebubbles"|"discord"|"google-chat"|"homeassistant"|"imessage"|"matrix"|"mattermost"|"msteams"|"ntfy"|"service"|"signal"|"slack"|"telegram"|"telephony"|"tui"|"web"|"webhook"|"whatsapp", targetId: string, failedAt: number, error: string, retryable: boolean }: A delivery attempt failed; `retryable` says whether another attempt will follow (false once every try is used, which DELIVERY_DEAD_LETTERED then announces).
- `DELIVERY_QUEUED` { deliveryId: string, jobId: string, runId: string, surfaceKind: "bluebubbles"|"discord"|"google-chat"|"homeassistant"|"imessage"|"matrix"|"mattermost"|"msteams"|"ntfy"|"service"|"signal"|"slack"|"telegram"|"telephony"|"tui"|"web"|"webhook"|"whatsapp", targetId: string, deliveryKind: "callback"|"notification"|"reply" }: A scheduled run's result was queued for delivery to a route: `surfaceKind` is the surface (Slack, a webhook, ntfy...), `targetId` the route, and `deliveryKind` whether it is a reply, a webhook callback or a notification.
- `DELIVERY_STARTED` { deliveryId: string, jobId: string, runId: string, surfaceKind: "bluebubbles"|"discord"|"google-chat"|"homeassistant"|"imessage"|"matrix"|"mattermost"|"msteams"|"ntfy"|"service"|"signal"|"slack"|"telegram"|"telephony"|"tui"|"web"|"webhook"|"whatsapp", targetId: string, startedAt: number }: An attempt to send a queued delivery began.
- `DELIVERY_SUCCEEDED` { deliveryId: string, jobId: string, runId: string, surfaceKind: "bluebubbles"|"discord"|"google-chat"|"homeassistant"|"imessage"|"matrix"|"mattermost"|"msteams"|"ntfy"|"service"|"signal"|"slack"|"telegram"|"telephony"|"tui"|"web"|"webhook"|"whatsapp", targetId: string, completedAt: number, durationMs: number }: A delivery reached its target; `durationMs` is how long the attempt took.
- `DELIVERY_WAITING` { jobId: string, runId: string, surface: "agent" }: Something is waiting for a surface that collects its own messages. The Agent reads occasion reminders through `occasions.pending`; this tells a connected Agent to read now instead of at its next turn or idle check. It carries no text: the reminder stays on the host until it is answered.

Domain `fleet` (access: admin):

- `FLEET_NODE_BLOCKED_ON_USER` { nodeId: string, kind: "acp-agent"|"agent"|"background-process"|"code-index"|"contract"|"contract-group"|"contract-unit"|"hook-action"|"observed-external"|"schedule"|"trigger"|"watcher"|"workflow", reason: "approval"|"conflict"|"input"|"pick", label: string, detail?: string, sessionId?: string, agentId?: string }: A node became blocked waiting for a human (approve/deny, input, a ready best-of-N pick, or a merge conflict).
- `FLEET_NODE_FINISHED` { nodeId: string, kind: "acp-agent"|"agent"|"background-process"|"code-index"|"contract"|"contract-group"|"contract-unit"|"hook-action"|"observed-external"|"schedule"|"trigger"|"watcher"|"workflow", state: "awaiting-approval"|"done"|"executing-tool"|"failed"|"idle"|"interrupted"|"killed"|"paused"|"queued"|"retrying"|"stalled"|"streaming"|"thinking", previousState: "awaiting-approval"|"done"|"executing-tool"|"failed"|"idle"|"interrupted"|"killed"|"paused"|"queued"|"retrying"|"stalled"|"streaming"|"thinking", label: string, sessionId?: string }: A node reached a terminal state (done/failed/killed/interrupted).
- `FLEET_NODE_STARTED` { nodeId: string, kind: "acp-agent"|"agent"|"background-process"|"code-index"|"contract"|"contract-group"|"contract-unit"|"hook-action"|"observed-external"|"schedule"|"trigger"|"watcher"|"workflow", label: string, state: "awaiting-approval"|"done"|"executing-tool"|"failed"|"idle"|"interrupted"|"killed"|"paused"|"queued"|"retrying"|"stalled"|"streaming"|"thinking", parentId?: string, sessionId?: string }: A node appeared in the fleet for the first time.
- `FLEET_NODE_STATE_CHANGED` { nodeId: string, kind: "acp-agent"|"agent"|"background-process"|"code-index"|"contract"|"contract-group"|"contract-unit"|"hook-action"|"observed-external"|"schedule"|"trigger"|"watcher"|"workflow", state: "awaiting-approval"|"done"|"executing-tool"|"failed"|"idle"|"interrupted"|"killed"|"paused"|"queued"|"retrying"|"stalled"|"streaming"|"thinking", previousState: "awaiting-approval"|"done"|"executing-tool"|"failed"|"idle"|"interrupted"|"killed"|"paused"|"queued"|"retrying"|"stalled"|"streaming"|"thinking", label: string, sessionId?: string }: A node's coarse state changed (non-terminal, non-block transition).
- `FLEET_NODE_UNBLOCKED` { nodeId: string, kind: "acp-agent"|"agent"|"background-process"|"code-index"|"contract"|"contract-group"|"contract-unit"|"hook-action"|"observed-external"|"schedule"|"trigger"|"watcher"|"workflow", state: "awaiting-approval"|"done"|"executing-tool"|"failed"|"idle"|"interrupted"|"killed"|"paused"|"queued"|"retrying"|"stalled"|"streaming"|"thinking", label: string, sessionId?: string }: A previously blocked node is no longer waiting on a human.

Domain `forensics` (access: admin):

- `FORENSICS_REPORT_CREATED` { reportId: string, classification: string, errorMessage?: string, taskId?: string, turnId?: string }: A new failure report has been generated for a terminal task or turn.

Domain `gate` (access: admin):

- `DECISION_EMITTED` { callId: string, tool: string, category: string, approved: boolean, source: string, sourceLayer?: string, persisted?: boolean, reasonCode?: string, classification?: string, riskLevel?: string, summary?: string }: The gate's final decision for the call.
- `GATE_REQUESTED` { callId: string, tool: string, args: object, category: string, classification?: string, riskLevel?: string, summary?: string, reasons?: string[] }: A tool call has reached the gate.
- `PRESET_CHANGED` { preset: string, previousPreset: string, mode: string, previousMode: string }: The active preset changed (normal, accept-edits, plan, auto, custom). Emitted whenever the `permissions.mode` setting changes so surfaces can render a live preset pill without polling. `mode` and `previousMode` are the setting's values ('prompt' | 'allow-all' | 'custom' | 'plan' | 'accept-edits'); `preset` and `previousPreset` are the preset names.

Domain `knowledge` (access: admin):

- `KNOWLEDGE_COMPILE_COMPLETED` { sourceId: string, nodeCount: number, edgeCount: number }: An extracted source was compiled into the knowledge graph: `nodeCount` nodes and `edgeCount` edges.
- `KNOWLEDGE_EXTRACTION_COMPLETED` { sourceId: string, extractionId: string, format: string, estimatedTokens: number }: The text of an ingested source was extracted and stored: `format` is what it was read as and `estimatedTokens` its size.
- `KNOWLEDGE_EXTRACTION_FAILED` { sourceId: string, error: string }: Extracting the text of an ingested source failed; nothing from it was stored.
- `KNOWLEDGE_INGEST_COMPLETED` { sourceId: string, status: string, artifactId?: string, title?: string }: A source was read into the knowledge store; `status` is the source's stored status, and `artifactId` and `title` name what was kept, when there is one.
- `KNOWLEDGE_INGEST_FAILED` { sourceId: string, error: string }: Reading a source into the knowledge store failed; `error` says why.
- `KNOWLEDGE_INGEST_STARTED` { sourceId: string, connectorId: string, sourceType: string, uri?: string }: Reading a source into the knowledge store began: `connectorId` is the connector reading it, `sourceType` its kind and `uri` where it is, when it has an address.
- `KNOWLEDGE_JOB_COMPLETED` { jobId: string, runId: string, durationMs: number }: A knowledge job finished; `durationMs` is how long it ran.
- `KNOWLEDGE_JOB_FAILED` { jobId: string, runId: string, error: string, durationMs: number }: A knowledge job failed after `durationMs`; `error` says why.
- `KNOWLEDGE_JOB_QUEUED` { jobId: string, runId: string, mode: "background"|"inline" }: A knowledge maintenance job was queued to run, either `inline` (now, in the caller) or in the `background`.
- `KNOWLEDGE_JOB_STARTED` { jobId: string, runId: string, mode: "background"|"inline" }: A queued knowledge job began running.
- `KNOWLEDGE_LINT_COMPLETED` { issueCount: number }: A knowledge store check finished; `issueCount` is the number of issues it recorded.
- `KNOWLEDGE_PACKET_BUILT` { task: string, itemCount: number, estimatedTokens: number, detail: "compact"|"detailed"|"standard" }: A packet of knowledge was assembled for a task (`task` is a preview of it): `itemCount` items, `estimatedTokens` in size, at `detail` level.
- `KNOWLEDGE_PROJECTION_MATERIALIZED` { targetId: string, artifactId: string, pageCount: number }: A Markdown projection was rendered and saved as an artifact (`artifactId`), `pageCount` pages.
- `KNOWLEDGE_PROJECTION_RENDERED` { targetId: string, pageCount: number }: Knowledge was rendered as Markdown pages for a projection target, without saving them; `pageCount` is how many.

Domain `mcp` (access: authenticated):

- `MCP_AUTH_REQUIRED` { serverId: string, authType: string }: MCP server requires authentication before proceeding.
- `MCP_CONFIGURED` { serverId: string, transport: string, url?: string, role?: "analytics"|"automation"|"browser"|"communication"|"custom"|"database"|"devops"|"docs"|"filesystem"|"general"|"git"|"ops"|"remote"|"search", trustMode?: "allow-all"|"ask-on-risk"|"blocked"|"constrained", allowedPaths?: string[], allowedHosts?: string[] }: MCP server configuration has been parsed and validated.
- `MCP_CONNECTED` { serverId: string, toolCount: number, resourceCount: number }: Connection to MCP server established successfully.
- `MCP_CONNECTING` { serverId: string }: Connection attempt to MCP server is in progress.
- `MCP_DEGRADED` { serverId: string, reason: string, availableTools: string[] }: MCP server is running in degraded mode (partial tool availability).
- `MCP_DISCONNECTED` { serverId: string, reason?: string, willRetry: boolean }: Connection to MCP server has been dropped or closed.
- `MCP_POLICY_UPDATED` { serverId: string, role: "analytics"|"automation"|"browser"|"communication"|"custom"|"database"|"devops"|"docs"|"filesystem"|"general"|"git"|"ops"|"remote"|"search", trustMode: "allow-all"|"ask-on-risk"|"blocked"|"constrained", allowedPaths: string[], allowedHosts: string[], deniedTools?: string[], allowedTools?: string[] }: MCP trust/role policy or a per-tool rule has changed. `deniedTools` and `allowedTools` are the per-tool rules in force (a deny wins).
- `MCP_RECONNECTING` { serverId: string, attempt: number, maxAttempts: number }: Attempting to re-establish a dropped MCP connection.
- `MCP_SCHEMA_QUARANTINED` { serverId: string, reason: "incompatible"|"operator_flagged"|"stale_threshold"|"unsupported", detail?: string }: MCP schema has been quarantined. Tool execution on this server is blocked until the schema is refreshed or an operator explicitly approves a temporary override.
- `MCP_SCHEMA_QUARANTINE_APPROVED` { serverId: string, operatorId: string }: An operator has acknowledged a quarantined schema and approved a temporary execution override. Freshness transitions to `stale`; a refresh is still recommended.

Domain `ops` (access: authenticated):

- `OPS_LISTENER_MISBEHAVING` { listenerId: string, eventType: string, errorMessage: string, errorCount: number }: A subscriber threw an error during event dispatch; emitted after dedup threshold.

Emitted so operators (and supervisors) see the daemon defending its own footprint instead of drifting toward OOM.
- `OPS_POWER_STATE_CHANGED` { inhibited: boolean, keepAwake: boolean, workReasons: string[], note?: string, sleepEdgeNote?: string }: The host sleep-ownership state changed (work inhibitor, keep-awake toggle, sleep edge).
- `OPS_TASK_CANCELLED` { taskId: string, reason: "ops_agent_cancel"|"ops_cancel"|"ops_pause"|"ops_resume"|"ops_retry"|"user_requested", note?: string }: Operator cancelled a running or queued task.
- `OPS_TASK_PAUSED` { taskId: string, reason: "ops_agent_cancel"|"ops_cancel"|"ops_pause"|"ops_resume"|"ops_retry"|"user_requested", note?: string }: Operator paused a running task (transitions to blocked).
- `OPS_TASK_RESUMED` { taskId: string, reason: "ops_agent_cancel"|"ops_cancel"|"ops_pause"|"ops_resume"|"ops_retry"|"user_requested", note?: string }: Operator resumed a blocked task.
- `OPS_TASK_RETRIED` { taskId: string, reason: "ops_agent_cancel"|"ops_cancel"|"ops_pause"|"ops_resume"|"ops_retry"|"user_requested", note?: string }: Operator retried a failed or cancelled task.

- `WORK_PLAN_TASK_UPDATED` { task: object, previousTask: object, projectId: string, knowledgeSpaceId: string, workPlanId: string, revision: number }: A work plan task changed; `task` is the task now and `previousTask` before.

Domain `providers` (access: authenticated):

- `BATCH_JOB_SETTLED` { jobId: string, status: "cancelled"|"completed"|"dead_lettered"|"expired"|"failed", provider: string, model: string, completedAt: number, providerBatchId?: string, errorCode?: string, errorMessage?: string }: A daemon batch job reached its final state, so a surface can show the result without polling. Domain `tools` (access: admin):

- `BUDGET_EXCEEDED_COST` { callId: string, turnId: string, tool: string, phase: string, limitCostUsd: number, usedCostUsd: number }: A tool call reported a cost (`usedCostUsd`, its result's costUsd) over `runtime.toolBudget.maxCostUsd` (`limitCostUsd`).
- `BUDGET_EXCEEDED_MS` { callId: string, turnId: string, tool: string, phase: string, limitMs: number, elapsedMs: number }: A tool call went over its `runtime.toolBudget.*` limit (with `runtime.toolBudget.enforced` on). `phase` is `executing` when the time limit stopped the call, `completed` when the call finished over a limit (it still succeeded; the model is told which limit it went over).
- `BUDGET_EXCEEDED_TOKENS` { callId: string, turnId: string, tool: string, phase: string, limitTokens: number, usedTokens: number }: A tool call reported more tokens (`usedTokens`, its result's tokenCount) than `runtime.toolBudget.maxTokens` (`limitTokens`).
- `TOOL_CANCELLED` { callId: string, turnId: string, tool: string, reason?: string }: Tool call was cancelled before completion.
- `TOOL_DISPATCH_ERROR` { ruleId: string, tool?: string, reason?: string, playbooks: string[] }: Every tool the health system tracks is failing, so turns that call them are affected. Published by the tool-failed health rule, with the playbooks that diagnose it; `tool` is the tool whose failure tipped the domain.
- `TOOL_EXECUTING` { callId: string, turnId: string, tool: string, startedAt: number }: Tool is actively executing.
- `TOOL_FAILED` { callId: string, turnId: string, tool: string, error: string, durationMs: number, result?: object }: Tool call failed with an error.
- `TOOL_PERMISSIONED` { callId: string, turnId: string, tool: string, approved: boolean, autonomousDecision?: object }: Permission check completed; call may proceed.
- `TOOL_RECEIVED` { callId: string, turnId: string, tool: string, args: object }: A tool call request was received from the LLM.
- `TOOL_RECONCILED` { turnId: string, count: number, callIds: string[], toolNames: string[], reason: string, timestamp: number, isMalformed?: boolean }: Tool results were synthesized to reconcile unresolved calls.
- `TOOL_SUCCEEDED` { callId: string, turnId: string, tool: string, durationMs: number, result?: object }: Tool call completed successfully.

Domain `transport` (access: authenticated):

- `STREAM_SUBSCRIBER_CONNECTED` { streamId: string, subscriberId: string, streamType: string }: An SSE subscriber connected to the event stream.
- `STREAM_SUBSCRIBER_DISCONNECTED` { streamId: string, subscriberId: string, streamType: string, reason?: string }: An SSE subscriber disconnected from the event stream.
- `TRANSPORT_AUTHENTICATING` { transportId: string }: Transport is authenticating with the remote endpoint.
- `TRANSPORT_BACKPRESSURE` { transportId: string, droppedCount: number, queueLength: number, queueBytes: number, reason: "message_too_large"|"queue_full" }: The WebSocket connector's outbound queue refused a message: it was full (count or bytes) while the socket was down or not yet authenticated, or the message alone was over the byte limit. Emitted on the first drop since the queue last drained and on every tenth after it, alongside `onBackpressure`.
- `TRANSPORT_CONNECTED` { transportId: string, endpoint: string }: Transport connection is established and ready.
- `TRANSPORT_CONNECTION_STATE` { transportId: string, state: "connected"|"connecting"|"disconnected"|"failed"|"reconnecting" }: The realtime transport connection state has changed. Emitted by `createWebSocketConnector` on every state transition. Subscribe to this in UI layers to drive connection-state badges (e.g. online/reconnecting indicators). The `onConnectionStateChange` callback in `RuntimeEventConnectorOptions` fires at the same time and provides the same state string for non-event-bus consumers.
- `TRANSPORT_DISCONNECTED` { transportId: string, reason?: string, willRetry: boolean }: Transport connection has been closed.
- `TRANSPORT_INITIALIZING` { transportId: string, protocol: string }: Transport layer is being initialised.
- `TRANSPORT_RECONNECT_ATTEMPT` { transportId: string, attempt: number, maxAttempts: number, delayMs: number, reason: string }: A realtime transport reconnect attempt is scheduled. Carries the attempt, the backoff delay and the reason, for diagnostic UIs.
- `TRANSPORT_RETRY_EXECUTED` { transportId: string, attempt: number, maxAttempts: number }: A scheduled retry is now being executed.
- `TRANSPORT_RETRY_SCHEDULED` { transportId: string, attempt: number, maxAttempts: number, backoffMs: number, reason: string }: A retry has been scheduled after a transient failure.
- `TRANSPORT_SYNCING` { transportId: string }: Transport is synchronising state with the remote.
- `TRANSPORT_TERMINAL_FAILURE` { transportId: string, error: string }: Transport has failed unrecoverably and will not retry.

Domain `turn` (access: admin):

- `DRAFT_WITHDRAWN` { turnId: string, reason: string }: The completion check sent back the draft streamed since the last STREAM_START: a reader removes that text (and stops speaking it); the next request streams the replacement from empty. `reason` is the check's reason.
- `LLM_REQUEST_STARTED` { turnId: string, provider: string, model: string, promptSummary: unknown }: An LLM request is about to be dispatched to the provider.
- `LLM_RESPONSE_RECEIVED` { turnId: string, provider: string, model: string, contentSummary: unknown, toolCallCount: number, inputTokens: number, outputTokens: number, cacheReadTokens?: number, cacheWriteTokens?: number, durationMs?: number, retries?: number, costUsdCents?: number, costSource?: "catalog"|"provider"|"subscription"|"unknown"|"user", signIn?: object, finishReason?: string, providerRequestId?: string, originTool?: string, originCallId?: string, originHook?: string, originMcpServer?: string, rateLimit?: object }: A provider chat call completed within the current turn iteration.
- `PREFLIGHT_FAIL` { turnId: string, reason: string, stopReason: "context_overflow"|"preflight_failed" }: Preflight checks failed; turn will not proceed.
- `PREFLIGHT_OK` { turnId: string }: Preflight checks (context, rate limits, etc.) passed.
- `STREAM_DELTA` { turnId: string, content: string, accumulated: string, provisional?: boolean, reasoning?: string, toolCalls?: object[] }: An incremental content chunk arrived from the provider. `content` is the chunk and `accumulated` the response's text so far. With `provisional`, the text is a draft: an answer the completion check sends back is replaced by the next request's stream (which starts again from empty), so a reader shows it as in progress until TURN_COMPLETED.
- `STREAM_END` { turnId: string, scope?: "provider", terminal?: boolean }: A provider stream iteration has ended. This is not the logical end of the turn when tools or multi-step provider calls are involved. Clients that need turn completion should wait for TURN_COMPLETED, TURN_ERROR, TURN_CANCEL, or PREFLIGHT_FAIL.
- `STREAM_RETRY` { turnId: string, provider: string, attempt: number, maxAttempts: number, delayMs: number, reason: string, status?: number, rateLimited?: boolean, retryAfterMs?: number }: A provider chat call hit a retryable transport error mid-stream and is about to retry the same request against the same provider after a delay. This is distinct from provider failover (a new provider chosen after a terminal TURN_ERROR): STREAM_RETRY fires from inside a single in-flight `provider.chat()` call, before any TURN_ERROR is ever raised.
- `STREAM_START` { turnId: string, scope?: "provider", terminal?: boolean }: A provider stream iteration has begun inside the logical turn.
- `TOOLS_DONE` { turnId: string }: All tool calls in the current batch have completed.
- `TOOL_BATCH_READY` { turnId: string, toolCalls: string[] }: A batch of tool calls is ready for execution.
- `TURN_CANCEL` { turnId: string, reason?: string, stopReason: "cancelled", requestedAt?: number }: Turn was cancelled by the user or system. `requestedAt` (epoch ms) is when the cancel was asked for, so the time the turn took to stop is the envelope's `ts` minus it.
- `TURN_COMPLETED` { turnId: string, response: string, stopReason: "completed"|"empty_response", metadata?: object }: Turn completed successfully with a final response. `metadata.memory.recordIds` carries the MEMORY-sourced knowledge-record ids that were injected into this turn (TurnInjectionRecord.injectedIds filtered to source 'memory', code-index hits are deliberately excluded). The path shape matches the documented surface convention exactly (`metadata.memory.recordIds: string[]`), so a provenance chip reads it unchanged. A turn with no memory injections carries NO metadata field, honest absence, never an empty array.
- `TURN_ERROR` { turnId: string, error: string, stopReason: "context_overflow"|"hook_denied"|"preflight_failed"|"provider_error"|"provider_exhausted"|"tool_loop_circuit_breaker"|"unexpected_error", status?: number, code?: string, attempts?: number, attemptTimes?: array, providerName?: string, provider?: string, model?: string, changes?: object, fallbackOrderSet?: boolean, fallbackNote?: string, refusal?: "daemon-unreachable"|"no-model"|"no-provider"|"workspace-not-registered" }: Turn failed with an error.
- `TURN_SUBMITTED` { turnId: string, prompt: string, origin?: object }: User prompt has been submitted for processing.

Domain `ui` (access: authenticated):

- `UI_PANEL_CLOSE` { panelId: string }: A panel was closed.
- `UI_PANEL_FOCUS` { panelId: string }: A panel became the focused (top) panel.
- `UI_PANEL_OPEN` { panelId: string }: A panel was opened.
- `UI_VIEW_CHANGED` { from: string, to: string }: The view that fills the screen changed (e.g. main -> agent:a1).

Domain `watchers` (access: authenticated):

- `WATCHER_CHECKPOINT_ADVANCED` { watcherId: string, sourceKind: "api"|"file"|"poll"|"stream"|"tail"|"webhook", checkpoint: string }: Published after a run whose checkpoint differs from the previous one; a run that sees the same checkpoint publishes only WATCHER_HEARTBEAT.
- `WATCHER_FAILED` { watcherId: string, sourceKind: "api"|"file"|"poll"|"stream"|"tail"|"webhook", error: string, retryable: boolean }: A watcher run failed; `retryable` says whether it will try again.
- `WATCHER_HEARTBEAT` { watcherId: string, sourceKind: "api"|"file"|"poll"|"stream"|"tail"|"webhook", seenAt: number, checkpoint: string }: A watcher ran and saw its source at `seenAt`; `checkpoint` is how far it has read. Published after every run.
- `WATCHER_STARTED` { watcherId: string, sourceKind: "api"|"file"|"poll"|"stream"|"tail"|"webhook", name: string }: A watcher began watching its source; `sourceKind` is how it reads it (poll, webhook, tail, file, api, stream) and `name` is its display name.
- `WATCHER_STOPPED` { watcherId: string, sourceKind: "api"|"file"|"poll"|"stream"|"tail"|"webhook", reason: string }: A watcher stopped watching; `reason` says why (`stopped` by default, `removed` when it was deleted).

Domain `workspace` (access: authenticated):

- `HUNK_REVERTED` { path: string, hunkHeader: string, sessionId: string|null, safetyCheckpointId: string|null, undoAvailable: boolean }: A single unified-diff hunk was reverse-applied to its file in the working tree (checkpoints.revertHunk), the per-hunk counterpart to a whole-checkpoint restore. `undoAvailable` is true when a pre-revert whole-tree safety checkpoint was recorded (restore it to reverse the revert).
- `REWIND_APPLIED` { sessionId: string, turnId: string|null, scope: "both"|"conversation"|"files", filesRestored: boolean, conversationRewound: boolean, undoAvailable: boolean }: A unified rewind was APPLIED (rewind.apply), the receipt surfaces render. `undoAvailable` is true when the apply recorded an undo point (a pre-restore safety checkpoint and/or a captured conversation snapshot) so the rewind can be reversed.
- `REWIND_PLANNED` { sessionId: string, turnId: string|null, scope: "both"|"conversation"|"files" }: A unified rewind was PREVIEWED (rewind.plan), a surface can render that a rewind to this turn anchor is staged and awaiting confirmation. Read-only: nothing has changed yet.
- `WORKSPACE_SWAP_COMPLETED` { from: string, to: string, persistedInDaemonSettings: boolean }: Emitted by the daemon once it serves on the new working directory after a move, or, on a host that cannot move, once the change is saved for its next start.
- `WORKSPACE_SWAP_FAILED` { from: string, to: string, code: "INVALID_PATH"|"REROOT_FAILED"|"UNKNOWN", reason: string }: Emitted when a working-directory change fails: the path could not be created or saved, or a move failed and the daemon started again on its previous root. Any subscriber that saw WORKSPACE_SWAP_STARTED without a subsequent WORKSPACE_SWAP_COMPLETED should watch for this event.
- `WORKSPACE_SWAP_REFUSED` { from: string, to: string, reason: string, retryAfter: number }: Emitted when a change is refused because the daemon is already moving.
- `WORKSPACE_SWAP_STARTED` { from: string, to: string }: Emitted when the daemon begins to move to another working directory (every service stops and starts again there).

## Errors

The JSON body of a failed request, the failure categories and kinds, the shared error codes, and every code a daemon route declares with its HTTP status and meaning.

### Error body

Every failed daemon request answers with a JSON body of this shape; only `error` is always present.

- `error` (string, required): Why the request was not carried out.
- `state` (string, optional): What is true now, when the daemon refused rather than failed.
- `next` (array of string, optional): Steps that would get past the refusal, most useful first.
- `hint` (string, optional): `next[0]` when `next` is present.
- `code` (string, optional): A stable code. Known values are listed in `x-known-codes`; treat any other as opaque.
- `category` (one of `"authentication"`, `"authorization"`, `"billing"`, `"rate_limit"`, `"timeout"`, `"network"`, `"bad_request"`, `"not_found"`, `"permission"`, `"tool"`, `"config"`, `"protocol"`, `"service"`, `"internal"`, `"unknown"`, optional): The kind of failure: authentication, authorization, billing, rate limit, timeout, network, a bad request, not found, a permission refusal, a tool, configuration, protocol, a service failure, an internal fault, or unknown.
- `source` (string, optional): The layer the failure came from, such as `provider`, `tool`, `transport`, `config`, `permission` or `runtime`.
- `recoverable` (boolean, optional): True when another attempt can succeed; false when retrying the same request cannot.
- `status` (integer, optional): The HTTP status of the failure, including one an upstream provider answered with.
- `provider` (string, optional): The model provider involved, when a provider failed.
- `operation` (string, optional): What was being done when it failed, such as `chat` or `embed`.
- `phase` (string, optional): Where in that operation it failed, such as `request`, `stream`, `response` or `auth`.
- `requestId` (string, optional): The request id to quote when reporting the failure: the daemon's own, or the one an upstream service returned.
- `providerCode` (string, optional): The error code the upstream provider gave, verbatim.
- `providerType` (string, optional): The error type the upstream provider gave, verbatim.
- `retryAfterMs` (number, optional): Present when retrying later can succeed.

### Categories and kinds

A failure has a `category` and a `kind`. The categories marked "on the wire" are the values the `category` field of an error body can hold. The `kind` is never sent: a client computes it from the category. The category `contract` is a client's own (a reply that broke the operator contract) and is never sent either.

| Category | Kind | Category on the wire |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `authentication` | `auth` | yes |
| `authorization` | `auth` | yes |
| `bad_request` | `validation` | yes |
| `billing` | `auth` | yes |
| `config` | `config` | yes |
| `internal` | `internal` | yes |
| `network` | `network` | yes |
| `not_found` | `not-found` | yes |
| `permission` | `auth` | yes |
| `protocol` | `protocol` | yes |
| `rate_limit` | `rate-limit` | yes |
| `service` | `service` | yes |
| `timeout` | `network` | yes |
| `tool` | `tool` | yes |
| `unknown` | `unknown` | yes |
| `contract` | `contract` | no (client only) |

### Engine error codes

The shared codes any GoodVibes error may carry in `code`: `AGENT_FAILED`, `AGENT_TIMEOUT`, `AUTH_REQUIRED`, `CANCELLED`, `CONFLICT`, `CONTRACT_MISMATCH`, `CREDENTIAL_DESTINATION_UNBOUND`, `CREDENTIAL_NOT_FOR_TARGET`, `ENGINE_CONFIGURATION_ERROR`, `ENGINE_CONTRACT_ERROR`, `ENGINE_HTTP_STATUS_ERROR`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`, `METHOD_NOT_FOUND`, `NETWORK_UNREACHABLE`, `NOT_FOUND`, `NOT_INVOKABLE`, `PAYMENT_REQUIRED`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `PROTOCOL_ERROR`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, `SESSION_CLOSED`, `TARGET_CHANGED`, `TIMEOUT`, `TOKEN_EXPIRED`, `TOOL_EXEC_FAILED`, `UNKNOWN`, `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

### Codes any route may answer

Codes the shared request layer and the daemon's routes put in `code` beyond those a method declares (next table), found in the routes themselves. The meaning is the route's own message; `<name>` stands for a value filled in. Category is the `category` the body carries, or, where the body carries none, the one a client reads from the status. A code marked "in an answer" is not an error status: it comes in the `refusal` of a successful answer that was not applied.
